### compound | 225acdotalm3/overview | What is 225Ac-DOTA-LM3?
kind: overview
title: 225Ac-DOTA-LM3
summary: An alpha-emitting radiolabeled somatostatin receptor antagonist for peptide receptor radionuclide therapy (PRRT) in neuroendocrine tumors. Unlike conventional beta-emitting Lu-177 therapies and SSTR agonists, 225Ac-DOTA-LM3 combines the higher cell-killing power of alpha particles with antagonist binding for enhanced tumor targeting. Clinical stage investigational therapy showing promise in Lu-177-refractory patients.
keyPoint: An alpha-emitting radiolabeled somatostatin receptor antagonist for peptide receptor radionuclide therapy (PRRT) in neuroendocrine tumors.
understood: resolved
method: canonical

### compound | 225acdotalm3/evidence | What research is listed for 225Ac-DOTA-LM3?
kind: evidence
title: 225Ac-DOTA-LM3: research listed by the sources
summary: Moderate evidence; 18 human studies listed. multiple uncontrolled retrospective/observational human cohorts (Heidelberg n=35 + NEN-G3 rescue + TANDEM), no RCT. Mechanism: SSTR2 target with binding + functional antagonist confirmation and a fully mapped alpha-radiobiology chain. Plausibility: full mechanism->dosimetry->outcome chain, coherent with PRRT oncology, strong same-class analogy (Lutathera). Global Coverage: clinical work concentrated in one German/Swiss cluster, ~28 studies, investigational only. Community Experience: dossier confirms no meaningful community/user reports (hospital-administered investigational). Effectiveness basis clinical (low confidence): quantified human efficacy for the antagonist DOTA-LM3 class (85.1% disease control, 36.2% PR in the n=51 177Lu-DOTA-LM3 first-in-humans study) plus a 35-patient 225Ac-DOTA-LM3 Lu-177-refractory salvage series.

  *: PeptideDosage.org: No published human safety data exist for 5-Amino-1MQ; the entire safety profile is extrapolated from rodent preclinical work, which showed no overt toxicity at 20 mg/kg/day for 11 days but did not include extended-duration toxicology or carcinogenicity assessment [1].; Theoretical concerns center on systemic NNMT inhibition: NNMT also regulates methylation of biogenic amines and may affect histamine metabolism, with potential for altered methyl-pool homeostasis affecting epigenetic regulation across tissues.; Anecdotal user reports (not from controlled trials) describe mild gastrointestinal effects (nausea, soft stools), transient mild headache, and occasional insomnia at higher doses - none of which has been characterized in any published clinical trial.; Because NNMT activity also produces 1-methylnicotinamide, an endogenous compound with vascular and anti-inflammatory effects, NNMT inhibition may reduce circulating 1-MNA - the long-term consequences of this are unstudied in humans.; Drug-drug interactions are essentially uncharacterized; 5-Amino-1MQ's interaction with other
  *: PeptideDeck: Promotes fat cell metabolism and energy expenditure Increases NAD+ levels in adipose tissue May support 'browning' of white fat No central nervous system stimulation Potential muscle preservation effects May improve metabolic flexibility Reduces fat cell differentiation and growth Complementary to diet and exercise Active research area with published studies Research into NNMT inhibition for metabolic disease has accumulated primarily from genetic studies and, more recently, from pharmacological NNMT inhibitors like 5-Amino-1MQ. The seminal 2014 Nature paper demonstrated that mice with reduced NNMT (through genetic knockdown or antisense oligonucleotides) were protected from diet-induced obesity. Even when fed a high-fat diet, these mice gained less weight, had smaller fat cells, and showed improved insulin sensitivity. Crucially, this occurred without changes in food intake-the mice ate the same amount but accumulated less fat.

kind: overview
title: Abaloparatide
summary: An FDA-approved synthetic 34-amino-acid PTHrP analogue used as TYMLOS for osteoporosis in eligible postmenopausal women and men. Strong evidence is specific to labeled osteoporosis use, not anti-aging.
keyPoint: An FDA-approved synthetic 34-amino-acid PTHrP analogue used as TYMLOS for osteoporosis in eligible postmenopausal women and men.

method: canonical

  -: An FDA-approved synthetic 34-amino-acid PTHrP analogue used as TYMLOS for osteoporosis in eligible postmenopausal women and men.
section: How it works in the research
  -: Abaloparatide is a synthetic 34-amino-acid analogue of human PTHrP(1-34) that activates the PTH1 receptor.
section: Evidence strength
  -: PeptideDeck: Human clinical research; population: Human; Human evidence with design limitations to check. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Main limitations
  -: ⚠️ Black Box Warning: Abaloparatide carries an FDA black box warning regarding potential osteosarcoma (bone cancer) risk based on rat studies where the drug was given at much higher doses and for longer durations than human therapeutic use.

### compound | abaloparatide/evidence | What research is listed for Abaloparatide?
kind: evidence
title: Abaloparatide: research listed by the sources
summary: strong-human. The ACTIVE randomized trial included 2,463 postmenopausal women with osteoporosis and found lower vertebral and nonvertebral fracture incidence with abaloparatide than placebo. Those findings apply to the studied postmenopausal osteoporosis population; total trial enrollment must not be read as the abaloparatide treatment-arm size. Current TYMLOS labeling separately includes treatment to increase bone density in men with osteoporosis at high fracture risk or with appropriate treatment-failure/intolerance context. The strong evidence rating reflects established osteoporosis evidence and labeled use, not anti-aging. Stimulates new bone formation (anabolic effect) Reduces vertebral fracture risk by 86% vs placebo in clinical trials Reduces nonvertebral fracture risk by 43% vs placebo Improves bone mineral density at spine and hip Lower incidence of hypercalcemia than teriparatide Once-daily subcutaneous administration Can be followed by antiresorptive therapy to maintain gains FDA-approved with established safety profile Active research area with published studies The clinical development of abaloparatide centered on the ACTIVE program-a comprehensive series of trials that established its efficacy and safety profile. These studies provide robust evidence for its fracture reduction benefits. The pivotal Abaloparatide Comparator Trial In Vertebral Endpoints (ACTIVE) was an 18-month, randomized, double-blind trial comparing abaloparatide 80 mcg daily to both placebo and teriparatide 20 mcg daily in 2,463 postmenopausal women with osteoporosis.

section: Limitations
  -: Abaloparatide caused a dose-dependent increase in osteosarcoma in rat studies; it is unknown whether TYMLOS causes osteosarcoma in humans, and observational studies with PTH analogues have not shown an increased human risk
  -: Avoid use in patients at increased baseline risk of osteosarcoma, including patients with open epiphyses, metabolic bone diseases such as Paget’s disease, bone metastases or skeletal malignancies, prior skeletal radiation, or hereditary disorders predisposing to osteosarcoma
  -: Orthostatic hypotension can occur, particularly with early doses
  -: TYMLOS can cause hypercalcemia and is not recommended in patients with pre-existing hypercalcemia or underlying hypercalcemic disorders
  -: Hypercalciuria and urolithiasis can occur; monitoring may be appropriate in patients with suspected hypercalciuria or active urolithiasis
  -: TYMLOS is contraindicated in patients with a history of systemic hypersensitivity to abaloparatide or product components
  -: ⚠️ Black Box Warning: Abaloparatide carries an FDA black box warning regarding potential osteosarcoma (bone cancer) risk based on rat studies where the drug was given at much higher doses and for longer durations than human therapeutic use.
  -: The source does not clearly state the study population or design in PEARL's reviewed record.
  -: The reviewed record is animal research and cannot establish human effectiveness or safety.

### compound | ace031/overview | What is ACE-031?
kind: overview
title: ACE-031
summary: ACE-031 (ramatercept, ActRIIB-Fc) is an investigational soluble activin type IIB receptor fusion protein: the extracellular ligand-binding domain of human ActRIIB joined to a human IgG1 Fc fragment. It belongs to the myostatin/activin inhibitor class and works as a circulating "ligand trap," sequestering myostatin (GDF-8), activin A and B, GDF-11 and related TGF-beta superfamily proteins before they can signal through their native receptors and restrain skeletal muscle growth. In every published human study it was given by subcutaneous injection, so the ACE-031 dosage discussed in trials is weight-based: 0.02 to 3 mg/kg subcutaneously every 2 to 4 weeks, with measurable gains in lean mass (+3.3%) and thigh muscle volume (+5.1%) seen only at the top 3 mg/kg single dose in healthy postmenopausal women. The elimination half-life is roughly 10 to 15 days.
keyPoint: ACE-031 (ramatercept, ActRIIB-Fc) is an investigational soluble activin type IIB receptor fusion protein: the extracellular ligand-binding domain of human ActRIIB joined to a human IgG1 Fc fragment.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high

  connectedTo: ACE-031

section: How it works in the research
  -: ACE-031 is a recombinant dimeric fusion protein built from the extracellular ligand-binding domain of the human activin receptor type IIB (ActRIIB, gene ACVR2B) genetically linked to the Fc region of human immunoglobulin G1 (IgG1) [1][3].

  *: Very high Effectively no human safety data; safety claims are extrapolations from animal work or anecdote. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Development halted in 2013 due to safety signals (nosebleeds, vascular issues). [source-listed source severity]
  *: Theoretical reproductive disruption (myostatin / activin pathway). [source-listed source severity]
  *: WADA S1.2 / S4 prohibited. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Nosebleeds (epistaxis) Gum bleeding Telangiectasias (dilated blood vessels in skin) Injection site reactions Development discontinued due to vascular safety signals Long-term effects unknown Effects on other TGF-β pathways Development discontinued-not available for use History of bleeding disorders would have been. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Epistaxis (spontaneous nosebleeds) - the primary and program-terminating adverse effect from clinical trials; directly caused by BMP9/BMP10 trapping disrupting nasal mucosal vascular integrity; onset typically within the first 2-4 weeks; severity ranges from minor to persistent bleeding requiring intervention. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Telangiectasias (dilated superficial blood vessels) - small, visible dilated capillaries on the skin and mucosal surfaces; a direct consequence of BMP9/BMP10 pathway disruption; may persist after cessation of ACE-031. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Injection site erythema and local reactions - redness, swelling, induration at subcutaneous injection site; reported in Phase 1 trials as the most common injection-related adverse event. [source-listed source severity]

### compound | ace031/evidence | What research is listed for ACE-031?
kind: evidence
title: ACE-031: research listed by the sources
summary: Vascular bleeding events were the defining safety problem and the reason development stopped: dose-related epistaxis (nosebleeds), gum/gingival bleeding, and cutaneous telangiectasia (small dilated skin vessels) occurred in both healthy adults and boys with Duchenne muscular dystrophy [2][6].; These vascular effects are attributed to off-target trapping of BMP9 and BMP10, two TGF-beta ligands essential for endothelial and vascular integrity that ActRIIB also binds; this is an on-mechanism, not idiosyncratic, risk of broad ActRIIB ligand traps [3].; Injection-site reactions, particularly erythema at the subcutaneous site, were reported in the Phase 1 study even though the drug was otherwise generally well tolerated [1].; As a human IgG1 Fc fusion protein, ACE-031 carries an inherent risk of immunogenicity (formation of anti-drug antibodies) that can reduce exposure or, in principle, cause hypersensitivity; this is a general class risk for biologic ligand traps.; Because ActRIIB binds activins that regulate the reproductive (FSH) and other endocrine axes, broad activin blockade has Animal/cell evidence only Discontinued investigational compound. Acceleron Pharma stopped development of ACE-031 in 2013 after safety signals. Not a licensed UK medicine; not currently in active clinical development. Prohibited under WADA S1.2 / S4. Human evidence grade D, Animal/cell evidence only. Citation quality grade C, Limited human evidence.

section: What the research shows
  -: PeptideDosage.org: ACE-031 (ramatercept, ActRIIB-Fc) is an investigational soluble activin type IIB receptor fusion protein: the extracellular ligand-binding domain of human ActRIIB joined to a human IgG1 Fc fragment.
  -: Peptide Authority: A myostatin/activin decoy receptor designed to promote muscle growth, researched for muscular dystrophy but development discontinued.
  -: PeptideJournal: ACE-031 was supposed to be a breakthrough for boys with Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
  -: Peptide University Codex: ACE-031 (ramatercept, ACVR2B-Fc) is not a traditional peptide but a soluble fusion protein - the extracellular domain of the activin type IIB receptor (ActRIIB) fused to an IgG1 Fc antibody fragment.
section: Evidence strength
  -: PeptideDosage.org: Randomized or controlled human research; population: Human; Direct controlled human evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: Peptide Authority: Animal research; population: Human; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: PeptideJournal: Source summary; study design not clearly stated; population: Not clearly stated; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: Peptide University Codex: Source summary; study design not clearly stated; population: Not clearly stated; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Limitations
  -: ACE-031 (ramatercept, ActRIIB-Fc) is an investigational soluble activin type IIB receptor fusion protein: the extracellular ligand-binding domain of human ActRIIB joined to a human IgG1 Fc fragment.
  -: Whether grey-market 'ACE-031' contains the originally developed compound or a different myostatin-pathway molecule.
  -: Long-term safety beyond the trials that ended in 2013.
  -: No active clinical development; only historical Phase 1/2 data available.
  -: The source does not clearly state the study population or design in PEARL's reviewed record.
  -: Bleeding disorders of any type - epistaxis and vascular fragility are direct pharmacological consequences of ACE-031's mechanism; any pre-existing coagulation disorder dramatically amplifies hemorrhagic risk.
  -: Anticoagulant or antiplatelet therapy - warfarin, heparin, aspirin, clopidogrel, NOACs; additive bleeding risk with BMP9/BMP10 pathway disruption.
  -: Uncontrolled hypertension - elevated blood pressure combined with compromised vascular wall integrity from BMP9/BMP10 blockade increases risk of spontaneous vessel rupture.
  -: Known hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia (HHT) or family history of vascular malformations - BMP9 is the primary genetic driver of HHT; ACE-031 mechanistically recapitulates HHT pathology.
  -: Active malignancy - ActRIIB ligand trapping removes activin A suppression, which may release growth restraints on tumor cells.
  -: History of cancer - exercise caution; myostatin/activin pathway manipulation has theoretical tumor growth implications.
  -: Pregnancy - fusion protein safety not established; avoid.
  -: Breastfeeding - safety not established.

  *: PeptideJournal: ACE-031 was supposed to be a breakthrough for boys with Duchenne muscular dystrophy. Early trials showed lean body mass climbing by 3-5% in just weeks, muscle volume expanding without exercise, and the kind of pharmacological effects that had researchers talking about reversing the irreversible. ACE-031 represents both the promise and the peril of myostatin inhibition. It worked-lean body mass increased, muscle volume expanded, and biomarkers moved in favorable directions. The science was sound. The results were real. But biology doesn't respect precision when your drug binds to proteins that regulate blood vessel integrity. The molecule's failure was not a failure of the myostatin hypothesis. Myostatin is still a validated target for muscle wasting, and related growth factors like IGF-1 LR3 and MGF continue to be studied for their anabolic effects. ACE-031's discontinuation was a failure of selectivity-a cautionary tale about the risks of broad-spectrum inhibition in a family of signaling molecules as tightly interconnected as the TGF-β superfamily.

It's the first place to show signs of aging, fluid retention, and lack of sleep. Under-eye puffiness and dark circles can make you look tired even when you're not. This is where acetyl tetrapeptide-5 comes in. Acetyl tetrapeptide-5 is a well-designed cosmetic peptide with a clear target: reducing under-eye puffiness and improving the appearance of the periorbital area. It works by reducing vascular permeability, inhibiting ACE, and preventing glycation-three mechanisms that directly address fluid accumulation, inflammation, and structural degradation. Clinical data shows that most users see measurable improvement in puffiness within 15 to 60 days of consistent use. The peptide also appears to improve skin elasticity and reduce dark circles, though results vary depending on the underlying cause. The main limitation is the lack of large-scale, independent, peer-reviewed studies.

### compound | acth/overview | What is ACTH?

title: ACTH
summary: A pituitary hormone that stimulates cortisol production, used diagnostically and therapeutically for various conditions including infantile spasms.

  source: The therapeutic mechanisms of ACTH were historically attributed entirely to corticotropic actions, but recent research has clarified that direct anti-inflammatory effects and immunomodulatory activity acting through mela <https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3932770/>
  source: In Addison's disease, the adrenal glands fail to produce cortisol. Without cortisol's negative feedback, ACTH levels rise dramatically. High ACTH stimulates melanocytes, darkening the skin and mucous membranes <https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4880116/>
  source: Clinical trials have demonstrated similar efficacies for ACTH and intravenous methylprednisolone in MS relapses <https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/2544829/>
  source: ACTH and melanocortins regulate anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory functions involving lymphocytes, macrophages, and reduction of pro-inflammatory cytokines <https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3573675/>
  source: Acthar Gel has re-emerged as a potentially effective therapy for nephrotic syndrome, particularly for patients who have failed more conventional immunosuppressive therapies <https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7292987/>

### compound | acth/evidence | What research is listed for ACTH?
kind: evidence
title: ACTH: research listed by the sources
summary: Strong human evidence UK prescription-only medicine. Synacthen (synthetic ACTH analogue) is used by NHS endocrinology for adrenal-function testing. Prohibited at all times under WADA S2. Human evidence grade A, Strong human evidence. Citation quality grade A, Strong human evidence. Adrenocorticotropic hormone-ACTH for short-is one of the body's master stress regulators. It doesn't show up in wellness marketing or longevity forums. It's not found in compounded peptide vials. ACTH is a 39-amino-acid pituitary hormone that plays a critical role in cortisol production and stress response. It's not a lifestyle peptide. It's not sold by compounding pharmacies. It's a prescription medication with FDA-approved indications for serious medical conditions: infantile spasms, multiple sclerosis relapses, nephrotic syndrome, rheumatic disorders, and diagnostic testing of adrenal function. The two pharmaceutical forms-Acthar Gel and cosyntropin-are distinct products with different uses. Acthar Gel is a repository injection used therapeutically in patients who have failed other treatments. It works through a combination of steroidogenic effects (raising cortisol) and direct immunomodulatory effects mediated by melanocortin receptors on immune cells. Cosyntropin is a synthetic diagnostic agent used in a one-time test to assess adrenal responsiveness.
keyPoint: Strong human evidence UK prescription-only medicine.

### compound | adamax/overview | What is Adamax?
kind: overview
title: Adamax
summary: Adamax (Ac-MEHFPGP-AG-NH2) is a synthetic nonapeptide derivative of Semax with an N-terminal acetyl group and a C-terminal Ala-Gly amide tail engineered to confer greater enzymatic stability and lipophilicity than the parent ACTH(4-10) analogue [1]. It belongs to the broader family of melanocortin-derived nootropic peptides developed within the Russian Academy of Sciences' neuropeptide program. Like Semax, Adamax is investigated for melanocortin receptor activity, BDNF/TrkB upregulation, and protection against ischemic and oxidative neuronal injury, with the modified backbone giving it longer in vivo half-life and stronger blood-brain barrier penetration on a per-dose basis [2]. Research dosing is typically 100-600 mcg intranasally one to two times daily, well below the equivalent Semax dose range, with cycle lengths of 2-6 weeks.
keyPoint: Adamax (Ac-MEHFPGP-AG-NH2) is a synthetic nonapeptide derivative of Semax with an N-terminal acetyl group and a C-terminal Ala-Gly amide tail engineered to confer greater enzymatic stability and lipophilicity than the parent ACTH(4-10)...

title: Adamax: research listed by the sources
summary: No human safety database exists for Adamax; reported adverse effects are limited to anecdotal reports from research-chemical use and inferred risks from the closely related Semax compound.; Transient nasal irritation, mild burning, or rhinorrhea at the site of intranasal application are the most commonly described effects, generally resolving within minutes.; Mild headache may occur, particularly at higher cumulative doses; dose reduction and hydration usually resolve symptoms.; Insomnia or difficulty initiating sleep may occur if Adamax is dosed late in the day; morning and early afternoon administration is the conservative practice.; No HPA axis activation is expected on theoretical grounds, but cortisol elevation has not been formally excluded in human use.; Blood pressure and heart rate effects are not characterized; cardiovascular monitoring is reasonable in users with hypertension or arrhythmia.; Reproductive, pregnancy, and lactation safety are entirely unstudied; use should be avoided in these populations.; Drug-drug interactions are uncharacterized; concurrent use with MAO Route Dose Range Frequency Notes Intranasal 100-600 μg/day 1-2 times daily Analogous to Semax dosing with potentially longer intervals Subcutaneous 100-500 μg/day Once daily Enhanced stability allows subcutaneous route Note: Adamax dosing is extrapolated from Semax clinical data. section: Limitations
  -: Adamax (Ac-MEHFPGP-AG-NH2) is a synthetic nonapeptide derivative of Semax with an N-terminal acetyl group and a C-terminal Ala-Gly amide tail engineered to confer greater enzymatic stability and lipophilicity than the parent ACTH(4-10) analogue [1].
  -: The reviewed record does not state a specific limitation. The linked paper still needs to be checked for design, size and bias.
  -: 14 Important Note This content is intended for therapeutic educational purposes only and does not constitute medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment.
  -: Adamax is a research chemical for laboratory use and is not approved for human consumption.
  -: Always consult with a qualified healthcare professional before undertaking any research protocol involving peptides.
  -: Concurrent Semax use - Adamax is a pharmacokinetically superior derivative of Semax acting on identical TrkB/MC4R/BDNF targets; co-administration produces supraphysiological receptor agonism without incremental benefit while amplifying all stimulant-adjacent adverse effects and accelerating TrkB downregulation; these
  -: Severe anxiety disorders or active panic disorder - Adamax's enhanced CNS penetration amplifies the MC4R-driven dopaminergic activation and arousal effects of the Semax pharmacophore significantly beyond what parent Semax produces; subjects with anxiety disorders may experience pronounced worsening.
  -: Active manic episode or bipolar I disorder (manic phase) - dopaminergic and noradrenergic amplification from high-CNS-penetrance MC4R agonism can trigger or accelerate manic states in susceptible individuals.
  -: Active psychotic disorders - contraindicated for the same reasons as Semax, with greater urgency given the amplified CNS potency.
  -: Late-day administration (after noon) - the half-life of 1-2 hours means direct receptor activity clears reasonably quickly, but the BDNF transcription and MC4R-driven arousal effects persist several hours; evening administration reliably causes insomnia.
  -: Known hypersensitivity to Semax, Adamax, adamantane-modified peptides, or formulation excipients.
  -: Concurrent MAOI use - dopaminergic and serotonergic potentiation via MC4R creates serotonin/dopamine excess risk in the presence of monoamine oxidase inhibition.
  -: Pregnancy - no safety data; BDNF signaling plays critical roles in fetal neural development; exogenous supraphysiological BDNF stimulation in utero is not established as safe.
  *: Source rating: 2 out of 5, limited evidence

  -: Adipotide is an experimental chimeric peptidomimetic designed to target white-adipose vasculature.
section: Evidence strength
  -: PeptideDeck: Human clinical research; population: Human; Human evidence with design limitations to check. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Main limitations
  -: The 28-day primate study duration means nothing is known about longer-term effects of sustained vascular apoptosis in adipose tissue. Questions about fat tissue regeneration, lymphatic system integrity, and metabolic adaptation remain unanswered.

section: What the research shows
  -: The Peptide Handbook: An investigational preclinical peptide whose approved evidence is bounded to obese rhesus-macaque work.
  -: PeptideDosage.org: Adipotide (FTPP, fat-targeting peptide-peptidomimetic) is a 22-amino-acid bipartite peptide consisting of a homing sequence (CKGGRAKDC) that selectively binds prohibitin on white-adipose-tissue blood vessels, conjugated via a glycine-glycine linker to a pro-apoptotic peptidomimetic sequence D(KLAKLAK)2 that disrupts...
  -: PeptideDeck: Recommended
  -: PeptideDeck: Published March 6, 2026 Updated July 22, 2026 Quick Brief Adipotide is a peptidomimetic compound that targets white fat vasculature in research models.
  -: PeptideDosages.com: 09 How This Works Adipotide is a peptidomimetic compound designed to selectively target blood vessels within white adipose tissue by binding to prohibitin‑1 on the vascular endothelium [2] [8] .

section: Limitations
  -: Renal toxicity in the obese rhesus-macaque study is a material translational limitation.
  -: No human interventional evidence or human safety profile is established.
  -: Adipotide (FTPP, fat-targeting peptide-peptidomimetic) is a 22-amino-acid bipartite peptide consisting of a homing sequence (CKGGRAKDC) that selectively binds prohibitin on white-adipose-tissue blood vessels, conjugated via a glycine-glycine linker to a pro-apoptotic peptidomimetic sequence D(KLAKLAK)2 that disrupts
  -: While adipotide's homing domain preferentially targets adipose vasculature, the selectivity is relative rather than absolute. Prohibitin is expressed throughout the body-it's a fundamental protein in mitochondrial biology and cell membrane function.
  -: The 28-day primate study duration means nothing is known about longer-term effects of sustained vascular apoptosis in adipose tissue. Questions about fat tissue regeneration, lymphatic system integrity, and metabolic adaptation remain unanswered.
  -: 14 Important Note This content is intended for therapeutic educational purposes only and does not constitute medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment.
  -: Adipotide’s clinical development was discontinued due to safety concerns.
  -: This information is for research purposes only.
  -: Not for human consumption.
  *: Source rating: 2 out of 5, limited evidence
  *: The Peptide Handbook: preliminary. The canonical study is a nonhuman-primate experiment. Its results, including the reported renal safety signal, are preclinical and cannot be translated into a human dose or therapeutic conclusion.
  *: PeptideDosage.org: The Phase 1 oncology trial (Stadler et al., 2016) documented dose-limiting renal toxicity - acute kidney injury including transient creatinine elevation and reduced eGFR - at higher exposure levels. This emerged as the principal barrier to further human development [3].; In the rhesus monkey study, transient mild dehydration and reduced fluid intake were observed during the active dosing period, generally resolving within 1-2 weeks of completion [2].; Injection-site reactions (mild erythema, induration) occurred at rates similar to other subcutaneous peptides; daily dosing schedules may amplify cumulative site irritation compared to weekly drugs.; Apoptosis induction in target tissue raises theoretical concerns about off-target endothelial apoptosis in other vascular beds where prohibitin may be transiently elevated (e.g., inflammation, tumor angiogenesis) - though preclinical work suggested adequate selectivity at therapeutic doses.; No human cardiovascular, hepatic or hematologic toxicity has been characterized in the limited Phase 1 dataset; long-term safety beyond 28 days of
  *: PeptideDeck: Selective targeting of white adipose tissue vasculature Rapid and significant weight reduction in primate studies Reduction of abdominal/visceral fat deposits Improved insulin sensitivity in treated primates Decreased BMI without caloric restriction in animal models Novel mechanism independent of appetite suppression or metabolic modulation Potential for targeted fat reduction in specific depots Reduction of circulating triglycerides in preclinical models Active research area with published studies The foundational adipotide research was published in Nature Medicine in 2004 by Kolonin, Saha, Chan, Pasqualini, and Arap. Using obese mice (ob/ob genetic model and diet-induced obesity model), the researchers demonstrated that targeted ablation of adipose tissue vasculature could reverse obesity.
  *: PeptideDeck: Chemical name: CKGGRAKDC-GG-D(KLAKLAK)₂ Also known as: FTPP (fat-targeted proapoptotic peptide) Mechanism: Targets prohibitin on white adipose vasculature → apoptosis of fat-feeding blood vessels → fat cell death Research status: Discontinued human clinical trials; preclinical animal data only Key risk identified: Reversible kidney toxicity in primate models Research class: Peptidomimetic / targeted proapoptotic peptide ~11% Body Weight Loss (Primate) 28 days Treatment Duration Discontinued Clinical Status The landmark study published in Science Translational Medicine (Barnhart et al., 2011) is the central piece of Adipotide research ( PubMed ). Researchers administered Adipotide to obese rhesus monkeys - a primate model considered highly relevant to human obesity physiology. Before the primate study, Adipotide had been tested in obese mouse models with promising results. Kolonin et al. (2004) first demonstrated the prohibitin-targeting concept in rodents, showing fat mass reduction with the CKGGRAKDC homing peptide ( Nature Medicine ).
  *: Peptide University Codex: Peptide University labels its records as aggregated from empirical research and anecdotal community data. This record is retained as supplied and is not upgraded to clinical evidence.
  *: A Peptidomimetic Targeting White Fat Causes Weight Loss and Improved Insulin Resistance in Obese Monkeys (Science Translational Medicine 2011): Barnhart, Kolonin, Arap, Pasqualini et al. demonstrated that the proapoptotic peptide adipotide (CKGGRAKDC-GG-D(KLAKLAK)₂) selectively targeted white adipose tissue vasculature in obese rhesus monkeys, producing ~11% body weight loss over 28 days - the primary proof-of-concept study for adipotide as a targeted fat elimination agent.

### compound | afamelanotide/evidence | What research is listed for Afamelanotide?
kind: evidence
title: Afamelanotide: research listed by the sources
summary: strong-human. Human randomized evidence supports SCENESSE for adult EPP, where the treatment increased pain-free light exposure in the studied population. The current product is a controlled-release 16 mg implant placed above the anterior supra-iliac crest every 2 months, with an apparent half-life of approximately 15 hours for the implant formulation. EPP evidence must not be transferred to cosmetic tanning, generalized UV protection, anti-aging, or non-EPP photoprotection. Two Phase III, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials (CUV039 in Europe, CUV040 in the US) provided the basis for regulatory approval: CUV039 (n=74): Afamelanotide significantly increased median daily duration of direct sunlight exposure without pain (69.4 vs. 40.5 minutes/day) and increased quality of life scores CUV040 (n=94): Significant increase in total time in direct sunlight with reduced phototoxicity severity Grimes et al. (2013) demonstrated that afamelanotide combined with narrowband UVB phototherapy produced faster and more complete repigmentation in vitiligo patients compared to NB-UVB alone, particularly in skin types IV-VI. Studies in healthy volunteers have demonstrated that afamelanotide-induced melanization provides meaningful photoprotection equivalent to approximately SPF 3-4, with the additional benefit of enhanced DNA repair capacity. [ 1 ] [ 2 ] [ 3 ] [ 4 ] [ 5 ] [ 6 ] ↑ 1.0 1.1 Langendonk JG, Balwani M, Anderson KE, et al. (2015). "Afamelanotide for erythropoietic protoporphyria." New England Journal of Medicine . 373(1):48-59.

### compound | ahkcu/overview | What is AHK-Cu?
kind: overview
title: AHK-Cu
summary: A synthetic tripeptide-copper complex structurally related to GHK-Cu, differing by a single amino acid (alanine replacing glycine). Studied in cosmeceutical research for collagen synthesis, skin remodeling, and hair follicle biology, with a more limited evidence base than GHK-Cu.
keyPoint: A synthetic tripeptide-copper complex structurally related to GHK-Cu, differing by a single amino acid (alanine replacing glycine).
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: AHK-Cu
  connectedTo: AHK-Cu
section: Why it is researched
  -: A synthetic tripeptide-copper complex structurally related to GHK-Cu, differing by a single amino acid (alanine replacing glycine).
section: How it works in the research
  -: A synthetic tripeptide-copper complex structurally related to GHK-Cu, in which alanine replaces glycine at the N-terminus (Ala-His-Lys vs Gly-His-Lys).
section: Evidence strength
  -: PeptideDosage.org: Animal research; population: Animal; Preclinical animal evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Main limitations
  -: AHK-Cu is a synthetic copper-binding tripeptide, L-alanyl-L-histidyl-L-lysine (Ala-His-Lys) chelated to a divalent copper ion, marketed in cosmetics as Copper Tripeptide-3 and used almost exclusively as a topical hair- and scalp-care active.

[source-listed source severity]
  *: Severe Post-Injection Pain (PIP) and welting - the primary and expected adverse effect of subcutaneous AHK-Cu; burning, stinging, redness, and local welt formation at the injection site; copper ion-mediated; identical in mechanism to GHK-Cu PIP. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Bruising and localized hematoma - common with daily administration; the 8-week cycle with rotation manages but does not eliminate this. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Local induration and redness - tissue copper deposition response; self-resolving between injections. [source-listed source severity]

### compound | ahkcu/evidence | What research is listed for AHK-Cu?
kind: evidence
title: AHK-Cu: research listed by the sources
summary: preliminary. AHK-Cu has a substantially smaller published evidence base than its structural relative GHK-Cu. Available research - conducted primarily in vitro and in small animal models - suggests stimulation of collagen and elastin synthesis through mechanisms proposed by analogy to GHK-Cu, including growth-factor-mediated effects on hair follicle biology reported in laboratory models. The existing literature is dominated by cosmeceutical industry studies and manufacturer-sponsored in vitro assays. Independent, peer-reviewed, placebo-controlled clinical trials in humans are absent. Until such trials are conducted, AHK-Cu's efficacy relative to GHK-Cu, or relative to vehicle control, cannot be established from the published record. Topical AHK-Cu is generally well tolerated; the most common effects are mild, transient scalp redness, stinging, or itching at the application site, especially on compromised or freshly microneedled skin.; The copper complex is intrinsically blue-green and can temporarily tint light hair, skin, pillowcases, and fabrics; this is cosmetic and washes out.; Allergic contact dermatitis is possible in people with copper or nickel sensitivity; a patch test is prudent for anyone with a history of metal allergy or persistent dermatitis.; Do not co-apply with high-strength vitamin C (ascorbic acid): copper catalyzes ascorbate oxidation, which can degrade both actives and may increase irritation; alternate them at different times of day.; No controlled human safety data exist for AHK-Cu specifically; the in-vitro and ex-vivo evidence base means long-term tolerability, optimal concentration, and drug interactions are not formally established.; Injectable or intradermal use is not validated and is not recommended: it can cause localized blue-green pigmentation, pain, bruising, or swelling, and
keyPoint: preliminary.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: AHK-Cu
  connectedTo: AHK-Cu
section: What the research shows
  -: The Peptide Handbook: A synthetic tripeptide-copper complex structurally related to GHK-Cu, differing by a single amino acid (alanine replacing glycine).
  -: PeptideDosage.org: AHK-Cu is a synthetic copper-binding tripeptide, L-alanyl-L-histidyl-L-lysine (Ala-His-Lys) chelated to a divalent copper ion, marketed in cosmetics as Copper Tripeptide-3 and used almost exclusively as a topical hair- and scalp-care active.
  -: WikiPep: From Wikipep - The Peptide Encyclopedia AHK-Cu Chemical name AHK-Cu (Copper Tripeptide AHK) Molecular formula C₁₅H₂₆CuN₆O₄ Molecular weight 417.9 g/mol CAS number Not publicly assigned Sequence Ala-His-Lys-Cu²⁺ (3 amino acids + copper ion; His imidazole coordinates copper binding) Length 3 amino acids (copper-binding...
  -: Peptide University Codex: AHK-Cu (alanyl-histidyl-lysyl copper complex, also known as Copper Tripeptide-3) is a synthetic copper-binding tripeptide structurally related to GHK-Cu but with a distinct amino acid sequence - alanine replaces glycine at the N-terminal position.
section: Evidence strength
  -: The Peptide Handbook: Animal research; population: Animal; Preclinical animal evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: PeptideDosage.org: Animal research; population: Animal; Preclinical animal evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: WikiPep: Animal research; population: Animal; Preclinical animal evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: Peptide University Codex: Source summary; study design not clearly stated; population: Not clearly stated; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Limitations
  -: Very limited systemic human safety data; injectable use is without an established safety profile; theoretical copper accumulation at high injectable doses; topical cosmetic use is well-tolerated based on commercial history
  -: AHK-Cu is a synthetic copper-binding tripeptide, L-alanyl-L-histidyl-L-lysine (Ala-His-Lys) chelated to a divalent copper ion, marketed in cosmetics as Copper Tripeptide-3 and used almost exclusively as a topical hair- and scalp-care active.
  -: The reviewed record is animal research and cannot establish human effectiveness or safety.
  -: Wilson's disease or other genetic copper metabolism disorders - the injectable copper complex bypasses normal hepatic copper handling; contraindicated in any subject with impaired copper transport.
  -: Known copper hypersensitivity or copper allergy - systemic injection may provoke significant immune/inflammatory reactions in copper-sensitive individuals.
  -: Active malignancy - AHK-Cu promotes endothelial cell proliferation and angiogenesis; in the context of active cancer these mechanisms could support tumor vascularization.
  -: Pregnancy - no human safety data; copper homeostasis is critical during fetal development.
  -: Breastfeeding - no established safety data.
  -: Known hypersensitivity to AHK-Cu or peptide excipients.
  -: Concurrent use of copper-chelating agents (e.g., penicillamine, trientine, high-dose zinc) - will competitively neutralize the copper complex.
  -: Elevated baseline serum copper levels or hemochromatosis - impaired metal homeostasis increases copper toxicity risk at injectable doses.
  *: Source rating: 2 out of 5, limited evidence
  *: The Peptide Handbook: preliminary. AHK-Cu has a substantially smaller published evidence base than its structural relative GHK-Cu. Available research - conducted primarily in vitro and in small animal models - suggests stimulation of collagen and elastin synthesis through mechanisms proposed by analogy to GHK-Cu, including growth-factor-mediated effects on hair follicle biology reported in laboratory models. The existing literature is dominated by cosmeceutical industry studies and manufacturer-sponsored in vitro assays. Independent, peer-reviewed, placebo-controlled clinical trials in humans are absent. Until such trials are conducted, AHK-Cu's efficacy relative to GHK-Cu, or relative to vehicle control, cannot be established from the published record.
  *: PeptideDosage.org: Topical AHK-Cu is generally well tolerated; the most common effects are mild, transient scalp redness, stinging, or itching at the application site, especially on compromised or freshly microneedled skin.; The copper complex is intrinsically blue-green and can temporarily tint light hair, skin, pillowcases, and fabrics; this is cosmetic and washes out.; Allergic contact dermatitis is possible in people with copper or nickel sensitivity; a patch test is prudent for anyone with a history of metal allergy or persistent dermatitis.; Do not co-apply with high-strength vitamin C (ascorbic acid): copper catalyzes ascorbate oxidation, which can degrade both actives and may increase irritation; alternate them at different times of day.; No controlled human safety data exist for AHK-Cu specifically; the in-vitro and ex-vivo evidence base means long-term tolerability, optimal concentration, and drug interactions are not formally established.; Injectable or intradermal use is not validated and is not recommended: it can cause localized blue-green pigmentation, pain, bruising, or swelling, and

### compound | aicar/overview | What is AICAR?
kind: overview
title: AICAR
summary: AICAR (5-aminoimidazole-4-carboxamide ribonucleoside), also known as acadesine, is a cell-permeable adenosine analog that is phosphorylated intracellularly to ZMP, an AMP mimetic that allosterically activates AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK), the master cellular energy sensor. AICAR mimics several physiological consequences of endurance exercise: increased fatty acid oxidation, glucose uptake, mitochondrial biogenesis, and oxidative gene expression. The landmark Narkar et al. Cell 2008 study showed that four weeks of AICAR administration to sedentary mice increased running endurance by 44 percent. In humans, intravenous acadesine has been studied in cardiac surgery and acute myeloid leukemia at doses up to 0.1 mg/kg/min for several hours; the World Anti-Doping Agency prohibits AICAR as an exercise mimetic. AICAR is not approved for any chronic indication, and self-administered research subcutaneous doses (10-50 mg per session) lack any safety or efficacy validation in humans.

### compound | aicar/safety | What are the risks of AICAR?
kind: safety
title: AICAR: source-listed risks
summary: Source-listed risks only. Missing human safety data does not mean a compound is safe.
keyPoint: Source-listed risks only.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: AICAR
  connectedTo: AICAR
  *: 10 Potential Benefits & Side Effects Observations from preclinical and limited human research. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Endurance Enhancement: Sedentary mice treated with AICAR showed a remarkable +44% increase in endurance without training [2] , demonstrating exercise-mimetic effects. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Metabolic Improvements: Increases mitochondrial enzymes, fatty-acid oxidation capacity, and skeletal muscle glucose uptake [3] ; improves insulin sensitivity in animal models. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Therapeutic Potential: Research suggests potential for diabetic neuropathy protection and metabolic syndrome treatment in animal models [7] . [source-listed source severity]
  *: Safety Profile: Human trials (acadesine, IV) showed tolerable safety up to 210 mg/kg single dose with only mild, transient side effects [5] ; research subcutaneous doses are a small fraction of this. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Side Effects: Generally well tolerated in studies; possible mild injection-site reactions (redness, irritation) with subcutaneous use. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Important: Despite promising preclinical results, AICAR remains experimental; no confirmed clinical benefit in humans has been established, and long-term risks are unknown. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Hypoglycemia - the most significant acute adverse effect; AICAR drives aggressive glucose uptake via GLUT4 in muscle tissue; risk is highest when dosed fasted without planned exercise; always pre-workout, always with subsequent energy expenditure. [source-listed source severity]

### compound | aicar/evidence | What research is listed for AICAR?
kind: evidence
title: AICAR: research listed by the sources
summary: Intravenous acadesine in clinical trials has been associated with transient hypotension, headache, dizziness, nausea, and reductions in serum uric acid; high doses can produce significant lactic acidosis through AMPK-mediated changes in substrate utilization.; AICAR can produce hypoglycemia, particularly when combined with insulin, sulfonylureas, or other glucose-lowering agents, due to enhanced peripheral glucose uptake and decreased hepatic glucose output.; Hyperuricemia or hypouricemia and reduced renal urate clearance have been reported, and AICAR can cause crystallization of intermediates in the purine salvage pathway, particularly at high parenteral doses.; Subcutaneous self-administration at research doses (10-50 mg) has no published safety data and carries risks of injection-site reactions, infection from non-sterile preparations, and unpredictable systemic exposure due to variable bioavailability.; Long-term effects of chronic AMPK activation are uncharacterized; theoretical concerns include effects on cancer cell metabolism (potentially both protective and promotive Peptide University labels its records as aggregated from empirical research and anecdotal community data. This record is retained as supplied and is not upgraded to clinical evidence.

section: What the research shows
  -: PeptideDosage.org: AICAR (5-aminoimidazole-4-carboxamide ribonucleoside), also known as acadesine, is a cell-permeable adenosine analog that is phosphorylated intracellularly to ZMP, an AMP mimetic that allosterically activates AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK), the master cellular energy sensor.
  -: PeptideDosages.com: 09 How This Works AICAR functions as an AMPK agonist, essentially mimicking an energy-depleted cellular state.
  -: Peptide University Codex: AICAR (5-aminoimidazole-4-carboxamide ribonucleoside, also known as acadesine) is a cell-permeable nucleoside analog that is phosphorylated intracellularly to ZMP (5-aminoimidazole-4-carboxamide ribonucleotide) - a structural and functional mimetic of AMP (adenosine monophosphate).
section: Evidence strength
  -: PeptideDosage.org: Systematic review or meta-analysis; population: Human; Higher-level human evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: PeptideDosages.com: Source summary; study design not clearly stated; population: Not clearly stated; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: Peptide University Codex: Source summary; study design not clearly stated; population: Not clearly stated; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Limitations
  -: AICAR (5-aminoimidazole-4-carboxamide ribonucleoside), also known as acadesine, is a cell-permeable adenosine analog that is phosphorylated intracellularly to ZMP, an AMP mimetic that allosterically activates AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK), the master cellular energy sensor.
  -: 14 Important Note This content is intended for therapeutic educational purposes only and does not constitute medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment.
  -: AICAR is for research use only and is not approved for human consumption.
  -: AICAR is prohibited by the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) for use in competitive sports.
  -: Cardiovascular instability or active cardiac arrhythmia - AICAR affects cardiac adenosine metabolism and can influence heart rate and rhythm; contraindicated in subjects with unstable cardiac conditions.
  -: Insulin therapy or sulfonylurea use without clinical supervision - AICAR's GLUT4 upregulation and glucose uptake enhancement creates additive hypoglycemia risk with insulin or insulin secretagogues.
  -: Metformin use - both AICAR and metformin activate AMPK; overlapping activation intensifies the glucose-lowering and metabolic effects; monitor closely.
  -: Gout or hyperuricemia - AICAR increases uric acid levels through purine catabolism pathway modulation; in subjects with gout, elevated baseline uric acid, or reduced renal uric acid clearance, AICAR may precipitate gout flares.
  -: Renal impairment - AICAR and its metabolites are renally cleared; impaired elimination may cause accumulation and exaggerated pharmacological effects.
  -: Active malignancy - AMPK activation has complex effects in cancer metabolism; AICAR's anti-proliferative effects have been noted in some cancer models, but its metabolic support of oxidative phosphorylation in other tumor types is not fully characterized.
  -: Athletes competing under WADA anti-doping regulations - AICAR is explicitly listed on the WADA Prohibited List as an AMPK activator.
  -: Known hypersensitivity to AICAR or nucleoside analog compounds.
  *: Source rating: 1 out of 5, very limited evidence
  *: PeptideDosage.org: Intravenous acadesine in clinical trials has been associated with transient hypotension, headache, dizziness, nausea, and reductions in serum uric acid; high doses can produce significant lactic acidosis through AMPK-mediated changes in substrate utilization.; AICAR can produce hypoglycemia, particularly when combined with insulin, sulfonylureas, or other glucose-lowering agents, due to enhanced peripheral glucose uptake and decreased hepatic glucose output.; Hyperuricemia or hypouricemia and reduced renal urate clearance have been reported, and AICAR can cause crystallization of intermediates in the purine salvage pathway, particularly at high parenteral doses.; Subcutaneous self-administration at research doses (10-50 mg) has no published safety data and carries risks of injection-site reactions, infection from non-sterile preparations, and unpredictable systemic exposure due to variable bioavailability.; Long-term effects of chronic AMPK activation are uncharacterized; theoretical concerns include effects on cancer cell metabolism (potentially both protective and promotive
  *: Peptide University Codex: Peptide University labels its records as aggregated from empirical research and anecdotal community data. This record is retained as supplied and is not upgraded to clinical evidence.

### compound | alixorexton/overview | What is Alixorexton?
kind: overview
title: Alixorexton
summary: An oral orexin receptor 2 (OX2R) agonist developed by Alkermes for narcolepsy type 1 (NT1). Phase 2 clinical trials demonstrated improvements in excessive daytime sleepiness and cataplexy with once-daily dosing. Represents a novel approach to restore orexin signaling in patients who have lost orexin-producing neurons.
keyPoint: An oral orexin receptor 2 (OX2R) agonist developed by Alkermes for narcolepsy type 1 (NT1).

### compound | alphadefensins/overview | What is Alpha-Defensins?
kind: overview
title: Alpha-Defensins
summary: A family of small cationic antimicrobial peptides (29-35 amino acids) that are key components of innate immunity in humans. Produced primarily by neutrophils (HNP-1 to 4) and Paneth cells (HD-5, HD-6), they exhibit broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity and immunomodulatory functions. Well-characterized biochemically with extensive research, though therapeutic development faces challenges.
keyPoint: A family of small cationic antimicrobial peptides (29-35 amino acids) that are key components of innate immunity in humans.

confidence: high

section: How it works in the research
  -: Alpha-defensins function as key effectors of innate immunity through several pathways: Membrane Disruption Cationic peptides bind to anionic microbial membranes, insert into lipid bilayer, and form pores causing ion leakage and cell death.

### compound | alphadefensins/evidence | What research is listed for Alpha-Defensins?
kind: evidence
title: Alpha-Defensins: research listed by the sources
summary: Moderate evidence; 40 human studies listed. abundant controlled observational human data (Crohn's, HIV, dyslipidemia biomarker cohorts) but no RCT of defensin administration for efficacy. Mechanism: membrane disruption, nanonet self-assembly, and chemotaxis well characterized in vivo. Plausibility: mechanism-to-surrogate solid; in-vivo translation limited by salt sensitivity. Global coverage: robustly replicated across many independent groups and countries; no regulatory approval. Community: endogenous peptides with negligible documented exogenous use. Effectiveness not-established: no quantified human efficacy estimate for administered defensins and no meaningful community effect signal.

Effectiveness not-established: no quantified human efficacy estimate for administered defensins and no meaningful community effect signal.

  -: Endogenous Krebs-cycle metabolite.

  -: Alpha-ketoglutarate (AKG), also called 2-oxoglutarate, is an endogenous Krebs-cycle metabolite.
section: Evidence strength
  -: The Peptide Handbook: Observational or case-based human research; population: Animal; Limited observational human evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Main limitations
  -: The Ca-AKG mouse findings do not establish efficacy for free AKG, other AKG salts, or humans
  -: The retrospective Rejuvant report studied a multi-ingredient AKG-based formulation and a DNA-methylation-age endpoint; it does not establish isolated AKG reversal of aging
  -: Human lifespan extension has not been established

### compound | alphaketoglutarate/evidence | What research is listed for Alpha-Ketoglutarate?
kind: evidence
title: Alpha-Ketoglutarate: research listed by the sources
summary: preliminary. A cited Cell Metabolism study reported lifespan, healthspan, and morbidity findings in C57BL/6 mice administered Ca-AKG. It is preclinical evidence for that calcium salt and cannot establish human longevity benefit or effects of free AKG or other salts. A separate retrospective analysis of 42 individuals using a multi-ingredient Ca-AKG-based Rejuvant formulation reported changes in a DNA-methylation-age measure after an average of seven months; its formulation, retrospective design, and biomarker endpoint do not establish that isolated AKG reverses aging or extends lifespan. The ABLE publication describes a randomized placebo-controlled sustained-release Ca-AKG protocol with aging-biomarker endpoints; it is a protocol, not efficacy results.

### compound | alphaklotho/overview | What is α-Klotho?
kind: overview
title: α-Klotho
summary: A transmembrane glycoprotein first identified through a 1997 mouse-genetics experiment showing a phenotype resembling premature ageing when the gene was disrupted. In a human hemodialysis population, lower circulating soluble Klotho has been associated with higher mortality and cardiovascular events - an observational finding, not a demonstrated anti-aging or treatment effect.

### compound | alphaklotho/evidence | What research is listed for α-Klotho?
kind: evidence
title: α-Klotho: research listed by the sources
summary: preliminary. α-Klotho's mouse-genetics evidence base is striking: klotho-deficient mice develop a phenotype resembling premature ageing (Kuro-o et al., 1997), and klotho-overexpressing mice have been reported to live longer - but these are mouse findings, not human evidence. In a human hemodialysis cohort, lower circulating soluble Klotho was independently associated with higher mortality and cardiovascular events (Memmos et al., 2019); this is an observational association in a specific patient population, not a general anti-aging or causal claim, and does not indicate that raising Klotho (by any means) improves outcomes. No human interventional trial of exogenous Klotho protein has been identified. The protein's other proposed roles - Wnt/IGF-1 signaling suppression, antioxidant activity, cognitive and renal protection - remain supported mainly by preclinical and mechanistic work. Current human research is centered on using circulating sKlotho as a biomarker rather than as a therapeutic target.
keyPoint: preliminary.
understood: resolved

  -: Unknown; potential effects on phosphate homeostasis, Wnt signaling, and insulin sensitivity require careful characterization before human use

### compound | alprostadil/overview | What is Alprostadil?
kind: overview
title: Alprostadil
summary: Alprostadil is synthetic prostaglandin E1 (PGE1) - a naturally occurring 20-carbon eicosanoid lipid mediator derived from dihomo-γ-linolenic acid through the cyclooxygenase pathway. Endogenous PGE1 is produced locally in penile vascular and cavernosal smooth muscle tissue where it acts on EP2 and EP4 prostaglandin receptors (Gs-coupled GPCRs) to activate adenylyl cyclase, increase intracellular cAMP, and activate protein kinase A - producing smooth muscle relaxation, vasodilation of the helicine arteries of the corpora cavernosa, and venous outflow restriction through sinusoidal dilation. This vascular mechanism produces erection through direct local hemodynamic control: blood flows into the corpora cavernosa faster than it drains, producing the intracorporeal pressure elevation that constitutes erection.
keyPoint: Alprostadil is synthetic prostaglandin E1 (PGE1) - a naturally occurring 20-carbon eicosanoid lipid mediator derived from dihomo-γ-linolenic acid through the cyclooxygenase pathway.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: Alprostadil
  connectedTo: Alprostadil
section: Why it is researched
  -: Alprostadil is synthetic prostaglandin E1 (PGE1) - a naturally occurring 20-carbon eicosanoid lipid mediator derived from dihomo-γ-linolenic acid through the cyclooxygenase pathway.
section: How it works in the research
  -: Alprostadil is synthetic prostaglandin E1 (PGE1) - a naturally occurring 20-carbon eicosanoid lipid mediator derived from dihomo-γ-linolenic acid through the cyclooxygenase pathway.
section: Evidence strength
  -: Peptide University Codex: Source summary; study design not clearly stated; population: Not clearly stated; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Main limitations
  -: Sickle cell anemia and sickle cell trait - the red blood cell sickling triggered by the hypoxic, acidotic environment of sustained erection dramatically increases the risk of ischemic priapism in sickle cell subjects; absolute contraindication.
  -: Leukemia and other conditions with abnormal blood viscosity or hypercoagulability - abnormal blood cell populations obstructing cavernosal venous outflow create priapism risk independent of dose.
  -: Multiple myeloma and polycythemia vera - hyperviscosity states increase intracavernosal stasis and priapism risk.

### compound | alprostadil/safety | What are the risks of Alprostadil?
kind: safety
title: Alprostadil: source-listed risks
summary: Source-listed risks only. Missing human safety data does not mean a compound is safe.
keyPoint: Source-listed risks only.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: Alprostadil
  connectedTo: Alprostadil
  *: Penile pain at injection site - the most commonly reported adverse effect; occurs in approximately 30-50% of subjects with intracavernosal injection; caused by direct PGE1 nociceptor activation in cavernosal tissue (EP1 receptor stimulation); typically mild to moderate; the primary reason men discontinue. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Priapism (prolonged erection > 4 hours) - the most serious adverse effect; ischemic priapism destroys cavernosal smooth muscle through hypoxia and acidosis; frequency approximately 1-5% per injection; higher with excessive doses; constitutes a urological emergency requiring immediate intervention; the driver of the. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Penile fibrosis and Peyronie's disease development - repeated intracavernosal injections at the same site cause chronic micro-trauma and fibrotic healing; produces penile curvature, plaques, and eventually impairs the erectile mechanism. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Hematoma at injection site - subcutaneous or intracorporeal bleeding from the injection; more common with poor technique or anticoagulation; managed with sustained pressure. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Hypotension - systemic absorption of PGE1 from intracavernosal administration produces peripheral vasodilation at higher doses; typically mild but symptomatic in subjects with cardiovascular disease or baseline hypotension. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Dizziness and lightheadedness - secondary to the mild hypotensive effect; positional changes during the active erection period should be managed carefully. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Urethral burning - if injection inadvertently contacts periurethral tissue; not characteristic of correct intracavernosal technique. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Prolonged or recurrent erection not reaching priapism threshold - erections lasting 2-4 hours that spontaneously resolve with activity, cold application, or mild exercise; a warning sign that dose reduction is warranted. [source-listed source severity]

### compound | alprostadil/evidence | What research is listed for Alprostadil?
kind: evidence
title: Alprostadil: research listed by the sources
summary: Peptide University labels its records as aggregated from empirical research and anecdotal community data. This record is retained as supplied and is not upgraded to clinical evidence.
keyPoint: Peptide University labels its records as aggregated from empirical research and anecdotal community data.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: Alprostadil
  connectedTo: Alprostadil
section: What the research shows
  -: Peptide University Codex: Alprostadil is synthetic prostaglandin E1 (PGE1) - a naturally occurring 20-carbon eicosanoid lipid mediator derived from dihomo-γ-linolenic acid through the cyclooxygenase pathway.
section: Evidence strength
  -: Peptide University Codex: Source summary; study design not clearly stated; population: Not clearly stated; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Limitations
  -: Sickle cell anemia and sickle cell trait - the red blood cell sickling triggered by the hypoxic, acidotic environment of sustained erection dramatically increases the risk of ischemic priapism in sickle cell subjects; absolute contraindication.
  -: Leukemia and other conditions with abnormal blood viscosity or hypercoagulability - abnormal blood cell populations obstructing cavernosal venous outflow create priapism risk independent of dose.
  -: Multiple myeloma and polycythemia vera - hyperviscosity states increase intracavernosal stasis and priapism risk.
  -: Thrombocytopenia or bleeding disorders - intracavernosal injection in subjects with impaired hemostasis creates risk of uncontrolled intracorporeal hematoma.
  -: Concurrent anticoagulant therapy (warfarin, novel oral anticoagulants, therapeutic heparin) - same mechanism as bleeding disorder risk; must be weighed carefully.
  -: Concurrent use with other vasoactive erectile agents (PDE5 inhibitors, PT-141 within 24 hours) - additive vasodilatory effects dramatically increase priapism risk; combination of intracavernosal alprostadil with oral PDE5 inhibitors is specifically warned against.
  -: Penile anatomical abnormalities (severe Peyronie's disease with plaques, penile fibrosis, penile angulation) - intracavernosal injection into abnormal tissue carries injection complication risk and may not produce physiological erection.
  -: Hypersensitivity to alprostadil, prostaglandin E1, or formulation excipients.
  *: Source rating: 1 out of 5, very limited evidence
  *: Peptide University Codex: Peptide University labels its records as aggregated from empirical research and anecdotal community data. This record is retained as supplied and is not upgraded to clinical evidence.

### compound | amycretin/overview | What is Amycretin?
kind: overview
title: Amycretin
summary: A novel single-molecule dual GLP-1/amylin receptor agonist developed by Novo Nordisk. Unlike CagriSema (a fixed-dose combination), amycretin is a unified peptide that activates both pathways. Phase 1 trials showed superior weight loss signals versus semaglutide, with both oral and subcutaneous formulations in development.

### compound | amycretin/evidence | What research is listed for Amycretin?
kind: evidence
title: Amycretin: research listed by the sources
summary: Moderate evidence; 8 human studies listed Gastrointestinal events dominated the safety profile: in the subcutaneous phase 1b/2a trial, nausea was reported in up to ~82%, vomiting in ~53%, and diarrhea in ~41% of treated participants, most often during dose escalation and generally mild to moderate and transient [1][6].; A serious adverse event of gallstone (biliary) pancreatitis occurred in a participant on the 20 mg subcutaneous dose; it recurred but ultimately resolved - gallbladder and pancreatitis events are a recognized class concern with incretin therapies [1].; Decreased appetite is part of the intended mechanism but can lead to reduced food and fluid intake with a risk of dehydration; slow titration and adequate hydration are used to mitigate this [3].; Modest resting heart-rate increases are expected with GLP-1/amylin agonists; longer and larger trials are needed to characterize cardiovascular effects, which were not the primary endpoint of these early-phase studies [1].; As with semaglutide- and tirzepatide-class agents, a portion of the weight lost is lean body mass; adequate dietary protein and resistance

### compound | amylin/overview | What is Amylin?
kind: overview
title: Amylin
summary: From Wikipep - The Peptide Encyclopedia Amylin Chemical name Islet Amyloid Polypeptide (IAPP) Molecular formula C₁₆₅H₂₆₁N₅₁O₅₅S₂ Molecular weight 3903.3 g/mol CAS number 106602-62-4 Sequence KCNTATCATQRLANFLVHSSNNFGAILSSTNVGSNTY-NH₂ (disulfide Cys2-Cys7) Length 37 amino acids Source Pancreatic beta cells (co-secreted with insulin) Half-life ~15 minutes Targets Amylin receptors (CTR/RAMP complexes), Area postrema Bioavailability Endogenous Legal status Endogenous hormone Amylin (also known as Islet Amyloid Polypeptide or IAPP ) is a 37-amino acid peptide hormone co-secreted with insulin by pancreatic beta cells in response to nutrient stimulation. Discovered in 1987 by Per Westermark, amylin plays a critical complementary role to insulin in glucose homeostasis by slowing gastric emptying, suppressing postprandial glucagon secretion, and promoting satiety. Its synthetic analog pramlintide (Symlin) is FDA-approved for diabetes treatment.

Cagrilintide (an analogue) is in late-stage clinical development with Novo Nordisk for obesity. Human evidence grade B, Moderate human evidence. Citation quality grade B, Moderate human evidence.
  *: PeptideJournal: The race to unlock body weight control through peptide therapeutics has intensified dramatically. While GLP-1 agonists like [semaglutide](/peptides/semaglutide-complete-pharmacology-guide/) captured mainstream attention with 15-20% weight loss, the next frontier pairs them with a different hormone Amylin represents a metabolic control system that has been hiding in plain sight since the discovery of insulin over a century ago. While researchers focused on insulin's role in glucose disposal, amylin quietly controlled glucose appearance-slowing gastric emptying, suppressing glucagon, and regulating appetite through central and peripheral mechanisms. Pramlintide proved the concept but struggled with practicality: three daily injections, frequent nausea, hypoglycemia risk, and modest benefits limited adoption. Its discontinuation in 2025 closed a chapter on first-generation amylin therapy. Cagrilintide opens a new one.
  *: Progressive reduction in body weight after treatment with the amylin analog pramlintide in obese subjects: a phase 2, randomized, placebo-controlled, dose-escalation study (Journal of Clinical Endocrinology and Metabolism 2007): Aronne et al. Phase 2 RCT (n=204 obese, non-insulin-treated) showing pramlintide up to 240 mcg three times daily produced progressive, dose-dependent weight loss vs. placebo over 16 weeks - the primary human RCT establishing amylin analog as a standalone obesity treatment.

### compound | anamorelin/overview | What is Anamorelin?
kind: overview
title: Anamorelin
summary: Anamorelin (ONO-7643, RC-1291; brand name Adlumiz/Edlumiz) is a selective, orally active, non-peptide ghrelin/growth-hormone-secretagogue-receptor 1a (GHS-R1a) agonist developed for cancer cachexia. As a small-molecule ghrelin mimetic rather than a true peptide, it survives the gut and is taken by mouth once daily, binding the same receptor as endogenous ghrelin to stimulate appetite and to amplify growth hormone (GH), insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1) and IGFBP-3 - a hormonal profile that drives gains in lean body mass and body weight [1][5]. The standard, well-established Anamorelin dosage is 100 mg orally once daily on an empty stomach, with treatment reassessed at three weeks and most trials capping exposure at about 12 weeks [3][9]. Because the real-world product is a 50 mg oral tablet, the subcutaneous vial-and-bacteriostatic-water figures on this page are an educational reconstitution reference only, not the clinical route.
keyPoint: Anamorelin (ONO-7643, RC-1291; brand name Adlumiz/Edlumiz) is a selective, orally active, non-peptide ghrelin/growth-hormone-secretagogue-receptor 1a (GHS-R1a) agonist developed for cancer cachexia.

### compound | anamorelin/evidence | What research is listed for Anamorelin?
kind: evidence
title: Anamorelin: research listed by the sources
summary: Hyperglycemia and new or worsening diabetes are among the most clinically important effects, reflecting the GH/IGF-1 axis activation; fasting glucose should be monitored and caution is needed in patients with diabetes, prediabetes or metabolic syndrome [4][9].; Cardiac conduction effects, including QT-interval prolongation and other ECG changes, have been reported; baseline and on-treatment ECG monitoring is advised, and anamorelin is generally avoided with other QT-prolonging drugs or significant cardiac disease [9].; Hepatic effects such as elevated liver enzymes and hepatic dysfunction occurred in trials (for example, raised transaminases in the gastrointestinal-cancer study); liver function should be monitored [4].; Gastrointestinal effects including nausea and changes in appetite-related symptoms can occur, though overall tolerability was broadly comparable to placebo in the ROMANA 3 safety extension [6].; Because it is taken on an empty stomach and partly metabolized via CYP3A4, food impairs absorption and strong CYP3A4 inhibitors or inducers can alter exposure; co-medication ROMANA 1 (n=484): Anamorelin vs placebo in NSCLC cachexia - significant LBM increase (+1.10 kg, p<0.0001) at 12 weeks ROMANA 2 (n=495): Confirmatory trial - significant LBM increase (+0.75 kg, p<0.0001) ROMANA 3 : Extension study - sustained LBM gains over 24 weeks Japanese Phase 3 : Led to approval in Japan; similar efficacy with acceptable safety Combination with exercise interventions for cachexia Investigation in other cachexia etiologies (COPD, heart failure, chronic kidney disease) Biomarker-driven patient selection strategies [ 1 ] [ 2 ] [ 3 ] ↑ 1.0 1.1 Temel JS, et al. "Anamorelin in patients with non-small-cell lung cancer and cachexia (ROMANA 1 and ROMANA 2)." Lancet Oncol . 2016;17(4):519-531. ↑ 2.0 2.1 Currow DC, et al. "ROMANA 3: a phase 3 safety extension study of anamorelin in advanced non-small-cell lung cancer." Ann Oncol . 2017;28(8):1949-1956. ↑ 3.0 3.1 Hamauchi S, et al. "Phase 2 study of anamorelin in Japanese patients with cachexia and NSCLC." Jpn J Clin Oncol . 2019.

  *: Resolved: modelled administration routes. Use only the route stated in the original study or official product information. Do not convert an oral, intranasal, intramuscular or investigational product into a generic subcutaneous vial protocol. PeptideDosage.org applies a common reconstitution and syringe format even to products such as Ventfort that it identifies as oral. That format is not evidence that the modelled route was studied or is suitable. Confidence: high.

Keep only links whose NCBI record matches the stated research subject. NCBI identifies PMID 11157505 as a Hodgkin-disease cell-fusion paper, PMID 16640009 as a Freeman-Sheldon syndrome case report, and PMID 18677858 as a neonatal-mortality paper.   *: Source rating: 3 out of 5
  *: The Peptide Handbook: moderate. Direct human administration and clinical research are study-specific. Published and registered-trial sources support investigational context only; they do not establish general dosing, a universal half-life, outpatient use, or an approved therapeutic indication. Angiotensin-(1-7) has also reached human oncology studies. A Phase I trial enrolled 18 patients with advanced solid tumors refractory to standard therapy; one patient had a 19% reduction in tumor measurements and three others had disease stabilization lasting more than 3 months. A subsequent Phase II study in metastatic sarcoma reported a median progression-free survival of 2.7 months, with two patients with vascular sarcomas experiencing prolonged disease stabilization of 10 and 19 months. These findings remain investigational and do not establish Angiotensin-(1-7) as an effective cancer treatment.
  *: WikiPep: Ang-(1-7) is widely used in cardiovascular, renal, and pulmonary research: Elucidation of the ACE2/Ang-(1-7)/Mas axis Counter-regulatory RAS signaling studies COVID-19 pathophysiology and therapeutic development Heart failure and cardiac remodeling research Diabetic nephropathy and renal fibrosis studies Ang-(1-7) and its analogs are under clinical investigation for: Cardiovascular disease: Heart failure, hypertension, post-MI recovery Cancer: Phase I/II trials in solid tumors (TXA127, a clinical formulation of Ang-(1-7)) COVID-19: Clinical trials investigating Ang-(1-7) as a treatment for acute COVID-19 Diabetic nephropathy: Renal protection in type 2 diabetes Intravenous infusion: 1-20 ng/kg/min in preclinical and clinical studies Subcutaneous: Osmotic minipump delivery (preclinical); 24 μg/kg/h commonly used in rat models Intranasal: Under investigation as a non-invasive delivery route Reconstitution: Dissolve in sterile saline or phosphate-buffered saline (PBS); pH 7.4 Stability: Extremely short plasma half-life necessitates continuous infusion or stabilized formulations for in
  *: PeptideJournal: Angiotensin 1-7 (Ang 1-7) is a seven-amino-acid peptide that sits at the center of one of medicine's most important control systems: the renin-angiotensin system (RAS). Angiotensin 1-7 represents a shift in how scientists think about the renin-angiotensin system. For decades, the focus was on blocking angiotensin II - the "bad actor" that drives hypertension, heart failure, and kidney disease. ACE inhibitors and ARBs work by reducing Ang II or preventing it from binding to receptors. But angiotensin 1-7 reframes the problem. Instead of just removing the harmful peptide, the body actively produces a protective one from it. ACE2 converts Ang II into Ang 1-7, which then activates the Mas receptor to undo the damage. This is not just suppression - it's active counter-regulation. The research base is strong. In animal models, Ang 1-7 protects the heart from hypertrophy and fibrosis, shields the kidneys from diabetic damage, improves metabolic dysfunction, reduces atherosclerosis, and mitigates lung injury.
  *: Phase I/II Dose Escalation Study of Angiotensin 1-7 in Breast Cancer Patients (Cancer Chemotherapy and Pharmacology 2006): Human Phase I/II trial: Ang 1-7 administered before and after chemotherapy stimulated hematopoietic progenitor cell proliferation with acceptable tolerability.
