  *: PepCodex: High evidence; 18 human studies listed. multiple large placebo-controlled RCTs incl. Phase 3 REDEFINE 1 (n=3,417) and REDEFINE 2, total human N well over 1,000, no published meta-analysis yet. Mechanism: amylin AMY1/2/3 receptors named with binding + functional confirmation and characterized satiety pathway. Plausibility: full mechanism to weight-loss outcome chain supported, coherent with amylin biology and same-class pramlintide. Global Coverage: international multi-country trials but single sponsor (Novo Nordisk) and FDA review pending, limiting independence. Community Experience: trial-only, near-negligible real-world usage signal. Effectiveness basis clinical: REDEFINE 1 (NCT05567796) showed -20.4% weight loss with cagrilintide-semaglutide versus -3.0% with placebo at 68 weeks.
  *: The Peptide Handbook: moderate. A randomized cagrilintide monotherapy study reported weight-loss findings in adults with overweight or obesity. Separate Phase III publications report results for the cagrilintide/semaglutide combination CagriSema in obesity and type 2 diabetes populations. These outcomes must not be attributed to cagrilintide monotherapy, and neither product is FDA-approved.
  *: Halflife Labs: Evidence context is stated on the linked compound page.
  *: PeptideDosage.org: Gastrointestinal events occurred at notably lower rates than for GLP-1 agonists. In the Phase 2 dose-finding trial, nausea was reported in 27% of participants on 4.5 mg cagrilintide vs 11% on placebo, vomiting in 12% vs 4%, and diarrhea in 10% vs 6% - comparable to or lower than liraglutide 3.0 mg [1].; Decreased appetite, the intended pharmacologic effect, was reported in 25-35% of participants on active doses; this is distinct from nausea-mediated appetite loss and contributes to the durable weight-loss effect.; Injection-site reactions (mild erythema, induration) occurred in roughly 4-7% of participants, comparable to other weekly subcutaneous peptides.
  *: PeptideDeck: Significant appetite suppression Enhanced satiety after meals Slows gastric emptying Suppresses glucagon secretion Once-weekly dosing convenience Synergistic with GLP-1 agonists May improve glycemic control Potential for best-in-class weight loss when combined Cagrilintide has been evaluated in a structured clinical development program spanning early dose-finding studies through large phase 3 trials, both as a single agent and as part of the CagriSema combination. The research consistently shows dose-dependent appetite suppression and weight loss.
  *: CagriSema Phase 3 REDEFINE Trial (NEJM 2025): 23% average weight loss on-treatment at 68 weeks vs 8.1% semaglutide alone (REDEFINE 1). NDA filed Dec 2025.

### compound | cagrilintidesemaglutide/overview | What is Cagrilintide + Semaglutide?
kind: overview
title: Cagrilintide + Semaglutide
summary: CagriSema is the fixed-dose combination of cagrilintide (a long-acting amylin analogue) and semaglutide (a GLP-1 receptor agonist), both at 2.4 mg weekly, developed by Novo Nordisk and submitted to the FDA in December 2025 based on the Phase 3 REDEFINE-1 trial. The combination exploits complementary satiety pathways: cagrilintide engages amylin/calcitonin-receptor signaling in the brainstem while semaglutide acts on hypothalamic GLP-1 receptors - producing an additive rather than redundant effect on appetite suppression and weight loss. In REDEFINE-1, CagriSema 2.4/2.4 mg weekly produced 22.7% mean weight loss at 68 weeks compared to 11.8% with cagrilintide alone, 16.1% with semaglutide alone, and 2.3% with placebo [1]. CagriSema is not yet FDA approved (NDA review expected to complete in 2026). Standard dosing escalates both peptides in parallel through a 16-20 week titration to the 2.4 mg / 2.4 mg maintenance dose.

### compound | cagrilintidesemaglutide/evidence | What research is listed for Cagrilintide + Semaglutide?
kind: evidence
title: Cagrilintide + Semaglutide: research listed by the sources
summary: Gastrointestinal events in REDEFINE-1 occurred at rates broadly similar to semaglutide monotherapy: nausea approximately 45%, diarrhea 30%, vomiting 25% and constipation 22% on CagriSema vs 16%, 18%, 8% and 12% on placebo. Most were mild-to-moderate and concentrated during titration [1].; Importantly, the additive efficacy of CagriSema does not appear to come at the cost of proportionally additive GI burden - discontinuation rates for GI events were approximately 6% on CagriSema vs 4% on semaglutide alone, suggesting the amylin component adds efficacy without substantially worsening tolerability [1].; Heart-rate elevation of 3-5 beats per minute on average was observed, broadly consistent with semaglutide monotherapy.
keyPoint: Gastrointestinal events in REDEFINE-1 occurred at rates broadly similar to semaglutide monotherapy: nausea approximately 45%, diarrhea 30%, vomiting 25% and constipation 22% on CagriSema vs 16%, 18%, 8% and 12% on placebo.

### compound | cagrisema/overview | What is CagriSema?
kind: overview
title: CagriSema
summary: A fixed-dose combination of cagrilintide (amylin analog) and semaglutide (GLP-1 agonist) for chronic weight management. Phase 3 REDEFINE trials demonstrate 20-23% weight loss at 68 weeks. NDA submitted to FDA December 2025. First GLP-1/amylin combination therapy.
keyPoint: A fixed-dose combination of cagrilintide (amylin analog) and semaglutide (GLP-1 agonist) for chronic weight management.

  -: Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia Type 2 (MEN2) - MEN2 patients have a near-universal predisposition to MTC; the GLP-1RA component's thyroid C-cell stimulation is absolutely contraindicated in this genetic syndrome.

  -: Active pancreatitis or history of pancreatitis - GLP-1 receptor agonists carry a class-level association with acute pancreatitis; history of pancreatitis is a relative-to-absolute contraindication depending on clinical context.
  -: Type 1 diabetes without insulin coverage - the GLP-1RA component suppresses glucagon and slows gastric emptying, but does not replace insulin; T1DM subjects using CagriSema without adequate insulin therapy face severe hypoglycemia risk.

### compound | calcitonin/overview | What is Calcitonin?
kind: overview
title: Calcitonin
summary: A 32-amino-acid peptide hormone that reduces osteoclast activity and lowers serum calcium. Calcitonin salmon remains FDA-approved for selected bone and calcium disorders, but its role in osteoporosis is now limited and current labeling states that fracture-reduction efficacy has not been demonstrated.
keyPoint: A 32-amino-acid peptide hormone that reduces osteoclast activity and lowers serum calcium.
understood: resolved
method: canonical

section: How it works in the research
  -: Calcitonin is a 32-amino-acid peptide hormone involved in calcium and bone metabolism.
section: Evidence strength
  -: The Peptide Handbook: Human clinical research; population: Human; Human evidence with design limitations to check. 65 human studies listed by the source; 80 animal studies listed by the source
section: Main limitations
  -: Serious hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis, have been reported with calcitonin salmon
  -: Hypocalcemia can occur and should be corrected before treatment
  -: A meta-analysis of randomized trials found a higher incidence of malignancies in calcitonin salmon-treated patients than placebo-treated patients; a definitive causal relationship has not been established

### compound | calcitonin/evidence | What research is listed for Calcitonin?
kind: evidence
title: Calcitonin: research listed by the sources
summary: strong-human. Calcitonin salmon has decades of human clinical experience. The 5-year PROOF trial reported a reduction in new vertebral fractures with the 200 IU/day nasal dose, but other tested doses did not show the same statistically significant effect and current U.S. labeling states that fracture-reduction efficacy has not been demonstrated. Injectable calcitonin remains useful for selected patients with symptomatic Paget’s disease and for early treatment of hypercalcemic emergencies because it can lower serum calcium relatively quickly. A meta-analysis of randomized trials found a higher incidence of malignancies among calcitonin-treated patients than placebo-treated patients, although a definitive causal relationship has not been established. European regulators subsequently removed nasal calcitonin’s osteoporosis use. Moderate human evidence UK prescription-only medicine (Miacalcic). Long-term osteoporosis use was restricted in 2013 following EMA review of cancer-risk signals; short-term use for hypercalcaemia and Paget's disease remains appropriate. Human evidence grade B, Moderate human evidence. Citation quality grade A, Strong human evidence.
keyPoint: strong-human.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: Calcitonin
  connectedTo: Calcitonin
section: What the research shows
  -: The Peptide Handbook: A 32-amino-acid peptide hormone that reduces osteoclast activity and lowers serum calcium.
  -: Peptide Authority: A thyroid hormone involved in calcium regulation, used therapeutically for osteoporosis, Paget's disease, and hypercalcemia.
section: Evidence strength
  -: The Peptide Handbook: Human clinical research; population: Human; Human evidence with design limitations to check. 65 human studies listed by the source; 80 animal studies listed by the source
  -: Peptide Authority: Animal research; population: Human; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Limitations
  -: Serious hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis, have been reported with calcitonin salmon
  -: Hypocalcemia can occur and should be corrected before treatment
  -: A meta-analysis of randomized trials found a higher incidence of malignancies in calcitonin salmon-treated patients than placebo-treated patients; a definitive causal relationship has not been established
  -: Because of the possible malignancy association, the need for continued calcitonin therapy should be periodically re-evaluated
  -: Whether off-label long-term use carries the same cancer signal as restricted indication.
  -: Superseded by bisphosphonates / denosumab / teriparatide for routine osteoporosis.

The primary PE-22-28 publication describes a seven-amino-acid shortened spadin analogue with TREK-1 inhibition in hTREK-1/HEK cells and antidepressant-like, neurogenesis, and synaptogenesis findings in mouse models. These are preclinical findings and do not establish antidepressant efficacy or safety in people. PE-22-28 has no documented human safety data; reported side effects are limited to anecdotal reports from research-chemical use, without controlled adverse-event surveillance.; Theoretical risks based on TREK-1 pharmacology include increased neuronal excitability and the possibility of agitation or anxiety, though preclinical data suggest the effect is regional and does not generalize to global hyperexcitability.; Mild injection site reactions (redness, irritation) with subcutaneous administration are anecdotally reported.; Sleep disruption has been reported anecdotally with evening dosing, possibly reflecting the increased monoaminergic tone produced by TREK-1 blockade.; Cardiac arrhythmia risk is theoretically low based on rodent data but has not been formally excluded in humans; ECG monitoring is reasonable in users with pre-existing arrhythmia.; Drug interactions are uncharacterized; concurrent use with SSRIs, SNRIs, or other monoaminergic drugs is theoretically additive and may increase serotonergic effects.; No tolerance or dependence has been documented in rodent chronic
  *: Pinealon: Source rating: 2 out of 5, limited evidence. Russian peptide bioregulator research (Khavinson). Limited Western RCT data.

### compound | capromorelin/overview | What is Capromorelin?
kind: overview
title: Capromorelin
summary: Capromorelin is a small-molecule, orally active ghrelin / growth hormone secretagogue receptor (GHS-R1a) agonist marketed for veterinary use as Entyce (dogs) and Elura (cats). Originally developed by Pfizer as CP-424,391 for age-related functional decline in humans, it was repurposed by Aratana Therapeutics (now Elanco) for appetite and weight support in animals. Rather than a true peptide it is a peptidomimetic that mimics endogenous ghrelin, binding receptors in the hypothalamus to drive hunger and in the pituitary to release growth hormone and raise IGF-1 [1]. The headline Capromorelin dosage is 3 mg/kg orally once daily in dogs and 2 mg/kg once daily in cats, supplied as a flavored oral solution (30 mg/mL for dogs, 20 mg/mL for cats) [5][6]. In the pivotal canine field study, 68.6% of treated dogs showed improved appetite versus 44.6% on placebo (P = 0.008) [3].
keyPoint: Capromorelin is a small-molecule, orally active ghrelin / growth hormone secretagogue receptor (GHS-R1a) agonist marketed for veterinary use as Entyce (dogs) and Elura (cats).
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high

### compound | capromorelin/mechanism | How does Capromorelin work?
kind: overview
title: Capromorelin
summary: Capromorelin is a small-molecule, orally active ghrelin / growth hormone secretagogue receptor (GHS-R1a) agonist marketed for veterinary use as Entyce (dogs) and Elura (cats). Originally developed by Pfizer as CP-424,391 for age-related functional decline in humans, it was repurposed by Aratana Therapeutics (now Elanco) for appetite and weight support in animals. Rather than a true peptide it is a peptidomimetic that mimics endogenous ghrelin, binding receptors in the hypothalamus to drive hunger and in the pituitary to release growth hormone and raise IGF-1 [1]. The headline Capromorelin dosage is 3 mg/kg orally once daily in dogs and 2 mg/kg once daily in cats, supplied as a flavored oral solution (30 mg/mL for dogs, 20 mg/mL for cats) [5][6]. In the pivotal canine field study, 68.6% of treated dogs showed improved appetite versus 44.6% on placebo (P = 0.008) [3].

### compound | capromorelin/evidence | What research is listed for Capromorelin?
kind: evidence
title: Capromorelin: research listed by the sources
summary: Gastrointestinal effects are most common in dogs: in the canine field study diarrhea (~7.0%), vomiting (~6.4%), polydipsia (~4.1%) and hypersalivation (~2.3%) were reported; hypersalivation often reflects the bitter taste of the oral solution [5].; In cats, adverse signs are more frequent: vomiting (~29.6%), hypersalivation (~21.2%), inappetence (~18.6%), behavioral changes (~14.4%) and lethargy (~13.6%) were seen in the ELURA field study, though several of these also occur with the underlying kidney disease [6].; Elura labeling warns of transient decreases in heart rate and blood pressure for up to about 4 hours after dosing; use cautiously in animals with cardiac disease or significant dehydration, and post-marketing reports include bradycardia and hypotension [6].; Because capromorelin stimulates growth hormone, it can transiently raise blood glucose and IGF-1; it has not been evaluated in diabetic animals and is contraindicated in cats with hypersomatotropism (acromegaly) [5][6].; It is contraindicated in animals hypersensitive to capromorelin, and elevated blood urea nitrogen [ 1 ] [ 2 ] [ 3 ] [ 4 ] ↑ 1.0 1.1 White HK, et al. ### compound | cardiogen/overview | What is Cardiogen?
kind: overview
title: Cardiogen
summary: A synthetic tripeptide (Ala-Glu-Asp, AED) developed by Russian scientist Vladimir Khavinson and marketed as a cardiac "bioregulator." Despite that marketing, no PubMed-indexed study has examined AED in heart, cardiomyocyte, or myocardial tissue. The only published AED research is in vitro and non-cardiac - anti-aging gene-expression effects in cultured stem cells, fibroblasts, kidney and immune cells. No human or animal data and no regulatory approval anywhere.

### compound | cardiogen/evidence | What research is listed for Cardiogen?
kind: evidence
title: Cardiogen: research listed by the sources
summary: only in-vitro cell-culture data exists for AED (Ala-Glu-Asp), all in NON-cardiac tissue (stem cells, fibroblasts, kidney, thymocytes); no cardiac human or animal studies, no RCTs. Mechanism: AED penetrates cells and binds DNA minor groove (docking + gene-expression readout) but lacks knockout/in-vivo confirmation. Plausibility: cardioprotection is a large leap from generic non-cardiac gene-expression effects. Global coverage: AED replicated by an independent Italian group (Russia + Italy), modest volume, no regulatory approval. Community experience: negligible documented use. Effectiveness: not-established (no clinical efficacy data and no meaningful community effect signal). NOTE: all 8 cardiac PMIDs in this dossier are fabricated/mismatched and were excluded; no cardiac-specific AED study exists on PubMed. No controlled human safety data exist for Cardiogen; its adverse-effect profile is unknown, and the points below are extrapolated from injectable peptides and the Khavinson bioregulator class generally.; Subcutaneous injection can cause local reactions including redness, itching, swelling, bruising, or transient pain at the injection site.; Any injected peptide carries a theoretical risk of immune or hypersensitivity reactions; stop use and seek care for rash, hives, facial or throat swelling, or difficulty breathing.; Research-grade peptides are not manufactured to pharmaceutical standards, so contamination, endotoxin, incorrect sequence, or inaccurate vial content are realistic risks; sterility and purity cannot be assumed.; There are no drug-interaction studies; people taking cardiac, anticoagulant, or other medications should not assume Cardiogen is inert or compatible.; Cardiogen has not been evaluated in pregnancy, breastfeeding, in children, or in people with active heart disease, and should be avoided in these groups.; Because the proposed mechanisms involve modulating cell

section: Limitations
  -: The reviewed record is animal research and cannot establish human effectiveness or safety.
  -: Cardiogen (CardioCytogen) is a synthetic tetrapeptide bioregulator with the sequence Ala-Glu-Asp-Arg (AEDR, molecular weight about 489.5 Da), developed within Vladimir Khavinson's short-peptide program at the St.
  -: Active myocarditis or infectious endocarditis - the cardiomyocyte-level bioregulator activity of Cardiogen during active cardiac infection/inflammation has not been evaluated; the inflammatory cardiac milieu of myocarditis represents an unpredictable context for cardiomyocyte gene program modulation.
  -: Recent cardiac surgery (within 4 weeks) - the acute post-surgical healing phase involves specific cardiomyocyte stress response programs; exogenous bioregulator activity during the immediate post-operative window has not been characterized.
  -: Severe decompensated heart failure requiring inotropic support - in subjects with cardiogenic shock or acutely decompensated heart failure, the priority is hemodynamic stabilization; Cardiogen is a chronic bioregulator not an acute cardiac support agent.
  -: Known hypersensitivity to Cardiogen (Ala-Glu-Asp-Arg tetrapeptide) or formulation excipients.
  -: Pregnancy - cardiomyocyte-level bioregulator effects during the significant cardiac remodeling of pregnancy are not characterized.
  -: Severe hepatic or renal impairment - peptide clearance and metabolic processing in severely impaired organ function has not been evaluated for Cardiogen.
  -: Concurrent use with high-dose cardiotoxic chemotherapy (anthracyclines, trastuzumab) - while Cardiogen's cardioprotective mechanism might theoretically be beneficial in this context, the interaction between cardiomyocyte bioregulator activity and chemotherapy-induced cardiomyocyte injury has not been characterized and

### compound | carnosine/evidence | What research is listed for Carnosine?
kind: evidence
title: Carnosine: research listed by the sources
summary: Extensive human data for anti-glycation and antioxidant effects. Long history of safe use.
keyPoint: Extensive human data for anti-glycation and antioxidant effects.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: Carnosine
  connectedTo: Carnosine
section: What the research shows
  -: The Peptide Handbook: An endogenous dipeptide studied for its roles as a pH buffer, antioxidant, and anti-glycation agent.
section: Evidence strength
  -: The Peptide Handbook: Randomized or controlled human research; population: Human; Direct controlled human evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Limitations
  -: No serious risks identified at standard doses; high-dose long-term safety data limited
  *: Source rating: 3 out of 5
  *: The Peptide Handbook: preliminary. Carnosine's anti-glycation and antioxidant mechanisms are well established biochemically, but human clinical evidence is limited to three small, short randomized trials with narrow, exploratory endpoints: glycemic/lipid biomarker changes in type 2 diabetes (12 weeks), improved oral glucose tolerance in prediabetes/T2D (14 weeks), and a reduced urinary fibrosis biomarker in diabetic nephropathy without a change in renal function (12 weeks). None of these trials support broader claims of cognitive enhancement, anti-aging effects, or exercise-performance benefits, which remain preclinical or are supported mainly by the separate beta-alanine ergogenic-aid literature. Oral supplementation is also limited by rapid plasma hydrolysis by carnosinase, constraining achievable tissue levels.
  *: Physiology and Pathophysiology of Carnosine (Physiological Reviews 2013): Comprehensive review establishing carnosine's physiological roles via pH-buffering, metal-ion chelation, antioxidant capacity, and protection against advanced glycation and lipoxidation end-products - making it a key anti-aging dipeptide in muscle and neural tissue.

### compound | cartalax/evidence | What research is listed for Cartalax?
kind: evidence
title: Cartalax: research listed by the sources
summary: only single-group in-vitro (MSC/chondrocyte/fibroblast) and a few animal OA models; an unstructured mention of oral use in elderly OA patients lacks any described controlled design, so no creditable human tier. Mechanism: AED modulates Ki-67/CD98hc/MMP9/SASP markers in cell models but target is inferred with no binding/knockout validation. Plausibility: chondrogenic-marker (SOX9, COL2, aggrecan) coherence is decent though mechanism-to-cartilage-outcome links remain unproven. Global coverage: all work originates from the Khavinson/Linkova St. Petersburg group with no independent or non-Russian replication. Community experience: negligible - no meaningful user reports. Effectiveness not-established: no quantified human efficacy estimate and no meaningful community effect signal. Cartalax is generally well tolerated in Russian observational use; reported adverse effects are infrequent and mild.; The most common reported effect is transient injection-site discomfort with subcutaneous administration.; Occasional mild gastrointestinal upset (nausea, loose stools) has been reported with oral capsule formulations, particularly at higher milligram doses.; No tolerance, dependence, or withdrawal phenomena have been reported, consistent with epigenetic rather than receptor-occupancy mechanism.; Hypersensitivity reactions are rare; allergic skin responses to peptide preparations should prompt discontinuation.; No HPA axis activation, hormonal disturbance, or significant metabolic effects have been documented at research-typical doses.; Drug-drug interaction data are not available; theoretical interactions with chondroprotective drugs, NSAIDs, or corticosteroids are unstudied.; Reproductive, pregnancy, and lactation safety data are absent; use during these periods is not recommended.
keyPoint: only single-group in-vitro (MSC/chondrocyte/fibroblast) and a few animal OA models; an unstructured mention of oral use in elderly OA patients lacks any described controlled design, so no creditable human tier.

section: Evidence strength

section: Limitations
  -: The reviewed record does not state a specific limitation. The linked paper still needs to be checked for design, size and bias.
  -: Cartalax is a synthetic tripeptide (Ala-Glu-Asp, AED) developed by Vladimir Khavinson and colleagues as a tissue-specific bioregulator targeting cartilage, chondrocytes, and musculoskeletal connective tissue [1][2].
  -: The reviewed record is animal research and cannot establish human effectiveness or safety.
  -: 14 Important Note This content is intended for therapeutic educational purposes only and does not constitute medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment.
  -: Active septic arthritis - bioregulator chondrocyte activity during active bacterial joint infection is contraindicated; antimicrobial treatment and joint drainage are the priority.
  -: Active inflammatory arthritis in acute flare (rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, gout flare) - the inflammatory milieu of acute arthritic flare creates a poor context for chondrocyte gene program normalization; Cartalax is a chronic bioregulator for non-inflammatory cartilage restoration.
  -: Chondrosarcoma or malignant bone/cartilage tumors - chondrocyte bioregulator activity in the context of malignant cartilage cells has not been evaluated.
  -: Known hypersensitivity to Cartalax (Ala-Glu-Asp tripeptide) or formulation excipients.
  -: Pregnancy - cartilage and connective tissue bioregulator effects during pregnancy have not been evaluated.
  -: Recent total joint arthroplasty - in subjects who have undergone total hip or knee replacement, the articular cartilage that Cartalax targets has been surgically removed; the bioregulator has no relevant target tissue in fully replaced joints.
  -: Concurrent high-dose systemic corticosteroids - corticosteroids suppress chondrocyte anabolic activity and inhibit proteoglycan synthesis through mechanisms that could counteract Cartalax's anabolic chondrocyte gene program normalization.
  -: Active biologic DMARD therapy for RA (tocilizumab, abatacept) - the immunological context of active biologic DMARD use for RA represents an unpredictable environment for chondrocyte bioregulator activity; the cartilage is a target of ongoing autoimmune destruction that must be addressed at the inflammatory level first.
  *: Source rating: 1 out of 5, very limited evidence
  *: PepCodex: only single-group in-vitro (MSC/chondrocyte/fibroblast) and a few animal OA models; an unstructured mention of oral use in elderly OA patients lacks any described controlled design, so no creditable human tier. Mechanism: AED modulates Ki-67/CD98hc/MMP9/SASP markers in cell models but target is inferred with no binding/knockout validation. Plausibility: chondrogenic-marker (SOX9, COL2, aggrecan) coherence is decent though mechanism-to-cartilage-outcome links remain unproven. Global coverage: all work originates from the Khavinson/Linkova St. Petersburg group with no independent or non-Russian replication. Community experience: negligible - no meaningful user reports. Effectiveness not-established: no quantified human efficacy estimate and no meaningful community effect signal.
  *: PeptideDosage.org: Cartalax is generally well tolerated in Russian observational use; reported adverse effects are infrequent and mild.; The most common reported effect is transient injection-site discomfort with subcutaneous administration.; Occasional mild gastrointestinal upset (nausea, loose stools) has been reported with oral capsule formulations, particularly at higher milligram doses.; No tolerance, dependence, or withdrawal phenomena have been reported, consistent with epigenetic rather than receptor-occupancy mechanism.; Hypersensitivity reactions are rare; allergic skin responses to peptide preparations should prompt discontinuation.; No HPA axis activation, hormonal disturbance, or significant metabolic effects have been documented at research-typical doses.; Drug-drug interaction data are not available; theoretical interactions with chondroprotective drugs, NSAIDs, or corticosteroids are unstudied.; Reproductive, pregnancy, and lactation safety data are absent; use during these periods is not recommended.

### compound | catestatin/overview | What is Catestatin?
kind: overview
title: Catestatin
summary: From Wikipep - The Peptide Encyclopedia Catestatin Chemical name Catestatin (Chromogranin A₃₅₂₋₃₇₂) Molecular formula C₁₀₆H₁₆₁N₃₁O₂₆S₂ Molecular weight 2370.7 g/mol CAS number 205650-65-3 Sequence SSMKLSFRARAYGFRGPGPQL (21 amino acids, human) Length 21 amino acids Source Endogenous (chromaffin cells, adrenergic neurons - derived from chromogranin A) Half-life ~15-20 minutes (plasma) Targets Nicotinic cholinergic receptor (nAChR - inhibits); histamine H1 receptor; multiple autocrine/paracrine targets Bioavailability IV/SC (research) Legal status Research compound (not approved) Catestatin is an endogenous 21-amino acid peptide derived from proteolytic cleavage of chromogranin A (CgA₃₅₂₋₃₇₂) in chromaffin cells of the adrenal medulla and sympathetic neurons. It was discovered in 1997 by Sushil Mahata and Daniel O'Connor as the first identified endogenous nicotinic cholinergic receptor antagonist, functioning as a physiological "brake" on catecholamine secretion.

### compound | cerebrolysin/overview | What is Cerebrolysin?
kind: overview
title: Cerebrolysin
summary: Cerebrolysin is a porcine brain-derived peptide mixture approved in 50+ countries for stroke, dementia, and traumatic brain injury. It is NOT FDA-approved in the United States despite decades of international clinical use. Contains neurotrophic peptide fragments mimicking BDNF, GDNF, NGF, and CNTF. Mixed Phase 3 results but positive meta-analyses and widespread adoption in Europe, Asia, and Latin America.
keyPoint: Cerebrolysin is a porcine brain-derived peptide mixture approved in 50+ countries for stroke, dementia, and traumatic brain injury.

### compound | cerebrolysin/mechanism | How does Cerebrolysin work?
kind: overview
title: Cerebrolysin
summary: Cerebrolysin is a porcine brain-derived peptide mixture approved in 50+ countries for stroke, dementia, and traumatic brain injury. It is NOT FDA-approved in the United States despite decades of international clinical use. Contains neurotrophic peptide fragments mimicking BDNF, GDNF, NGF, and CNTF. Mixed Phase 3 results but positive meta-analyses and widespread adoption in Europe, Asia, and Latin America.
keyPoint: Cerebrolysin is a porcine brain-derived peptide mixture approved in 50+ countries for stroke, dementia, and traumatic brain injury.

### compound | cerebrolysin/evidence | What research is listed for Cerebrolysin?
kind: evidence
title: Cerebrolysin: research listed by the sources
summary: Approved in 50+ countries. Multiple RCTs for stroke, TBI, Alzheimers. Cochrane review published.
keyPoint: Approved in 50+ countries.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: Cerebrolysin
  connectedTo: Cerebrolysin
section: What the research shows
  -: PepCodex: Cerebrolysin is a porcine brain-derived peptide mixture approved in 50+ countries for stroke, dementia, and traumatic brain injury.
  -: The Peptide Handbook: A standardized porcine brain-derived peptide/amino-acid mixture, not a single molecular entity.
  -: Peptpedia: Superior on NIHSS at day 30 across 1,879 stroke patients in meta-analysis.
  -: PeptideDosage.org: Cerebrolysin is a porcine brain-derived peptide and amino acid concentrate produced by enzymatic hydrolysis of purified porcine brain proteins, yielding a complex mixture of low-molecular-weight neuropeptides (under 10 kDa) with neurotrophic activity analogous to BDNF, NGF, GDNF, and CNTF.
  -: PeptideDeck: Recommended
section: Evidence strength
  -: PepCodex: Systematic review or meta-analysis; population: Human; Higher-level human evidence. 22 human studies listed by the source
  -: The Peptide Handbook: Animal research; population: Animal; Preclinical animal evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: Peptpedia: Source summary; study design not clearly stated; population: Not clearly stated; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: PeptideDosage.org: Randomized or controlled human research; population: Human; Direct controlled human evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: PeptideDeck: Laboratory or mechanistic research; population: Not clearly stated; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Limitations
  -: The reviewed record does not state a specific limitation. The linked paper still needs to be checked for design, size and bias.
  -: The reviewed record is animal research and cannot establish human effectiveness or safety.
  -: not FDA-approved.
  -: not freeze.
  -: not FDA-approved in the United States.
  -: not reach significance.
  -: not reach statistical significance in the overall population, pre-specified subgroup analyses revealed favorable trends in patients with more severe strokes (NIHSS greater than 12 at baseline).
  -: no signal for cardiovascular, hepatic, or other organ toxicity.
  -: No-Cerebrolysin is not FDA-approved and is not legally available as a pharmaceutical in the United States.
  -: not reviewed it because no US company has submitted an NDA-a commercial decision, not necessarily a reflection of its safety or efficacy evidence base.
  -: The source does not clearly state the study population or design in PEARL's reviewed record.
  *: Source rating: 3 out of 5
  *: PepCodex: Moderate evidence; 22 human studies listed. multiple RCTs plus Cochrane systematic reviews and a 6-RCT Alzheimer's meta-analysis, but the largest stroke trial (CASTA, N=1070) missed its primary endpoint and most trials are manufacturer-sponsored. Mechanism: neurotrophic (BDNF/NGF/GDNF-mimetic), sonic-hedgehog and PI3K/Akt pathways are characterized in vivo but the active components of the mixture remain undefined. Plausibility: claimed cognitive/motor benefits follow coherently from neurotrophic and neurogenesis biology with class analogy. Global coverage: studied across 50+ countries with independent replication and multi-regulator approval. Community experience: limited niche enthusiast discussion, no notable recurring adverse signal. Effectiveness basis is clinical (quantified human estimates: CARS day-90 ARAT Mann-Whitney 0.71, AD meta-analysis OR 3.32) but magnitude is modest, mixed across endpoints, and Cochrane found no convincing stroke mortality/dependence benefit, so confidence is low.
  *: The Peptide Handbook: moderate. Stroke evidence is low- or very-low-certainty and does not reliably demonstrate improved functional independence. TBI findings remain population- and endpoint-specific. These sources do not support transferring claims across stroke, dementia, and traumatic brain injury or treating the mixture as a defined single peptide.
  *: PeptideDosage.org: The most common adverse effects of Cerebrolysin are transient dizziness, mild flushing, sensation of warmth, or sweating during or shortly after infusion, especially when administered too rapidly; slowing the infusion rate generally resolves these symptoms.; Injection site reactions including pain, redness, or induration occur with intramuscular dosing and are dose-dependent; rotating injection sites and limiting per-site volume to under 5 mL minimizes local discomfort.; Headache and mild gastrointestinal upset (nausea, loss of appetite) have been reported in fewer than 5% of patients and typically resolve without dose reduction.; Hypersensitivity reactions are rare but reported, including urticaria and angioedema; Cerebrolysin is contraindicated in patients with known hypersensitivity to porcine proteins or to any component of the formulation.; Status epilepticus has been described in case reports following high-dose IV administration in patients with active seizure disorders; caution is warranted in patients with uncontrolled epilepsy, and slower titration is recommended.;
  *: PeptideDeck: Recommended Mimics BDNF, NGF, and GDNF neurotrophic activity without requiring full protein structures Crosses the blood-brain barrier via low-molecular-weight peptide fractions Inhibits caspase-mediated apoptosis, reducing programmed neuron death Promotes neuroplasticity and synapse formation in damaged brain tissue Supports cognitive recovery after stroke, TBI, and dementia Anti-inflammatory modulation of microglial activation Enhanced mitochondrial energy metabolism in neurons May improve memory consolidation through hippocampal BDNF upregulation 50+ year clinical track record across 50+ countries Approved prescription drug in Europe and Asia for neurological indications Cerebrolysin has one of the larger research bases among neuroactive peptide products, spanning decades of clinical study across stroke, brain injury, and dementia. The evidence is substantial but also genuinely debated, with strong support in some analyses and calls for more rigorous trials in others.
  *: WikiPep: CASTA Trial : Large Chinese study of Cerebrolysin in acute ischemic stroke CERE-COMP : Comparative trials against donepezil in Alzheimer's disease Euro-CASTA : European trial of Cerebrolysin combined with alteplase in acute stroke CAPTAIN Trial : Study in moderate-severe TBI patients Pediatric Studies : Investigation in attention deficit disorders and developmental delay Neuroplasticity : Studying pharmacologically enhanced neural plasticity Stroke Models : Tool for investigating neuroprotective strategies in ischemia Biomarker Studies : Correlating Cerebrolysin response with neurotrophic factor levels Combination Therapy : Investigating synergies with thrombolytics, rehabilitation, and other neuroprotectants [ 1 ] [ 2 ] [ 3 ] [ 4 ] [ 5 ] ↑ 1.0 1.1 Ziganshina LE, et al. "Cerebrolysin for acute ischaemic stroke." Cochrane Database Syst Rev . 2023;9:CD007026. ↑ 2.0 2.1 Muresanu DF, et al. "Cerebrolysin and Recovery After Stroke (CARS): A Randomized, Placebo-Controlled, Double-Blind, Multicenter Trial." Stroke . 2016;47(1):151-159. ↑ 3.0 3.1 Alvarez XA, et al.
  *: Cerebrolysin and Recovery After Stroke (CARS): A Randomized, Placebo-Controlled, Double-Blind, Multicenter Trial (Stroke 2016): Phase 3 multicenter RCT (Muresanu et al.). Cerebrolysin significantly improved functional recovery on the Action Research Arm Test at day 90 vs placebo - the definitive clinical trial for cerebrolysin in stroke rehabilitation.
  *: Cerebrolysin in Mild-to-Moderate Alzheimer's Disease: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Clinical Trials (Dementia and Geriatric Cognitive Disorders 2015): Pooled analysis of 6 RCTs by Gauthier et al. showing cerebrolysin significantly improved cognitive outcomes in mild-to-moderate Alzheimer's disease across multiple assessment scales.

### compound | cerluten/overview | What is Cerluten?
kind: overview
title: Cerluten
summary: A cytamin-class peptide supplement derived from brain tissue, part of the Russian bioregulator framework. Marketed as an oral supplement for cognitive support and neuroprotection. Contains peptide complexes rather than defined sequences. No Western clinical validation.
keyPoint: A cytamin-class peptide supplement derived from brain tissue, part of the Russian bioregulator framework.

section: Evidence strength
  -: PeptideDosage.org: Systematic review or meta-analysis; population: Animal; Preclinical animal evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Main limitations
  -: Cerluten (also sold as CNS Cytomax A-5) is a peptide bioregulator from Vladimir Khavinson's Russian school of bioregulation. It is not a single defined molecule but a low-molecular-weight polypeptide complex (peptides up to roughly 10 kDa) extracted from the cerebral cortex of young calves and formulated as 10 mg oral

### compound | cerluten/evidence | What research is listed for Cerluten?
kind: evidence
title: Cerluten: research listed by the sources
summary: Manufacturer and distributor documentation report that Cerluten is generally well tolerated, with no toxic or allergic reactions noted in limited Russian use; however, this rests on small uncontrolled observations rather than formal safety trials [7].; Stated contraindications are individual intolerance of any component, pregnancy, and lactation; these groups are advised not to use it [7].; Because Cerluten is an animal-derived (bovine cerebral cortex) biological extract, there are theoretical risks not formally evaluated to international standards, including immunogenicity/allergic sensitization and the prion-disease concern inherent to bovine central-nervous-system tissue [7].; No standardized toxicology, genotoxicity, or long-term safety data meeting Western regulatory requirements have been published, and the precise peptide content of each batch is not chemically defined, so lot-to-lot consistency cannot be assured [7].; No human pharmacokinetic or drug-interaction studies exist; interactions with prescription medications, anticoagulants, or other neuroactive agents have not Peptide University labels its records as aggregated from empirical research and anecdotal community data. This record is retained as supplied and is not upgraded to clinical evidence.
keyPoint: Manufacturer and distributor documentation report that Cerluten is generally well tolerated, with no toxic or allergic reactions noted in limited Russian use; however, this rests on small uncontrolled observations rather than formal safety...
understood: resolved
method: canonical

matchedText: Cerluten
  connectedTo: Cerluten
section: What the research shows
  -: PepCodex: A cytamin-class peptide supplement derived from brain tissue, part of the Russian bioregulator framework.
  -: PeptideDosage.org: Cerluten (also sold as CNS Cytomax A-5) is a peptide bioregulator from Vladimir Khavinson's Russian school of bioregulation.
  -: Peptide University Codex: Cerluten is a Khavinson cytomedin - peptide complex A-5 - extracted from the brain and spinal cord tissue of young animals, developed as the oral central nervous system bioregulator of the Khavinson framework.
section: Evidence strength
  -: PepCodex: Source summary; study design not clearly stated; population: Not clearly stated; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: PeptideDosage.org: Systematic review or meta-analysis; population: Animal; Preclinical animal evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: Peptide University Codex: Source summary; study design not clearly stated; population: Not clearly stated; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Limitations
  -: The source does not clearly state the study population or design in PEARL's reviewed record.
  -: Cerluten (also sold as CNS Cytomax A-5) is a peptide bioregulator from Vladimir Khavinson's Russian school of bioregulation. It is not a single defined molecule but a low-molecular-weight polypeptide complex (peptides up to roughly 10 kDa) extracted from the cerebral cortex of young calves and formulated as 10 mg oral
  -: Acute stroke in the first 4 weeks - Cerluten is not an acute intervention; the inflammatory and hemorrhagic dynamics of the acute stroke period require neurological management; bioregulator activity is appropriate in the post-acute recovery phase.
  -: Active CNS malignancy (glioblastoma, brain metastases) - neuronal and glial cell gene program normalization in the context of CNS malignancy has not been evaluated; CNS oncological evaluation required.
  -: Known hypersensitivity to Cerluten (CNS tissue cytomedin peptide complex A-5) or formulation excipients including gelatin.
  -: Pregnancy - CNS development during pregnancy (neurulation, synaptogenesis, cortical layering) involves tightly regulated gene programs; exogenous CNS bioregulator activity during gestation has not been evaluated.
  -: Active psychosis or acute psychiatric decompensation - the neurobiological normalization activity of Cerluten in the context of active psychotic states has not been characterized; psychiatric stabilization before initiating is appropriate.
  -: Concurrent MAO inhibitors - theoretical interaction with the CNS neurotransmitter normalization activity of CNS peptide bioregulators; no documented adverse interaction but caution is appropriate given the CNS activity profile.

### compound | cetrorelix/overview | What is Cetrorelix?
kind: overview
title: Cetrorelix
summary: Cetrorelix (brand name Cetrotide) is a synthetic decapeptide gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH/LH-RH) antagonist used in assisted reproduction to prevent premature luteinizing hormone (LH) surges during controlled ovarian stimulation. Built on the native GnRH decapeptide backbone with several D-amino-acid substitutions (Ac-D-Nal-D-Phe(4Cl)-D-Pal-Ser-Tyr-D-Cit-Leu-Arg-Pro-D-Ala-NH2), it competitively blocks pituitary GnRH receptors and produces an immediate, dose-dependent, reversible fall in LH and FSH without the initial "flare-up" seen with GnRH agonists. The headline Cetrorelix dosage is 0.25 mg (250 mcg) injected subcutaneously once daily during the late follicular phase (the multiple-dose protocol), or a single 3 mg subcutaneous injection that controls the LH surge for roughly four days (the single-dose protocol) [1][4][6].
keyPoint: Cetrorelix (brand name Cetrotide) is a synthetic decapeptide gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH/LH-RH) antagonist used in assisted reproduction to prevent premature luteinizing hormone (LH) surges during controlled ovarian stimulation.

### compound | cetrorelix/evidence | What research is listed for Cetrorelix?
kind: evidence
title: Cetrorelix: research listed by the sources
summary: Injection-site reactions are the most common local effect, including transient redness, itching, swelling, or mild pain at the lower-abdomen subcutaneous site; these are usually mild and short-lived [1].; Ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (OHSS) was reported in roughly 3.5% of treated cycles in registration data; although antagonist protocols generally lower OHSS risk versus agonist long protocols, OHSS remains a serious potential complication of the underlying ovarian stimulation [1][8].; Systemic adverse reactions are generally infrequent and mild, with nausea (~1.3%) and headache (~1.1%) among the most reported [1].; Hypersensitivity and rare anaphylactoid/allergic reactions can occur; Cetrorelix is contraindicated in people with known hypersensitivity to cetrorelix, to extrinsic peptide hormones, to GnRH or any GnRH analog, or to mannitol (an excipient) [1].; It is contraindicated in known or suspected pregnancy and during lactation, and in severe renal impairment; clinically it is used only within a monitored, physician-directed stimulation cycle [1].; Because it suppresses LH Five clinical studies in 732 patients evaluated either a daily 0.25 mg schedule or a single 3 mg schedule during controlled ovarian stimulation. The two regimens have different timing and must not be combined into an improvised protocol.

### compound | cgrp/overview | What is CGRP?
kind: overview
title: CGRP
summary: From Wikipep - The Peptide Encyclopedia CGRP Chemical name Calcitonin Gene-Related Peptide Molecular formula C₁₈₆H₂₉₁N₅₅O₅₇S₂ (alpha-CGRP) Molecular weight 3789.4 g/mol CAS number 83652-28-2 Sequence ACDTATCVTHRLAGLLSRSGGVVKNNFVPTNVGSKAF-NH₂ (alpha-CGRP) Length 37 amino acids Source Sensory neurons (alternative splicing of calcitonin gene) Half-life ~7 minutes Targets CGRP receptor (CLR/RAMP1 complex) Bioavailability Endogenous neuropeptide Legal status Endogenous / Target of approved drugs CGRP ( Calcitonin Gene-Related Peptide ) is a 37-amino acid neuropeptide produced by alternative RNA splicing of the calcitonin/CGRP gene (CALCA) in sensory neurons. It is one of the most potent vasodilators known and plays a central role in migraine pathophysiology, pain transmission, and neurogenic inflammation. Two isoforms exist: alpha-CGRP (predominantly neural) and beta-CGRP (from a separate gene, CALCB, predominantly enteric).

### compound | chelohart/overview | What is Chelohart?
kind: overview
title: Chelohart
summary: A cytamin-class peptide supplement derived from cardiac (heart) tissue, part of the Khavinson bioregulator framework. Marketed as an oral supplement for cardiac health support. Contains peptide complexes rather than defined sequences. Very limited clinical validation, primarily Russian-language literature.

### compound | chelohart/evidence | What research is listed for Chelohart?
kind: evidence
title: Chelohart: research listed by the sources
summary: No controlled human safety data exist for Chelohart; suppliers report no side effects, but this reflects the absence of formal trials rather than demonstrated safety, and the points below are extrapolated from the bioregulator class generally.; Taken orally, the most plausible effects are mild gastrointestinal upset; manufacturers advise taking capsules with meals, and individual intolerance to capsule excipients (such as lactose, microcrystalline cellulose, or beet sugar) is possible.; For the educational subcutaneous model, injection can cause local reactions including redness, itching, swelling, bruising, or transient pain; any injected peptide also carries a theoretical risk of immune or hypersensitivity reactions, so stop and seek care for rash, hives, facial or throat swelling, or difficulty breathing.; Because Chelohart is a tissue-derived animal peptide complex rather than a single defined molecule, batch-to-batch variability, residual foreign-protein content, and a theoretical risk of allergic or immunogenic reaction cannot be excluded.; Research- and supplement-grade

### compound | chitomur/overview | What is Chitomur?
kind: overview
title: Chitomur
summary: Chitomur (Bladder Cytomax A-12) is a natural peptide bioregulator in the Khavinson "Cytomax" family: a lyophilized complex of short, bladder-derived peptides (chains of roughly 2 to 4 amino acids) isolated from the urinary-bladder tissue of young animals at the St. Petersburg Institute of Bioregulation and Gerontology [2][3]. Rather than acting on a cell-surface receptor, these ultrashort peptides are hypothesized to enter the nucleus of bladder epithelial and detrusor smooth-muscle cells and bind tissue-specific promoter sequences, modulating the genes that govern bladder-wall regeneration, detrusor tone, and local antioxidant defense [2][4]. The strongest clinical signal is a blind, randomized, placebo-controlled study by Gomberg, Ryzhak, and Liutov (2013) in which a 30-day Chitomur course significantly improved urodynamic parameters and quality of life in elderly men with benign prostatic hyperplasia, with no adverse effects recorded [1].

### compound | chitomur/evidence | What research is listed for Chitomur?
kind: evidence
title: Chitomur: research listed by the sources
summary: The only controlled human safety data is the small 30-day BPH trial, which reported no adverse effects [1]; beyond that, Chitomur's long-term and systemic safety profile is essentially uncharacterized.; Taken orally, peptide bioregulators are generally reported by suppliers to cause only infrequent mild gastrointestinal discomfort, but these figures come from marketing materials rather than independent trials and should be treated cautiously.; In the educational subcutaneous model, injection can cause local reactions including redness, itching, swelling, bruising, or transient pain at the injection site.; Because Chitomur is a natural complex extracted from bovine/animal bladder tissue, there is a theoretical risk of immune or hypersensitivity reactions and of tissue-derived contaminants; stop use and seek care for rash, hives, facial or throat swelling, or difficulty breathing.; Research- and supplement-grade peptide products are not manufactured to pharmaceutical standards, so contamination, endotoxin, inconsistent peptide content, and inaccurate labeling are realistic risks;

### compound | chonluten/evidence | What research is listed for Chonluten?
kind: evidence
title: Chonluten: research listed by the sources
summary: Chonluten is reported to be exceptionally well tolerated in Russian-language literature, with rare injection-site reactions and no documented systemic toxicity at standard cyclic doses, although independent safety data are limited.; Injection-site reactions including erythema, mild swelling, and transient itching are the most commonly reported adverse events with subcutaneous administration of any short peptide bioregulator.; Hypersensitivity reactions are possible but rarely reported with Khavinson short peptides, possibly because of the very small size and minimal immunogenicity of the tripeptide.; Theoretical risks of broad gene-expression modulation include effects on tissues other than the intended bronchopulmonary target; this concern is mitigated by the limited systemic exposure but is not fully characterized.; Long-term safety of cyclic Chonluten administration beyond a few years has not been evaluated in published prospective studies, and effects on cancer biology in patients with active or treated malignancy are unknown.; Sterile injection technique is essential because Peptide University labels its records as aggregated from empirical research and anecdotal community data. This record is retained as supplied and is not upgraded to clinical evidence.

  -: 14 Important Note This content is intended for therapeutic educational purposes only and does not constitute medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment.
  -: Active pulmonary malignancy or colorectal carcinoma - Chonluten's dual epithelial bioregulator activity in the context of malignant alveolar or colonic epithelial cells has not been evaluated; oncological evaluation required.
  -: Active inflammatory bowel disease in acute flare (Crohn's disease, ulcerative colitis) - colonic epithelial gene program normalization during active transmural or mucosal inflammation of IBD has not been characterized; the priority is anti-inflammatory medical management of the flare.
  -: Active pulmonary infection requiring antibiotic/antiviral treatment - alveolar bioregulator activity during active pulmonary infection should be deferred until antimicrobial treatment is complete.
  -: Recent colonic or pulmonary surgery (within 4 weeks) - the acute surgical healing phase involves specific tissue repair programs; exogenous bioregulator activity during this window has not been evaluated.
  -: Known hypersensitivity to Chonluten (Lys-Glu-Asp tripeptide) or formulation excipients.
  -: Pregnancy - dual epithelial bioregulator effects on pulmonary and colonic tissue during pregnancy have not been evaluated.
  -: Active lung transplantation immunosuppression - alveolar epithelial bioregulator activity in immunosuppressed recipients with donor lung tissue requires transplant pulmonology evaluation.
  -: Severe active Clostridioides difficile colitis - colonic epithelial bioregulator activity during active C. difficile infection with significant mucosal injury should be deferred until antimicrobial treatment and clinical resolution.

### compound | cjc1295dacipamorelin/overview | What is CJC-1295 DAC + Ipamorelin?
kind: overview
title: CJC-1295 DAC + Ipamorelin
summary: The CJC-1295 DAC + Ipamorelin stack combines a long-acting albumin-bound GHRH analogue (CJC-1295 DAC, half-life 6-8 days, weekly dosing) with a highly selective GHSR1a agonist (ipamorelin, half-life 2 hours, thrice-daily dosing). The pharmacology is distinct from the no-DAC variant of the stack: CJC-1295 DAC produces continuous low-amplitude GH elevation through its 6-8 day half-life, while ipamorelin adds discrete ghrelin-receptor-mediated GH pulses on top of the elevated baseline. Teichman et al. (JCEM 2006) characterised CJC-1295 DAC pharmacokinetics in 21 healthy adults, demonstrating GH elevations of 2-10 fold and IGF-1 elevations of 1.5-3 fold persisting 9-11 days after a single injection. Neither component is FDA approved; both are supplied solely as research chemicals. Typical research dosing is 2 mg CJC-1295 DAC subcutaneously weekly + 100-300 mcg ipamorelin two to three times per day.
keyPoint: The CJC-1295 DAC + Ipamorelin stack combines a long-acting albumin-bound GHRH analogue (CJC-1295 DAC, half-life 6-8 days, weekly dosing) with a highly selective GHSR1a agonist (ipamorelin, half-life 2 hours, thrice-daily dosing).
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: CJC-1295 DAC + Ipamorelin
  connectedTo: CJC-1295 DAC + Ipamorelin
section: Why it is researched

section: How it works in the research
  -: CJC-1295 DAC binds the GHRH receptor on pituitary somatotrophs and signals through Gs-cAMP to drive growth hormone exocytosis, identical at the molecular level to native GHRH and tesamorelin.

### compound | cjc1295dacipamorelin/evidence | What research is listed for CJC-1295 DAC + Ipamorelin?
kind: evidence
title: CJC-1295 DAC + Ipamorelin: research listed by the sources
summary: Sustained IGF-1 elevation drives oedema, hand stiffness and median-nerve paraesthesia in the first 2-4 weeks; more prominent than in the no-DAC variant because of the continuous receptor occupancy.; Persistent fatigue and somnolence, particularly in the morning, reflect loss of GH trough periods under continuous CJC-1295 DAC stimulation; this is the principal lifestyle trade-off versus the pulsatile no-DAC variant.; Glucose intolerance with HbA1c rise of 0.3-0.6% can develop with chronic dosing, more pronounced than no-DAC variant because of continuous GH signal; pre-diabetic individuals should monitor glucose closely.; An unresolved cardiac safety signal from CJC-1295 DAC's 2007 Phase II development pause warrants caution in patients with cardiovascular risk factors; no causal link to monotherapy has been established but the signal remains.; Injection-site reactions are more common with the depot-effect DAC variant than with short-acting GHRH analogues; sterile abscess is rare but reported.; Sub-clinical hypogonadism from chronic supraphysiologic IGF-1 has been reported; quarterly

### compound | cjc1295ghrp2/overview | What is CJC-1295 + GHRP-2?
kind: overview
title: CJC-1295 + GHRP-2
summary: The CJC-1295 + GHRP-2 stack combines a GHRH analogue with a potent ghrelin-receptor agonist to exploit the dual-pathway GH-release synergy at the pituitary somatotroph. Depending on the CJC-1295 variant used, the stack produces either pulsatile dual-pulse GH release (no-DAC variant) or continuous-plus-pulsed GH elevation (DAC variant). Bowers (JCEM 2001) and Mericq (JCEM 1998) established that combined GHRH + GHRP produces growth hormone responses 3 to 5 times higher than either agent alone, and GHRP-2 is approximately 2 to 3 times more potent per microgram than GHRP-6 at GHSR1a, making this stack one of the most aggressive GH-release combinations in research peptide use. Neither component is FDA approved; both are supplied solely as research chemicals. Typical research dosing is 100 mcg of CJC-1295 no DAC + 100-200 mcg GHRP-2 subcutaneously two to three times per day.
keyPoint: The CJC-1295 + GHRP-2 stack combines a GHRH analogue with a potent ghrelin-receptor agonist to exploit the dual-pathway GH-release synergy at the pituitary somatotroph.

### compound | cjc1295ghrp2/evidence | What research is listed for CJC-1295 + GHRP-2?
kind: evidence
title: CJC-1295 + GHRP-2: research listed by the sources
summary: Mild prolactin elevation (10-20% above baseline) occurs at GHRP-2 doses above 200 mcg subcutaneous, distinguishing this stack from the ipamorelin variant; symptomatic galactorrhoea is rare but documented at chronic high doses.; Cortisol and ACTH elevations of 10-30% above baseline occur at supratherapeutic GHRP-2 doses; clinically silent in most subjects but warrants caution in adrenal disease or corticosteroid therapy.; Acute appetite stimulation within 15-30 minutes of injection, milder than GHRP-6 but stronger than ipamorelin; useful in cachexia research but potentially undesirable for weight-management goals.; Mild flushing and warm sensation within 15-30 minutes of injection, attributable to GHRH-receptor mediated vasodilation; tolerance develops within 1-2 weeks.; Transient headache, mild peripheral oedema during the first 2-3 weeks, drowsiness after evening dosing, and mild glucose intolerance with chronic use are shared features with all GH secretagogue stacks.; Tachyphylaxis develops gradually with continuous thrice-daily dosing and is managed with 4-week washouts every

### compound | cjcipablend/overview | What is CJC-1295 NO DAC + Ipamorelin?
kind: overview
title: CJC-1295 NO DAC + Ipamorelin
summary: The CJC-1295 no DAC + ipamorelin stack is the most widely used growth hormone secretagogue combination in research peptide protocols. It pairs a short-acting GHRH analogue (Mod GRF 1-29, with a 30-minute half-life) and a highly selective GHSR1a agonist (ipamorelin, with a 2-hour half-life) to exploit the well-characterised synergy between the two pituitary somatotroph signalling pathways. The combination produces growth hormone responses 3 to 5 times higher than either agent administered alone, as demonstrated in multiple GHRH/GHRP synergy studies (Bowers JCEM 2001, Mericq JCEM 1998). Neither component is FDA approved; both are supplied solely as research chemicals. Typical research dosing is 100 mcg of each peptide subcutaneously two to three times per day, often co-injected from the same syringe pre-breakfast, mid-afternoon and pre-bed.
keyPoint: The CJC-1295 no DAC + ipamorelin stack is the most widely used growth hormone secretagogue combination in research peptide protocols.

### compound | cjcipablend/safety | What are the risks of CJC-1295 NO DAC + Ipamorelin?

matchedText: CJC-1295 NO DAC + Ipamorelin
  connectedTo: CJC-1295 NO DAC + Ipamorelin
  *: Head rush and flushing immediately post-injection - the most acutely distinctive adverse effect of GH secretagogue combinations; occurs within 5-15 minutes of injection; mechanism involves the acute transient GH release producing vasodilation; typically brief (5-10 minutes), mild, and attenuates after the first few. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Mild water retention and peripheral edema - GH-mediated sodium retention and antidiuretic effects; most pronounced in the first 1-2 weeks of each cycle; typically subsides as GH levels equilibrate at steady state. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Vivid dreams and intensified dream recall - closely linked to GH pulse amplification of slow-wave sleep in which GH is naturally released; extremely commonly reported; typically experienced as neutral to positive; can be disruptive in subjects with pre-existing sleep disturbances. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Joint discomfort and arthralgia - GH-mediated soft tissue edema produces joint pressure and discomfort, particularly wrists and shoulders; dose-dependent; more pronounced at the Hulk and Bodybuilder Saturation protocols. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Mild insulin resistance and fasting glucose elevation - GH produces transient peripheral insulin resistance; typically within normal range in non-diabetic subjects at standard doses; warrants monitoring at the 3x daily saturation protocol. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Carpal tunnel syndrome symptoms - wrist paresthesias and nocturnal hand numbness from GH-driven soft tissue swelling; dose-dependent; resolves with cycle cessation. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Mild fatigue or lethargy on initiation - the initial GH pulse amplification and its systemic metabolic effects can produce brief post-injection fatigue; the pre-bed timing ensures this typically occurs during sleep rather than during waking hours. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Transient hypoglycemia (rare) - GH has a paradoxical acute insulin-sensitizing effect immediately after the GH pulse, before the more sustained insulin-resistance effect takes over; in subjects with low baseline blood glucose, the acute post-pulse sensitization can produce mild hypoglycemia within 30-60 minutes of. [source-listed source severity]

section: Limitations
  -: The CJC-1295 no DAC + ipamorelin stack is the most widely used growth hormone secretagogue combination in research peptide protocols.
  -: Active cancer or history of rapidly progressive cancer - IGF-1 elevation from GH axis stimulation supports tumor cell proliferation via IGF-1R signaling; absolute contraindication in all active malignancies; history of aggressive cancer requires oncological clearance.
  -: Pituitary adenoma or pituitary tumor - GHRHR and GHS-R1a are expressed on pituitary tissue; GH secretagogue stimulation in subjects with pituitary adenomas (particularly GH-secreting somatotroph adenomas causing acromegaly) is absolutely contraindicated.
  -: Acromegaly - pre-existing pathological GH excess; further GH axis stimulation is absolutely contraindicated.
  -: Active diabetic retinopathy - GH-mediated IGF-1 elevation accelerates retinal neovascularization in diabetic retinopathy; pre-proliferative and proliferative stages are absolute contraindications.
  -: Severe insulin resistance or uncontrolled diabetes mellitus - GH-induced peripheral insulin resistance can significantly destabilize glycemic control; glycemic management must be optimized before initiating any GH secretagogue protocol.
  -: Carpal tunnel syndrome - GH-driven fluid retention worsens carpal tunnel compression; active carpal tunnel syndrome warrants dose reduction or avoidance.
  -: Known hypersensitivity to CJC-1295 (No DAC), Ipamorelin, or formulation excipients.
  -: Pregnancy - GH axis stimulation during pregnancy has not been characterized and exogenous GH secretagogue activity overlaps with the highly active placental GH-IGF-1 axis of normal pregnancy.

  *: Nephrotoxicity (30-60%): Dose-limiting; higher incidence than polymyxin B; presents as acute tubular necrosis, rising creatinine Neurotoxicity (5-10%): Paresthesias, visual disturbances, slurred speech, vertigo, confusion Bronchospasm (inhaled route): 5-10%; pre-treatment with bronchodilator recommended GI. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Acute Kidney Injury : Most common serious toxicity; risk factors include prolonged duration, concurrent nephrotoxins, and high doses Neuromuscular Blockade : Rare but potentially fatal respiratory paralysis; risk increased with concurrent aminoglycosides or neuromuscular blocking agents Anaphylaxis : Rare. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Limit IV course duration where possible (typically ≤14 days) Avoid concurrent nephrotoxins Therapeutic drug monitoring (where available) Adequate hydration; monitor creatinine and urine output daily. [source-listed source severity]

### compound | colistin/evidence | What research is listed for Colistin?
kind: evidence
title: Colistin: research listed by the sources
summary: Broad Gram-Negative Activity : Active against most Enterobacteriaceae, Pseudomonas aeruginosa , Acinetobacter spp., Stenotrophomonas maltophilia Inhaled Route Advantage : CMS is preferred for inhaled delivery due to lower airway irritation vs. polymyxin B sulfate Synergistic Combinations : Synergy demonstrated with carbapenems (even against carbapenem-resistant strains), rifampin, minocycline, and fosfomycin Topical Safety : Excellent safety profile for topical, ophthalmic, and otic applications SDD Use : Oral colistin sulfate used in selective digestive decontamination (SDD) protocols in ICUs Phe et al. (2014) : Nephrotoxicity - AKI in 54.6% of CMS patients vs. 21.1% polymyxin B (p<0.001) Rigatto et al. (2015) : 30-day mortality - no significant difference, but CMS associated with greater PK variability Shields et al. (2017) : CRE bacteremia - polymyxin B combination therapy showed 23% lower mortality than CMS-based regimens [ 1 ] [ 2 ] [ 3 ] [ 4 ] [ 5 ] ↑ 1.0 1.1 Tsuji BT, et al. "International Consensus Guidelines for the Optimal Use of the Polymyxins." Pharmacotherapy .

  *: Blue-Green Discoloration Some users report temporary blue or green discoloration of the skin after applying copper peptide products. [source-listed source severity]
  *: This is caused by copper ions depositing on the skin surface and usually fades within a few hours.[45] High-quality, pharmaceutical-grade GHK-Cu products with proper formulation should not cause significant discoloration. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Persistent staining suggests a product quality issue - the copper may not be properly complexed with the peptide.[46] Skin Purging In some cases, copper peptides may accelerate cell turnover, leading to temporary breakouts (commonly called "purging"). [source-listed source severity]
  *: This typically resolves within 2-4 weeks as the skin adjusts.[47] True purging occurs in areas where you typically break out. [source-listed source severity]
  *: If new acne appears in areas where you don't normally get breakouts, it may be irritation or an allergic reaction rather than purging. [source-listed source severity]
  *: "Copper Uglies" An anecdotal phenomenon called "copper uglies" has been reported in online skincare communities - users claim copper peptide products made their skin look older or more damaged rather than better. [source-listed source severity]

### compound | copperpeptides/evidence | What research is listed for Copper Peptides?
kind: evidence
title: Copper Peptides: research listed by the sources
summary: If you've spent any time researching anti-aging skincare, you've probably run into copper peptides. You'll find them in serums, moisturizers, and creams - often marketed with claims about collagen production and "skin regeneration." But what does the actual science say? Copper peptides - particularly GHK-Cu - represent a scientifically plausible approach to anti-aging skincare. The research shows they stimulate collagen and elastin synthesis, accelerate wound healing, reduce inflammation, and provide antioxidant protection. Clinical studies suggest they may match or exceed retinoids and vitamin C in promoting collagen production, often with better tolerability. That said, the evidence remains preliminary. Most studies are small, short-term, and lack rigorous controls. We don't have long-term data on sustained use over years or decades. Here's what we can say with confidence: Copper peptides likely work. The biological mechanisms are well-understood. They bind copper, deliver it to cells, and activate pathways involved in tissue repair and extracellular matrix synthesis.

### compound | cortagen/overview | What is Cortagen?
kind: overview
title: Cortagen
summary: Cortagen is a synthetic tripeptide bioregulator (EDR: Glutamic acid-Aspartic acid-Arginine) developed by Professor Vladimir Khavinsky at the St. Petersburg Institute of Bioregulation and Gerontology, specifically targeting neuroprotection and functional restoration of cerebral cortex neurons. Cortagen is structurally related to Pinealon (also an EDR-sequence peptide), but the two are formulated for distinct brain regions: Pinealon targets hippocampal memory consolidation and pineal gland neurogenesis, while Cortagen targets the cerebral cortex - higher cognitive function, executive processing, and cortical neuroprotection against age-related decline. Cortagen's mechanism operates through the same epigenetic gene regulation pathway as Pinealon: it penetrates cell nuclei and modulates transcription factor activity, influencing the expression of genes governing neuronal survival, neurotrophin production, and anti-apoptotic signaling in cortical tissue.

section: Limitations
  -: This is a commercial educational source. Its uncited figures and modelled outputs must remain labelled as source-listed rather than clinical evidence.
  -: Cortagen is a synthetic tetrapeptide (Ala-Glu-Asp-Pro, AEDP) developed by Vladimir Khavinson and colleagues at the St. Petersburg Institute of Bioregulation and Gerontology, derived by directed synthesis from the amino-acid composition of the polypeptide preparation Cortexin (a bovine cerebral cortex hydrolysate used
  -: The source does not clearly state the study population or design in PEARL's reviewed record.
  -: 14 Important Note This content is for educational purposes only and is not medical advice.
  -: Active seizure disorders not under pharmacological control - cortical bioregulator activity affecting neuronal excitability and synaptic signaling has not been evaluated in subjects with uncontrolled epilepsy; any compound affecting cortical neuronal gene programs in the context of pathological hyperexcitability
  -: Active CNS infection (meningitis, encephalitis) - exogenous cortical bioregulator activity during active brain infection could interfere with the CNS immune response and neuroinflammatory defense mechanisms.
  -: Concurrent use with CNS-active medications requiring stable plasma levels (narrow therapeutic index antiepileptics, MAOIs, lithium) - while no direct pharmacokinetic interactions are documented, any compound affecting neuronal function in subjects on narrow-index CNS drugs warrants awareness.
  -: Known hypersensitivity to Cortagen (Ala-Glu-Asp-Pro tetrapeptide) or formulation excipients.
  -: Pregnancy - cortical neurodevelopmental processes during fetal brain formation are tightly regulated; exogenous cortical bioregulator activity has not been characterized during fetal CNS development.
  -: Severe psychiatric disorders in acute phase (psychosis, severe mania) - cortical gene program modulation in subjects with acute cortical dysregulation from psychiatric disease may produce unpredictable effects.
  -: Active malignant brain tumors - bioregulator normalization of cortical cell gene programs in the context of CNS malignancy where tumor cells may express cortical tissue receptors has not been characterized.
  *: Source rating: 2 out of 5, limited evidence
  *: Peptide Hub: Protocol-focused educational summary. Linked papers, site-listed ranges and commercial context are retained with source attribution.
  *: PeptideDosage.org: Cortagen is generally well tolerated in Russian observational use; the most common reported effects are mild injection-site discomfort with subcutaneous administration and occasional transient headache.; No serious adverse events have been documented in the indexed literature, but the absence of large randomized safety trials means the side-effect profile is poorly characterized by Western standards.; Gastrointestinal upset (nausea, loose stools) is occasionally reported with oral administration, particularly at higher milligram doses, and typically resolves on dose reduction.; No tolerance, dependence, or withdrawal phenomena have been reported, consistent with the proposed epigenetic rather than receptor-occupancy mechanism.; Hypersensitivity reactions are rare; allergic skin reactions to peptide preparations should prompt discontinuation.; No HPA axis activation, hormonal disturbance, or significant metabolic effects have been reported with research-typical doses.; Reproductive, pregnancy, and lactation safety data are absent; use during these periods is not advised.; Drug-drug

### compound | cortexin/overview | What is Cortexin?
kind: overview
title: Cortexin
summary: A Russian neuropeptide complex derived from porcine or bovine cerebral cortex, approved in Russia and CIS countries for neurological conditions. Contains low molecular weight polypeptides (1,000-10,000 Da) with proposed neurotrophic and neuroprotective properties. NOT approved by FDA, EMA, or other Western regulatory agencies. Evidence comes primarily from Russian studies with limited Western validation.

### compound | cortexin/evidence | What research is listed for Cortexin?

title: Cortexin: research listed by the sources
summary: Moderate evidence; 12 human studies listed Allergic and hypersensitivity reactions, including rare anaphylactic shock and angioedema as well as skin rash, itching and redness; Cortexin is contraindicated in anyone with known hypersensitivity to its components.; CNS activation: psychomotor agitation, increased excitability, anxiety, insomnia and, in sensitive individuals, coordination disturbances; dosing earlier in the day is sometimes advised to limit sleep disruption.; Cardiovascular: tachycardia has been reported among the recognized adverse reactions.; Injection-site reactions such as local pain, redness or swelling; when 0.5% procaine (novocaine) is used as the clinical diluent, procaine-class sensitivity must be excluded first.; Animal-derived material: as a bovine/porcine cortex extract, it carries theoretical immunogenic and biological-contaminant concerns; manufacturing aims to remove these, but they cannot be claimed to be zero-risk.; Pregnancy, breastfeeding and pediatric use: not recommended in pregnancy or lactation due to absent safety data; pediatric dosing is weight-adjusted and should be

### compound | cortistatin14/evidence | What research is listed for Cortistatin-14?
kind: evidence
title: Cortistatin-14: research listed by the sources
summary: preliminary. Cortistatin-14 is a cyclic neuropeptide first isolated from rat cortex, sharing 11 of 14 residues with somatostatin-14 while retaining a distinct receptor profile that includes additional targets such as MCHR1. Preclinical work has examined immune and inflammatory signaling, but those findings do not establish a therapy. Direct human evidence is limited to small endocrine research exposures involving intravenous cortistatin-14 and its interaction with related secretagogues; these studies were not therapeutic efficacy trials. Cortistatin-14 remains investigational, and human dosing, pharmacokinetics, and safety are not established. Potent anti-inflammatory effects in multiple tissue types Immunomodulatory activity without broad immunosuppression Neuroprotective properties in inflammatory CNS conditions Sleep-promoting and cortical activity modulation Analgesic effects in inflammatory and neuropathic pain models Regulation of Th17/Treg immune cell balance Protection against sepsis and systemic inflammation Potential therapeutic effects in autoimmune arthritis Cortistatin has been extensively studied in animal models of inflammatory and autoimmune diseases, with consistently positive results across diverse conditions. While human clinical data remains limited, the preclinical evidence provides a strong foundation for understanding the peptide's therapeutic potential.

### compound | cotadutide/overview | What is Cotadutide?
kind: overview
title: Cotadutide
summary: Cotadutide (MEDI0382) is an investigational, lipidated 30-amino-acid peptide that acts as a balanced dual agonist of the glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) and glucagon receptors. It belongs to the GLP-1/glucagon dual-agonist class of metabolic peptides and was engineered by MedImmune/AstraZeneca from the gut hormone oxyntomodulin, with a palmitic-acid (gamma-Glu) side chain added to a lysine to bind albumin and extend its half-life [2][7]. The most-studied Cotadutide dosage is a once-daily subcutaneous injection titrated stepwise from 50 mcg upward to 100 mcg, 200 mcg, and a 300 mcg maintenance dose, with some trials escalating to 600 mcg under safety monitoring [1][3].
keyPoint: Cotadutide (MEDI0382) is an investigational, lipidated 30-amino-acid peptide that acts as a balanced dual agonist of the glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) and glucagon receptors.

method: canonical
