section: How it works in the research
  -: Cotadutide is a synthetic 30-amino-acid peptide derived from oxyntomodulin, an endogenous gut hormone that naturally engages both the GLP-1 and glucagon receptors.

### compound | cotadutide/evidence | What research is listed for Cotadutide?
kind: evidence
title: Cotadutide: research listed by the sources
summary: Gastrointestinal effects are dose-limiting and the most common: in the 54-week phase 2b study nausea occurred in about 35% and vomiting in about 17% of cotadutide-treated participants, with event rates declining over time as patients adapted [3].; Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, decreased appetite, and constipation are driven mainly by GLP-1-mediated slowing of gastric emptying; escalating the dose too quickly markedly worsens these symptoms, which is why slow titration from 50 mcg is essential [1][3].; Because the glucagon component transiently raises endogenous glucose production via glycogenolysis, careful dosing and the dominant GLP-1 insulinotropic effect are needed to keep net glycemic control favorable rather than worsening blood sugar [2][6].; As with other incretin agents, there is risk of hypoglycemia when combined with insulin or sulfonylureas; injection-site reactions and increased heart rate have also been reported with GLP-1-based therapies.; Dehydration from vomiting or diarrhea can stress the kidneys; although PK was unchanged in renal impairment, fluid status should be Route Frequency Titration Target Dose Subcutaneous Once daily (current) or weekly (extended formulations in development) Gradual escalation over 4-8 weeks 300-600 μg/day (dose-finding ongoing) [ 1 ] [ 2 ] [ 3 ] [ 4 ] ↑ 1.0 1.1 Ambery P, et al. ### compound | crystagen/overview | What is Crystagen?
kind: overview
title: Crystagen
summary: Crystagen is a synthetic immune peptide bioregulator from the Khavinson family of ultra-short peptides. It is built on the tripeptide sequence Glu-Asp-Pro (EDP, molecular weight ~359 Da) and is sometimes catalogued as "Immune cytogen EDP." Structurally it is an EDP core closely related to Cortagen (Ala-Glu-Asp-Pro) and is described as a fragment-type signal derived from the thymic regulator Thymalin. Rather than acting through receptor occupancy and mass-dependent pharmacology, peptides of this class are proposed to enter cells, bind DNA in a sequence-specific manner, and modulate the expression of genes governing immune-cell development, cytokine output, and thymic function. Historically, cytogen-class bioregulators are given either as a microgram-range intramuscular or subcutaneous injection or as an oral "lingual" (sublingual) capsule.
keyPoint: Crystagen is a synthetic immune peptide bioregulator from the Khavinson family of ultra-short peptides.

### compound | crystagen/safety | What are the risks of Crystagen?
kind: safety
title: Crystagen: source-listed risks
summary: Source-listed risks only. Missing human safety data does not mean a compound is safe.
keyPoint: Source-listed risks only.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: Crystagen
  connectedTo: Crystagen
  *: Mild flu-like symptoms in first cycle days - the most commonly reported adverse effect; as NK cells, T-cells, and macrophages are activated and cytokine production normalizes, a transient systemic immune activation response manifests as mild fatigue, myalgia, and low-grade temperature elevation; typically resolves. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Mild lymph node awareness or tenderness - regional lymph node activation as lymphocyte proliferation and immune cell trafficking increases; benign; typically self-limiting within the first week. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Mild fatigue - related to the metabolic demand of immune system activation; most pronounced in the first 3-5 days of a new cycle. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Fasting requirement compliance challenge - unlike most Khavinson compounds, Crystagen requires a fasted state at bedtime; subjects who eat late or have acid reflux conditions that worsen with fasting may find this administration requirement difficult. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Transient worsening of subclinical autoimmune manifestations - subjects with undiagnosed autoimmune predisposition may experience a mild flare of previously subclinical autoimmune symptoms as immune surveillance and reactivity are restored; warrants discontinuation and evaluation if it occurs. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Mild skin changes - as NK cell and T-cell surveillance improves, some subjects with chronic viral skin manifestations (subclinical herpes, HPV-related) may notice transient flares as the immune system engages these previously tolerated infections more actively. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Mild fever on initiation (rare) - a small minority reports low-grade fever (< 38.0°C) in the first 1-2 days; a sign of immune activation rather than infection; resolves spontaneously without intervention. [source-listed source severity]
  *: No serious immune adverse events documented in the Khavinson literature at standard protocol doses - Crystagen's safety profile in the aging and immunosenescence research cohorts is clean at standard doses; the most practically significant safety dimension is the autoimmune and transplant contraindication. [source-listed source severity]

### compound | crystagen/evidence | What research is listed for Crystagen?
kind: evidence
title: Crystagen: research listed by the sources
summary: Direct human safety data for Crystagen are very limited; most safety information is extrapolated from small Russian studies of related cytogen and Thymalin preparations, and long-term outcomes are unknown [7].; Injection-site reactions (transient redness, swelling, soreness, or bruising) are the most likely adverse effects with subcutaneous or intramuscular administration.; Self-reconstitution and self-injection carry sterility and contamination risks; non-sterile technique can cause local or systemic infection and abscess formation.; Hypersensitivity or allergic reactions to the peptide or to diluent components (for example benzyl alcohol preservative in bacteriostatic water) are possible; discontinue if rash, itching, or swelling occurs.; Because the proposed action is immune modulation, theoretical risks include unwanted immune activation; caution is warranted in autoimmune disease, active malignancy, organ transplant, or with immunosuppressant therapy, where effects are unstudied.; Drug-interaction data are essentially absent; combining Crystagen with other immunomodulators, Peptide University labels its records as aggregated from empirical research and anecdotal community data. This record is retained as supplied and is not upgraded to clinical evidence.

section: Evidence strength
  -: PeptideDosage.org: Human clinical research; population: Human; Human evidence with design limitations to check. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: Peptide University Codex: Source summary; study design not clearly stated; population: Not clearly stated; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Limitations
  -: Crystagen is a synthetic immune peptide bioregulator from the Khavinson family of ultra-short peptides. It is built on the tripeptide sequence Glu-Asp-Pro (EDP, molecular weight ~359 Da) and is sometimes catalogued as "Immune cytogen EDP."
  -: Active autoimmune disease - the broad and intense peripheral immune activation mechanism of Crystagen is directly contraindicated in any autoimmune condition where immune activation amplifies the self-reactive immune response; this includes rheumatoid arthritis, systemic lupus erythematosus, multiple sclerosis,
  -: Organ transplant recipients on immunosuppressive therapy - Crystagen's NK cell activation, T-cell normalization, and broad immune competence restoration directly opposes the immunosuppressive regimen required to prevent rejection; absolute contraindication.
  -: Concurrent biologic immunosuppressive therapy (TNF-alpha inhibitors, IL-6 inhibitors, IL-17 inhibitors, JAK inhibitors) - Crystagen's immune activation mechanism conflicts with the intended immunosuppressive mechanism of these biologics.
  -: Active hematological malignancies involving lymphoid lineages (lymphoma, CLL, T-cell malignancies) - NK cell activation, T-cell normalization, and B-cell stimulation in the context of malignant lymphoid clonal expansion requires oncological evaluation.
  -: Known hypersensitivity to Crystagen (Lys-Glu-Asp tripeptide) or formulation excipients.
  -: Active severe infection requiring antimicrobial management - Crystagen's immune activation during acute severe infection could dysregulate the already activated innate immune response.
  -: Pregnancy - broad immune system modulation during pregnancy, where maternal immune tolerance of the semi-allogeneic fetus is critically maintained, has not been evaluated and carries theoretical risks to the maternal-fetal immune interface.
  -: Pediatric subjects with normally functioning immune systems - intense immune bioregulator stimulation in subjects with fully competent immune function has no established therapeutic target and could produce immune hyperactivation.
  *: Source rating: 2 out of 5, limited evidence

### compound | ct388/overview | What is CT-388?
kind: overview
title: CT-388
summary: A dual GLP-1/GIP receptor agonist (INN enicepatide; also RO7795068) acquired by Roche through the $2.7 billion Carmot Therapeutics acquisition in 2024. The published Phase 1 trial (NCT04838405) showed 4.7-8.0% mean weight loss vs 0.5% placebo over 4 weeks; a more widely reported ~18.8% placebo-adjusted figure at 24 weeks comes from an unpublished Phase 1 extension reported via press release. Phase 2 obesity and T2D trials are completed or ongoing and Phase 3 began in 2026, positioning it as a competitive obesity therapeutic with a mechanism similar to tirzepatide.
keyPoint: A dual GLP-1/GIP receptor agonist (INN enicepatide; also RO7795068) acquired by Roche through the $2.7 billion Carmot Therapeutics acquisition in 2024.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: CT-388
  connectedTo: CT-388
section: Why it is researched
  -: A dual GLP-1/GIP receptor agonist (INN enicepatide; also RO7795068) acquired by Roche through the $2.7 billion Carmot Therapeutics acquisition in 2024.
section: How it works in the research
  -: CT-388 activates two hormone receptors simultaneously to reduce appetite and improve metabolism: GLP-1 Receptor Signals fullness to the brain, slows stomach emptying , and enhances glucose-dependent insulin release from the pancreas.
section: Evidence strength

section: Main limitations

### compound | ct388/evidence | What research is listed for CT-388?
kind: evidence
title: CT-388: research listed by the sources
summary: Moderate evidence; 6 human studies listed Gastrointestinal effects were the most common adverse events and a class effect of incretin agonists: in the Phase 1 multiple-dose cohorts, GI-related events affected about 83% of CT-388 participants, most often decreased appetite (reported in 100% of CT-388 recipients), nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea; events were generally mild to moderate and transient [1].; Slow titration is used specifically to limit nausea and vomiting; one Phase 1 single-dose participant experienced moderate intractable vomiting considered probably related to study drug, underscoring the importance of dose escalation [1].; Transient increases in heart rate were observed, consistent with the mechanism of action, without clinically significant abnormal heart-rate values; modest decreases in systolic blood pressure also occurred [1].; Decreased appetite and reduced food intake can lead to dehydration or inadequate nutrient and protein intake if fluids and protein are not maintained during titration, a recognized concern across the GLP-1/GIP class.; As with other incretin therapies, class-level risks such as

Unlike all currently approved GLP-1 receptor agonists which are injectable peptides (or oral peptide formulations like oral semaglutide requiring the SNAC absorption enhancer), danuglipron is a true small molecule that can be manufactured using standard pharmaceutical chemistry at potentially much lower cost than peptide-based therapies.

### compound | dapiglutide/overview | What is Dapiglutide?
kind: overview
title: Dapiglutide
summary: Dapiglutide (development code ZP 7570) is an investigational, first-in-class dual GLP-1 receptor and GLP-2 receptor agonist developed by Zealand Pharma for obesity and its inflammation-related comorbidities. Structurally it is a 33-amino-acid peptide carrying a C18 fatty-acyl chain that drives reversible albumin binding and extends the terminal half-life to roughly 123-129 hours (about five days), enabling once-weekly subcutaneous dosing. It is engineered to be roughly three times more selective for the GLP-1 receptor than the GLP-2 receptor: the GLP-1 arm suppresses appetite and slows gastric emptying to drive weight loss, while the GLP-2 arm improves intestinal barrier function and dampens low-grade inflammation.
keyPoint: Dapiglutide (development code ZP 7570) is an investigational, first-in-class dual GLP-1 receptor and GLP-2 receptor agonist developed by Zealand Pharma for obesity and its inflammation-related comorbidities.

### compound | dapiglutide/evidence | What research is listed for Dapiglutide?
kind: evidence
title: Dapiglutide: research listed by the sources
summary: Gastrointestinal events were the most common adverse effects across all trials, with nausea and vomiting predominating and generally dose-related; they were mostly mild-to-moderate, and only two participants in the 28-week Phase 1b trial discontinued for adverse events [2][3].; Anti-drug (anti-dapiglutide) antibodies were detected in approximately 14% of participants in the multiple-ascending-dose study; no clear loss of pharmacologic effect was attributed to them, but immunogenicity remains under evaluation [3].; Mild injection-site reactions (erythema, induration) were reported in a small number of participants; rotating subcutaneous sites between the abdomen, thigh and upper arm reduces incidence [2].; Chronic GLP-2 receptor agonism is intestinotrophic; because exogenous GLP-2 has promoted colonic adenoma growth in rodent models, the long-term risk of intestinal polyps or neoplasia with prolonged dosing is a recognized theoretical concern not yet resolved in humans [5].; As a GLP-1 receptor agonist, dapiglutide carries the class-associated cautions of the incretin family -

### compound | decapeptide12/overview | What is Decapeptide-12?
kind: overview
title: Decapeptide-12
summary: Decapeptide-12 (trade name Lumixyl) is a synthetic decapeptide (Tyr-Arg-Ser-Arg-Lys-Tyr-Ser-Ser-Trp-Tyr; YRSRKYSSWY, ~1,395 Da) in the class of cosmetic tyrosinase-inhibiting, skin-brightening peptides. Identified through a peptide-library screen by Abu Ubeid, Hantash and colleagues, it competitively inhibits tyrosinase, the rate-limiting enzyme of melanin synthesis, with roughly 17-fold greater in-vitro potency than hydroquinone and without the melanocyte cytotoxicity that hydroquinone causes [1]. Clinically it is used as a 0.01% (100 ppm) topical cream, and the headline Decapeptide-12 dosage is one application twice daily to pigmented areas, typically alongside a buffered glycolic-acid lotion and broad-spectrum sunscreen [3][5]. Open-label studies report progressive lightening of melasma (mean MASI reductions reaching about 60% at 16 weeks), post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation, and photodamage, with excellent tolerability and no reported adverse events [4][5][6].
keyPoint: Decapeptide-12 (trade name Lumixyl) is a synthetic decapeptide (Tyr-Arg-Ser-Arg-Lys-Tyr-Ser-Ser-Trp-Tyr; YRSRKYSSWY, ~1,395 Da) in the class of cosmetic tyrosinase-inhibiting, skin-brightening peptides.

title: Decapeptide-12: research listed by the sources
summary: In open-label clinical studies the 0.01% decapeptide-12 cream was non-irritating and well tolerated, with no peptide-attributable adverse events reported across photodamage and melasma trials [3][4][5].; Most stinging, transient erythema, dryness or peeling seen with Lumixyl regimens is attributable to the accompanying 20% buffered glycolic-acid lotion rather than to the peptide itself; reducing glycolic-acid frequency usually resolves it [3][5].; As with any topical peptide, allergic contact dermatitis or sensitization is theoretically possible; a patch test before full-face use is prudent, especially in sensitive or reactive skin.; Decapeptide-12 is not a sunscreen and does not prevent new pigment formation from UV exposure; daily broad-spectrum photoprotection is required or melasma and post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation will recur or worsen [5].; Because the native peptide is hydrophilic and large (~1,395 Da), passive skin penetration is limited; results can be slow or modest without delivery enhancement (exfoliation, palmitoylation, microneedles, or in-office dermalinfusion) Split-face studies: significant improvement in melasma and post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation at 12-16 weeks Non-irritating - suitable for sensitive skin and post-procedure use Compatible with retinoids, chemical peels, and laser treatments [ 1 ] [ 2 ] [ 3 ] ↑ 1.0 1.1 Abu Ubeid A, et al. ### compound | defensins/evidence | What research is listed for Defensins?
kind: evidence
title: Defensins: research listed by the sources
summary: Animal/cell evidence only Endogenous family of antimicrobial peptides. Synthetic defensin analogues are in early development; not currently a licensed UK medicine for any indication. Human evidence grade E, Theoretical / insufficient. Citation quality grade C, Limited human evidence. The rise of antibiotic-resistant bacteria poses one of the most urgent threats to modern medicine. Conventional antibiotics are losing ground against pathogens that evolve faster than drug development pipelines can adapt. Defensins represent an ancient, evolutionarily refined defense system that mammals have used for millions of years to combat infection. These small, cysteine-rich peptides are produced by neutrophils, Paneth cells, and epithelial cells throughout the body. They kill bacteria, fungi, and enveloped viruses by disrupting membranes, inhibiting cell wall synthesis, and interfering with microbial metabolism. Unlike conventional antibiotics, defensins also modulate immune responses, recruit immune cells, shape the gut microbiome, and promote wound healing. The rise of antibiotic-resistant bacteria has renewed interest in defensins as potential therapeutic agents. Their broad-spectrum activity, low propensity for resistance development, and multifunctional immune effects make them attractive alternatives to failing antibiotics.
keyPoint: Animal/cell evidence only Endogenous family of antimicrobial peptides.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: Defensins
  connectedTo: Defensins
section: What the research shows
  -: Peptide Authority: A family of antimicrobial peptides forming a crucial part of innate immunity, with activity against bacteria, fungi, and viruses.
  -: PeptideJournal: The rise of antibiotic-resistant bacteria poses one of the most urgent threats to modern medicine.
section: Evidence strength
  -: Peptide Authority: Animal research; population: Human; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: PeptideJournal: Laboratory or mechanistic research; population: Laboratory; Early laboratory evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Limitations
  -: Whether any 'defensin supplement' contains intact defensin peptide.
  -: Whether oral / nasal defensin products produce any meaningful effect.
  -: Long-term consequences of exogenous antimicrobial peptide signalling.
  -: Whether they interact with prescribed antibiotics.
  -: Synthetic defensin development is early-stage; no UK-licensed product.
  -: Pharmacokinetics of any exogenous delivery route in humans absent.
  -: Long-term safety entirely unstudied.
  -: While defensins hold promise, several limitations constrain their immediate therapeutic use.
  -: In Vivo Stability Human defensins show limited stability in vivo due to sensitivity to proteases, osmolarity, and pH .
  -: Serum proteases can degrade defensins, reducing their half-life and effectiveness.
  -: This is particularly problematic for systemic applications where defensins would be exposed to blood for extended periods.
  -: Toxicity to Host Cells Defensins target negatively charged membranes, which are characteristic of bacteria but also present to some degree on mammalian cells.
  -: At high concentrations, defensins can disrupt host cell membranes , raising concerns about toxicity, particularly with systemic use.
  -: The therapeutic window - the concentration range where defensins kill pathogens without harming host cells - must be carefully defined for each application.
  -: Salt Sensitivity The antimicrobial activity of many defensins is reduced in high-salt environments.
  *: Source rating: 2 out of 5, limited evidence

### compound | degarelix/safety | What are the risks of Degarelix?
kind: safety
title: Degarelix: source-listed risks
summary: Source-listed risks only. Missing human safety data does not mean a compound is safe.

matchedText: Degarelix
  connectedTo: Degarelix
  *: QT/QTc prolongation may occur with androgen-deprivation therapy; product labeling advises clinical consideration and monitoring. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Injection-site reactions and hypersensitivity reactions are described in FIRMAGON labeling. [source-listed source severity]
  *: PRONOUNCE was terminated early and does not establish cardiovascular superiority of degarelix. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Injection site reactions: Pain, erythema, swelling, induration, and nodule formation at the injection site (40%). Most reactions are mild to moderate and resolve within 1-2 weeks. More common with the loading dose. Hot flashes: 26% incidence (expected consequence of androgen deprivation). Weight gain: 11% incidence. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Injection site reactions (severe): Rare cases of injection site abscess or necrosis. Long QT syndrome: Androgen deprivation therapy may prolong the QT interval. Obtain baseline and periodic ECGs. Osteoporosis: Long-term androgen deprivation increases fracture risk. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Known hypersensitivity to degarelix or any excipient Women and pediatric patients (not indicated) Severe hepatic impairment (not studied). [source-listed source severity]

### compound | degarelix/evidence | What research is listed for Degarelix?
kind: evidence
title: Degarelix: research listed by the sources
summary: strong-human. CS21 provides comparator-specific evidence for rapid testosterone suppression without an initial surge. A short-term cardiovascular safety comparison has limited interpretability, and PRONOUNCE's early termination means it does not show cardiovascular superiority. FIRMAGON labeling remains the source for the represented product's indication, administration, and warnings. CS21 (pivotal phase III): Randomized, open-label trial (n=610) comparing degarelix 240/80 mg and 240/160 mg with leuprolide 7.5 mg in advanced prostate cancer over 12 months. Demonstrated non-inferiority for testosterone suppression. Degarelix achieved faster castration (96% at day 3 vs. 0% for leuprolide) and showed improved PSA progression-free survival in patients with PSA >20 ng/mL (p=0.04). CS28 (extension study): 5-year extension demonstrating maintained efficacy and safety with long-term degarelix treatment. CS30 (cross-over study): Demonstrated that patients switching from leuprolide to degarelix achieved sustained testosterone suppression with lower FSH levels. Meta-analyses: Several meta-analyses suggest potential cardiovascular benefit of GnRH antagonists vs. agonists, though definitive evidence from prospective randomized trials is still emerging. HERO trial (relugolix): While testing a different GnRH antagonist (oral relugolix), this trial provided further evidence supporting the cardiovascular safety advantage of the antagonist mechanism.

### compound | deslorelin/safety | What are the risks of Deslorelin?
kind: safety
title: Deslorelin: source-listed risks
summary: Source-listed risks only. Missing human safety data does not mean a compound is safe.
keyPoint: Source-listed risks only.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: Deslorelin
  connectedTo: Deslorelin
  *: Implant site reactions: Mild swelling, redness, or pain at the injection site (resolves within 1-2 weeks) Initial flare effect: Temporary increase in sex hormones and associated behaviors (1-4 weeks) Weight gain: Modest weight gain observed in some treated animals (similar to surgical castration) Lethargy: Temporary. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Known hypersensitivity to deslorelin or GnRH analogues Use in breeding animals intended for near-term reproduction (temporary infertility) Caution in females with pyometra risk during initial estrogen flare. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Chronic use studies spanning multiple years of repeated implantation in dogs have not identified significant long-term adverse effects. Fertility recovery has been documented even after prolonged suppression, though time to recovery may increase with cumulative duration of treatment. [source-listed source severity]

### compound | desmopressin/overview | What is Desmopressin?
kind: overview
title: Desmopressin
summary: A synthetic vasopressin analogue used in several FDA-approved formulations for conditions including central diabetes insipidus, selected bleeding disorders, primary nocturnal enuresis, and nocturia due to nocturnal polyuria. Approved uses and safety differ by formulation.
keyPoint: A synthetic vasopressin analogue used in several FDA-approved formulations for conditions including central diabetes insipidus, selected bleeding disorders, primary nocturnal enuresis, and nocturia due to nocturnal polyuria.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: Desmopressin
  connectedTo: Desmopressin
section: Why it is researched
  -: A synthetic vasopressin analogue used in several FDA-approved formulations for conditions including central diabetes insipidus, selected bleeding disorders, primary nocturnal enuresis, and nocturia due to nocturnal polyuria.
section: How it works in the research
  -: Desmopressin is a synthetic analogue of arginine vasopressin engineered to provide strong antidiuretic activity with substantially reduced vasopressor activity.
section: Evidence strength
  -: The Peptide Handbook: Human clinical research; population: Human; Human evidence with design limitations to check. 120 human studies listed by the source; 65 animal studies listed by the source
section: Main limitations
  -: Desmopressin can cause severe, potentially life-threatening hyponatremia, including seizures, coma, respiratory arrest, or death
  -: Fluid intake restriction and serum sodium monitoring are important with formulations carrying significant hyponatremia risk
  -: Moderate to severe renal impairment, current or prior hyponatremia, SIADH, polydipsia, and certain interacting drugs or illnesses can substantially increase hyponatremia risk
  followUp: Show the research evidence for Desmopressin

  *: Injectable desmopressin can cause hypotension or hypertension and requires appropriate monitoring in susceptible patients. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Desmopressin can increase thrombosis risk in patients with type IIB von Willebrand disease and is not indicated for that condition. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Severe hypersensitivity reactions can occur. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Dilutional hyponatremia is the most serious adverse effect of desmopressin and can be life-threatening. The mechanism is straightforward: desmopressin causes water retention while patients continue drinking fluids, diluting serum sodium. [source-listed source severity]

### compound | desmopressin/evidence | What research is listed for Desmopressin?
kind: evidence
title: Desmopressin: research listed by the sources
summary: strong-human. Desmopressin has extensive human clinical use across several established indications. Injectable formulations are used for central diabetes insipidus and selected patients with hemophilia A or type 1 von Willebrand disease. Oral tablets are used for central diabetes insipidus and primary nocturnal enuresis, while NOCDURNA is specifically approved for nocturia due to nocturnal polyuria in adults. Hyponatremia and water intoxication are the major safety concerns across formulations and can become severe or life-threatening. Formulation-specific labeling is important because indications, dosing, pharmacokinetics, and risk differ substantially between injectable, oral, nasal, and sublingual products. Dramatic reduction in urine output in diabetes insipidus (central type) Normalization of fluid balance without the pressor effects of vasopressin Prolonged duration of action (hours vs. minutes for native vasopressin) Multiple administration routes allowing flexibility for different clinical scenarios Predictable dose-response relationship enabling individualized therapy Non-blood product alternative for bleeding management in mild hemophilia A and type 1 vWD Avoidance of transfusion-related risks (viral transmission, alloimmunization) Rapid onset of hemostatic effect (30-60 minutes after IV administration) Useful for surgical prophylaxis in patients with mild bleeding disorders Cost-effective compared to plasma-derived or recombinant factor concentrates Mannucci et al.

### compound | dia39c20/overview | What is Dual Regulator (DIA-39-C20)?
kind: overview
title: Dual Regulator (DIA-39-C20)
summary: DIA-39-C20 (Dual Regulator) is a 39-amino acid dual incretin agonist belonging to the Peptide Receptor Modulator Research Series. It simultaneously targets both the GLP-1 receptor (GLP-1R) and the GIP receptor (GIPR), producing synergistic - not merely additive - metabolic effects through co-activation of overlapping downstream signaling pathways. The backbone is engineered from a GIP-based scaffold with Aib substitutions at positions 2 and 13 for DPP-4 resistance, and carries a C20 fatty diacid (eicosanedioyl) side chain via a γ-Glu-2x AEEA linker for albumin binding and extended once-weekly half-life. CAS: 2023788-19-2. Structurally analogous in class to tirzepatide. Once-weekly subcutaneous injection. Key reference literature: Coskun et al. (Cell Metabolism 2022) - LY3437943 triple receptor agonist, discovery to clinical proof; Urva et al. (Lancet 2022) - Phase 1b multiple-ascending dose trial; Jastreboff et al.
keyPoint: DIA-39-C20 (Dual Regulator) is a 39-amino acid dual incretin agonist belonging to the Peptide Receptor Modulator Research Series.

  *: Resolved: site-listed dose ranges. Published study protocols with species, route, population, frequency and duration take priority. Uncited commercial ranges remain labelled and secondary. A product or calculator range is not evidence that a dose was studied, effective or safe. Confidence: high.
  *: Resolved: modelled administration routes. Use only the route stated in the original study or official product information. Do not convert an oral, intranasal, intramuscular or investigational product into a generic subcutaneous vial protocol. PeptideDosage.org applies a common reconstitution and syringe format even to products such as Ventfort that it identifies as oral. That format is not evidence that the modelled route was studied or is suitable. Confidence: high.
  *: Resolved: mental-health citation identity. Exclude three unrelated PubMed identifiers copied under Semax, NAC and Selank claims. Keep only links whose NCBI record matches the stated research subject. NCBI identifies PMID 11157505 as a Hodgkin-disease cell-fusion paper, PMID 16640009 as a Freeman-Sheldon syndrome case report, and PMID 18677858 as a neonatal-mortality paper. None supports the peptide claim beside which it appeared. Confidence: high.

### compound | dihexa/overview | What is Dihexa?
kind: overview
title: Dihexa
summary: An angiotensin IV analog developed by Washington State University researchers, claimed to enhance cognition through HGF/c-Met signaling. Gained attention for extreme potency claims (10 million times more potent than BDNF), but evidence is limited to rodent studies from a single research group with no human clinical trials. Sold as a research chemical with unknown safety profile.
keyPoint: An angiotensin IV analog developed by Washington State University researchers, claimed to enhance cognition through HGF/c-Met signaling.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: Dihexa
  connectedTo: Dihexa
section: Why it is researched
  -: An angiotensin IV analog developed by Washington State University researchers, claimed to enhance cognition through HGF/c-Met signaling.
section: How it works in the research
  -: Dihexa is theorized to act as a cognitive enhancer through HGF/c-Met pathway modulation: HGF Potentiation Proposed to enhance hepatocyte growth factor binding to c-Met receptor, amplifying downstream neurotrophic signaling.
section: Evidence strength
  -: Peptide Authority: Animal research; population: Human; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Main limitations
  -: Whether a UK-purchased product contains Dihexa at the labelled concentration.
  -: Whether oral or sublingual administration produces meaningful CNS exposure.
  -: What the cancer risk is from sustained c-Met agonism in any age group.

matchedText: Dihexa
  connectedTo: Dihexa
  *: Very limited human safety data - experimental [high source severity]
  *: Theoretical cancer risk (HGF/MET pathway) [high source severity]
  *: Long half-life - effects persist long after dosing [med source severity]

kind: evidence
title: Dihexa: research listed by the sources
summary: Animal data only. No published human trials. Highly experimental. CRITICAL: The two foundational Dihexa papers (Kawas 2012, Benoist 2014, J Pharmacol Exp Ther) were retracted in April 2025 due to data fabrication by a co-author. The 7-million-times-BDNF claim originated from these retracted papers.
keyPoint: Animal data only.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: Dihexa
  connectedTo: Dihexa
section: What the research shows
  -: PepCodex: An angiotensin IV analog developed by Washington State University researchers, claimed to enhance cognition through HGF/c-Met signaling.
  -: The Peptide Handbook: A synthetic peptide designed to penetrate the blood-brain barrier and activate the HGF/c-Met signaling pathway, which promotes synapse formation between neurons.
  -: Peptpedia: Potentiates HGF at c-Met, driving synaptogenesis at picomolar doses - but has no published human trials.
  -: Peptide Hub: Dihexa (also known as PNB-0408) is a synthetic angiotensin IV-derived heptapeptide studied primarily for its synaptogenic properties - its ability to stimulate the formation of new synaptic connections in the brain.
  -: PeptideDosage.org: Dihexa (PNB-0408; N-hexanoic-Tyr-Ile-(6)-aminohexanoic amide) is a synthetic, orally active peptidomimetic in the angiotensin IV-derived hepatocyte growth factor (HGF)/c-Met nootropic class, engineered at Washington State University to be metabolically stable and blood-brain-barrier permeable.
section: Evidence strength
  -: PepCodex: Source summary; study design not clearly stated; population: Not clearly stated; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.

  -: Peptpedia: Source summary; study design not clearly stated; population: Not clearly stated; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.

section: Limitations
  -: The source does not clearly state the study population or design in PEARL's reviewed record.
  -: Extremely long half-life makes overconsumption difficult to reverse; pro-oncogenic via HGF/c-Met pathway (c-Met is a known oncogene); insufficient human safety data
  -: no published human trials.
  -: no human trials of any kind have been published, and its long-term safety is entirely unknown.

  -: No formal half-life measurement has been published.

  -: Dihexa (PNB-0408; N-hexanoic-Tyr-Ile-(6)-aminohexanoic amide) is a synthetic, orally active peptidomimetic in the angiotensin IV-derived hepatocyte growth factor (HGF)/c-Met nootropic class, engineered at Washington State University to be metabolically stable and blood-brain-barrier permeable.
  *: Source rating: 1 out of 5, very limited evidence
  *: The Peptide Handbook: Preclinical only, with no validated human dose. The 2012 HGF/Met development paper and the 2014 HGF/c-Met mechanism paper were formally retracted in 2025. A separate 2013 rat cognition paper remains available, but the overall evidence base is weak and the proposed mechanism is no longer reliable.
  *: Peptide Hub: Protocol-focused educational summary. Linked papers, site-listed ranges and commercial context are retained with source attribution.
  *: PeptideDosage.org: No human safety, toxicology, or pharmacokinetic data exist for Dihexa; every statement about its risk profile is extrapolation, not evidence.[8]; Its proposed target, the HGF/c-Met pathway, is a well-characterized oncogenic signaling axis, raising a theoretical and unstudied risk of promoting tumor growth or spread; no long-term carcinogenicity studies have ever been performed.[1]; The foundational papers describing how Dihexa works were retracted in 2025 after a research-misconduct finding of fabricated data, so even its mechanism of action is now in serious doubt.[4][5]; Community users anecdotally report headaches, irritability or mood changes, sleep disturbance, and brain fog; these reports are uncontrolled and unverified.; Dihexa is poorly water-soluble and is often applied topically in DMSO, a penetration enhancer that carries its own risks of skin irritation and of carrying contaminants through the skin.; As an angiotensin IV-derived molecule, theoretical effects on blood pressure or the renin-angiotensin system cannot be excluded but have not been studied in humans.; Rodent
  *: PeptideDeck: Potent enhancement of synaptic connectivity Improved memory formation and recall in research Promotes new neural connections (synaptogenesis) Potential cognitive protection in neurodegenerative models May reverse cognitive deficits from aging or damage Enhanced learning capacity in animal studies Orally bioavailable (unlike most peptides) Long-lasting effects from single administration Dihexa research has demonstrated remarkable effects in animal models, though human clinical trials are notably absent. The foundational 2013 paper in the Journal of Pharmacology and Experimental Therapeutics demonstrated dihexa's effects in rat models of cognitive impairment. Animals with scopolamine-induced cognitive deficits (a model for dementia) showed complete restoration of performance on memory tasks following dihexa administration. Notably, these effects persisted long after the compound cleared, consistent with structural brain changes. Subsequent research confirmed these findings and extended them to aged animals showing natural cognitive decline.
  *: WikiPep: Preclinical Only : All published data from animal models and in vitro systems No Clinical Trials : No registered human clinical trials as of current date Academic Research : Primarily studied at Washington State University Tool Compound : Used to investigate HGF/c-Met role in neural plasticity and cognition Patent Protected : Covered by multiple patents from WSU research group Oral Administration : Active when given orally in animal studies (key advantage) Subcutaneous : Also administered SC in some research protocols Intranasal : Explored for direct CNS delivery Animal Dosing : Typically 0.5-2 mg/kg in rat studies (oral and SC) Solubility : Soluble in DMSO, with further dilution into aqueous vehicles for in vivo use [ 1 ] [ 2 ] [ 3 ] [ 4 ] [ 5 ] ↑ 1.0 1.1 McCoy AT, et al.   -: PepCodex: A nonapeptide discovered in 1977 that was initially thought to induce delta wave sleep.
  -: The Peptide Handbook: A naturally occurring neuropeptide originally isolated from rabbit blood during deep sleep, studied for its potential effects on sleep architecture and the stress response.
  -: Halflife Labs: DSIP (Delta Sleep-Inducing Peptide) half-life is ~30-40 min IV per Graf & Kastin, Peptides 1986.
  -: Peptpedia: Normalizes sleep architecture rather than sedating - with a 7-8 minute blood half-life but lasting effects.
  -: PeptideDosage.org: DSIP (Delta Sleep-Inducing Peptide) is a naturally occurring nonapeptide (Trp-Ala-Gly-Gly-Asp-Ala-Ser-Gly-Glu) first isolated by Schoenenberger and Monnier in 1977 from the cerebral venous dialysate of rabbits undergoing slow-wave sleep induced by intralaminar thalamic stimulation [1][2].

### compound | dulaglutide/overview | What is Dulaglutide?
kind: overview
title: Dulaglutide
summary: Dulaglutide (Trulicity) is a long-acting glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist developed by Eli Lilly under the code LY2189265 for type 2 diabetes. Unlike small-peptide GLP-1 drugs, it is a recombinant fusion biologic: two modified human GLP-1(7-37) analog chains, each carrying Ala8-to-Gly, Gly22-to-Glu and Arg36-to-Gly substitutions, joined by a peptide linker to a modified human immunoglobulin G4 (IgG4) Fc fragment. This roughly 63 kDa design resists DPP-4 cleavage and exploits neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn) recycling to give an elimination half-life of about 5 days, enabling once-weekly subcutaneous injection. The standard Dulaglutide dosage starts at 0.75 mg once weekly, with a label maintenance dose of 1.5 mg and optional escalation to 3.0 mg and a maximum of 4.5 mg weekly, each step held for at least 4 weeks (AWARD-11).
keyPoint: Dulaglutide (Trulicity) is a long-acting glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist developed by Eli Lilly under the code LY2189265 for type 2 diabetes.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: Dulaglutide
  connectedTo: Dulaglutide
section: Why it is researched
  -: Dulaglutide (Trulicity) is a long-acting glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist developed by Eli Lilly under the code LY2189265 for type 2 diabetes.

  -: Dulaglutide is not a small peptide but a recombinant fusion protein of roughly 63 kDa.

### compound | dulaglutide/mechanism | How does Dulaglutide work?
kind: overview
title: Dulaglutide
summary: Dulaglutide (Trulicity) is a long-acting glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist developed by Eli Lilly under the code LY2189265 for type 2 diabetes. Unlike small-peptide GLP-1 drugs, it is a recombinant fusion biologic: two modified human GLP-1(7-37) analog chains, each carrying Ala8-to-Gly, Gly22-to-Glu and Arg36-to-Gly substitutions, joined by a peptide linker to a modified human immunoglobulin G4 (IgG4) Fc fragment. This roughly 63 kDa design resists DPP-4 cleavage and exploits neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn) recycling to give an elimination half-life of about 5 days, enabling once-weekly subcutaneous injection. The standard Dulaglutide dosage starts at 0.75 mg once weekly, with a label maintenance dose of 1.5 mg and optional escalation to 3.0 mg and a maximum of 4.5 mg weekly, each step held for at least 4 weeks (AWARD-11).
keyPoint: Dulaglutide (Trulicity) is a long-acting glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist developed by Eli Lilly under the code LY2189265 for type 2 diabetes.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high

### compound | dulaglutide/safety | What are the risks of Dulaglutide?
kind: safety
title: Dulaglutide: source-listed risks
summary: Source-listed risks only. Missing human safety data does not mean a compound is safe.
keyPoint: Source-listed risks only.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: Dulaglutide
  connectedTo: Dulaglutide
  *: Dulaglutide's safety profile is well characterized across tens of thousands of patient-years of exposure from the AWARD program, REWIND, and post-marketing surveillance. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Common Side Effects The most frequently reported adverse reactions (occurring in 5% or more of patients) are gastrointestinal: Nausea (12-21%, dose-dependent) Diarrhea (8-12%) Vomiting (6-12%) Abdominal pain (6-9%) Decreased appetite (4-8%) Dyspepsia (4-6%) Fatigue (4-6%) These GI effects are typical of the GLP-1. [source-listed source severity]
  *: They are usually mild to moderate in severity and rarely require discontinuation. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Serious Warnings Dulaglutide carries a boxed warning regarding the risk of thyroid C-cell tumors. [source-listed source severity]
  *: In rodent studies, GLP-1 receptor agonists caused dose-dependent thyroid C-cell tumors, including medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC). [source-listed source severity]
  *: It is unknown whether dulaglutide causes thyroid C-cell tumors in humans. [source-listed source severity]
  *: The drug is contraindicated in patients with a personal or family history of MTC or in patients with Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia syndrome type 2 (MEN 2). [source-listed source severity]
  *: Other serious risks include: Pancreatitis : Acute pancreatitis has been reported. [source-listed source severity]

### compound | dulaglutide/evidence | What research is listed for Dulaglutide?
kind: evidence
title: Dulaglutide: research listed by the sources
summary: Gastrointestinal events are the dominant adverse effects: nausea, diarrhea, vomiting, abdominal pain, dyspepsia and decreased appetite. They are dose-related, usually mild-to-moderate, concentrated during initiation and dose escalation, and tend to subside within 1-2 weeks of a stable dose; in AWARD-11 nausea occurred in roughly 13-16% and vomiting in 6-9% across doses [1][4].; Boxed warning: dulaglutide causes thyroid C-cell (medullary) tumors in rodents. Large randomized human trials include REWIND for cardiovascular outcomes and AWARD-7 in adults with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease.
keyPoint: Gastrointestinal events are the dominant adverse effects: nausea, diarrhea, vomiting, abdominal pain, dyspepsia and decreased appetite.

  *: PeptideDeck: Large randomized human trials include REWIND for cardiovascular outcomes and AWARD-7 in adults with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease.
  *: WikiPep: REWIND trial: The Researching Cardiovascular Events with a Weekly INcretin in Diabetes (REWIND) trial demonstrated a 12% reduction in MACE (cardiovascular death, nonfatal MI, nonfatal stroke) in patients with type 2 diabetes, including those without established cardiovascular disease. This was notably the first GLP-1 RA trial to enroll a majority of patients without established CVD. Stroke reduction: Post-hoc analyses suggested particular benefit in reducing nonfatal stroke events. AWARD program (Assessment of Weekly AdministRation of LY2189265 in Diabetes): Series of 11 phase III trials comparing dulaglutide to placebo, metformin, sitagliptin, exenatide twice daily, insulin glargine, and liraglutide. AWARD-1: Demonstrated superiority over exenatide twice daily in HbA1c reduction. AWARD-6: Non-inferiority to liraglutide 1.8 mg daily; liraglutide showed slightly greater weight loss. REWIND trial: Cardiovascular outcomes trial (n=9,901) over median 5.4 years demonstrating 12% reduction in MACE (HR 0.88; 95% CI, 0.79-0.99). Notable for including 69% of patients without established CVD.
  *: PeptideJournal: Before semaglutide became a household name, dulaglutide was the world's best-selling GLP-1 receptor agonist. Marketed as Trulicity by Eli Lilly, it peaked at $7.4 billion in annual revenue in 2022 and spent years as the go-to weekly injectable for type 2 diabetes.

### compound | dynorphina/evidence | What research is listed for Dynorphin A?
kind: evidence
title: Dynorphin A: research listed by the sources
summary: Pain research: Understanding the transition from acute to chronic pain Addiction studies: Elucidating the role of KOR in withdrawal and relapse Depression research: KOR antagonists as novel antidepressants based on dynorphin/KOR dysfunction in mood disorders Stress biology: Mapping the neuroendocrine stress response Elevated cerebrospinal fluid dynorphin levels have been observed in chronic pain conditions Dynorphin levels may serve as biomarkers for stress-related psychiatric conditions Altered dynorphin expression is associated with neurodegenerative diseases Reconstitution: Dissolve in sterile water or physiological saline; avoid DMSO if possible Stock Concentration: Typically prepared at 1 mM in water Working Concentrations: In vitro assays typically use 0.1 nM to 10 mcM In Vivo Research Doses: Intrathecal administration at 1-30 nmol in rodent studies Route: Intrathecal, intracerebroventricular, or systemic injection in animal models Dysphoria: KOR activation produces aversive states (opposite of mu-opioid euphoria) Sedation: Dose-dependent sedative effects Diuresis: KOR

### compound | ecnoglutide/evidence | What research is listed for Ecnoglutide?
kind: evidence
title: Ecnoglutide: research listed by the sources
summary: Moderate evidence; 6 human studies listed Gastrointestinal effects are the most common adverse events, including nausea, diarrhea, decreased appetite, vomiting and constipation; they are usually mild to moderate, transient, and most frequent during dose escalation [2][3][4].; Asthenia (weakness/fatigue) and reduced appetite are also commonly reported, consistent with the appetite-suppressing action of the GLP-1 class [4].; A minority of participants discontinued for adverse events (roughly 6% in the phase 3 obesity trial); slow, stepwise titration over four-week intervals improves tolerability [3].; Hypoglycemia risk rises when ecnoglutide is combined with insulin or sulfonylureas; because GLP-1 action is glucose-dependent, dose reductions of those background agents may be needed to avoid low blood sugar [2].; GLP-1 receptor agonists as a class carry warnings for acute pancreatitis, gallbladder disease (cholelithiasis/cholecystitis), a modest rise in resting heart rate, and acute kidney injury from dehydration with severe vomiting or diarrhea; patients should stay hydrated and report severe abdominal pain.; As with other

### compound | efinopegdutide/overview | What is Efinopegdutide?
kind: overview
title: Efinopegdutide
summary: Efinopegdutide (development codes MK-6024, JNJ-64565111 and HM12525A) is an investigational once-weekly GLP-1/glucagon receptor dual co-agonist originally engineered by Hanmi Pharmaceutical and advanced by Janssen and then Merck for obesity, type 2 diabetes and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH/NASH). It is a long-acting peptide attached to a proprietary flexible linker and immunoglobulin-Fc carrier that extends its terminal half-life to roughly 5 days, supporting subcutaneous once-weekly injection [7]. Mechanistically, the GLP-1 arm suppresses appetite, slows gastric emptying and enhances glucose-dependent insulin secretion, while the glucagon arm raises energy expenditure and drives hepatic fatty-acid oxidation, a combination especially suited to clearing liver fat [1][8]. The most-studied Efinopegdutide dosage is 5, 7.4 or 10 mg subcutaneously once weekly, with 10 mg the target dose reached after an 8-week titration in the liver-disease program [1][2][3].

title: Efinopegdutide: research listed by the sources
summary: Gastrointestinal effects are the dominant and dose-related adverse events: nausea, vomiting, diarrhea and decreased appetite. Overall GI adverse-event rates ranged from about 71% at lower doses up to ~84% at the 10 mg dose, versus ~28% with placebo and ~60% with liraglutide, and were concentrated during titration [2].; Because the glucagon-receptor arm can raise hepatic glucose output, efinopegdutide did not improve HbA1c in type 2 diabetes and could transiently raise blood glucose; people with diabetes should have glucose monitored and not assume a glycemic benefit [3].; Like other incretin agents, it can modestly increase resting heart rate and cause early satiety; dehydration from vomiting or diarrhea can occur, raising a theoretical risk of acute kidney injury if fluid intake is not maintained.; Injection-site reactions (redness, itching, nodules) can occur with subcutaneous dosing; rotating sites between the abdomen, thigh and upper arm reduces local irritation.; As a GLP-1 receptor agonist class effect, it carries the standard cautions around pancreatitis and gallbladder Published randomized human phase 2 studies and registered trials. The strongest completed NAFLD study compared efinopegdutide 10 mg with semaglutide 1 mg over 24 weeks after titration.

section: Limitations
  -: Efinopegdutide (development codes MK-6024, JNJ-64565111 and HM12525A) is an investigational once-weekly GLP-1/glucagon receptor dual co-agonist originally engineered by Hanmi Pharmaceutical and advanced by Janssen and then Merck for obesity, type 2 diabetes and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis
  -: Investigational; study arms are not an approved general-use schedule.
  -: Gastrointestinal adverse events were common and some diabetes-study measures did not improve.
  -: The reviewed record does not state a specific limitation. The linked paper still needs to be checked for design, size and bias.

### compound | efocipegtrutide/overview | What is Efocipegtrutide?
kind: overview
title: Efocipegtrutide
summary: Efocipegtrutide (HM15211, "LAPS Triple Agonist") is an investigational long-acting peptide that simultaneously activates the GLP-1, GIP, and glucagon receptors, engineered by Hanmi Pharmaceutical using its LAPScovery platform, which conjugates the active peptide to a human IgG4-derived aglycosylated Fc fragment through a non-peptidyl flexible linker [5][7]. That Fc moiety preserves pH-dependent FcRn recycling, which extends the molecule's terminal half-life enough to support once-weekly subcutaneous dosing [3][5]. The headline Efocipegtrutide dosage studied in the Phase 2 biopsy-confirmed NASH/MASH program (NCT04505436, HM-TRIA-201) is 2 mg, 4 mg, or 6 mg by subcutaneous injection once weekly, given as fixed parallel-dose arms without titration [1][2].

### compound | efocipegtrutide/evidence | What research is listed for Efocipegtrutide?
kind: evidence
title: Efocipegtrutide: research listed by the sources
summary: Gastrointestinal effects (nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, decreased appetite) are the most common class effects of GLP-1/GIP/glucagon agonists and increased in a dose-dependent manner in the Efocipegtrutide single-ascending-dose study, especially at higher cohorts [3].; Nervous-system adverse events (e.g., headache, dizziness) were also reported as dose-dependent in early-phase dosing and may overlap with GI symptoms during dose escalation [3].; The glucagon-receptor component can raise hepatic glucose output and energy expenditure; glucose, heart rate, and blood pressure are monitored in trials, and the long-term metabolic impact of sustained glucagon agonism in humans is not fully characterized [5][6].; As a subcutaneous injectable, it can cause injection-site reactions (redness, itching, transient nodules); rotating abdominal injection sites helps limit local irritation.; GLP-1-class agents carry warnings for pancreatitis, gallbladder events, and (in rodent studies of related drugs) thyroid C-cell effects; these have not been specifically established or excluded for Efocipegtrutide

kind: overview
title: Efruxifermin
summary: From Wikipep - The Peptide Encyclopedia Efruxifermin Chemical name Efruxifermin (EFX / AKR-001) Molecular formula Fc-FGF21 fusion protein Molecular weight ~80,000 g/mol (Fc fusion homodimer) CAS number Not assigned (biologic) Sequence Human IgG1 Fc domain fused to modified FGF21 (N-terminal Fc, C-terminal FGF21) Length Biologic fusion protein Source Synthetic (Akero Therapeutics) Half-life ~3-3.5 days Targets FGFR1c/β-Klotho complex (same as native FGF-21) Bioavailability Subcutaneous injection (once weekly) Legal status FDA Breakthrough Therapy Designation (NASH/MASH); Phase 2b/3 Efruxifermin ( EFX , formerly AKR-001 ) is an Fc-FGF21 fusion protein developed by Akero Therapeutics as a long-acting FGF-21 analog for the treatment of non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH/MASH). By fusing the Fc domain of human IgG1 to a modified FGF-21, efruxifermin achieves a half-life of ~3-3.5 days (vs ~1-2 hours for native FGF-21), enabling once-weekly subcutaneous dosing.

### compound | egf/overview | What is EGF?
kind: overview
title: EGF
summary: EGF (epidermal growth factor) is a single-chain, 53-amino-acid, roughly 6 kDa signaling polypeptide first isolated by Stanley Cohen, whose work earned the 1986 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine [1]. It is the prototype ligand of the epidermal growth factor family and drives wound healing and skin regeneration by binding the EGF receptor (EGFR/ErbB1) tyrosine kinase, switching on the PI3K/AKT and MAPK/ERK pathways that stimulate keratinocyte and fibroblast proliferation, migration and re-epithelialization [6]. The best-validated clinical EGF dosage comes from Heberprot-P, a Cuban recombinant human EGF product infiltrated intralesionally at 75 mcg three times per week into advanced diabetic foot ulcers until the wound closes [2][3][4]. In cosmetic and dermatologic use, EGF is applied topically at roughly 10-50 mcg/mL (about 1-5 ppm) for photoaging, wrinkles and post-procedure recovery [6][7].
keyPoint: EGF (epidermal growth factor) is a single-chain, 53-amino-acid, roughly 6 kDa signaling polypeptide first isolated by Stanley Cohen, whose work earned the 1986 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine [1].

method: canonical

summary: In the intralesional diabetic-foot-ulcer trials, the most frequent adverse events were tremors (around 55%), chills (around 40%), pain and a burning sensation at the injection site (around 25% each), and local infection (around 20%), with less common weakness, fever, headache and transient hypotension [3][4].; Local injection reactions (pain, erythema, odor and burning at the infiltration site) are expected with intralesional dosing; the procedure is performed under medical supervision with wound debridement and infection control.; Topical cosmetic EGF is generally well tolerated; the most common effects are transient erythema or irritation, and micro-spicule or microneedle delivery systems can cause short-lived redness at the application site [8].; Because EGFR is overexpressed in many epithelial cancers and EGF stimulates cell proliferation, EGF should not be applied to or injected near undiagnosed, suspicious or malignant lesions; although reviews report no evidence that topical rhEGF stimulates cancer-cell proliferation, EGF is best avoided in people with active malignancy or [ 1 ] [ 2 ] [ 3 ] ↑ 1.0 1.1 Cohen S. ### compound | eloralintide/overview | What is Eloralintide?
kind: overview
title: Eloralintide
summary: Eloralintide (development code LY3841136) is an investigational long-acting amylin receptor agonist developed by Eli Lilly for chronic weight management in obesity and overweight. It is a 37-amino-acid synthetic amylin analog engineered with three non-coded amino-acid residues, a methylene-thioacetal bridge that replaces native amylin's labile disulfide bond, and a C20 fatty-diacid chain conjugated at lysine-26 that drives reversible albumin binding and an exceptionally long elimination half-life of roughly 13 to 15 days. Mechanistically it is a selective full agonist of the human amylin-1 receptor (AMY1R), about 11- to 12-fold more potent at AMY1R than at the calcitonin receptor or AMY3R, a profile intended to reproduce amylin's satiety, gastric-emptying and glucagon-suppressing actions while limiting off-target receptor engagement.
keyPoint: Eloralintide (development code LY3841136) is an investigational long-acting amylin receptor agonist developed by Eli Lilly for chronic weight management in obesity and overweight.

### compound | eloralintide/mechanism | How does Eloralintide work?

title: Eloralintide

  *: Nausea - the most common adverse event in Phase 2; highly dose-dependent, ranging from 11% at 1mg to 64% at 6mg (fixed dose without titration) versus 14% in placebo; the Phase 2 escalation arms (3→9mg and 6→9mg) produced lower nausea rates than the fixed 6mg and 9mg arms, confirming that gradual titration. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Fatigue and asthenia - dose-dependent; 0% at 1mg to 46% at 9mg in Phase 2 versus 12% placebo; related to both central AMY1R CNS effects and the metabolic consequences of rapid weight loss; typically most pronounced in the first 4-8 weeks of each dose escalation step and attenuates with continued dosing. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Decreased appetite - the intended pharmacological effect; reported as an adverse event in 19% of Phase 1 subjects (11% in Phase 1b at doses up to 12mg); reflects the appetite suppression mechanism that drives the weight loss benefit; classified as adverse only in subjects who found the degree of appetite reduction. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Headache - reported in 12% of Phase 1b subjects overall; more common at higher dose levels (6mg and 12mg); mechanism unclear; typically mild and transient; attenuates with dose stabilization. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Pulse rate reduction - a notable and dose-dependent pharmacodynamic effect: mean decreases from baseline of −7.1 bpm at 3mg, −8.3 bpm at 6mg, and −14.4 bpm at 12mg in Phase 1b; the mechanism reflects AMY1R-mediated cardiac chronotropic modulation; no symptomatic bradycardia was reported in Phase 1 or Phase 2 trials at. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Injection site reactions - dose-dependent; injection site pain, erythema, and edema more common at 3mg and above; typically mild; the slow subcutaneous absorption profile (slow tmax, flat concentration curve) means the injection depot persists longer than short-half-life peptides, which may contribute to the injection. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Diarrhea - reported in approximately 10% of Phase 1b subjects; more common at higher doses (12mg: 11.1%); typically mild. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Vomiting - reported in approximately 4% of Phase 1b subjects and up to 8.3% at 12mg; less common than nausea; dose-dependent; managed by dose reduction and gradual titration. [source-listed source severity]

### compound | eloralintide/evidence | What research is listed for Eloralintide?
kind: evidence
title: Eloralintide: research listed by the sources
summary: Gastrointestinal effects (nausea, vomiting, decreased appetite, constipation or diarrhea) are the most common adverse events and increase with dose; in Phase 2 they were predominantly mild-to-moderate and were reduced by gradual dose escalation, with low-dose arms tracking close to placebo [2][3].; Fatigue was reported more frequently at higher doses in the Phase 2 trial, consistent with the central appetite-suppressing mechanism and reduced energy intake [2][3].; Because amylin agonism slows gastric emptying, early dosing can cause early satiety, bloating and altered absorption of co-administered oral medications, mirroring the class effect characterized for pramlintide [6][7].; Rapid or substantial weight loss of the magnitude seen at higher doses can carry the general risks associated with that class of therapy, including gallbladder events and loss of lean mass; long-term safety of eloralintide specifically has not yet been established beyond 48 weeks [2].; As an injectable peptide, injection-site reactions (redness, itching, transient nodules) are possible; rotating sites and Peptide University labels its records as aggregated from empirical research and anecdotal community data. This record is retained as supplied and is not upgraded to clinical evidence.

section: Limitations
  -: Eloralintide (development code LY3841136) is an investigational long-acting amylin receptor agonist developed by Eli Lilly for chronic weight management in obesity and overweight.
  -: Personal or family history of Medullary Thyroid Carcinoma (MTC) - the theoretical thyroid C-cell tumor risk associated with calcitonin receptor-family agonism applies to this class; although eloralintide's AMY1R selectivity substantially reduces calcitonin receptor activation relative to cagrilintide, residual AMY3R
  -: Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia Type 2 (MEN2) - MEN2 patients have near-universal MTC predisposition; the calcitonin receptor-family class signal warrants avoidance pending definitive eloralintide-specific thyroid safety data from Phase 3.
  -: Type 1 or Type 2 diabetes - excluded from all eloralintide clinical trials to date; the amylin receptor-mediated glucagon suppression in the context of existing diabetes management (particularly insulin therapy) carries hypoglycemia risk; the glycemic effects of eloralintide in dysglycemic populations have not been
  -: Concurrent insulin therapy - the amylin class carries a precedent for severe hypoglycemia when co-administered with insulin, established by the FDA boxed warning on pramlintide (Symlin); eloralintide's amylin receptor agonism in the context of insulin-dependent subjects carries this class-level hypoglycemia risk.
  -: Concurrent insulin secretagogues (sulfonylureas, meglitinides) - increased hypoglycemia risk from the combination of enhanced glucose-dependent insulin secretion amplification and amylin receptor-mediated appetite/caloric suppression.
  -: Concurrent use of other amylin receptor agonists (cagrilintide, pramlintide, petrelintide) or CagriSema - redundant amylin receptor loading produces additive adverse effects without additional therapeutic benefit; CagriSema already contains cagrilintide as the amylin component.
  -: Pre-existing gastroparesis - while eloralintide's Phase 1 data suggests the gastric emptying delay may be transient rather than sustained, the initial gastric motility effect at cycle initiation in subjects with pre-existing gastroparesis warrants caution; this contraindication may be revised as Phase 3 gastric
  -: Chronic heart disease, hepatic impairment, or renal impairment - excluded from Phase 1 and Phase 2 trials; pharmacokinetics and safety in these populations have not been characterized.

### compound | endoluten/evidence | What research is listed for Endoluten?

title: Endoluten: research listed by the sources
summary: Peptide University labels its records as aggregated from empirical research and anecdotal community data. This record is retained as supplied and is not upgraded to clinical evidence.

matchedText: Endoluten
  connectedTo: Endoluten
section: What the research shows
  -: PepCodex: A cytamin-class peptide supplement derived from pineal gland tissue, part of the Russian bioregulator framework.
  -: Peptide University Codex: Endoluten is a Khavinson cytomedin - peptide complex A-8 - extracted from the pineal gland tissue of young animals, and widely regarded as the most foundational oral bioregulator in the Khavinson longevity framework.
section: Evidence strength
  -: PepCodex: Source summary; study design not clearly stated; population: Not clearly stated; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: Peptide University Codex: Source summary; study design not clearly stated; population: Animal; Preclinical animal evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Limitations
  -: The source does not clearly state the study population or design in PEARL's reviewed record.
  -: Hormone-sensitive cancers with melatonin receptor expression - pineal gland peptides and melatonin have complex relationships with certain hormone-sensitive tumors; subjects with active breast cancer, melanoma, or other melatonin receptor-expressing tumors should obtain oncological evaluation before initiating.
  -: Autoimmune conditions requiring strict immune suppression - melatonin has direct thymopoietic and immunostimulatory effects; Endoluten's melatonin-normalizing mechanism could stimulate immune activity in subjects requiring immunosuppression for autoimmune disease management.
  -: Concurrent high-dose exogenous melatonin supplementation - Endoluten normalizes endogenous melatonin synthesis; combining with high-dose exogenous melatonin creates an uncharacterized additive effect on circadian amplitude and receptor sensitivity.
  -: Known hypersensitivity to Endoluten (pineal gland tissue cytomedin peptide complex A-8) or formulation excipients including gelatin.
  -: Pregnancy - pineal-regulated circadian and neuroendocrine programs during pregnancy involve specific gestational adaptations; exogenous pineal bioregulator activity has not been evaluated in this context.
  -: Active endocrine tumors (pituitary adenoma, carcinoid, pheochromocytoma) - Endoluten's neuroendocrine axis modulation in the context of active endocrine hypersecretion requires endocrinological evaluation.
  -: Severe active depression or bipolar disorder in manic phase - circadian rhythm disruption is both a feature and driver of mood disorders; Endoluten's circadian normalization activity in subjects with active psychiatric circadian dysregulation requires psychiatric supervision.
  *: Source rating: 1 out of 5, very limited evidence
  *: Peptide University Codex: Peptide University labels its records as aggregated from empirical research and anecdotal community data. This record is retained as supplied and is not upgraded to clinical evidence.
  *: PMID:1485734 (journal not listed): Open the linked source for the full study design, population and results.

kind: overview

A product or calculator range is not evidence that a dose was studied, effective or safe. Confidence: high.
  *: Resolved: modelled administration routes. Use only the route stated in the original study or official product information. Do not convert an oral, intranasal, intramuscular or investigational product into a generic subcutaneous vial protocol. That format is not evidence that the modelled route was studied or is suitable. Confidence: high.

### compound | endothelin1/evidence | What research is listed for Endothelin-1?
kind: evidence
title: Endothelin-1: research listed by the sources
summary: While ET-1 itself is not used therapeutically, understanding its biology has been essential for: ET-1 is an indispensable research tool for studying: Vascular tone regulation Endothelial function and dysfunction Pulmonary vascular biology Cardiac hypertrophy Renal physiology ET-1 is one of the most widely used peptides in cardiovascular research: Vasoconstriction studies: Standard agonist for studying vascular smooth muscle contraction in wire myography, organ bath, and perfusion experiments Hypertrophy models: Used to induce cardiac myocyte hypertrophy in cell culture (standard in vitro model) Fibrosis research: Induces fibroblast-to-myofibroblast transition for fibrosis studies Pulmonary hypertension: ET-1 models for studying pulmonary vascular remodeling Endothelial function: Studying the balance between ET-1 (constriction) and NO (dilation) Drug development: Screening and characterization of endothelin receptor antagonists In vitro vasoconstriction: 10⁻¹⁰ to 10⁻⁷ M (typically 10⁻⁸ M for maximal contraction) Cardiac hypertrophy (cell culture): 10-100 nM for 24-48 hours In vivo:

### compound | enfuvirtide/overview | What is Enfuvirtide?
kind: overview
title: Enfuvirtide
summary: A prescription HIV-1 fusion-inhibitor peptide used with other antiretroviral medicines in treatment-experienced patients with ongoing viral replication.
keyPoint: A prescription HIV-1 fusion-inhibitor peptide used with other antiretroviral medicines in treatment-experienced patients with ongoing viral replication.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: Enfuvirtide
  connectedTo: Enfuvirtide
section: Why it is researched
  -: A prescription HIV-1 fusion-inhibitor peptide used with other antiretroviral medicines in treatment-experienced patients with ongoing viral replication.
section: How it works in the research
  -: It binds the HIV-1 gp41 envelope protein and prevents fusion of viral and host-cell membranes.
section: Evidence strength
  -: WikiPep: Randomized or controlled human research; population: Human; Direct controlled human evidence. 2 human studies listed by the source
section: Main limitations
  -: It must be used as part of a clinically selected antiretroviral combination.
  -: Resistance history and specialist monitoring determine suitability.
  followUp: Show the research evidence for Enfuvirtide
  followUp: Show the human research studies for Enfuvirtide
  compound: Enfuvirtide

### compound | epitalon/evidence | What research is listed for Epitalon?
kind: evidence
title: Epitalon: research listed by the sources
summary: preliminary. Epitalon has been studied primarily by Vladimir Khavinson's group at the Saint Petersburg Institute of Bioregulation and Gerontology. A verified in-vitro study (Khavinson et al., 2003) demonstrated telomerase activation and telomere elongation in human somatic cells - this is the primary verified mechanistic finding in this record. Claims regarding lifespan extension in aged rodents, melatonin normalization in aging pineal glands, and reduced tumor incidence were previously cited in this record, but the associated PubMed identifiers could not be verified as correct entities and have been removed. Small human observational studies have been published within the Khavinson group, but source identifiers for those studies are not verified in this record. Independent replication by groups outside the Khavinson laboratory is very limited. Overall evidence remains preliminary. Animal Study + limited human evidence
keyPoint: preliminary.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: Epitalon
  connectedTo: Epitalon
section: What the research shows
  -: The Peptide Handbook: A synthetic tetrapeptide originally derived from a bovine pineal gland extract, studied for its potential connections to telomere biology, antioxidant activity, and age-related changes in the pineal gland.
  -: Halflife Labs: Epitalon (tetrapeptide Ala-Glu-Asp-Gly) half-life is not established; estimated ~30 min from structural analog data.
  -: PeptideDosage.org: Epitalon (also Epithalon, Epithalamin tetrapeptide) is a synthetic tetrapeptide Ala-Glu-Asp-Gly (AEDG) developed by Vladimir Khavinson by directed synthesis from the amino-acid composition of bovine pineal extract Epithalamin [1][2].
  -: Peptide Authority: A synthetic tetrapeptide based on epithalamin, researched for its potential effects on telomerase activation and biological ageing.
  -: PeptideJournal: Epitalon is a synthetic tetrapeptide that reactivates telomerase to rebuild chromosome caps.
section: Evidence strength
  -: The Peptide Handbook: Human clinical research; population: Human; Human evidence with design limitations to check. 3 human studies listed by the source; 22 animal studies listed by the source
  -: Halflife Labs: Animal research; population: Human; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: PeptideDosage.org: Observational or case-based human research; population: Animal; Limited observational human evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: Peptide Authority: Animal research; population: Human; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: PeptideJournal: Animal research; population: Animal; Preclinical animal evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Limitations
  -: Insufficient long-term human safety data; theoretical concern regarding telomerase activation and cancer cell proliferation
  -: The reviewed record does not state a specific limitation. The linked paper still needs to be checked for design, size and bias.
  -: Epitalon (also Epithalon, Epithalamin tetrapeptide) is a synthetic tetrapeptide Ala-Glu-Asp-Gly (AEDG) developed by Vladimir Khavinson by directed synthesis from the amino-acid composition of bovine pineal extract Epithalamin [1][2].
  -: Whether a UK-purchased vial actually contains Epitalon at the labelled concentration.
  -: Whether telomere lengthening in a Petri dish translates to longevity in humans.
  -: What the cancer risk profile is over decades of intermittent use.
  -: How it interacts with statins, metformin, or other longevity stack drugs.
  -: Most positive human data comes from a single Russian research group.
  -: No independent Western replication of lifespan or telomere findings.
  -: No registered Phase 3 trials anywhere in the world.
  -: Long-term oncologic surveillance does not exist.
  -: Epitalon is fascinating, but intellectual honesty requires laying out where the evidence falls short.
  -: Concentration of Research Most Epitalon research comes from Khavinson's group.
  -: The Alzheimer's Drug Discovery Foundation's Cognitive Vitality review explicitly notes the absence of modern, large randomized controlled trials and the replication limits outside the original group.
  -: Independent work is growing - the 2025 Biogerontology study came from outside the original group - but the field needs more confirmation.
  -: No Large-Scale Western Clinical Trials The human studies are small by modern standards.

  *: Halflife Labs: Animal Study + limited human evidence
  *: PeptideDosage.org: Epitalon is generally well tolerated in Russian clinical and observational use; reported adverse effects are infrequent and mild.; The most common reported effect is transient injection-site discomfort with subcutaneous administration, resolving spontaneously.; Occasional reports of mild fatigue or sleep disturbance during early dosing have been described, possibly reflecting changes in circadian melatonin patterns as the peptide normalizes pineal function.; Mild headache has been reported in a minority of users, generally at higher doses, and typically resolves on dose adjustment.; Theoretical concerns about telomerase activation and oncogenic potential have not been borne out in published rodent or human data; Anisimov's studies actually show reduced spontaneous and induced tumor incidence in Epitalon-treated cohorts.; No tolerance, dependence, or withdrawal phenomena have been documented in chronic dosing protocols.; Hypersensitivity reactions are rare; allergic skin reactions to peptide preparations should prompt discontinuation.; Reproductive, pregnancy, and lactation safety
  *: Peptide Authority: Animal/cell evidence only Not a licensed UK medicine. A short tetrapeptide investigated almost exclusively in Russian studies for telomerase-related anti-ageing endpoints. Findings have not been broadly replicated by independent groups; human evidence is limited. Human evidence grade E, Theoretical / insufficient. Citation quality grade D, Animal/cell evidence only.
