### compound | epitalon-thymalin-combo/evidence | What research is listed for Epitalon + Thymalin Combo?
kind: evidence
title: Epitalon + Thymalin Combo: research listed by the sources
summary: Russian 15-year follow-up study showed 1.8x reduced mortality in treated vs control group.
keyPoint: Russian 15-year follow-up study showed 1.8x reduced mortality in treated vs control group.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: Epitalon + Thymalin Combo
  connectedTo: Epitalon + Thymalin Combo
section: What the research shows
section: Evidence strength
section: Limitations
  *: Source rating: 3 out of 5
  *: Peptides of Pineal Gland and Thymus Prolong Human Life (Neuroendocrinology Letters 2003): In 266 elderly patients followed 6-8 years, annual combined treatment with Epithalamin (pineal) and Thymalin (thymic) reduced mortality 4.1-fold vs controls, with Thymalin alone reducing it 2.0-2.1-fold - the core St. Petersburg Institute combo longevity study.
  *: Peptide Geroprotector from the Pituitary Gland Inhibits Rapid Aging of Elderly People: Results of 15-Year Follow-Up (Bulletin of Experimental Biology and Medicine 2011): In a 15-year follow-up of elderly coronary patients, 6 courses of Epithalamin over 3 years decelerated cardiovascular aging, preserved physical endurance, normalized melatonin circadian rhythm, and produced significantly lower mortality vs controls.

section: Evidence strength
  -: PepCodex: Human clinical research; population: Human; Human evidence with design limitations to check. 5 human studies listed by the source
  -: Peptpedia: Observational or case-based human research; population: Human; Limited observational human evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.

  -: WikiPep: Animal research; population: Animal; Preclinical animal evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Limitations
  -: The reviewed record does not state a specific limitation. The linked paper still needs to be checked for design, size and bias.
  -: limited with no peer-reviewed human clinical trials published.
  -: No formal pharmacokinetic study - no measured half-life, volume of distribution, bioavailability, or clearance value - has been published for epithalon in any species.
  -: limited (PMID 40141333).
  -: Not Measurements: Any plasma half-life figure attributed to epithalon in secondary sources is an extrapolation from tetrapeptide-class behavior - no peer-reviewed study reports a measured value in any species, at any dose, by any route.
  -: no independent laboratory has published pharmacokinetic or pharmacodynamic replication (PMID 19830585).
  -: no published phase I safety trials for epithalon in peer-reviewed Western journals, and essentially all data originates from a single research group.
  -: not established.
  -: limited to observational reports from the originating group (for example, effects on melatonin and mortality in elderly cohorts); no independent, controlled, peer-reviewed human safety or efficacy trials have been published, and the evidence base cannot be evaluated by standard evidence-based-medicine criteria.
  -: This is a commercial educational source. Its uncited figures and modelled outputs must remain labelled as source-listed rather than clinical evidence.
  -: Important caveats: most research comes from one research group (Khavinson's institute), independent replication is limited, and no long-term controlled human trials exist. The animal results are impressive, but rodent lifespan studies don't always translate to humans.
  -: The reviewed record is animal research and cannot establish human effectiveness or safety.
  *: Source rating: 2 out of 5, limited evidence
  *: PepCodex: Low evidence; 5 human studies listed
  *: Peptpedia: Human evidence is limited to observational reports from the originating group (for example, effects on melatonin and mortality in elderly cohorts); no independent, controlled, peer-reviewed human safety or efficacy trials have been published, and the evidence base cannot be evaluated by standard evidence-based-medicine criteria. Epithalon's evidence base has significant limitations that researchers should consider. The overwhelming majority of published research comes from a single laboratory (Khavinson et al. at the St. Petersburg Institute), which does not allow for assessment of reproducibility. Published studies are largely in Russian-language journals or low-impact English-language translations. There are no large, independently conducted, peer-reviewed Phase I/II/III clinical trials in Western peer-reviewed journals. Preprint availability and lack of registered clinical trials further limit evidence quality assessment. This does not mean the effects are false, but the evidence cannot be evaluated by standard evidence-based medicine criteria.
  *: Peptide Hub: Protocol-focused educational summary. Linked papers, site-listed ranges and commercial context are retained with source attribution.
  *: PeptideDeck: Activates telomerase enzyme May help maintain telomere length Increases natural melatonin production Improves sleep quality and circadian rhythm Antioxidant properties Extended lifespan in animal studies May improve immune function with age Supports pineal gland function Epithalon research spans cell culture studies, animal lifespan experiments, and limited human trials-primarily from Khavinson's institute. Research published in Bulletin of Experimental Biology and Medicine demonstrated Epithalon extends the replicative capacity of human fibroblasts beyond the normal limit. Cells treated with Epithalon continued dividing when control cells had stopped-and the mechanism was confirmed to involve telomerase activation and telomere elongation. Studies in fruit flies (Drosophila) showed Epithalon extended lifespan by 11-16% depending on the study. Mouse studies reported even more dramatic results-one found lifespan extension of up to 52% in a tumor-prone strain. The animals showed delayed age-related changes, maintained function longer, and had lower tumor incidence.

  *: Epithalon Peptide Induces Telomerase Activity and Telomere Elongation in Human Somatic Cells (Bulletin of Experimental Biology and Medicine 2003): Addition of Epithalon to telomerase-negative human fetal fibroblasts induced expression of the telomerase catalytic subunit, enzymatic activity, and telomere elongation - demonstrating reactivation of telomerase in somatic cells.

### compound | epo/overview | What is EPO?
kind: overview
title: EPO
summary: From Wikipep - The Peptide Encyclopedia EPO Chemical name Erythropoietin Molecular formula C₈₀₉H₁₃₀₁N₂₂₉O₂₄₀S₅ (protein core) Molecular weight 30,400 g/mol (glycosylated) CAS number 113427-24-0 Sequence 166 amino acid glycoprotein (4 glycosylation sites) Length 166 amino acids Source Kidney (endogenous) / Recombinant (CHO cells) Half-life 4-13 hours (epoetin alfa IV); 24 hours (SC); 48-300 hours (darbepoetin/PEG forms) Targets Erythropoietin receptor (EpoR) Bioavailability ~37% (subcutaneous) Legal status FDA Approved (1989) EPO ( Erythropoietin ) is a 166-amino acid glycoprotein hormone primarily produced by peritubular fibroblasts in the renal cortex in response to hypoxia. It is the master regulator of red blood cell (erythrocyte) production (erythropoiesis), stimulating the proliferation, differentiation, and survival of erythroid progenitor cells in the bone marrow.

### compound | epo/safety | What are the risks of EPO?
kind: safety
title: EPO: source-listed risks
summary: Source-listed risks only. Missing human safety data does not mean a compound is safe.
keyPoint: Source-listed risks only.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: EPO
  connectedTo: EPO
  *: Hypertension (5-25%) - most common, dose-related Injection site pain Headache, arthralgia Pure red cell aplasia (PRCA) - rare but devastating (anti-EPO antibodies destroy erythroid precursors). [source-listed source severity]
  *: Increased mortality, cardiovascular events, and tumor progression when targeting hemoglobin >11 g/dL Thromboembolic events : Stroke, MI, DVT, PE - risk increases with higher hemoglobin targets Tumor progression : Shortened overall survival in cancer patients in multiple trials (BEST, ENHANCE, DAHANCA-10) PRCA : Rare. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Polycythemia and hyperviscosity - the direct pharmacological consequence of EPO's mechanism at supratherapeutic doses; hematocrit above 50-55% dramatically increases whole blood viscosity, reducing microcirculatory flow and creating systemic thrombotic risk; the primary reason EPO has killed athletes. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Thromboembolism (stroke, MI, DVT, PE) - the most serious and potentially fatal adverse effect; blood clots forming in cerebral, coronary, or deep venous vessels from hyperviscous blood; risk is highest during sleep when heart rate and cardiac output are lowest, slowing already-thick blood through vessels. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Hypertension - EPO raises blood pressure in virtually all subjects; multiple mechanisms including viscosity, direct EPOR-mediated vascular smooth muscle vasoconstriction, and endothelin upregulation; blood pressure monitoring throughout protocol is mandatory. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Headache - commonly reported; related to increased blood viscosity and mild hypertension. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Flu-like symptoms (fever, chills, myalgia, arthralgia) - particularly during loading phase; related to the acute hematopoietic response and cytokine release from bone marrow stimulation. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Injection site reactions - pain, redness, bruising at subcutaneous injection site; standard. [source-listed source severity]

understood: resolved

matchedText: EPO
  connectedTo: EPO
section: What the research shows
  -: WikiPep: From Wikipep - The Peptide Encyclopedia EPO Chemical name Erythropoietin Molecular formula C₈₀₉H₁₃₀₁N₂₂₉O₂₄₀S₅ (protein core) Molecular weight 30,400 g/mol (glycosylated) CAS number 113427-24-0 Sequence 166 amino acid glycoprotein (4 glycosylation sites) Length 166 amino acids Source Kidney (endogenous) / Recombinant...
  -: Peptide University Codex: Erythropoietin (EPO) is an endogenous glycoprotein hormone produced primarily by peritubular cells in the renal cortex in response to tissue hypoxia - sensed via the HIF-1α (Hypoxia-Inducible Factor 1-alpha) pathway.
section: Evidence strength
  -: WikiPep: Animal research; population: Animal; Preclinical animal evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: Peptide University Codex: Source summary; study design not clearly stated; population: Not clearly stated; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Limitations
  -: Increased mortality, cardiovascular events, and tumor progression when targeting hemoglobin >11 g/dL Thromboembolic events : Stroke, MI, DVT, PE - risk increases with higher hemoglobin targets Tumor progression : Shortened overall survival in cancer patients in multiple trials (BEST, ENHANCE, DAHANCA-10) PRCA : Rare
  -: Elevated baseline hematocrit (>50% males, >45% females) - EPO will drive hematocrit further above normal range into dangerous polycythemia territory; absolute contraindication until baseline is confirmed normal.
  -: Uncontrolled hypertension - EPO increases blood pressure through increased blood viscosity, direct vasoconstriction via EPOR on vascular smooth muscle, and endothelin-1 upregulation; pre-existing hypertension is dramatically worsened and increases stroke risk.
  -: History of thromboembolism, deep vein thrombosis, or pulmonary embolism - EPO-induced polycythemia creates a profoundly hypercoagulable state; any history of clotting disorders makes EPO potentially lethal.
  -: History of stroke or TIA - increased blood viscosity in subjects with prior cerebrovascular events creates extremely high risk of repeat ischemic stroke.
  -: Coronary artery disease or recent myocardial infarction - viscous blood in narrowed coronary vessels significantly elevates risk of acute myocardial infarction.
  -: Known hypersensitivity to erythropoietin, albumin, or any formulation excipients - including pure red cell aplasia (PRCA) antibody development.
  -: Active malignancy - EPO receptors are expressed on many tumor cell types; EPOR signaling can drive tumor cell proliferation, survival, and angiogenesis; EPO administration in cancer is associated with reduced survival in several randomized trials.
  -: Hemoglobinopathies (sickle cell disease, thalassemia) - increasing red cell mass in subjects with abnormal hemoglobin dramatically worsens blood viscosity and vaso-occlusive crisis risk.
  *: Source rating: 1 out of 5, very limited evidence

### compound | exenatide/evidence | What research is listed for Exenatide?
kind: evidence
title: Exenatide: research listed by the sources
summary: strong-human. In the EXSCEL randomized cardiovascular-outcomes trial, once-weekly exenatide met the prespecified noninferiority criterion for major cardiovascular events versus placebo but did not demonstrate superiority. This result is specific to the studied formulation and population. Gastrointestinal effects are the most common adverse events: nausea is dose-dependent and frequent (often 40-50% of immediate-release users early on), with vomiting, diarrhea, constipation and decreased appetite also reported. Symptoms are usually mild-to-moderate, peak during initiation, and are reduced by the 5 mcg → 10 mcg titration [1][3].; The extended-release (Bydureon / Bydureon BCise) formulation commonly causes injection-site reactions, including small subcutaneous nodules at the depot site that can persist for weeks; rotating injection sites reduces but does not eliminate them [2].; Acute pancreatitis, including fatal and non-fatal hemorrhagic or necrotizing cases, has been reported with exenatide and the GLP-1 class.

  *: PeptideDeck: First FDA-approved GLP-1 agonist (2005) Proven efficacy for blood sugar control Moderate weight loss effects Available in twice-daily and once-weekly forms Extensive long-term safety data Lower cost than newer GLP-1 agonists Does not require dose titration (Bydureon) Natural origin (Gila monster peptide) Active research area with published studies Active research area with published studies Exenatide has extensive clinical trial data as the first approved GLP-1 agonist. The original development program showed HbA1c reductions of 0.8-1.0% and average weight loss of 2-4 kg-significant at the time of approval but modest by current standards. The EXSCEL trial examined cardiovascular outcomes in 14,752 patients. Results showed exenatide was non-inferior to placebo for cardiovascular safety, but didn't achieve statistical significance for cardiovascular benefit (unlike semaglutide's SUSTAIN-6 or liraglutide's LEADER). 7x Quality Tested Bac Water Don't ruin a $300 peptide on generic bac water.   *: WikiPep: AMIGO program: Three pivotal phase III trials evaluating exenatide twice daily as add-on to metformin, sulfonylurea, or combination therapy. Demonstrated consistent HbA1c reductions and weight loss. DURATION program: Series of trials comparing exenatide once weekly (Bydureon) with twice-daily exenatide, sitagliptin, pioglitazone, metformin, and insulin glargine. EXSCEL trial: Cardiovascular outcomes trial (n=14,752) demonstrating non-inferiority for MACE with a favorable trend (HR 0.91; 95% CI, 0.83-1.00). Neuroprotective potential: Exenatide has shown promise in preclinical models of Parkinson's disease and Alzheimer's disease. Parkinson's disease clinical trial: A phase II trial demonstrated improvements in motor function scores in Parkinson's patients treated with exenatide, with effects persisting after drug washout. Traumatic brain injury: Investigated for neuroprotective effects in preclinical TBI models. [ 1 ] [ 2 ] [ 3 ] [ 4 ] [ 5 ] [ 6 ] ↑ 1.0 1.1 Eng J, Kleinman WA, Singh L, et al.

DailyMed label: immediate-release dosing (5→10 mcg twice daily before meals), how supplied (250 mcg/mL pens), renal limits (CrCl <30 mL/min), pharmacokinetics (t½ ~2.4 h, Tmax 2.1 h, renal elimination), and warnings. (journal not listed): Open the linked source for the full study design, population and results.
  *: FDA Prescribing Information - BYDUREON BCISE (exenatide extended-release) injectable suspension, AstraZeneca. DailyMed label: 2 mg subcutaneously once every 7 days, boxed warning for thyroid C-cell tumors, and contraindications (MTC/MEN 2). A product or calculator range is not evidence that a dose was studied, effective or safe. Confidence: high.
  *: Resolved: modelled administration routes. Use only the route stated in the original study or official product information. Do not convert an oral, intranasal, intramuscular or investigational product into a generic subcutaneous vial protocol. PeptideDosage.org applies a common reconstitution and syringe format even to products such as Ventfort that it identifies as oral. That format is not evidence that the modelled route was studied or is suitable. Confidence: high.

Keep only links whose NCBI record matches the stated research subject. ### compound | exendin4/overview | What is Exendin-4?
kind: overview
title: Exendin-4
summary: From Wikipep - The Peptide Encyclopedia Exendin-4 Chemical name Exendin-4; Exenatide (synthetic form); AC2993 Molecular formula C₁₈₄H₂₈₂N₅₀O₆₀S Molecular weight 4186.6 g/mol CAS number 141758-74-9 Sequence HGEGTFTSDLSKQMEEEAVRLFIEWLKNGGPSSGAPPPS-NH₂ Length 39 amino acids Source Heloderma suspectum (Gila monster) salivary venom Half-life 2.4 hours (subcutaneous injection) Targets GLP-1 receptor (GLP-1R) Bioavailability ~65-75% (subcutaneous) Legal status FDA-approved as exenatide (Byetta, Bydureon); Research compound Exendin-4 is a 39-amino acid peptide originally isolated from the salivary venom of the Gila monster ( Heloderma suspectum ), a venomous lizard native to the southwestern United States and northwestern Mexico. Exendin-4 is a potent agonist of the glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor (GLP-1R) and shares approximately 53% amino acid sequence homology with human GLP-1 (7-36) amide .

### compound | exendin4/safety | What are the risks of Exendin-4?
kind: safety
title: Exendin-4: source-listed risks

keyPoint: Source-listed risks only.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: Exendin-4
  connectedTo: Exendin-4
  *: Nausea (44% with twice-daily; 20% with weekly formulation) - most common adverse effect; typically decreases over time with continued use Vomiting (13% twice-daily; 10% weekly) Diarrhea (13% twice-daily; 9% weekly) Injection site reactions (5-10%; nodules with weekly formulation due to microsphere depot) Headache (9%). [source-listed source severity]
  *: Pancreatitis: Post-marketing reports of acute pancreatitis; FDA requires label warning. Discontinue if pancreatitis suspected. Causal relationship debated but monitoring is recommended Thyroid C-cell tumors: GLP-1 receptor agonists cause thyroid C-cell hyperplasia and medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC) in rodents at. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia syndrome type 2 (MEN 2) History of serious hypersensitivity to exenatide Severe gastrointestinal disease (gastroparesis) End-stage renal disease (eGFR <15 mL/min) History of pancreatitis (relative contraindication). [source-listed source severity]

### compound | eyeseryl/overview | What is Eyeseryl?
kind: overview
title: Eyeseryl
summary: Eyeseryl (INCI Acetyl Tetrapeptide-5) is a synthetic, acetylated tetrapeptide cosmetic ingredient marketed by Lipotec/Lubrizol for the eye-contour area, where it is positioned as an anti-puffiness and anti-dark-circle active. Its sequence is acetyl-beta-alanyl-histidyl-seryl-histidine (Ac-betaAla-His-Ser-His; molecular formula C20H28N8O7, average mass about 492.5 Da, CAS 820959-17-9) [1]. Mechanistically it is described as a local angiotensin-converting-enzyme (ACE) inhibitor that exerts a draining, decongestant effect, reduces capillary permeability and interstitial fluid accumulation, and inhibits protein glycation, helping preserve the collagen and elastin that support the thin infraorbital skin [2][3]. The real-world Eyeseryl dosage is purely topical: finished serums and creams contain roughly 1-10% of the Eyeseryl trade solution (which itself carries only about 0.05% active peptide), applied twice daily to the under-eye area.
keyPoint: Eyeseryl (INCI Acetyl Tetrapeptide-5) is a synthetic, acetylated tetrapeptide cosmetic ingredient marketed by Lipotec/Lubrizol for the eye-contour area, where it is positioned as an anti-puffiness and anti-dark-circle active.

### compound | eyeseryl/evidence | What research is listed for Eyeseryl?
kind: evidence
title: Eyeseryl: research listed by the sources
summary: Topical Eyeseryl is generally well tolerated, with reported reactions limited to mild, transient erythema, stinging or a sensation of tightness at the application site, particularly when layered with other actives such as retinoids or acids.; Because the product is applied close to the eye, accidental ocular contact can cause transient conjunctival irritation, watering or burning; keep the product off the lid margin and rinse promptly with water if it migrates onto the eye surface.; True allergic contact dermatitis to acetyl tetrapeptide-5 is uncommon; most adverse skin reactions to eye-contour products are caused by other formulation components such as preservatives, fragrances or penetration enhancers and should be assessed by a dermatologist if persistent.; No systemic side effects have been documented, since absorption of this hydrophilic tetrapeptide through intact skin into the circulation is negligible and no measurable plasma exposure is expected after cosmetic use.; Safety data in pregnancy, lactation and pediatric use are absent; on a precautionary basis, avoiding

### compound | fdaapprovedpeptidedrugs/overview | What is FDA-Approved Peptide Drugs?
kind: overview
title: FDA-Approved Peptide Drugs

### compound | fgf21/overview | What is FGF-21?
kind: overview
title: FGF-21
summary: A metabolic hormone produced by the liver that regulates fat metabolism, insulin sensitivity, and energy balance, and is elevated naturally during fasting. Studied for its therapeutic potential in non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH/MASH), metabolic syndrome, and dyslipidemia.
keyPoint: A metabolic hormone produced by the liver that regulates fat metabolism, insulin sensitivity, and energy balance, and is elevated naturally during fasting.

### compound | fgf21/evidence | What research is listed for FGF-21?
kind: evidence
title: FGF-21: research listed by the sources
summary: preliminary. Native FGF21 is an endogenous metabolic hormone under investigation for its role in energy and lipid metabolism. Human therapeutic findings from engineered agents must remain separate: PMID 23536797 establishes LY2405319 as an engineered FGF21-based variant, and PMID 24011069 reports a human study of that LY2405319 analog rather than native FGF21. Pegozafermin, efruxifermin, and other long-acting analogs are likewise not direct native-FGF21 evidence. Native FGF21 has no approved therapeutic product or established clinical dosing. ### compound | fglpeptide/overview | What is FGL Peptide?
kind: overview
title: FGL Peptide
summary: From Wikipep - The Peptide Encyclopedia FGL Peptide Chemical name NCAM-FGL (FG Loop Peptide) Molecular formula C₇₂H₁₁₈N₂₀O₂₈ Molecular weight ~1635 Da CAS number N/A (research compound) Sequence EVYVVAENQQGKSKA Length 15 amino acids Source Synthetic (derived from NCAM) Half-life 2-4 hours (estimated, subcutaneous) Targets FGFR1, NCAM signaling pathways Bioavailability Moderate (subcutaneous) Legal status Research compound (unscheduled) FGL Peptide (also known as NCAM-FGL or FG Loop peptide ) is a 15-amino acid synthetic peptide derived from the second fibronectin type III module of the Neural Cell Adhesion Molecule (NCAM). The sequence EVYVVAENQQGKSKA corresponds to the FG loop region of NCAM that directly interacts with fibroblast growth factor receptor 1 (FGFR1). By mimicking this binding interface, FGL peptide activates FGFR1-mediated signaling cascades without requiring full NCAM protein expression.

title: Fisetin

keyPoint: A flavonoid with preclinical fisetin senolytic evidence and registered human research without posted results.

method: canonical
confidence: high

  connectedTo: Fisetin
section: Why it is researched
  -: A flavonoid with preclinical fisetin senolytic evidence and registered human research without posted results.
section: How it works in the research
  -: Fisetin is 3,3′,4′,7-tetrahydroxyflavone, a plant flavonoid studied for preclinical senolytic activity.
section: Evidence strength
  -: The Peptide Handbook: Animal research; population: Animal; Preclinical animal evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Main limitations
  -: Long-term human safety data is absent - the doses used in some research studies substantially exceed what would be obtained from dietary sources
  -: Potential drug interactions have not been systematically studied in humans
  -: Not recommended during pregnancy or breastfeeding due to insufficient safety data

### compound | fisetin/evidence | What research is listed for Fisetin?
kind: evidence
title: Fisetin: research listed by the sources
summary: AFFIRM-LITE trial (Mayo Clinic) published: fisetin reduced senescent cell burden in adipose tissue with acceptable safety in older women. Largest fisetin human trial to date. Strong animal aging data.
keyPoint: AFFIRM-LITE trial (Mayo Clinic) published: fisetin reduced senescent cell burden in adipose tissue with acceptable safety in older women.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: Fisetin
  connectedTo: Fisetin
section: What the research shows
  -: The Peptide Handbook: A flavonoid with preclinical fisetin senolytic evidence and registered human research without posted results.
section: Evidence strength
  -: The Peptide Handbook: Animal research; population: Animal; Preclinical animal evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Limitations
  -: Long-term human safety data is absent - the doses used in some research studies substantially exceed what would be obtained from dietary sources
  -: Potential drug interactions have not been systematically studied in humans
  -: Not recommended during pregnancy or breastfeeding due to insufficient safety data
  -: Bioavailability is a significant limitation: poor absorption may mean tissue concentrations after supplementation are substantially lower than doses shown to be active in preclinical studies
  -: Supplement quality and purity vary considerably across commercial products
  *: Source rating: 3 out of 5
  *: The Peptide Handbook: preliminary. PMID 30279143 supports preclinical fisetin senotherapeutic/senolytic findings, including effects in cellular and animal models; it is not human efficacy evidence. NCT03430037 and NCT03675724 are exact fisetin intervention registry records involving older adults and are listed as registered trials without posted results. Their registry status must not be generalized into demonstrated senolytic efficacy, lifespan extension, or an established therapeutic regimen. Dasatinib-plus-quercetin and quercetin-alone evidence is excluded from this fisetin-alone record.
  *: Fisetin is a Senotherapeutic that Extends Health and Lifespan (EBioMedicine 2018): Of 10 flavonoids screened, fisetin was the most potent senolytic. Chronic administration to aged wild-type mice reduced senescence burden across multiple tissues, suppressed age-related pathology, and extended median and maximum lifespan by roughly 10%.

  followUp: What source-listed dosage research is shown for Fisetin?

  source: Fisetin is a Senotherapeutic that Extends Health and Lifespan <https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30279143/>

  *: Source rating: 1 out of 5, very limited evidence

  *: The Peptide Handbook: preliminary. Follistatin-344 evidence is largely preclinical, with dramatic muscle hypertrophy demonstrated in animal models via myostatin and activin A inhibition. One Phase 1/2a human study (Mendell et al., 2015) examined follistatin gene therapy using an AAV1.CMV.FS344 vector for Becker muscular dystrophy. This gene-therapy study is NOT evidence for injectable FST-344 peptide protocols; the delivery system, mechanism, and regulatory pathway are entirely distinct. Direct injectable FST-344 peptide has never been formally studied in controlled human trials. The previously stored PubMed identifiers (PMID 19714099 and PMID 15059942) were confirmed as entity mismatches and have been removed. Foundational preclinical evidence (Lee & McPherron, 2001) demonstrates that myostatin inhibition and follistatin overexpression produce pronounced skeletal muscle hypertrophy in animal models; this preclinical evidence is distinct from and should not be conflated with the AAV1.CMV.FS344 gene-therapy human study or injectable FST-344 peptide use.
  *: PeptideDosage.org: There is no established human safety profile for exogenous subcutaneously injected follistatin protein; all human data come from intramuscular AAV gene therapy, so reports about injected FS-344 peptide are anecdotal and unverified, and dose-response and toxicity are essentially unknown [6][7][8].; Follistatin broadly inhibits activin and other TGF-β ligands that regulate the pituitary FSH axis, reproduction, inflammation, wound healing, and tissue homeostasis; the FS-344/FS-315 design was specifically chosen to limit pituitary involvement, and the gene-therapy trials reported no hormonal changes, but systemic inhibition with unregulated material carries theoretical endocrine and reproductive risk [6][7].; Rapid, large gains in muscle force can outpace adaptation of tendons, ligaments, and connective tissue, raising a theoretical risk of strain or tendon injury; effects on cardiac muscle from chronic myostatin/activin inhibition are not characterized in humans.; Activin signaling has tumor-suppressor and growth-regulatory roles in some tissues, so broad, sustained inhibition raises a
  *: PeptideDeck: Inhibition of myostatin (primary muscle growth limiter) Enhanced muscle protein synthesis potential May support muscle growth beyond genetic limits Reduced muscle wasting in disease models Potential fat reduction secondary to muscle effects May improve strength-to-bodyweight ratio Support for recovery from muscle injuries Possible anti-fibrotic effects Active research area with published studies Follistatin research spans from foundational animal studies to recent human clinical trials, with consistently impressive results in preclinical models. The foundational research demonstrated remarkable effects. In the original 'mighty mice' studies, myostatin knockout resulted in approximately double the muscle mass of normal mice. Later work showed that follistatin administration to normal adult mice could achieve similar results-demonstrating that even mature animals respond to myostatin inhibition. A pivotal 2009 study published in Science Translational Medicine examined follistatin gene therapy in primates (macaque monkeys).
  *: WikiPep: Follistatin-344 is extensively used in laboratory research: Recombinant protein studies: Purified FS-344 protein used in cell culture and in vivo experiments Gene therapy vector development: AAV-FS344 constructs for preclinical testing Myostatin biology: Tool for studying myostatin signaling and muscle regulation TGF-β superfamily research: Understanding ligand-receptor interactions and signaling pathway modulation Reproductive biology: Studying FSH regulation and gonadal function Fibrosis research: Investigating anti-fibrotic effects through TGF-β pathway modulation The three main follistatin isoforms have distinct properties: Isoform Mature Length C-terminal Tail HSPG Binding Distribution Activin Affinity FS-288 (FS-317) 288 aa Absent Strong Tissue-bound Highest FS-303 303 aa Partial Moderate Follicular fluid Intermediate FS-315 (FS-344) 315 aa Full 26-residue acidic tail Weak Serum (circulating) 10x lower than FS-288 FS-344/FS-315 is preferred for systemic therapeutic applications because: Its weak cell-surface binding allows systemic distribution Lower tissue trapping reduces
  *: Follistatin Gene Therapy for Becker Muscular Dystrophy (Molecular Therapy 2015): Phase 1/2a trial of follistatin gene therapy in Becker muscular dystrophy patients. Demonstrated safety and increased muscle mass - proof of concept for myostatin inhibition via follistatin.

### compound | follistatin315/evidence | What research is listed for Follistatin 315?
kind: evidence
title: Follistatin 315: research listed by the sources
summary: preliminary. Identity and isoform sources support FST315/FST288 biology. NCT01519349 and NCT02354781 concern FST344 gene transfer and must not be used as evidence for direct FST315 protein administration, pharmacokinetics, dosing, efficacy, or safety. No human safety data exist for injected follistatin protein. Every safety statement here is extrapolated from animal studies or from AAV gene-therapy trials that used a different delivery route, so the actual risk profile of subcutaneous FS-315 protein is genuinely unknown [7][8].; Follistatin is a broad ligand trap, not a myostatin-only blocker - it also neutralizes activin A, GDF-11 and several BMPs. Systemic activin/BMP inhibition could disturb processes these ligands govern, including reproductive endocrinology, inflammation and wound healing, vascular tone, and bone morphogenesis [1][2].; Excessive or sustained myostatin/activin inhibition is associated in animal models with tendon and connective-tissue changes and disproportionate muscle-to-tendon loading, raising a theoretical risk of tendon or ligament injury as muscle force outpaces connective-tissue adaptation.; As a recombinant glycoprotein, follistatin can provoke injection-site reactions and immunogenicity (anti-drug antibodies), which may cause local or systemic reactions and can neutralize activity; research-grade

section: Evidence strength
  -: The Peptide Handbook: Animal research; population: Animal; Preclinical animal evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: PeptideDosage.org: Animal research; population: Animal; Preclinical animal evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: WikiPep: Animal research; population: Animal; Preclinical animal evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Limitations
  -: The reviewed record is animal research and cannot establish human effectiveness or safety.
  -: Follistatin-315 (FS-315) is the major circulating isoform of follistatin, an autocrine/paracrine glycoprotein that acts as a high-affinity antagonist of TGF-beta superfamily ligands, most importantly myostatin (GDF-8) and activin A.
  *: Source rating: 2 out of 5, limited evidence
  *: The Peptide Handbook: preliminary. Identity and isoform sources support FST315/FST288 biology. NCT01519349 and NCT02354781 concern FST344 gene transfer and must not be used as evidence for direct FST315 protein administration, pharmacokinetics, dosing, efficacy, or safety.
  *: PeptideDosage.org: No human safety data exist for injected follistatin protein. Every safety statement here is extrapolated from animal studies or from AAV gene-therapy trials that used a different delivery route, so the actual risk profile of subcutaneous FS-315 protein is genuinely unknown [7][8].; Follistatin is a broad ligand trap, not a myostatin-only blocker - it also neutralizes activin A, GDF-11 and several BMPs. Systemic activin/BMP inhibition could disturb processes these ligands govern, including reproductive endocrinology, inflammation and wound healing, vascular tone, and bone morphogenesis [1][2].; Excessive or sustained myostatin/activin inhibition is associated in animal models with tendon and connective-tissue changes and disproportionate muscle-to-tendon loading, raising a theoretical risk of tendon or ligament injury as muscle force outpaces connective-tissue adaptation.; As a recombinant glycoprotein, follistatin can provoke injection-site reactions and immunogenicity (anti-drug antibodies), which may cause local or systemic reactions and can neutralize activity; research-grade

### compound | foxo4-dri/overview | What is FOXO4-DRI?
kind: overview
title: FOXO4-DRI
summary: A D-retro-inverso peptide designed to disrupt the FOXO4-p53 interaction, selectively eliminating senescent cells (senolytic). Preclinical studies in aged mice demonstrated restored fitness, fur density, and renal function. No human clinical trials conducted. More selective than BCL-2 inhibitors but remains unproven in humans.
keyPoint: A D-retro-inverso peptide designed to disrupt the FOXO4-p53 interaction, selectively eliminating senescent cells (senolytic).

### compound | foxo4-dri/evidence | What research is listed for FOXO4-DRI?
kind: evidence
title: FOXO4-DRI: research listed by the sources
summary: Landmark Baar et al. Nature Medicine 2017 animal study showed reversal of frailty, hair loss, and kidney dysfunction in fast-aging mice. Proof-of-concept in chemotherapy-induced senescence models. No published human clinical trials as of 2025. Human dosing is extrapolated from animal data with body surface area conversion - treat all doses as unvalidated.
keyPoint: Landmark Baar et al.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: FOXO4-DRI
  connectedTo: FOXO4-DRI
section: What the research shows
  -: PepCodex: A D-retro-inverso peptide designed to disrupt the FOXO4-p53 interaction, selectively eliminating senescent cells (senolytic).
  -: The Peptide Handbook: A synthetic peptide designed to disrupt a specific protein interaction that allows senescent cells to evade programmed cell death.
  -: Peptpedia: FOXO4-DRI cleared senescent cells in aged mice (Cell, 2017) - but no human trials have been published.
  -: Peptide Hub: FOXO4-DRI (FOXO4 D-Retro-Inverso) is the most researched peptide senolytic - a compound that selectively induces apoptosis in senescent cells by blocking the FOXO4-p53 pro-survival interaction.
  -: PeptideDosage.org: FOXO4-DRI is a 43-amino-acid synthetic senolytic peptide developed by Peter de Keizer and colleagues, first described in the landmark Cell 2017 paper as the first peptide-based agent to selectively eliminate senescent cells in mice through targeted disruption of the FOXO4-p53 interaction [1].
section: Evidence strength

  -: No human safety data; human risk profile is unknown
  -: Potential elimination of beneficial senescent cells (paracrine tissue repair role)
  -: Possible stem cell pool depletion

  -: no human trials have been published.

  -: This is a commercial educational source. Its uncited figures and modelled outputs must remain labelled as source-listed rather than clinical evidence.
  -: FOXO4-DRI is a 43-amino-acid synthetic senolytic peptide developed by Peter de Keizer and colleagues, first described in the landmark Cell 2017 paper as the first peptide-based agent to selectively eliminate senescent cells in mice through targeted disruption of the FOXO4-p53 interaction [1].
  *: Source rating: 2 out of 5, limited evidence
  *: The Peptide Handbook: preliminary. FOXO4-DRI has preclinical proof-of-concept data from a 2017 Cell publication in fast-aged progeroid and naturally aged mice, including restoration of selected fitness, fur, and renal-function measures through senescent-cell clearance. The evidence base is limited and has not established human efficacy, safety, pharmacokinetics, or dosing. The D-retro-inverso design may affect protease stability, but human tissue exposure and clearance remain unknown.
  *: Peptpedia: No human clinical trials have been conducted or published; all in-vivo evidence is from mice, and the only human-cell data is in vitro (senescent chondrocytes). Human pharmacokinetics, safe dosing, and long-term effects are entirely uncharacterized.
  *: Peptide Hub: Protocol-focused educational summary. Linked papers, site-listed ranges and commercial context are retained with source attribution.
  *: PeptideDosage.org: FOXO4-DRI has no documented human safety data; no controlled human pharmacokinetic, pharmacodynamic, or adverse-event studies have been published.; In mice, transient increases in liver enzymes and mild renal stress markers have been observed at therapeutic doses, generally resolving after course completion.; Theoretical risks include excessive apoptosis if non-senescent cells are inadvertently targeted, particularly in tissues with high cell turnover; the selectivity margin in clinical populations is unknown.; Inflammatory flare from sudden senescent cell clearance (analogous to cytokine release syndromes seen with other senolytics) is a theoretical concern, especially in patients with high senescent cell burden.; Injection-site reactions with subcutaneous or intraperitoneal administration are expected; the peptide is delivered parenterally and is not orally bioavailable.; Drug-drug interaction data are absent; concurrent use with chemotherapy or other senolytics is uncharacterized and theoretically additive.; Reproductive, pregnancy, and lactation safety are entirely unstudied and
  *: PeptideDeck: Studied as a selective senolytic research peptide Designed to disrupt FOXO4-p53 signaling in senescent cells D-retro-inverso structure improves protease resistance Used in cellular aging and senescence pathway research FOXO4-DRI has been studied primarily in laboratory and preclinical models of aging and senescence, where it serves as a proof-of-concept tool for the senolytic strategy of clearing senescent cells to improve tissue health. FOXO4-DRI is used in senescence research to test whether disrupting the FOXO4-p53 interaction can selectively eliminate senescent cells in culture. Studies in cellular models have examined how the peptide induces death in senescent cells while having limited effect on healthy dividing cells, supporting its intended selectivity and validating the FOXO4-p53 axis as a senolytic target.
  *: Targeted Apoptosis of Senescent Cells Restores Tissue Homeostasis (Nature Medicine 2017): FOXO4-DRI induced targeted apoptosis in senescent cells in vivo. Reversed frailty, hair loss, and restored kidney function in accelerated-aging mice. Landmark proof-of-concept for peptide senolytics.

### compound | galanin/overview | What is Galanin?
kind: overview
title: Galanin
summary: From Wikipep - The Peptide Encyclopedia Galanin Chemical name Galanin (1-30), human Molecular formula C₁₃₉H₂₁₀N₄₂O₄₃ Molecular weight 3157.4 g/mol CAS number 119418-04-1 Sequence GWTLNSAGYLLGPHAVGNHRSFSDKNGLTS Length 30 amino acids Source Endogenous neuropeptide; encoded by GAL gene Half-life ~6 minutes (plasma) Targets GalR1, GalR2, GalR3 (G-protein coupled receptors) Bioavailability Not orally bioavailable; requires parenteral administration Legal status Research compound; not FDA-approved as therapeutic Galanin is an endogenous neuropeptide consisting of 30 amino acids in humans (29 amino acids in most other mammalian species) that is widely expressed in the central nervous system , spinal cord , and gastrointestinal tract . First isolated from porcine intestinal extracts in 1983 by Tatemoto and colleagues, galanin derives its name from its N-terminal g lycine and C-terminal al anine residues (though human galanin actually terminates in serine rather than alanine).

  -: The primary challenges for therapeutic development of galanin-based compounds include: Rapid enzymatic degradation and short plasma half-life Poor blood-brain barrier penetration for peripherally administered peptides Opposing effects at different receptor subtypes complicating the therapeutic window Broad

summary: From Wikipep - The Peptide Encyclopedia Galanin Chemical name Galanin (1-30), human Molecular formula C₁₃₉H₂₁₀N₄₂O₄₃ Molecular weight 3157.4 g/mol CAS number 119418-04-1 Sequence GWTLNSAGYLLGPHAVGNHRSFSDKNGLTS Length 30 amino acids Source Endogenous neuropeptide; encoded by GAL gene Half-life ~6 minutes (plasma) Targets GalR1, GalR2, GalR3 (G-protein coupled receptors) Bioavailability Not orally bioavailable; requires parenteral administration Legal status Research compound; not FDA-approved as therapeutic Galanin is an endogenous neuropeptide consisting of 30 amino acids in humans (29 amino acids in most other mammalian species) that is widely expressed in the central nervous system , spinal cord , and gastrointestinal tract . First isolated from porcine intestinal extracts in 1983 by Tatemoto and colleagues, galanin derives its name from its N-terminal g lycine and C-terminal al anine residues (though human galanin actually terminates in serine rather than alanine).

### compound | galanin/evidence | What research is listed for Galanin?
kind: evidence
title: Galanin: research listed by the sources
summary: Galanin remains primarily a research tool in neuroscience and pharmacology. Synthetic galanin and selective receptor agonists/antagonists are widely used in preclinical studies to investigate pain mechanisms, seizure disorders, mood regulation, and neurodegenerative disease pathology. Several pharmaceutical companies have pursued galanin receptor-targeted drug discovery programs, particularly focused on GalR3 antagonists for depression and GalR1 agonists for epilepsy. === Diagnostic Biomarker Potential === [ 10 ] Altered galanin expression has been observed in several disease states, including Alzheimer's disease (where galanin is hyperexpressed in surviving cholinergic neurons), depression , chronic pain syndromes, and certain cancers. Galanin levels in cerebrospinal fluid and plasma have been investigated as potential biomarkers for neurological and psychiatric conditions, though no validated clinical diagnostic applications have been established to date.

section: What the research shows
  -: PepCodex: A naturally occurring copper-binding tripeptide with wound healing and skin regeneration properties.
  -: The Peptide Handbook: A naturally occurring copper-binding tripeptide found in human plasma, wound fluid, and saliva.
  -: Halflife Labs: Evidence context is stated on the linked compound page.
  -: Peptpedia: Modulates 4,128 human genes (~32% of the genome) and declines from 200 to 80 ng/mL with age.
  -: Peptide Hub: GHK-Cu (glycyl-L-histidyl-L-lysine copper) is a naturally occurring copper-binding tripeptide found in human plasma, saliva, and urine at concentrations that decline significantly with age - from approximately 200 ng/mL at age 20 to 80 ng/mL by age 60.
section: Evidence strength
  -: PepCodex: Human clinical research; population: Human; Human evidence with design limitations to check. 10 human studies listed by the source
  -: The Peptide Handbook: Randomized or controlled human research; population: Human; Direct controlled human evidence. 7 human studies listed by the source; 28 animal studies listed by the source
  -: Halflife Labs: Source summary; study design not clearly stated; population: Not clearly stated; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.

  -: Peptide Hub: Source summary; study design not clearly stated; population: Not clearly stated; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Limitations
  -: The reviewed record does not state a specific limitation. The linked paper still needs to be checked for design, size and bias.
  -: Systemic copper accumulation at very high injectable doses (theoretical); insufficient long-term human injectable data; cosmetic topical use is well-established and considered safe
  -: The source does not clearly state the study population or design in PEARL's reviewed record.
  -: not merely structural; it is essential for the peptide's enzymatic and gene-regulatory activity, and the free peptide without copper has significantly reduced biological function.
  -: limited, but its copper-binding equilibrium has been characterized with analytical precision, and its skin penetration behavior has been quantified in human tissue models.
  -: not a dosing parameter but the trajectory of its natural plasma concentration across a human lifespan.
  -: Not Just a Cargo: The copper-chelate hypothesis proposes that GHK facilitates copper uptake into cells - the peptide-bound ion enters through pathways distinct from free ionic copper, which is why the complex is biologically active at concentrations where free copper would be poorly tolerated (PMID 29986520).
  -: no peptide or copper permeated intact human skin, whereas microneedle pretreatment enabled permeation of 134 ± 12 nanomoles of peptide and 705 ± 84 nanomoles of copper (PMID 25690343).
  -: not merely structural-it is essential for the peptide's biological activity.
  -: not established.
  -: not definitively established in large RCTs, but the correlation has driven substantial research interest.

  *: Source rating: 3 out of 5
  *: PepCodex: Moderate evidence; 10 human studies listed
  *: The Peptide Handbook: preliminary. GHK-Cu is a naturally occurring tripeptide-copper complex with established cosmeceutical use. One randomized human study (Miller et al., 2006) evaluated topical copper tripeptide complex on CO2 laser-resurfaced skin; objective clinical outcomes - including erythema, wrinkle depth, and overall skin quality - were not significantly better than control, though patient-reported satisfaction was higher; this limited clinical evidence does not establish broad therapeutic efficacy for skin remodeling or wound healing. This single study does not establish broad improvements in skin thickness, wrinkle depth, and collagen density across the general population, and should not be characterized as multiple controlled trials. Genome-wide gene expression claims previously cited in this record (PMID 25660582) were confirmed as entity mismatches and have been removed; no replacement genome-wide source is added per implementation rules. Injectable systemic use lacks controlled human data.
  *: Halflife Labs: Evidence context is stated on the linked compound page.
  *: Peptide Hub: Protocol-focused educational summary. Linked papers, site-listed ranges and commercial context are retained with source attribution.
  *: PeptideDosage.org: Topical GHK-Cu is exceptionally well tolerated. The most common adverse event is mild, transient erythema or stinging at the application site, particularly when used on freshly resurfaced or compromised skin barriers.; The copper-tripeptide complex has an intrinsic blue-green color that can transiently tint skin, hair, and fabrics, particularly with high-concentration serums; this discoloration is cosmetic and washes off easily with cleansing.; Allergic contact dermatitis to GHK-Cu is rare but possible, especially in individuals with known copper sensitivity; patch testing is recommended for users with a history of metal allergy or persistent dermatitis.; Subcutaneous or intradermal injection in research settings can produce localized blue-green pigmentation, mild swelling, bruising, or pain at the injection site, and the long-term safety of injectable GHK-Cu has not been characterized in formal trials.; Excessive systemic copper exposure is theoretically possible with very high topical doses on broken skin or with injectable use; signs of copper excess (nausea, abdominal
  *: GHK Peptide as a Natural Modulator of Multiple Cellular Pathways in Skin Regeneration (BioMed Research International 2015): GHK-Cu modulates over 4,000 genes affecting collagen synthesis, anti-inflammatory pathways, wound healing, and antioxidant systems in skin regeneration.

One randomized human study (Miller et al., 2006) evaluated topical copper tripeptide complex on CO2 laser-resurfaced skin; objective clinical outcomes - including erythema, wrinkle depth, and overall skin quality - were not significantly better than control, though patient-reported satisfaction was higher; this limited clinical evidence does not establish broad therapeutic efficacy for skin remodeling or wound healing. This single study does not establish broad improvements in skin thickness, wrinkle depth, and collagen density across the general population, and should not be characterized as multiple controlled trials. Genome-wide gene expression claims previously cited in this record (PMID 25660582) were confirmed as entity mismatches and have been removed; no replacement genome-wide source is added per implementation rules. Injectable systemic use lacks controlled human data.

The most common adverse event is mild, transient erythema or stinging at the application site, particularly when used on freshly resurfaced or compromised skin barriers.; The copper-tripeptide complex has an intrinsic blue-green color that can transiently tint skin, hair, and fabrics, particularly with high-concentration serums; this discoloration is cosmetic and washes off easily with cleansing.; Allergic contact dermatitis to GHK-Cu is rare but possible, especially in individuals with known copper sensitivity; patch testing is recommended for users with a history of metal allergy or persistent dermatitis.; Subcutaneous or intradermal injection in research settings can produce localized blue-green pigmentation, mild swelling, bruising, or pain at the injection site, and the long-term safety of injectable GHK-Cu has not been characterized in formal trials.; Excessive systemic copper exposure is theoretically possible with very high topical doses on broken skin or with injectable use; signs of copper excess (nausea, abdominal
  *: GHK Peptide as a Natural Modulator of Multiple Cellular Pathways in Skin Regeneration (BioMed Research International 2015): GHK-Cu modulates over 4,000 genes affecting collagen synthesis, anti-inflammatory pathways, wound healing, and antioxidant systems in skin regeneration.

### compound | ghkcuglutathioneggh/overview | What is GHK-Cu Glutathione Recovery Blend (GGH)?
kind: overview
title: GHK-Cu Glutathione Recovery Blend (GGH)
summary: The GHK-Cu Glutathione Recovery Blend (product code GGH) is a regeneration and antioxidant injection that combines the copper peptide GHK-Cu with glutathione and supporting amino acids and coenzymes. It is a hybrid blend that pairs a peptide with vitamin and amino acid components, and it is given as a fixed direct dose with no titration. Each milliliter contains GHK-Cu 2000mcg, Glutathione 200mg, Histidine 100mg, Glycine 50mg, and NADH 50mg. GHK-Cu is a copper-binding peptide known for supporting skin remodeling, collagen production, wound healing, and tissue regeneration, glutathione is the master antioxidant supporting detoxification and cellular protection, histidine and glycine are amino acids that support tissue repair and are components of glutathione synthesis, and NADH provides a reduced coenzyme that supports cellular energy production.

section: Limitations
  -: Known hypersensitivity to GHK-Cu, glutathione, histidine, glycine, NADH, or any formulation excipient.
  -: Wilson disease or other copper metabolism disorders.
  -: Concurrent copper chelation therapy.
  -: Pregnancy or breastfeeding unless directed and supervised by a physician.
  -: Active malignancy unless medically supervised, given the tissue-growth and remodeling activity of GHK-Cu.

First isolated and characterized by Loren Pickart in the 1970s from human albumin preparations, GHK was identified based on its ability to cause old human liver tissue to synthesize proteins similar to younger tissue.

### compound | ghrelin/overview | What is Ghrelin?
kind: overview
title: Ghrelin
summary: The body's principal hunger-signaling hormone, a 28-amino-acid peptide secreted primarily by the stomach that simultaneously stimulates appetite and triggers growth hormone release. Widely studied in appetite regulation, energy balance, metabolic biology, and the neuroscience of hunger and reward.
keyPoint: The body's principal hunger-signaling hormone, a 28-amino-acid peptide secreted primarily by the stomach that simultaneously stimulates appetite and triggers growth hormone release.
understood: resolved
method: canonical

  connectedTo: Ghrelin
section: Why it is researched
  -: The body's principal hunger-signaling hormone, a 28-amino-acid peptide secreted primarily by the stomach that simultaneously stimulates appetite and triggers growth hormone release.
section: How it works in the research
  -: The endogenous ligand for the growth hormone secretagogue receptor (GHS-R1a), discovered in 1999.
section: Evidence strength
  -: Peptide Authority: Source summary; study design not clearly stated; population: Human; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.

  -: What 'ghrelin supplements' actually contain.
  -: Whether any meaningful effect occurs from oral ghrelin-pathway products.
  -: Ghrelin pharmacology happens through GHRPs / GLP-1 antagonists - not standalone ghrelin.

### compound | ghrelin/evidence | What research is listed for Ghrelin?
kind: evidence
title: Ghrelin: research listed by the sources
summary: strong-human. Ghrelin was discovered as an acylated endogenous ligand for the growth-hormone secretagogue receptor. Its active form requires Ser3 octanoylation, and its established human evidence concerns endogenous appetite, growth-hormone, and energy-homeostasis physiology. Cardiovascular, gastrointestinal, and immune topics remain research areas and should not be represented as broad therapeutic efficacy. This strong physiology evidence does not establish a universal exogenous dosing, pharmacokinetic, safety, or therapeutic-efficacy profile. Transient facial flushing is the most common acute effect, reported in roughly 10% of volunteers during or shortly after intravenous administration [2].; Gastrointestinal effects such as audible gastric rumbling (borborygmi), increased hunger, and accelerated gastric motility occur in a minority of subjects, consistent with ghrelin's prokinetic and orexigenic actions [2][3].; A consistent rise in blood glucose with unchanged or reduced insulin can occur; continuous or repeated infusion can worsen glucose tolerance, a particular concern for people with prediabetes, diabetes, or metabolic syndrome [4].; Ghrelin reliably increases circulating ACTH, cortisol, and prolactin, so it transiently activates the HPA axis; this is expected pharmacology rather than a defect but is relevant in endocrine-sensitive individuals [2].; Increased appetite and food intake are intrinsic effects and may be undesirable outside a cachexia/anorexia context; the orexigenic action is potent (comparable to NPY in human studies) [3].; Less common reports include thirst, mild sweating, somnolence, and transient

  -: Ghrelin (INN: lenomorelin; also called acyl-ghrelin) is a 28-amino-acid orexigenic peptide hormone secreted mainly by the X/A-like cells of the gastric oxyntic mucosa, and it is the only known circulating hormone that directly stimulates hunger.
  -: Ghrelin's short half-life and the need for acylation make it less practical than synthetic ghrelin mimetics like Ipamorelin or MK-677 for sustained effects.
  -: The reviewed record is animal research and cannot establish human effectiveness or safety.
  -: What 'ghrelin supplements' actually contain.
  -: Whether any meaningful effect occurs from oral ghrelin-pathway products.
  -: Ghrelin pharmacology happens through GHRPs / GLP-1 antagonists - not standalone ghrelin.

  *: PeptideDeck: Primary physiological hunger signal Potent growth hormone release Gastric motility stimulation Potential cachexia/anorexia treatment Metabolic regulation research Energy homeostasis insights GHS receptor pharmacology foundation Reward pathway modulation Active research area with published studies Since its discovery, ghrelin has been extensively studied for appetite regulation and potential therapeutic applications. Studies established ghrelin as the primary pre-meal hunger signal, with levels rising before and falling after meals. Gastric bypass surgery reduces ghrelin by removing producing tissue, contributing to reduced appetite post-surgery. Clinical trials have explored ghrelin and ghrelin mimetics for cachexia (cancer, heart failure, COPD-related wasting), showing ability to increase appetite and food intake. Research in anorexia nervosa has explored whether ghrelin signaling dysfunction contributes to the disease. 7x Quality Tested Bac Water Don't ruin a $300 peptide on generic bac water. ### compound | ghrp-1/overview | What is GHRP-1?
kind: overview
title: GHRP-1
summary: GHRP-1 is a first-generation synthetic growth hormone-releasing peptide (GHRP), a heptapeptide growth hormone secretagogue with the sequence Ala-His-D-2-Nal-Ala-Trp-D-Phe-Lys-NH2 (molecular weight ~955 Da). Derived structurally from met-enkephalin but stripped of opioid activity, it was developed during Cyril Bowers' "reverse pharmacology" program alongside GHRP-2, GHRP-6 and hexarelin. GHRP-1 does not act on the growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH) receptor; instead it is an agonist of the ghrelin/growth hormone secretagogue receptor type 1a (GHS-R1a) on pituitary somatotrophs and hypothalamic neurons, where it amplifies pulsatile growth hormone (GH) release and, downstream, IGF-1 [2][3][7]. In the one published pediatric study, GHRP-1 was given as a single intravenous bolus of ~1 mcg/kg and produced a clear GH rise peaking at 15-30 minutes, comparable to GHRH [1].
keyPoint: GHRP-1 is a first-generation synthetic growth hormone-releasing peptide (GHRP), a heptapeptide growth hormone secretagogue with the sequence Ala-His-D-2-Nal-Ala-Trp-D-Phe-Lys-NH2 (molecular weight ~955 Da).
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: GHRP-1

### compound | ghrp-1/mechanism | How does GHRP-1 work?
kind: overview
title: GHRP-1
summary: GHRP-1 is a first-generation synthetic growth hormone-releasing peptide (GHRP), a heptapeptide growth hormone secretagogue with the sequence Ala-His-D-2-Nal-Ala-Trp-D-Phe-Lys-NH2 (molecular weight ~955 Da). Derived structurally from met-enkephalin but stripped of opioid activity, it was developed during Cyril Bowers' "reverse pharmacology" program alongside GHRP-2, GHRP-6 and hexarelin. GHRP-1 does not act on the growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH) receptor; instead it is an agonist of the ghrelin/growth hormone secretagogue receptor type 1a (GHS-R1a) on pituitary somatotrophs and hypothalamic neurons, where it amplifies pulsatile growth hormone (GH) release and, downstream, IGF-1 [2][3][7]. In the one published pediatric study, GHRP-1 was given as a single intravenous bolus of ~1 mcg/kg and produced a clear GH rise peaking at 15-30 minutes, comparable to GHRH [1].
keyPoint: GHRP-1 is a first-generation synthetic growth hormone-releasing peptide (GHRP), a heptapeptide growth hormone secretagogue with the sequence Ala-His-D-2-Nal-Ala-Trp-D-Phe-Lys-NH2 (molecular weight ~955 Da).

  *: Source rating: 3 out of 5
  *: PeptideDosage.org: Because GHRP-1 activates the ghrelin receptor, it can stimulate appetite and cause a sensation of hunger or fullness; this is a class effect shared with GHRP-6 and GHRP-2 [5][6].; It can produce mild, dose-dependent increases in cortisol and ACTH, especially when a single injection exceeds the ~1 mcg/kg saturating dose, so larger per-dose amounts add stress-hormone activation without proportionally more GH [4][5].; Transient prolactin elevation has been documented for the GHRP super-analogs and may occur with GHRP-1; clinical relevance at low research doses is uncertain [5].; Sustained elevation of GH and IGF-1 carries the general risks of GH excess (fluid retention, peripheral edema, carpal-tunnel-type symptoms, arthralgia, and reduced insulin sensitivity with higher fasting glucose); people with prediabetes or diabetes are at particular risk.; Injection-route effects in the educational subcutaneous model include local redness, swelling, bruising or irritation at the injection site, plus the general risk of non-sterile technique; the only validated human route in the literature is

### compound | ghrp-2/overview | What is GHRP-2?
kind: overview
title: GHRP-2
summary: A synthetic hexapeptide GH secretagogue with the strongest GH-releasing potency in its class. More potent than GHRP-6 with different side effect profile: less appetite stimulation but greater cortisol and prolactin elevation. Approved in Japan as Pralmorelin for GH deficiency diagnosis. Extensively studied in human pharmacology with robust clinical data.
keyPoint: A synthetic hexapeptide GH secretagogue with the strongest GH-releasing potency in its class.

### compound | ghrp-2/evidence | What research is listed for GHRP-2?

summary: Human clinical pharmacology data.

matchedText: GHRP-2
  connectedTo: GHRP-2
section: What the research shows
  -: PepCodex: A synthetic hexapeptide GH secretagogue with the strongest GH-releasing potency in its class.
  -: The Peptide Handbook: A synthetic growth hormone secretagogue studied in controlled human GH-response, diagnostic, and appetite research.
  -: Halflife Labs: GHRP-2 half-life is approximately 15-30 minutes per Bowers et al.
  -: Peptpedia: Among the most potent GHRPs per microgram, with less hunger than GHRP-6.
  -: PeptideDosage.org: GHRP-2 (pralmorelin, D-Ala-D-2-Nal-Ala-Trp-D-Phe-Lys-NH2) is a synthetic hexapeptide growth hormone secretagogue and full agonist at the growth hormone secretagogue receptor type 1a (GHSR1a), the same receptor that endogenous ghrelin engages.
section: Evidence strength
  -: PepCodex: Human clinical research; population: Human; Human evidence with design limitations to check. 18 human studies listed by the source
  -: The Peptide Handbook: Animal research; population: Animal; Preclinical animal evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: Halflife Labs: Source summary; study design not clearly stated; population: Not clearly stated; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: Peptpedia: Source summary; study design not clearly stated; population: Not clearly stated; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: PeptideDosage.org: Source summary; study design not clearly stated; population: Not clearly stated; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Limitations
  -: The reviewed record does not state a specific limitation. The linked paper still needs to be checked for design, size and bias.
  -: Long-term clinical safety and therapeutic outcomes are not established by the cited studies.
  -: The source does not clearly state the study population or design in PEARL's reviewed record.
  -: not support the idea that GHRP-2 enhances slow-wave sleep: a placebo-controlled polysomnography study found evidence against a role for the GHRP axis in human slow-wave sleep, despite the temporal correlation between deep sleep and nocturnal GH secretion.
  -: not establish GHRP-2 as a sleep-enhancing agent.
  -: not GHRH or TRH - markedly synchronized the serum profiles of all three hormones (all P<=0.
  -: not produce a meaningful enhancement of slow-wave sleep, providing evidence against a causal role for the GHRP axis in human slow-wave sleep.
  -: not reflect a direct GHRP-driven promotion of deep sleep-an important caution against assuming GHRP-2 improves sleep quality.
  -: not approved for therapeutic GH replacement use anywhere.
  -: not support this.
  -: not meaningfully increase deep sleep.
  -: GHRP-2 (pralmorelin, D-Ala-D-2-Nal-Ala-Trp-D-Phe-Lys-NH2) is a synthetic hexapeptide growth hormone secretagogue and full agonist at the growth hormone secretagogue receptor type 1a (GHSR1a), the same receptor that endogenous ghrelin engages.
  *: Source rating: 3 out of 5
  *: PepCodex: Moderate evidence; 18 human studies listed
  *: The Peptide Handbook: moderate. GHRP-2 has controlled human endocrine and diagnostic research, including GH-response studies and adult GH-deficiency testing; one cited study reported increased food intake in healthy men. The published evidence in this record does not establish a preferred therapeutic use, chronic safety, anti-aging benefit, body-composition outcome, or recommendation-style dosing.
  *: Halflife Labs: Evidence context is stated on the linked compound page.
  *: PeptideDosage.org: Acute increase in subjective appetite within 15-30 minutes of injection is common, mediated by hypothalamic ghrelin-receptor activation; effect is milder than GHRP-6 but still notable, with 30-50% of users reporting hunger.; Mild prolactin elevation (10-20% above baseline) occurs at doses above 200 mcg subcutaneous, less prominent than with hexarelin but more than with ipamorelin; symptomatic galactorrhoea is rare but documented at chronic high doses.; Cortisol and ACTH elevations of 10-30% over baseline occur at supratherapeutic doses (>300 mcg per pulse); these are clinically silent in most subjects but warrant caution in those with adrenal disease or on corticosteroid therapy.; Transient flushing, warmth and mild headache within 30 minutes of injection occur in roughly 20% of users and reflect vasodilation from the GHSR1a engagement; tolerance develops within 1-2 weeks.; Mild glucose intolerance with HbA1c rise of 0.1-0.3% can develop with chronic dosing; the mechanism is the GH-mediated reduction in peripheral insulin sensitivity rather than a direct GHSR1a effect.;
  *: PeptideDeck: Strong growth hormone release More moderate appetite stimulation than GHRP-6 Enhanced recovery from exercise and injury Improved sleep quality Potential anti-aging effects from GH elevation Supports lean mass gains Approved medication in Japan (diagnostic use) Effective in GHRH combination stacks GHRP-2 has solid research backing its effects on GH release, body composition, and sleep. Research comparing GHRP-2 to GHRH and other secretagogues established its relative potency. Studies in healthy adults showed robust GH peaks, and in elderly subjects (where GH response often diminishes), GHRP-2 still produced meaningful release-important for anti-aging applications. Studies on GHRP-2 and sleep, published in the American Journal of Physiology , documented improvements in sleep architecture. The peptide increased slow-wave sleep, aligning with the expected effects of enhanced nighttime GH release.
  *: Effects of GHRP-2 and Hexarelin on GH, Prolactin, ACTH and Cortisol in Man (Peptides 1997): GHRP-2 and hexarelin both stimulated GH release in men. Also elevated prolactin, ACTH, and cortisol - establishing the hormonal side-effect profile of this class.

kind: evidence
title: GHRP-6: research listed by the sources

understood: resolved
method: canonical

matchedText: GHRP-6
  connectedTo: GHRP-6
section: What the research shows
  -: PepCodex: A first-generation growth hormone secretagogue that stimulates GH release through the ghrelin receptor.
  -: The Peptide Handbook: A growth hormone-releasing peptide studied for its ability to stimulate growth hormone secretion and, notably, to strongly stimulate appetite - a property that has attracted research interest in muscle wasting and cachexia contexts.
  -: Halflife Labs: Pharmacokinetic reference for GHRP-6 covering half-life (animal data), GH pulse duration, cortisol/prolactin effects, appetite stimulation mechanism, three-layer PK model, and in-class comparison with ipamorelin.
  -: Peptpedia: The first synthetic GH secretagogue - potent GH release plus strong appetite stimulation and cortisol/prolactin effects.
  -: PeptideDosage.org: GHRP-6 (His-D-Trp-Ala-Trp-D-Phe-Lys-NH2) is a synthetic hexapeptide growth hormone secretagogue and the first non-natural GHSR1a agonist with documented potent appetite-stimulating activity.
section: Evidence strength
  -: PepCodex: Human clinical research; population: Human; Human evidence with design limitations to check. 12 human studies listed by the source
  -: The Peptide Handbook: Laboratory or mechanistic research; population: Not clearly stated; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: Halflife Labs: Source summary; study design not clearly stated; population: Not clearly stated; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: Peptpedia: Source summary; study design not clearly stated; population: Animal model; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: PeptideDosage.org: Laboratory or mechanistic research; population: Laboratory; Early laboratory evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Limitations
  -: The reviewed record does not state a specific limitation. The linked paper still needs to be checked for design, size and bias.
  -: Experimental endocrine and appetite effects have been reported; long-term safety and clinical outcomes have not been established
  -: The source does not clearly state the study population or design in PEARL's reviewed record.
  -: No approved clinical indication exists as of 2026.
  -: not significantly elevating systemic GH.
  -: no human cardiac trials for GHRP-6 have been published.
  -: not medical advice, and the compounds covered are research chemicals not approved for human use unless explicitly stated otherwise.
  -: GHRP-6 (His-D-Trp-Ala-Trp-D-Phe-Lys-NH2) is a synthetic hexapeptide growth hormone secretagogue and the first non-natural GHSR1a agonist with documented potent appetite-stimulating activity.
  *: Source rating: 3 out of 5
  *: PepCodex: Moderate evidence; 12 human studies listed
  *: The Peptide Handbook: preliminary. Experimental studies in healthy men found that the GHRP-6 sequence can stimulate growth-hormone secretion, and preclinical work supports a receptor mechanism distinct from GHRH. These observations are historical and mechanistic; they do not establish clinical efficacy, long-term safety, or a use protocol.
  *: Halflife Labs: Evidence context is stated on the linked compound page.
  *: PeptideDosage.org: Prominent acute appetite stimulation within 15-30 minutes of injection is the defining adverse effect, with 60-80% of users reporting marked hunger; this is therapeutic in cachexia contexts but problematic for weight-management goals.; Mild prolactin elevation (10-20% above baseline) occurs at therapeutic doses; symptomatic galactorrhoea is rare but documented with chronic high-dose protocols.; Cortisol and ACTH rise modestly (10-25% above baseline), less than GHRP-2 but more than ipamorelin; clinically silent in most subjects.; Lethargy and somnolence after evening dosing are common and reflect the natural sleep-promoting GH-pulse effect plus ghrelin-receptor effects on hypothalamic sleep architecture.; Mild glucose intolerance with HbA1c rise of 0.1-0.3% can develop with chronic dosing; the effect is GH-mediated reduction in peripheral insulin sensitivity rather than direct GHSR1a action.; Transient flushing, warmth and mild headache within 30 minutes of injection occur in approximately 15% of users and reflect vasodilation from GHSR1a engagement.; Tachyphylaxis develops with
  *: PeptideDeck: Strong growth hormone release Significant appetite stimulation (useful for gaining weight) Enhanced recovery from training Improved sleep quality Potential anti-aging effects from elevated GH/IGF-1 May support joint and tissue healing Increased protein synthesis Cardioprotective effects in some research GHRP-6 has accumulated substantial research as one of the pioneering GH secretagogues. Multiple studies confirm GHRP-6 effectively releases GH in humans. Research published in the European Journal of Endocrinology demonstrated potent, specific GH release in healthy men and women. The response is dose-dependent, with higher doses producing greater GH peaks (though with more side effects). Interesting research published in Peptides demonstrated cardioprotective effects of GHRP-6 in heart failure and ischemia models. The peptide reduced damage from heart attacks and improved cardiac function in animal studies. This suggests benefits beyond simple GH elevation, possibly through direct effects on cardiac tissue.
  *: GHRPs Cytoprotective Effects: Historical Review (PMC 2017): GHRP-6 IV safe in dose-escalation trial. Cardioprotective properties established.

### compound | ghrp4/overview | What is GHRP-4?
kind: overview
title: GHRP-4
summary: From Wikipep - The Peptide Encyclopedia GHRP-4 Chemical name Growth Hormone Releasing Peptide-4 Molecular formula C₄₆H₅₆N₁₂O₆ Molecular weight ~869 Da CAS number 158861-67-7 Sequence D-Trp-D-Phe-Lys-Trp-D-Phe-Lys Length 6 amino acids Source Synthetic Half-life 15-30 minutes Targets Ghrelin receptor (GHS-R1a), hypothalamus, pituitary somatotrophs Bioavailability Subcutaneous/intramuscular Legal status Research compound (unscheduled) GHRP-4 ( Growth Hormone Releasing Peptide-4 ) is a synthetic hexapeptide growth hormone secretagogue (GHS) that stimulates the release of growth hormone (GH) from the anterior pituitary gland by activating the ghrelin receptor (GHS-R1a) . Developed as part of the GHRP peptide family pioneered by Cyril Bowers in the 1980s, GHRP-4 shares the core D-amino acid-containing hexapeptide structure common to all GHRPs but with specific substitutions that modulate its receptor binding kinetics and GH release profile.

### compound | gip/overview | What is GIP?
kind: overview
title: GIP
summary: An endogenous incretin hormone secreted after meals that stimulates insulin release, though its effect is blunted in type 2 diabetes. GIP receptor biology underlies the design of tirzepatide, a separate FDA-approved dual-agonist drug; this entry describes native GIP itself, not that drug's clinical outcomes.
keyPoint: An endogenous incretin hormone secreted after meals that stimulates insulin release, though its effect is blunted in type 2 diabetes.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: GIP
  connectedTo: GIP
section: Why it is researched
  -: An endogenous incretin hormone secreted after meals that stimulates insulin release, though its effect is blunted in type 2 diabetes.
section: How it works in the research
  -: Glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) is a 42-amino-acid incretin hormone (calculated MW ≈4,983.6 Da) secreted by duodenal and jejunal K-cells in response to nutrient ingestion.

  -: The Peptide Handbook: Human clinical research; population: Human; Human evidence with design limitations to check. The source does not give a reliable study count.

  -: Not applicable as a standalone compound; see Tirzepatide entry for therapeutic risk profile
