### compound | gip/evidence | What research is listed for GIP?
kind: evidence
title: GIP: research listed by the sources
summary: strong-human. Native GIP's insulinotropic physiology is well documented in direct human studies: IV GIP stimulates insulin secretion in both healthy volunteers and people with type 2 diabetes, though its effect is markedly blunted in type 2 diabetes, and it does not potentiate GLP-1's glucose-lowering effect when co-infused. This blunted native activity is why GIP was historically deprioritized as a monotherapy target. The discovery that GIPR agonism in adipose tissue can enhance GLP-1 receptor sensitivity motivated development of tirzepatide, a distinct FDA-approved dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist drug; tirzepatide's own clinical trial results (e.g., SURPASS, SURMOUNT) describe that separate drug product and are documented in its own entry, not transferred here to native GIP. ### compound | glandokort/overview | What is Glandokort?
kind: overview
title: Glandokort
summary: Glandokort (also sold as Adrenal Cytomax A-17) is an oral peptide bioregulator from Vladimir Khavinson's "cytomax" family, manufactured from purified bovine adrenal-cortex tissue at the St. Petersburg Institute of Bioregulation and Gerontology lineage of products [1]. As a cytomax it is a lyophilized complex of short, low-molecular-weight peptide fragments rather than a single synthetic sequence, and within the Khavinson framework it is proposed to act as a tissue-specific epigenetic regulator that supports the adrenal cortex and its output of cortisol, aldosterone, and adrenal androgens such as DHEA [1][2]. The standard Glandokort dosage is 20 mg per day, taken as two 10 mg capsules (1-2 capsules, 1-2 times daily) roughly 15-30 minutes before food, for a 30-day course that is typically repeated every 3-6 months, often with a shorter 10-day maintenance pulse.

### compound | glandokort/evidence | What research is listed for Glandokort?
kind: evidence
title: Glandokort: research listed by the sources
summary: The clinical route is oral capsules; the most commonly listed issues are individual intolerance or hypersensitivity to the adrenal peptide complex or to the excipients (methylcellulose capsule, microcrystalline cellulose, calcium stearate).; Manufacturer contraindications are pregnancy, breastfeeding, and known individual intolerance to any component; the product has not been studied in children.; Because Glandokort is intended to modulate the adrenal/HPA axis, people with primary adrenal disease (for example Addison's or Cushing's), those on corticosteroid therapy, or anyone on cortisol-affecting medication should not self-treat and should involve a clinician.; As a bovine tissue-derived preparation, individuals with beef or bovine-protein allergy should review the specific product composition before use.; The educational subcutaneous route introduces injection-specific risks that capsules do not: injection-site pain, bruising, redness, lipohypertrophy, and infection if sterile technique is not followed.; No GLP-grade toxicology, carcinogenicity, or controlled drug-interaction data

### compound | glepaglutide/overview | What is Glepaglutide?
kind: overview
title: Glepaglutide
summary: Glepaglutide (developmental code ZP1848) is a long-acting glucagon-like peptide-2 (GLP-2) receptor agonist, a synthetic analogue of the 33-amino-acid human gut hormone GLP-2, developed by Zealand Pharma to treat short bowel syndrome (SBS) with intestinal failure. By activating GLP-2 receptors on intestinal subepithelial cells and enteric neurons it drives mucosal growth, slows gastric emptying and increases intestinal blood flow, improving the absorption of fluid and nutrients so patients can reduce their dependence on parenteral (intravenous) support. Its defining feature is protraction: amino-acid modifications and a self-assembling subcutaneous depot give an effective half-life of roughly 88 hours, enabling once- or twice-weekly injection rather than the daily dosing required by the approved GLP-2 analogue teduglutide.

### compound | glepaglutide/evidence | What research is listed for Glepaglutide?
kind: evidence
title: Glepaglutide: research listed by the sources
summary: Gastrointestinal effects are the most common: nausea, abdominal pain, abdominal distension and vomiting were each reported in more than 20% of patients in Phase 2, reflecting the trophic and motility actions of GLP-2 on the gut [2].; Stoma-related complications occurred more often with active drug, and more frequently at higher dosing frequency (about 41% with twice-weekly vs 25% with once-weekly vs 0% with placebo in the stoma subgroup of the Phase 3 trial); stoma output, edema and bleeding warrant monitoring [1].; Fluid handling can shift as absorption improves: peripheral edema, polyuria and fluid overload were observed, requiring parenteral-support volumes to be down-titrated carefully to avoid over- or under-hydration [1][2].; As a class effect, GLP-2 receptor agonists stimulate intestinal growth, so there is a theoretical risk of accelerating colorectal polyps or neoplasia; the labeling for the approved analogue teduglutide requires baseline and periodic colonoscopy/imaging, a precaution that applies to investigational GLP-2 agonists [5].; GLP-2 agonism is also associated with Published human phase 2 and phase 3 trials. In the 106-participant phase 3 trial, 10 mg twice weekly reduced parenteral-support volume significantly versus placebo; the once-weekly arm did not show a statistically significant advantage on the primary endpoint.

TB-500 is the synthetic fragment of thymosin beta-4 comprising amino acids 17-23 (Ac-LKKTETQ), which contains the actin-binding domain responsible for most biological effects. Cleared primarily via proteolytic degradation. No published human PK data as of May 2026.

### compound | glp-2/overview | What is GLP-2?
kind: overview
title: GLP-2
summary: From Wikipep - The Peptide Encyclopedia GLP-2 Chemical name Glucagon-Like Peptide-2 Molecular formula C₁₅₅H₂₄₉N₄₃O₄₆S Molecular weight 3765.5 g/mol CAS number 125441-19-6 Sequence HADGSFSDEMNTILDNLAARDFINWLIQTKITD Length 33 amino acids Source Intestinal L-cells (proglucagon processing) Half-life ~7 minutes Targets GLP-2 receptor Bioavailability Endogenous (rapidly degraded by DPP-4) Legal status Endogenous hormone Glucagon-Like Peptide-2 ( GLP-2 ) is a 33-amino acid peptide hormone produced by intestinal L-cells through post-translational processing of proglucagon by prohormone convertase 1/3. It is the primary intestinotrophic hormone in humans, uniquely responsible for stimulating intestinal mucosal growth, enhancing nutrient absorption, and maintaining gut barrier integrity. GLP-2 is co-secreted with GLP-1 in response to nutrient ingestion, particularly fats and carbohydrates.

### compound | glp1/overview | What is Retatrutide (GLP-1/GIP/Glucagon)?
kind: overview
title: Retatrutide (GLP-1/GIP/Glucagon)
summary: GLP-3 class peptides are triple receptor agonists targeting GLP-1, GIP, and glucagon receptors simultaneously. Adding glucagon receptor activation to the dual GLP-1/GIP mechanism introduces a third lever: glucagon signaling increases energy expenditure and hepatic fat metabolism, which further amplifies the fat-reduction signal beyond what dual agonists achieve. The three receptor pathways work synergistically across the brain, liver, pancreas, and adipose tissue. Phase 2 clinical research on triple agonists showed mean body weight reduction of 24.2% at 48 weeks, with participants still losing weight at study end - indicating a plateau had not yet been reached. Phase 3 data has since reported up to 28.7% weight loss. The glucagon component also increases energy expenditure, which researchers propose may explain the energy and cognitive benefits often reported alongside weight reduction. Gastrointestinal tolerability is generally comparable to dual agonists.
keyPoint: GLP-3 class peptides are triple receptor agonists targeting GLP-1, GIP, and glucagon receptors simultaneously.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high

  *: The insulin-secretory effect of GLP-1 is strictly glucose-dependent . This is because: Beta-cell depolarization requires glucose metabolism to generate ATP and close K_ATP channels GLP-1/cAMP signaling amplifies the existing depolarization but cannot initiate it independently At normal or low blood glucose levels (<4. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Pancreatitis: Post-marketing reports of acute pancreatitis; FDA-required label warning. Causality debated but vigilance recommended. Discontinue if pancreatitis suspected Thyroid C-cell tumors: GLP-1 receptor agonists cause dose-dependent thyroid C-cell hyperplasia and medullary thyroid carcinoma in rodents. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia syndrome type 2 History of severe hypersensitivity to the specific GLP-1R agonist Severe gastroparesis. [source-listed source severity]

### compound | glp1native/evidence | What research is listed for GLP-1 (Native)?
kind: evidence
title: GLP-1 (Native): research listed by the sources
summary: strong-human. Native GLP-1(7-36)NH2's incretin physiology is established across direct human studies: infusion stimulates glucose-dependent insulin secretion and suppresses glucagon, and antagonist studies (exendin 9-39) confirm its physiological role in postprandial glucose control. Unlike GIP, native GLP-1's insulinotropic effect is preserved in type 2 diabetes. Its short (~1-2 minute) plasma half-life due to DPP-4 cleavage was the central pharmacological problem solved by DPP-4-resistant analogs. This entry is an educational reference for native GLP-1 physiology; the cardiovascular, renal, and long-term efficacy outcomes associated with GLP-1 receptor agonist drugs are documented in those drugs' own entries and are not evidence about the native hormone itself.

### compound | glp2native/evidence | What research is listed for GLP-2 (Native)?
kind: evidence
title: GLP-2 (Native): research listed by the sources
summary: moderate. GLP-2 is one of the proglucagon-derived peptides (with GLP-1 and glucagon), discovered as an intestinotrophic hormone by Daniel Drucker's group. Direct human evidence for native GLP-2 is modest in scale: a small acute-infusion study in healthy volunteers showed increased intestinal blood flow, and a small (11-patient) short bowel syndrome cohort treated for two years with native GLP-2 showed reduced fecal losses and maintained absorption in the 8 patients who completed the study, alongside transient GI discomfort in about half. These are small, largely uncontrolled human studies - informative but not sufficient to establish native GLP-2 as an approved or broadly effective therapy. The clinically approved therapy in this space, teduglutide (a DPP-4-resistant GLP-2 analog), is a distinct drug product developed using the mechanistic insight from native GLP-2 research; its approval and outcomes data do not transfer to native GLP-2 itself.

  -: The Peptide Handbook: Human clinical research; population: Human; Human evidence with design limitations to check. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Limitations
  -: Not applicable as standalone compound; see Teduglutide entry for therapeutic risk profile

### compound | glucagonpeptide/evidence | What research is listed for Glucagon Peptide?
kind: evidence
title: Glucagon Peptide: research listed by the sources
summary: Glucagon is the metabolic counterweight to insulin. While insulin lowers blood glucose, glucagon raises it. This 29-amino-acid peptide hormone, secreted by pancreatic alpha cells, maintains blood sugar stability between meals and prevents dangerous hypoglycemia. Glucagon is the metabolic counterbalance to insulin. This 29-amino-acid pancreatic hormone raises blood glucose when it drops too low, preventing hypoglycemia and maintaining fuel supply to the brain. Clinically, it is the first-line emergency treatment for severe hypoglycemia in people with diabetes, available in injectable and nasal formulations that have made administration faster and simpler. But glucagon's role extends beyond emergency rescue. It is a member of the proglucagon peptide family, sharing a genetic origin with GLP-1 and GLP-2, yet serving distinct physiological functions. And in recent years, glucagon has become a key player in next-generation metabolic therapies.

  *: The Peptide Handbook: preliminary. Glutathione's endogenous redox biology is extremely well established, but therapeutic-administration evidence is indication- and formulation-specific. A small open-label study (n=9) of IV glutathione in early Parkinson's disease reported symptom changes over 30 days without a placebo comparator - suggestive, not definitive. A historical randomized trial found IV/IM glutathione reduced cisplatin-induced neurotoxicity in a specific chemotherapy protocol for advanced gastric cancer - evidence specific to that regimen and population, not general chemoprotection. A subsequent review characterizes the Parkinson's disease evidence base as still limited. No citation supporting NAFLD or male-infertility efficacy claims was identified despite a targeted search, and those claims have been removed rather than carried forward unsupported. Oral bioavailability remains limited by intestinal hydrolysis.

Glutathione Peptide: Benefits, Dosage and Side Effects (2026) Procurement Embody Glutathione Ships from USA Start Glutathione Treatment Your body makes its own antioxidant. Glutathione is a tripeptide produced naturally in every cell, and it's the most abundant intracellular antioxidant in the human body. The problem is levels decline significantly with age, stress, illness, and alcohol use. By middle age, most people are running on roughly half the glutathione they had at 20. Supplementing directly or supporting the body's production is one of the most evidence-backed interventions in the antioxidant space. This guide covers the benefits, the forms that actually work, the right doses, and what to watch for.

### compound | gonadorelin/mechanism | How does Gonadorelin work?
kind: overview
title: Gonadorelin
summary: A synthetic version of GnRH - the natural hormone produced by the hypothalamus to regulate the reproductive hormone axis. Historical human evidence includes diagnostic and pulsatile-treatment contexts for hypogonadotropic hypogonadism; it does not establish a current U.S. marketed human product or a general TRT-adjunct use.

  *: Source rating: 4 out of 5
  *: The Peptide Handbook: strong-human. Historical human studies support pulsatile GnRH administration and diagnostic/treatment contexts in hypogonadotropic hypogonadism. This record does not support claims that twice-weekly gonadorelin preserves fertility or testicular function during testosterone therapy, or that it is superior to hCG.
  *: Halflife Labs: Evidence context is stated on the linked compound page.
  *: PeptideDosage.org: Gonadorelin is exceptionally well tolerated; the most commonly reported adverse events are mild injection-site discomfort, transient erythema, and infrequent headache, flushing, or nausea.; Rare hypersensitivity reactions including urticaria, bronchospasm, and anaphylaxis have been reported with parenteral gonadorelin; patients with known peptide hypersensitivity should be evaluated before initiation.; Pulsatile pump therapy can cause local skin reactions at the subcutaneous catheter site, occasional infections, and rarely sterile abscesses; rotation of infusion sites mitigates these risks.; Continuous (rather than pulsatile) GnRH exposure produces paradoxical pituitary desensitization and suppression of LH and FSH secretion, which is the basis for long-acting GnRH analog therapy in prostate cancer and endometriosis but is not the goal of gonadorelin therapy.; Theoretical risks of low-dose adjunctive gonadorelin in TRT include incomplete preservation of fertility, variable testicular response, and the absence of formal long-term safety data in this off-label context.; Gonadorelin
  *: PeptideDeck: Stimulates natural LH and FSH production Restores testosterone production (pulsatile use) FDA-approved for diagnostic and fertility uses Natural hormone sequence (exact match to endogenous GnRH) Useful for PCT to restore HPTA function Does not directly suppress natural hormones (vs hCG) Maintains testicular function during TRT (research) Diagnostic tool for pituitary function Active research area with published studies Gonadorelin research spans reproductive endocrinology, fertility treatment, and more recently, PCT protocols. Interest in gonadorelin for post-cycle therapy has grown as alternatives to hCG are sought. The rationale: after anabolic steroid use, the HPTA is suppressed at multiple levels. Gonadorelin, by stimulating the pituitary, may help restore the entire axis rather than just testicular function. Research protocols have explored gonadorelin alone or in combination with SERMs (selective estrogen receptor modulators) for PCT. Results are promising but protocols aren't standardized.
  *: WikiPep: Sperm Production : Maintains or restores spermatogenesis Testicular Function : Preserves Leydig and Sertoli cell activity Fertility Preservation : Critical for men wanting to maintain fertility Recovery Enhancement : Faster restoration of reproductive function Delivery Systems : Development of improved administration methods Combination Therapies : Research on synergistic combinations Personalized Medicine : Genetic factors affecting response Long-term Studies : Extended safety and efficacy evaluations Endocrine Research : Studies on HPG axis function Reproductive Biology : Investigation of fertility mechanisms Aging Research : Studies on hormone decline and restoration Therapeutic Development : New applications and protocols [ 1 ] [ 2 ] [ 3 ] [ 4 ] [ 5 ] ↑ 1.0 1.1 Knobil E, et al.   *: Pulsatile gonadotropin-releasing hormone treatment of men with idiopathic hypogonadotropic hypogonadism (Hormone Research 2002): Christiansen and Skakkebaek demonstrated that pulsatile GnRH (gonadorelin) therapy restored testosterone, LH, FSH, and spermatogenesis in men with idiopathic hypogonadotropic hypogonadism - establishing the clinical basis for pulsatile GnRH as a fertility-preserving testosterone restoration strategy.

### compound | gotratix/overview | What is Gotratix?
kind: overview
title: Gotratix
summary: Gotratix (also sold as Muscle Cytomax and labeled A-18) is an oral skeletal-muscle peptide bioregulator from the Khavinson "Cytomax" family, developed within Vladimir Khavinson's peptide-regulation program at the St. Petersburg Institute of Bioregulation and Gerontology. Its active ingredient is peptide complex A-18, a low-molecular-weight peptide fraction extracted from the triceps muscle of young calves (under 11 months). Like other Khavinson bioregulators, it is hypothesized to act not as a hormone but as a tissue-specific signal that enters the cell nucleus and modulates expression of muscle genes governing protein synthesis, satellite-cell activity, and mitochondrial function [1][2]. Manufacturers market it to support muscle recovery, reduce fatigue under heavy training, and counter age-related muscle loss, though no peer-reviewed human trials of Gotratix itself have been published.
keyPoint: Gotratix (also sold as Muscle Cytomax and labeled A-18) is an oral skeletal-muscle peptide bioregulator from the Khavinson "Cytomax" family, developed within Vladimir Khavinson's peptide-regulation program at the St.

### compound | gotratix/safety | What are the risks of Gotratix?
kind: safety
title: Gotratix: source-listed risks
summary: Source-listed risks only. Missing human safety data does not mean a compound is safe.
keyPoint: Source-listed risks only.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: Gotratix
  connectedTo: Gotratix
  *: Mild transient muscle soreness in first cycle days - as myocyte metabolic activity and protein synthesis increase in response to bioregulator stimulation, some subjects report mild muscle soreness in the first 2-3 days; similar to DOMS but not exercise-induced; resolves within the first week. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Mild fatigue on initiation - the metabolic demands of muscle gene program activation impose a transient energy cost; mild fatigue in days 1-3 is occasionally reported; resolves rapidly. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Mild gastrointestinal discomfort - as an oral cytomedin taken with meals; occasional mild gastric discomfort in first days; resolves with continued administration. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Injection site - not applicable (oral route). [source-listed source severity]
  *: Mild increased appetite in early cycle days - as muscle metabolic rate normalizes and protein synthesis gene programs activate, a mild increase in appetite is reported by some subjects; reflects increased anabolic energy demand; not a safety concern. [source-listed source severity]
  *: No serious musculoskeletal adverse events documented in the Khavinson research literature at standard protocol doses - Gotratix's safety profile in athletes, sarcopenic elderly subjects, and post-surgical populations is clean; no myotoxicity, rhabdomyolysis, or serious muscle pathology has been attributed to Gotratix. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Unknown interaction profile with statin therapy - statins produce myopathy as a dose-dependent adverse effect through mitochondrial CoQ10 depletion and myocyte metabolic disruption; Gotratix's mitochondrial biogenesis normalization activity in myocytes could theoretically partially counteract statin myopathy; not. [source-listed source severity]

### compound | gotratix/evidence | What research is listed for Gotratix?
kind: evidence
title: Gotratix: research listed by the sources
summary: No controlled human safety data exist for Gotratix specifically; the manufacturer describes a strong safety record, but the points below are extrapolated from the Khavinson bioregulator class and general peptide-supplement use.; Taken as intended (orally), the most plausible adverse effects are mild gastrointestinal upset, nausea, or allergic reaction; because the product is bovine-tissue-derived, anyone with a beef or bovine-protein allergy should avoid it.; As an animal-tissue extract rather than a defined synthetic peptide, batch-to-batch composition and purity cannot be assumed, and theoretical concerns about contaminants in bovine-derived material apply.; For the educational subcutaneous model only: injecting peptide solution can cause local redness, swelling, bruising, or pain, and any injected peptide carries a theoretical risk of hypersensitivity or immune reaction. Peptide University labels its records as aggregated from empirical research and anecdotal community data. This record is retained as supplied and is not upgraded to clinical evidence.
keyPoint: No controlled human safety data exist for Gotratix specifically; the manufacturer describes a strong safety record, but the points below are extrapolated from the Khavinson bioregulator class and general peptide-supplement use.; Taken as...
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: Gotratix
  connectedTo: Gotratix
section: What the research shows
  -: PeptideDosage.org: Gotratix (also sold as Muscle Cytomax and labeled A-18) is an oral skeletal-muscle peptide bioregulator from the Khavinson "Cytomax" family, developed within Vladimir Khavinson's peptide-regulation program at the St.
  -: Peptide University Codex: Gotratix is a Khavinson cytomedin - peptide complex A-18 - extracted from skeletal muscle tissue of young animals, developed at the St.
section: Evidence strength
  -: PeptideDosage.org: Systematic review or meta-analysis; population: Animal; Preclinical animal evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: Peptide University Codex: Source summary; study design not clearly stated; population: Animal; Preclinical animal evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Limitations
  -: Gotratix (also sold as Muscle Cytomax and labeled A-18) is an oral skeletal-muscle peptide bioregulator from the Khavinson "Cytomax" family, developed within Vladimir Khavinson's peptide-regulation program at the St. Petersburg Institute of Bioregulation and Gerontology.
  -: Rhabdomyolysis in active phase - myocyte bioregulator activity during active skeletal muscle destruction is not characterized; medical management of acute rhabdomyolysis takes priority.
  -: Inflammatory myopathies in active flare (polymyositis, dermatomyositis) - skeletal muscle cell gene program normalization during active autoimmune myositis has not been evaluated; immunosuppressive management takes priority.
  -: Skeletal muscle malignancy (rhabdomyosarcoma) - myocyte gene program normalization in the context of malignant muscle cells is contraindicated.
  -: Known hypersensitivity to Gotratix (skeletal muscle tissue cytomedin peptide complex A-18) or formulation excipients including gelatin.
  -: Pregnancy - skeletal muscle metabolic changes during pregnancy are hormonally regulated; exogenous muscle bioregulator activity has not been evaluated in this context.
  -: Duchenne or Becker muscular dystrophy in severe stage - the dystrophin-deficiency-related structural skeletal muscle failure in advanced DMD/BMD creates a context where bioregulator gene program normalization of surviving myocytes has not been characterized.
  *: Source rating: 1 out of 5, very limited evidence

  *: PeptideDosage.org: Local injection-site reactions including pain, erythema, and bruising are the most common adverse effects of subcutaneous or intramuscular hCG; rotation of injection sites and use of insulin syringes for SC administration improve tolerability.; Headache, fatigue, irritability, gynecomastia, water retention, and acne may occur in men using hCG, reflecting increased testosterone and downstream estradiol production through testicular aromatization; concurrent aromatase inhibition with anastrozole can mitigate estrogen-related effects.; In women undergoing ovulation induction, hCG can contribute to ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (OHSS), a potentially serious complication characterized by ovarian enlargement, ascites, hemoconcentration, and rarely thromboembolism; OHSS risk increases with higher hCG doses and in patients with polycystic ovary syndrome.; Rare hypersensitivity reactions including urticaria, angioedema, and anaphylaxis have been reported with both urinary-derived and recombinant hCG; patients with prior reactions should be evaluated before subsequent use.;

### compound | healthyhairskinnailshhb/overview | What is Healthy Hair Skin and Nails Blend (HHB)?
kind: overview
title: Healthy Hair Skin and Nails Blend (HHB)
summary: The Healthy Hair Skin and Nails Blend (product code HHB) is a beauty and wellness injection built from a full panel of B-vitamins plus biotin and folic acid to support the health of hair, skin, and nails. It is a vitamin blend rather than a peptide, working through nutritional cofactor support, and given as a fixed direct dose with no titration. Each milliliter contains Niacinamide 50mg, Thiamine HCl (B1) 50mg, Pantothenic Acid (B5) 25mg, Choline 10mg, Inositol 10mg, Niacin (B3) 5mg, Biotin 100mcg, Folic Acid 100mcg, and Riboflavin (B2) 100mcg. Biotin is the signature ingredient for keratin production and hair and nail strength, the B-vitamin panel supports skin health, cellular turnover, and energy metabolism, niacinamide and niacin support skin barrier function and circulation, folic acid supports cell division, and choline and inositol support general metabolic health.
keyPoint: The Healthy Hair Skin and Nails Blend (product code HHB) is a beauty and wellness injection built from a full panel of B-vitamins plus biotin and folic acid to support the health of hair, skin, and nails.

title: Healthy Hair Skin and Nails Blend (HHB)
summary: The Healthy Hair Skin and Nails Blend (product code HHB) is a beauty and wellness injection built from a full panel of B-vitamins plus biotin and folic acid to support the health of hair, skin, and nails. It is a vitamin blend rather than a peptide, working through nutritional cofactor support, and given as a fixed direct dose with no titration. Each milliliter contains Niacinamide 50mg, Thiamine HCl (B1) 50mg, Pantothenic Acid (B5) 25mg, Choline 10mg, Inositol 10mg, Niacin (B3) 5mg, Biotin 100mcg, Folic Acid 100mcg, and Riboflavin (B2) 100mcg. Biotin is the signature ingredient for keratin production and hair and nail strength, the B-vitamin panel supports skin health, cellular turnover, and energy metabolism, niacinamide and niacin support skin barrier function and circulation, folic acid supports cell division, and choline and inositol support general metabolic health.

title: Hepcidin: research listed by the sources
summary: Master Iron Regulator : Controls dietary iron absorption, macrophage iron recycling, and hepatocyte iron storage Disease Biomarker : Hepcidin levels diagnostic/prognostic for iron disorders, anemia of inflammation, and chronic kidney disease Therapeutic Target : Both hepcidin agonists (for iron overload) and antagonists (for anemia of inflammation) are in clinical development Evolutionary Conserved : Present in all vertebrates from zebrafish to humans, underscoring fundamental importance Connects Iron to Immunity : Explains the ancient link between infection, inflammation, and iron metabolism Biomarker : Serum hepcidin measurement (ELISA/mass spectrometry) used in iron disorder diagnosis, CKD anemia management, and athletic monitoring Nutritional Immunity : Understanding how pathogens evade hepcidin-mediated iron restriction (siderophore systems) Cancer : Tumor-derived hepcidin may contribute to cancer-associated anemia; ferroptosis (iron-dependent cell death) connects to hepcidin biology COVID-19 : Hyperferritinemia and elevated hepcidin observed in severe COVID-19; may contribute

  connectedTo: Hepcidin
  *: Resolved: site-listed dose ranges. Published study protocols with species, route, population, frequency and duration take priority. Uncited commercial ranges remain labelled and secondary. A product or calculator range is not evidence that a dose was studied, effective or safe. Confidence: high.
  *: Resolved: modelled administration routes. Use only the route stated in the original study or official product information. Do not convert an oral, intranasal, intramuscular or investigational product into a generic subcutaneous vial protocol. PeptideDosage.org applies a common reconstitution and syringe format even to products such as Ventfort that it identifies as oral. That format is not evidence that the modelled route was studied or is suitable. Confidence: high.

Keep only links whose NCBI record matches the stated research subject. NCBI identifies PMID 11157505 as a Hodgkin-disease cell-fusion paper, PMID 16640009 as a Freeman-Sheldon syndrome case report, and PMID 18677858 as a neonatal-mortality paper. None supports the peptide claim beside which it appeared. Confidence: high.

kind: overview
title: Hexapeptide-11
summary: From Wikipep - The Peptide Encyclopedia Hexapeptide-11 Chemical name Hexapeptide-11 (Myristoyl Hexapeptide-11) Molecular formula C₄₂H₇₆N₈O₉ (approximate, myristoylated form) Molecular weight ~837 Da (myristoylated form) CAS number 936544-53-5 Sequence Proprietary 6-amino acid sequence Length 6 amino acids (+ myristoyl lipid modification) Source Synthetic Half-life Topical application (not systemically absorbed) Targets Collagen synthesis, ECM remodeling, fibroblast activation Bioavailability Topical/transdermal Legal status Cosmetic ingredient (unregulated as drug) Hexapeptide-11 (INCI name, also referred to as Myristoyl Hexapeptide-11 when lipidated) is a synthetic cosmeceutical peptide designed to stimulate collagen production, improve skin elasticity, and reduce visible signs of aging. It belongs to the broader class of signal peptides - bioactive peptides that mimic natural signaling molecules to activate fibroblasts and promote extracellular matrix (ECM) renewal in the dermis.

### compound | hexarelin/overview | What is Hexarelin?
kind: overview
title: Hexarelin
summary: The most potent synthetic GHRP (Growth Hormone Releasing Peptide), a hexapeptide that strongly stimulates GH release via the ghrelin receptor. Notable for cardioprotective effects independent of GH release. Development discontinued due to rapid desensitization with repeated dosing. Italian research leads global investigation.
keyPoint: The most potent synthetic GHRP (Growth Hormone Releasing Peptide), a hexapeptide that strongly stimulates GH release via the ghrelin receptor.

### compound | hexarelin/evidence | What research is listed for Hexarelin?
kind: evidence
title: Hexarelin: research listed by the sources
summary: Extensive human pharmacology data. Cardioprotection via Circulation Research 1999 (Bodart/Ong et al., CD36 receptor identification).
keyPoint: Extensive human pharmacology data.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: Hexarelin
  connectedTo: Hexarelin
section: What the research shows
  -: PepCodex: The most potent synthetic GHRP (Growth Hormone Releasing Peptide), a hexapeptide that strongly stimulates GH release via the ghrelin receptor.
  -: The Peptide Handbook: A synthetic growth hormone secretagogue studied for its ability to stimulate growth hormone release, with additional research interest in potential cardioprotective and neuroprotective effects that appear to be independent of its hormonal activity.
  -: Halflife Labs: Hexarelin (examorelin) half-life is approximately 70 minutes per Laron et al.
  -: Peptpedia: Produces the highest GH peaks of any GHRP but desensitizes within 4-6 weeks.
  -: PeptideDosage.org: Hexarelin (examorelin) is a synthetic hexapeptide growth hormone secretagogue and agonist of the ghrelin/GHS-R1a receptor, developed by Mediolanum Farmaceutici from the GHRP-6 template (sequence His-D-2-methyl-Trp-Ala-Trp-D-Phe-Lys-NH2).
section: Evidence strength
  -: PepCodex: Human clinical research; population: Human; Human evidence with design limitations to check. 18 human studies listed by the source
  -: The Peptide Handbook: Human clinical research; population: Human; Human evidence with design limitations to check. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: Halflife Labs: Source summary; study design not clearly stated; population: Not clearly stated; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: Peptpedia: Source summary; study design not clearly stated; population: Not clearly stated; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: PeptideDosage.org: Animal research; population: Animal; Preclinical animal evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Limitations
  -: The reviewed record does not state a specific limitation. The linked paper still needs to be checked for design, size and bias.
  -: Experimental studies report endocrine effects; long-term safety and clinically meaningful outcomes have not been established
  -: The source does not clearly state the study population or design in PEARL's reviewed record.
  -: no significant effect on these cardiac parameters.
  -: not fully specific for GH: they also produce slight prolactin release and, in Cushing disease, ACTH and cortisol responses.
  -: not report a head-to-head potency ranking of Hexarelin against other GHSs.
  -: No other GHRP has this dual mechanism established in controlled research.
  -: not medical advice, and the compounds covered are research chemicals not approved for human use unless explicitly stated otherwise.
  -: Hexarelin (examorelin) is a synthetic hexapeptide growth hormone secretagogue and agonist of the ghrelin/GHS-R1a receptor, developed by Mediolanum Farmaceutici from the GHRP-6 template (sequence His-D-2-methyl-Trp-Ala-Trp-D-Phe-Lys-NH2).
  *: Source rating: 3 out of 5
  *: PepCodex: Moderate evidence; 18 human studies listed
  *: The Peptide Handbook: preliminary. Short studies in healthy volunteers found that intravenous, subcutaneous, intranasal, and oral experimental administration can stimulate growth-hormone release. A 16-week repeated-exposure study in 12 healthy elderly subjects found that the GH response to twice-daily subcutaneous hexarelin was partially attenuated over the study period; GH responsiveness recovered to near-baseline levels four weeks after treatment stopped, indicating that attenuation is reversible rather than permanent (Rahim and Shalet 1998). These pharmacodynamic data do not establish clinical efficacy or long-term safety, and claims of cardioprotection remain outside the human evidence summarized here.
  *: Halflife Labs: Evidence context is stated on the linked compound page.
  *: PeptideDosage.org: Transient flushing, warmth, sweating, and tingling or numbness of the face, head or hands shortly after injection are common with potent GHRPs and usually fade within minutes [1].; Increased appetite and hunger through ghrelin-receptor (GHS-R1a) agonism, sometimes with mild nausea or gastrointestinal discomfort, especially at higher per-dose amounts [8].; Elevations in cortisol and prolactin when single doses exceed roughly 100 mcg, because excess hexarelin engages corticotrophs and lactotrophs; selectivity is poorer than with ipamorelin [2][5].; Water and sodium retention, mild peripheral edema, joint aches (arthralgia), and carpal-tunnel-like tingling can occur from GH/IGF-1 elevation, typically early in use.; Sustained GH elevation can transiently reduce insulin sensitivity and raise blood glucose; caution is warranted in people with prediabetes, diabetes, or metabolic syndrome.; Tachyphylaxis: the GH response declines partially over weeks of daily dosing and recovers after a washout, so continuous high-frequency use yields diminishing returns [4].; Long-term human safety is not
  *: PeptideDeck: Strongest growth hormone release among GHRP peptides Cardioprotective effects independent of GH action Enhanced muscle mass and strength in research models Improved recovery and tissue repair Increased collagen synthesis and bone density Neuroprotective properties demonstrated in animal studies Fat metabolism enhancement through GH-mediated lipolysis No significant impact on appetite (unlike GHRP-6) Hexarelin has been extensively studied in both preclinical and clinical settings, with research spanning growth hormone physiology, cardiovascular protection, and metabolic effects. Multiple Phase I and II clinical trials have characterized Hexarelin's GH-releasing properties in humans. A landmark study in the Journal of Clinical Endocrinology & Metabolism examined healthy elderly subjects, finding that a single 1 μg/kg IV dose produced peak GH levels of approximately 45-60 ng/mL-substantially higher than achieved with equivalent GHRP-6 doses.
  *: Identification and Characterization of a New Growth Hormone-Releasing Peptide Receptor in the Heart (Circulation Research 1999): Bodart et al. identified and characterized a specific hexarelin/GHRP receptor in cardiac tissue, demonstrating cardioprotective effects of hexarelin independent of its GH-releasing activity and establishing CD36 as the mediating receptor - the foundational paper for hexarelin cardioprotection.
  *: Growth hormone-releasing activity of hexarelin, a new synthetic hexapeptide, after intravenous, subcutaneous, intranasal, and oral administration in man (Journal of Clinical Endocrinology and Metabolism 1994): Ghigo, Arvat et al. conducted the first human pharmacology study of hexarelin across multiple routes of administration, demonstrating potent and reproducible GH release - the primary human evidence base for hexarelin's GH-secretagogue activity.

### compound | hgf/overview | What is HGF?
kind: overview
title: HGF
summary: From Wikipep - The Peptide Encyclopedia HGF Chemical name Hepatocyte Growth Factor (Scatter Factor) Molecular formula Heterodimeric glycoprotein (α-chain 69 kDa + β-chain 34 kDa) Molecular weight ~103,000 g/mol (heterodimer) CAS number 122928-25-4 Sequence 728 amino acids (pre-pro-HGF, human) Length 728 amino acids (single chain pro-HGF) Source Endogenous (mesenchymal cells); recombinant Half-life ~3-5 minutes (plasma) Targets c-MET receptor tyrosine kinase (HGFR) Bioavailability IV/local injection (research) Legal status Research compound; gene therapy in clinical trials HGF ( Hepatocyte Growth Factor , also known as Scatter Factor ) is a pleiotropic growth factor and the sole ligand for the c-MET receptor tyrosine kinase. Originally identified for its ability to stimulate hepatocyte proliferation and epithelial cell scattering, HGF is now recognized as a master regulator of tissue repair, morphogenesis, and organ protection across virtually all epithelial and endothelial tissues.

### compound | hgh-191aa/overview | What is HGH 191AA?
kind: overview
title: HGH 191AA
summary: HGH 191AA, more accurately named somatropin, is recombinant human growth hormone produced by E. coli or mammalian expression systems and structurally identical to the 191-amino-acid pituitary-derived hormone. It is the only fully FDA-approved growth hormone replacement product and is licensed for adult and paediatric growth hormone deficiency, Turner syndrome, Prader-Willi syndrome, idiopathic short stature, chronic kidney disease and HIV wasting under brand names including Genotropin, Humatrope, Norditropin, Saizen, Omnitrope and Nutropin. The Molitch et al. Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline (JCEM 2011) established adult dosing at 0.15 to 0.3 mg subcutaneously once daily, titrated against IGF-1 in the mid-normal age- and sex-adjusted range, typically to 0.4 to 0.6 mg/day in younger adults and 0.2 to 0.4 mg/day in patients above 60 years.
keyPoint: HGH 191AA, more accurately named somatropin, is recombinant human growth hormone produced by E.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: HGH 191AA
  connectedTo: HGH 191AA
section: Why it is researched
  -: HGH 191AA, more accurately named somatropin, is recombinant human growth hormone produced by E.
section: How it works in the research
  -: Somatropin binds the growth hormone receptor (GHR), a class I cytokine receptor expressed on hepatocytes, adipocytes, chondrocytes, myocytes, immune cells and nearly every other tissue.
section: Evidence strength
  -: PeptideDosage.org: Human clinical research; population: Human; Human evidence with design limitations to check. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Main limitations
  -: The reviewed record does not state a specific limitation. The linked paper still needs to be checked for design, size and bias.

### compound | hgh-191aa/evidence | What research is listed for HGH 191AA?
kind: evidence
title: HGH 191AA: research listed by the sources
summary: FDA approved for specific indications. Extensive clinical data.
keyPoint: FDA approved for specific indications.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: HGH 191AA
  connectedTo: HGH 191AA
section: What the research shows
  -: PeptideDosage.org: HGH 191AA, more accurately named somatropin, is recombinant human growth hormone produced by E.
  -: PeptideDosages.com: 09 How This Works HGH 191AA is recombinant human growth hormone (somatropin) that is structurally identical to endogenous GH secreted by the pituitary gland [1] .
  -: Peptide University Codex: HGH 191AA (somatropin) is bio-identical human growth hormone - a 191 amino acid single-chain polypeptide with a molecular weight of approximately 22 kDa, structurally identical to the growth hormone produced by the anterior pituitary gland.
section: Evidence strength
  -: PeptideDosage.org: Human clinical research; population: Human; Human evidence with design limitations to check. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: PeptideDosages.com: Source summary; study design not clearly stated; population: Not clearly stated; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: Peptide University Codex: Source summary; study design not clearly stated; population: Not clearly stated; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Limitations
  -: The reviewed record does not state a specific limitation. The linked paper still needs to be checked for design, size and bias.
  -: 14 Important Note This content is intended for therapeutic educational purposes only and does not constitute medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment.
  -: HGH 191AA is a research peptide.
  -: Always consult qualified healthcare professionals before beginning any peptide protocol.
  -: Active cancer or evidence of neoplastic activity - exogenous GH and IGF-1 directly accelerates tumor cell proliferation; GH should not be initiated or continued if active malignancy is detected.
  -: Intracranial lesions that are not fully inactive and treated - antitumor therapy must be complete prior to GH initiation.
  -: Insulin resistance or pre-existing type 2 diabetes - HGH is diabetogenic at therapeutic doses; progressively worsens insulin sensitivity; fasting glucose must be monitored throughout.
  -: Diabetic ketoacidosis.
  -: Proliferative or severe non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy - GH/IGF-1 elevation worsens retinal vasculopathy.
  -: Concurrent use with CJC-1295 No DAC, CJC-1295 DAC, ipamorelin, tesamorelin, GHRP-2, GHRP-6, or sermorelin - redundant and counterproductive GH axis stimulation; secretagogues stimulate a pituitary that exogenous HGH has already suppressed.
  -: Acute critical illness - increased mortality observed in critically ill patients (open heart surgery, abdominal surgery, multiple trauma, acute respiratory failure) receiving high-dose GH; do not use in ICU or perioperative settings.
  -: Pregnancy - limited human data; use only if clearly needed; associated with fetal risks in animal studies.
  *: Source rating: 5 out of 5
  *: PeptideDosage.org: Peripheral oedema is the most common adverse effect, occurring in 15-25% of adult patients during titration and reflecting GH-mediated renal sodium retention plus IGF-1-driven extracellular fluid expansion; usually resolves with dose reduction.; Arthralgia, particularly in small joints of the hand, occurs in 10-20% of patients during the first 3 months and resolves with dose adjustment; persistent symptoms warrant IGF-1 reassessment.; Carpal tunnel syndrome and median-nerve paraesthesia develop in 5-10% of patients on supratherapeutic doses, related to extracellular fluid accumulation in the carpal canal; reversible with dose reduction.; Glucose intolerance and frank type 2 diabetes have been documented with chronic dosing in predisposed patients; HbA1c monitoring at 3-6 month intervals is standard, and somatropin is contraindicated in poorly controlled diabetes (HbA1c >8.5%).; Headache and intracranial pressure elevations have been reported in paediatric Prader-Willi and chronic kidney disease populations; presenting visual disturbance warrants prompt ophthalmologic review.;
  *: Peptide University Codex: Peptide University labels its records as aggregated from empirical research and anecdotal community data. This record is retained as supplied and is not upgraded to clinical evidence.
  *: Effects of human growth hormone in men over 60 years old (New England Journal of Medicine 1990): Landmark RCT (Rudman et al.) showing 6 months of recombinant human GH in older men with low IGF-1 increased lean body mass by 8.8%, reduced fat mass by 14.4%, and improved vertebral bone density by 1.6% vs placebo - the defining clinical trial establishing recombinant HGH body composition effects.

  *: PeptideJournal: Fragment 176-191 represents one of the more fascinating developments in peptide research: a truncated segment of human growth hormone that retains the fat-reducing properties of the parent molecule while shedding its growth-promoting effects. Fragment 176-191 represents an interesting proof-of-concept in peptide research: the idea that specific functions of a larger hormone can be isolated by identifying the responsible structural region. By extracting amino acids 176-191 from the 191-amino-acid growth hormone molecule, researchers created a peptide that stimulates fat breakdown while avoiding the growth-promoting, IGF-1-inducing, and diabetogenic effects of the full hormone. The animal research is promising. Studies in obese mice and rats demonstrate that Fragment 176-191 (and its modified analog AOD-9604) reduce body weight gain, increase fat oxidation, and stimulate lipolysis without affecting glucose metabolism or insulin sensitivity.

### compound | hghsomatropin/overview | What is HGH (Somatropin)?
kind: overview
title: HGH (Somatropin)
summary: Somatropin is recombinant human growth hormone (rhGH) -- a bioidentical, 191-amino-acid copy of the growth hormone naturally secreted by the anterior pituitary. It is FDA-approved under multiple brand names for a specific list of growth-disorder and deficiency indications, and separately (as Serostim) for HIV-associated wasting. Unlike the GH secretagogues elsewhere in this encyclopedia (e.g., ipamorelin, CJC-1295, GHRP-6), somatropin supplies growth hormone directly rather than stimulating the pituitary to release its own. Somatropin is produced via recombinant DNA technology (typically in E. coli or mammalian expression systems) and is structurally identical to the major isoform of endogenous human growth hormone: a 191-amino-acid, single-chain polypeptide with four cysteine residues forming two intrachain disulfide bonds.
keyPoint: Somatropin is recombinant human growth hormone (rhGH) -- a bioidentical, 191-amino-acid copy of the growth hormone naturally secreted by the anterior pituitary.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: HGH (Somatropin)
  connectedTo: HGH (Somatropin)
section: Why it is researched
  -: Somatropin is recombinant human growth hormone (rhGH) -- a bioidentical, 191-amino-acid copy of the growth hormone naturally secreted by the anterior pituitary.
section: How it works in the research
  -: Binds the growth hormone receptor (GHR), a class I cytokine receptor, causing receptor dimerization and activation of JAK2-STAT5 intracellular signaling.
section: Evidence strength
  -: Licensed reference library: Source summary; study design not clearly stated; population: Not clearly stated; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Main limitations
  -: FDA-approved (under multiple brand names: Genotropin, Humatrope, Norditropin, Omnitrope, Saizen, Nutropin, Zomacton) for growth hormone deficiency and specific growth disorders in children and adults, and (as Serostim) for HIV-associated wasting/cachexia.

### compound | hmg/overview | What is HMG?
kind: overview
title: HMG
summary: A urinary-derived glycoprotein hormone preparation containing both FSH and LH in approximately 1:1 ratio, FDA-approved for female infertility (ovulation induction, ART) and male hypogonadotropic hypogonadism. First used clinically in 1961 by Bruno Lunenfeld, HMG enabled the birth of the first American IVF baby in 1981 and remains a cornerstone of fertility medicine with over 60 years of clinical experience. Highly purified preparations (HP-hMG) demonstrate comparable or slightly superior live birth rates compared to recombinant FSH in IVF.
keyPoint: A urinary-derived glycoprotein hormone preparation containing both FSH and LH in approximately 1:1 ratio, FDA-approved for female infertility (ovulation induction, ART) and male hypogonadotropic hypogonadism.

### compound | hmg/evidence | What research is listed for HMG?
kind: evidence
title: HMG: research listed by the sources
summary: High evidence; 44 human studies listed Local injection-site reactions including pain, erythema, induration, and bruising are common with subcutaneous hMG; daily injections in IVF cycles increase cumulative discomfort but rarely cause serious local complications.; Ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (OHSS) is the most significant complication, particularly in young women with polycystic ovary syndrome, high antral follicle count, or high anti-Müllerian hormone levels; mild OHSS is common, while moderate and severe OHSS occur in approximately 3-8% and 0.5-2% of stimulated cycles respectively.; Multiple gestation risk is elevated with hMG use for ovulation induction without IVF, since multiple follicles often develop simultaneously; ultrasound monitoring and dose individualization are essential to minimize this risk.; Headache, mood changes, breast tenderness, abdominal distension, and pelvic discomfort are common during stimulation cycles and reflect rising estradiol and ovarian enlargement.; Thromboembolic events including deep vein thrombosis and rarely pulmonary embolism have been reported with gonadotropin stimulation,

section: What the research shows
  -: PepCodex: A urinary-derived glycoprotein hormone preparation containing both FSH and LH in approximately 1:1 ratio, FDA-approved for female infertility (ovulation induction, ART) and male hypogonadotropic hypogonadism.
  -: PeptideDosage.org: Human menopausal gonadotropin (hMG, menotropins) is a purified mixture of follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) and luteinizing hormone (LH) activity extracted from the urine of postmenopausal women, typically in a 1:1 FSH:LH bioactivity ratio.

  -: PeptideDosages.com: 09 How This Works HMG provides both FSH and LH activity in a 1:1 ratio, derived from purified human menopausal urine [2] .
  -: Peptide University Codex: Human Menopausal Gonadotropin (hMG, menotroPin) is a purified biological extract derived from the urine of postmenopausal women - a source chosen specifically because postmenopausal pituitary gonadotropin output is dramatically elevated (due to absent negative sex hormone feedback), making postmenopausal urine a rich...

  -: PepCodex: Human clinical research; population: Human; Human evidence with design limitations to check. 44 human studies listed by the source

section: Limitations
  -: The reviewed record does not state a specific limitation. The linked paper still needs to be checked for design, size and bias.
  -: The reviewed record is animal research and cannot establish human effectiveness or safety.
  -: 14 Important Note This content is intended for therapeutic educational purposes only and does not constitute medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment.
  -: HMG therapy should only be undertaken under the supervision of a qualified healthcare provider with appropriate monitoring of hormone levels and semen parameters.
  -: For research use only.
  -: Not intended for human consumption.
  -: High baseline FSH (indicative of primary testicular failure/Sertoli cell damage) - elevated serum FSH in men signals irreversible testicular damage with absent or severely compromised Sertoli cell function; hMG provides no spermatogenic benefit when the target tissue is non-functional and only adds side effect burden.
  -: Known or suspected hormone-dependent tumors (prostate cancer, ovarian cancer, endometrial cancer, breast cancer) - gonadotropin stimulation of sex hormone production is contraindicated in hormone-sensitive malignancies.
  -: Ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (OHSS) history or high risk - in women with polycystic ovarian syndrome (PCOS) or other high-responder states, FSH stimulation from hMG can trigger severe and potentially life-threatening OHSS.
  -: Uncontrolled adrenal dysfunction, thyroid dysfunction, or hyperprolactinemia - these endocrine conditions must be treated before gonadotropin therapy to ensure the HPG axis is capable of responding appropriately.
  -: Presence of ovarian cysts unrelated to PCOS (in women) - exogenous FSH may stimulate cyst growth or rupture.
  -: Intracranial lesions (pituitary tumor, hypothalamic disease) incompatible with gonadotropin therapy.
  -: Known hypersensitivity to hMG, urinary-derived gonadotropin preparations, or any formulation excipients.
  -: Pregnancy (outside medically supervised ovulation induction) - absolute contraindication to any gonadotropin administration in established pregnancy.

  *: Resolved: modelled administration routes. Use only the route stated in the original study or official product information. Do not convert an oral, intranasal, intramuscular or investigational product into a generic subcutaneous vial protocol. PeptideDosage.org applies a common reconstitution and syringe format even to products such as Ventfort that it identifies as oral. That format is not evidence that the modelled route was studied or is suitable. Confidence: high.
  *: Resolved: mental-health citation identity. Exclude three unrelated PubMed identifiers copied under Semax, NAC and Selank claims. Keep only links whose NCBI record matches the stated research subject. NCBI identifies PMID 11157505 as a Hodgkin-disease cell-fusion paper, PMID 16640009 as a Freeman-Sheldon syndrome case report, and PMID 18677858 as a neonatal-mortality paper.   *: Source rating: 2 out of 5, limited evidence
  *: PepCodex: Moderate evidence; 10 human studies listed
  *: The Peptide Handbook: preliminary. Humanin was discovered in 2001 (Hashimoto et al., PNAS) as an endogenous neuroprotective peptide encoded in mitochondrial DNA. The discovery paper demonstrated that humanin blocks neuronal cell death induced by a wide spectrum of familial Alzheimer's disease genes and amyloid-beta in cellular models - all evidence from this foundational work is preclinical and cellular. Endogenous circulating humanin levels have been studied in human observational research: published data report associations with longevity biomarkers and centenarian offspring, and inverse correlations with IGF-1 signaling. These observations concern endogenous, naturally produced humanin and do not constitute evidence that administration of exogenous humanin extends human lifespan. No interventional human trials of administered humanin or HNG have been published. Animal and cellular models demonstrate neuroprotective, insulin-sensitizing, and cardioprotective effects, all preclinical.
  *: Peptide Hub: Protocol-focused educational summary. Linked papers, site-listed ranges and commercial context are retained with source attribution.
  *: PeptideDosage.org: There is no human safety data for exogenous Humanin: the entire profile derives from cell-culture and animal studies, so tolerability, long-term effects, and a maximum tolerated dose in humans are unknown [5].; Because humanin is a potent, broadly acting anti-apoptotic and cytoprotective factor, there is a theoretical concern that it could promote the survival of damaged or malignant cells; humanin signaling (BAX inhibition, STAT3 activation) overlaps pathways implicated in tumor cell survival [5].; Metabolic effects are a key consideration: humanin and its analogs lower blood glucose and improve insulin sensitivity in animals, creating a theoretical risk of hypoglycemia and additive effects if combined with insulin or other glucose-lowering agents [3].; Humanin binds IGFBP-3 and intersects the GH/IGF-1 axis, so interactions with growth-factor signaling are plausible and unstudied in humans [2][6].; For the educational subcutaneous model, injection-site reactions (redness, irritation, bruising, or infection) are possible; sterile technique, fresh syringes, and proper storage are
  *: PeptideDeck: Neuroprotective effects in Alzheimer's disease models Cytoprotective action against oxidative stress Improved insulin sensitivity in metabolic studies Anti-apoptotic effects protecting cells from programmed death Reduced amyloid-beta toxicity in neuronal cultures Cardioprotective properties in ischemia models Potential longevity and healthspan extension Mitochondrial function support Active research area with published studies Since its discovery in 2001, Humanin has accumulated a substantial research literature spanning neuroprotection, metabolic health, cardiovascular disease, and fundamental aging biology. The following summarizes key findings across major research areas.
  *: A rescue factor abolishing neuronal cell death by a wide spectrum of familial Alzheimer's disease genes and Aβ (Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 2001): Hashimoto et al. discovered Humanin as a small peptide encoded in the mitochondrial 16S rRNA that completely blocked neuronal apoptosis induced by multiple familial Alzheimer's disease genes and amyloid-beta - the foundational discovery paper establishing Humanin as a mitochondria-derived cytoprotective peptide.
  *: Humanin: A Novel Central Regulator of Peripheral Insulin Action (PLoS ONE 2009): Muzumdar et al. demonstrated that Humanin acts centrally to regulate peripheral insulin action. Intracerebroventricular Humanin administration improved whole-body insulin sensitivity and glucose metabolism in rodent models, linking mitochondrial signaling to systemic metabolic regulation.

### compound | icatibant/evidence | What research is listed for Icatibant?
kind: evidence
title: Icatibant: research listed by the sources
summary: strong-human. In the Phase III randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled FAST-3 trial of cutaneous or abdominal HAE attacks, median time to at least 50% reduction in symptom severity was 2.0 hours with icatibant versus 19.8 hours with placebo (P < 0.001). Median time to almost complete symptom relief was 8.0 hours versus 36.0 hours, respectively (P = 0.012). These findings support strong randomized human evidence for acute HAE treatment. ACE-inhibitor angioedema has a bradykinin-based rationale, but randomized evidence is conflicting: one smaller randomized trial reported median complete-resolution time of 8.0 hours with icatibant versus 27.1 hours with comparator treatment (P = 0.002), while a later larger randomized placebo-controlled trial found median time to discharge criteria of 4.0 hours with icatibant versus 4.0 hours with placebo (P = 0.63). Efficacy for ACE-inhibitor angioedema is therefore not established. FAST-1 (US/Argentina): Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial; icatibant produced clinically meaningful faster symptom relief versus placebo at multiple time points FAST-2 (Europe): Randomized, double-blind trial comparing icatibant to tranexamic acid; icatibant demonstrated significantly faster symptom relief FAST-3: Open-label extension study confirming long-term safety and consistent efficacy with repeated use across multiple attacks Icatibant has been invaluable as a research tool for studying the bradykinin-kinin system Used to validate bradykinin's role in various pathological conditions Tool compound in pain, inflammation, and vascular permeability research Reference compound for development of next-generation B2 receptor antagonists [ 1 ] [ 2 ] [ 3 ] [ 4 ] [ 5 ] ↑ 1.0 1.1 Cicardi M, Banerji A, Bracho F, et al. "Icatibant, a new bradykinin-receptor antagonist, in hereditary angioedema." New England Journal of Medicine . 2010;363(6):532-541. ↑ 2.0 2.1 Lumry WR, Li HH, Levy RJ, et al.
keyPoint: strong-human.
understood: resolved

section: Limitations
  -: Laryngeal HAE attacks require immediate medical evaluation and monitoring after FIRAZYR treatment because airway obstruction can still progress
  -: Theoretical cardiovascular risk - weigh the potential benefit against theoretical risk in acute coronary ischemia, unstable angina, or during the weeks following stroke
  -: The reviewed record does not state a specific limitation. The linked paper still needs to be checked for design, size and bias.
  *: Source rating: 5 out of 5
  *: The Peptide Handbook: strong-human. In the Phase III randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled FAST-3 trial of cutaneous or abdominal HAE attacks, median time to at least 50% reduction in symptom severity was 2.0 hours with icatibant versus 19.8 hours with placebo (P < 0.001). Median time to almost complete symptom relief was 8.0 hours versus 36.0 hours, respectively (P = 0.012). These findings support strong randomized human evidence for acute HAE treatment. ACE-inhibitor angioedema has a bradykinin-based rationale, but randomized evidence is conflicting: one smaller randomized trial reported median complete-resolution time of 8.0 hours with icatibant versus 27.1 hours with comparator treatment (P = 0.002), while a later larger randomized placebo-controlled trial found median time to discharge criteria of 4.0 hours with icatibant versus 4.0 hours with placebo (P = 0.63). Efficacy for ACE-inhibitor angioedema is therefore not established.
  *: WikiPep: FAST-1 (US/Argentina): Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial; icatibant produced clinically meaningful faster symptom relief versus placebo at multiple time points FAST-2 (Europe): Randomized, double-blind trial comparing icatibant to tranexamic acid; icatibant demonstrated significantly faster symptom relief FAST-3: Open-label extension study confirming long-term safety and consistent efficacy with repeated use across multiple attacks Icatibant has been invaluable as a research tool for studying the bradykinin-kinin system Used to validate bradykinin's role in various pathological conditions Tool compound in pain, inflammation, and vascular permeability research Reference compound for development of next-generation B2 receptor antagonists [ 1 ] [ 2 ] [ 3 ] [ 4 ] [ 5 ] ↑ 1.0 1.1 Cicardi M, Banerji A, Bracho F, et al. "Icatibant, a new bradykinin-receptor antagonist, in hereditary angioedema." New England Journal of Medicine . 2010;363(6):532-541. ↑ 2.0 2.1 Lumry WR, Li HH, Levy RJ, et al.

### compound | igf-1-lr3/evidence | What research is listed for IGF-1 LR3?

keyPoint: Significant preclinical and clinical IGF-1 data.

method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: IGF-1 LR3
  connectedTo: IGF-1 LR3
section: What the research shows
  -: PepCodex: A modified form of IGF-1 with an extended half-life due to reduced binding protein affinity.
  -: The Peptide Handbook: Long R3 IGF-I is a research variant that must be distinguished from native IGF-1, mecasermin, DES(1-3)-IGF-I, and other analogues.
  -: Halflife Labs: Pharmacokinetics of IGF-1 LR3: half-life ~20-30 hours in animal models, mechanism of IGFBP evasion, regulatory status, and comparison to native IGF-1 and mecasermin.
  -: Peptpedia: Evades IGF-binding proteins for up to ~2× the potency of native IGF-1 via PI3K/Akt/mTOR.
  -: PeptideDosage.org: IGF-1 LR3 (Long-Arg3-IGF-1) is an 83-amino-acid recombinant analogue of insulin-like growth factor-1 with two engineered modifications: an arginine substitution at position 3 and a 13-amino-acid N-terminal extension derived from methionyl-porcine GH.
section: Evidence strength
  -: PepCodex: Human clinical research; population: Human; Human evidence with design limitations to check. 8 human studies listed by the source
  -: The Peptide Handbook: Animal research; population: Human; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: Halflife Labs: Source summary; study design not clearly stated; population: Not clearly stated; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: Peptpedia: Laboratory or mechanistic research; population: Laboratory; Early laboratory evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: PeptideDosage.org: Animal research; population: Animal; Preclinical animal evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Limitations
  -: The reviewed record does not state a specific limitation. The linked paper still needs to be checked for design, size and bias.
  -: Long-term human safety data are not established.
  -: The source does not clearly state the study population or design in PEARL's reviewed record.
  -: no human pharmacokinetic data - every claimed property is preclinical.
  -: not from persistence (no human pharmacokinetic data exist for LR3).
  -: No human PK data.
  -: no extended half-life and is actually cleared substantially faster than native IGF-1 in animal models because it cannot bind the protective IGFBP-3 complex (PMID 7693845).
  -: not what the published clearance data show - the measured effect runs in the opposite direction.
  -: not from improved receptor interaction (PMID 1378742).
  -: Not Slower, Clearance: In catheterized rats, LR3IGF-I's metabolic clearance rate was 9.
  -: no peer-reviewed basis.
  -: IGF-1 LR3 (Long-Arg3-IGF-1) is an 83-amino-acid recombinant analogue of insulin-like growth factor-1 with two engineered modifications: an arginine substitution at position 3 and a 13-amino-acid N-terminal extension derived from methionyl-porcine GH.
  *: Source rating: 3 out of 5
  *: PepCodex: Low evidence; 8 human studies listed
  *: The Peptide Handbook: preliminary. The retained literature reports variant IGF-I effects in rats, pigs, marmosets, and adolescent monkeys. It is nonhuman evidence and must not be presented as clinical evidence for an exact manufactured Long R3 IGF-I product.
  *: Halflife Labs: Evidence context is stated on the linked compound page.
  *: PeptideDosage.org: Hypoglycaemia is the most clinically significant adverse effect and reflects IGF-1R cross-activation of the insulin receptor; symptoms (sweating, tremor, palpitations) typically appear 1-4 hours after injection and respond to oral carbohydrate.; Localised muscle pain at injection site (so-called pump or fullness) is commonly reported in research-context use and reflects acute IGF-1R-driven cellular fluid uptake; usually transient.; Suppression of endogenous GH and IGF-1 secretion through hypothalamic-pituitary IGF-1R feedback occurs with continuous dosing and is the rationale for cycle-and-washout protocols (typically 4-6 weeks on, 4-6 weeks off).; Peripheral oedema and hand stiffness can develop with chronic high-dose use through the same extracellular fluid expansion that occurs with exogenous GH; resolves with dose reduction.; Theoretical concern for accelerated growth of occult malignancy exists because IGF-1R activation is mitogenic in many cancer cell lines; chronic use is contraindicated in patients with known or suspected malignancy.; Cardiac hypertrophy has been reported in
  *: PeptideDeck: Enhanced bioavailability compared to native IGF-1 Reduced binding to IGF binding proteins Extended half-life for sustained signaling Potent stimulation of protein synthesis Promotes satellite cell proliferation in muscle tissue Supports nutrient partitioning toward lean tissue Facilitates recovery and tissue repair mechanisms Valuable research tool for studying IGF-1 pathway Active research area with published studies Research on IGF-1 LR3 spans several decades, building on the extensive literature surrounding native IGF-1 and the broader IGF system. While most research involves the native peptide, studies specifically examining LR3 have demonstrated its enhanced potency and provided insights into IGF-1 biology.
  *: IGF-I stimulation of muscle protein synthesis in the awake rat: permissive role of insulin and amino acids (American Journal of Physiology - Endocrinology and Metabolism 1996): IGF-I infusion significantly increased skeletal muscle protein synthesis in gastrocnemius and soleus, establishing the anabolic effect requires permissive insulin and amino acid availability.

### compound | igf1des/overview | What is IGF-1 DES?
kind: overview
title: IGF-1 DES
summary: IGF-1 DES (DES(1-3)IGF-1) is a 67-amino-acid truncated analogue of insulin-like growth factor-1, created by removing the N-terminal tripeptide Gly-Pro-Glu from the 70-residue parent molecule. It is a naturally occurring IGF-1 fragment first isolated from bovine colostrum and later found in fetal and adult brain tissue, not a purely synthetic construct. The deletion sharply reduces binding to the insulin-like growth factor binding proteins (IGFBPs) while preserving full agonist activity at the type 1 IGF receptor (IGF-1R), which makes the free peptide roughly ten-fold more potent than native IGF-1 in IGFBP-rich systems. Unlike long-acting analogues such as IGF-1 LR3, IGF-1 DES has a very short circulating half-life (about 20-30 minutes), so it is used as a fast, locally acting research growth factor rather than a sustained systemic agent.
keyPoint: IGF-1 DES (DES(1-3)IGF-1) is a 67-amino-acid truncated analogue of insulin-like growth factor-1, created by removing the N-terminal tripeptide Gly-Pro-Glu from the 70-residue parent molecule.

### compound | igf1des/safety | What are the risks of IGF-1 DES?
kind: safety
title: IGF-1 DES: source-listed risks

matchedText: IGF-1 DES
  connectedTo: IGF-1 DES
  *: Safety data for IGF-1 DES in humans remains limited because the peptide has not undergone formal clinical development or regulatory approval. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Available information derives from animal research, in vitro studies, and extrapolation from native IGF-1 pharmacology. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Theoretical Safety Concerns: Based on the peptide's mechanism of action, several categories of adverse effects warrant consideration: Hypoglycemia: IGF-1 signaling overlaps with insulin signaling, particularly through the PI3K/Akt pathway that promotes glucose uptake and GLUT4 translocation. [source-listed source severity]
  *: While Des(1-3)IGF-1 shows minimal cross-reactivity with insulin receptors, it can lower blood glucose through IGF1R-mediated mechanisms. [source-listed source severity]
  *: The short half-life of IGF-1 DES (20-30 minutes) provides a safety advantage here - any hypoglycemic episode would be transient compared to longer-acting analogs. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Proliferative Effects: IGF-1 signaling promotes cell proliferation and inhibits apoptosis, raising theoretical concerns about cancer risk with chronic exposure. [source-listed source severity]
  *: IGF-1 has been associated with increased cancer risk in epidemiological studies, though the relationship is complex and involves many confounding factors. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Des(1-3)IGF-1's short half-life and localized effects may mitigate this concern compared to systemic, long-acting IGF-1 elevation, but no long-term data exist. [source-listed source severity]

### compound | igf1des/evidence | What research is listed for IGF-1 DES?
kind: evidence
title: IGF-1 DES: research listed by the sources
summary: Hypoglycaemia is the most predictable adverse effect and reflects IGF-1R cross-activation of insulin signalling; symptoms (sweating, tremor, light-headedness, palpitations) can appear within 1-2 hours and respond to oral carbohydrate. The short half-life tends to make episodes brief but does not eliminate them [7].; Injection-site reactions, local pain, transient fullness or pump near the injected muscle, erythema and induration are commonly described in research-context use and reflect acute local IGF-1R activation and fluid uptake.; Theoretical promotion of occult tumour growth is a serious concern because IGF-1R activation is mitogenic across many cell lines; chronic use is contraindicated in anyone with known or suspected malignancy [8].; Frequent dosing can contribute to feedback suppression of endogenous growth hormone and IGF-1 secretion; the effect is generally smaller than with long-acting analogues because exposure is brief, but it is the rationale for limiting cycle length.; Fluid retention, peripheral oedema or joint and hand stiffness can occur through the same Enhanced bioavailability compared to native IGF-1 Approximately 10x greater potency for cell proliferation No sequestration by IGF binding proteins Promotes satellite cell activation and muscle repair Supports protein synthesis via PI3K/Akt pathway Shorter half-life enables localized, targeted effects Hyperplasia (new cell formation) rather than just hypertrophy Valuable research tool for IGF-1 receptor studies Research on IGF-1 DES spans several decades, with studies examining its enhanced potency, mechanisms of action, and potential applications in understanding muscle biology and tissue repair. Foundational research in the late 1980s and early 1990s established IGF-1 DES's enhanced biological activity. A landmark 1989 study in Biochemical and Biophysical Research Communications demonstrated that the increased potency was directly attributable to reduced binding protein affinity. When researchers compared IGF-1 DES and native IGF-1 in systems with and without binding proteins, the potency difference was only observed in the presence of IGFBPs.

kind: evidence
title: IGF-1 DES: source differences
summary: The knowledge base keeps conflicting claims and records why one is preferred or why no single value has been chosen.

method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: IGF-1 DES
  connectedTo: IGF-1 DES
  *: Resolved: site-listed dose ranges. Published study protocols with species, route, population, frequency and duration take priority. Uncited commercial ranges remain labelled and secondary. A product or calculator range is not evidence that a dose was studied, effective or safe. Confidence: high.
  *: Resolved: modelled administration routes. Use only the route stated in the original study or official product information. Do not convert an oral, intranasal, intramuscular or investigational product into a generic subcutaneous vial protocol. PeptideDosage.org applies a common reconstitution and syringe format even to products such as Ventfort that it identifies as oral. That format is not evidence that the modelled route was studied or is suitable. Confidence: high.
  *: Resolved: mental-health citation identity. Exclude three unrelated PubMed identifiers copied under Semax, NAC and Selank claims. Keep only links whose NCBI record matches the stated research subject. NCBI identifies PMID 11157505 as a Hodgkin-disease cell-fusion paper, PMID 16640009 as a Freeman-Sheldon syndrome case report, and PMID 18677858 as a neonatal-mortality paper. None supports the peptide claim beside which it appeared. Confidence: high.

### compound | immunologicalenhancementgaz/overview | What is Immunological Enhancement (GAZ)?
kind: overview
title: Immunological Enhancement (GAZ)
summary: Immunological Enhancement (product code GAZ) is an antioxidant and immune-support injection built around glutathione, vitamin C, and zinc. It is a vitamin and antioxidant blend rather than a peptide, working through antioxidant defense and immune-cofactor pathways, and given as a fixed direct dose with no titration. Each milliliter contains Glutathione 200mg, Ascorbic Acid (Vitamin C) 200mg, and Zinc Sulfate 2.5mg. Glutathione is the body master antioxidant and plays a central role in detoxification, immune cell function, and cellular protection, vitamin C is a potent antioxidant that supports immune function and regenerates glutathione, and zinc is an essential mineral that supports immune cell development, wound healing, and hundreds of enzymatic processes. In practice, GAZ is used by people who want to support their immune system, antioxidant status, and general resilience, particularly during periods of high stress, heavy training, travel, or seasonal illness risk.
