### compound | immunologicalenhancementgaz/mechanism | How does Immunological Enhancement (GAZ) work?
kind: overview
title: Immunological Enhancement (GAZ)
summary: Immunological Enhancement (product code GAZ) is an antioxidant and immune-support injection built around glutathione, vitamin C, and zinc. It is a vitamin and antioxidant blend rather than a peptide, working through antioxidant defense and immune-cofactor pathways, and given as a fixed direct dose with no titration. Each milliliter contains Glutathione 200mg, Ascorbic Acid (Vitamin C) 200mg, and Zinc Sulfate 2.5mg. Glutathione is the body master antioxidant and plays a central role in detoxification, immune cell function, and cellular protection, vitamin C is a potent antioxidant that supports immune function and regenerates glutathione, and zinc is an essential mineral that supports immune cell development, wound healing, and hundreds of enzymatic processes. In practice, GAZ is used by people who want to support their immune system, antioxidant status, and general resilience, particularly during periods of high stress, heavy training, travel, or seasonal illness risk.

### compound | inhibina/overview | What is Inhibin A?
kind: overview
title: Inhibin A
summary: From Wikipep - The Peptide Encyclopedia Inhibin A Chemical name Inhibin Alpha-Beta A Heterodimer Molecular formula Protein heterodimer Molecular weight ~32,000 Da (heterodimer) CAS number 57285-09-3 Sequence α subunit + βA subunit (disulfide-linked) Length α: 134 aa (mature) + βA: 116 aa (mature) Source Endogenous (granulosa cells, Sertoli cells) Half-life 30-60 minutes (circulatory) Targets Activin type II receptors, anterior pituitary gonadotrophs Bioavailability Endogenous hormone (not administered exogenously) Legal status Endogenous hormone / diagnostic reagent Inhibin A is an endogenous glycoprotein hormone belonging to the transforming growth factor-beta (TGF-β) superfamily . It is a heterodimer composed of an α subunit (18 kDa) disulfide-linked to a βA subunit (14 kDa), distinguishing it from Inhibin B which pairs the same α subunit with a βB subunit.

### compound | inhibinb/overview | What is Inhibin B?

summary: From Wikipep - The Peptide Encyclopedia Inhibin B Chemical name Inhibin Alpha-Beta B Heterodimer Molecular formula Protein heterodimer Molecular weight ~32,000 Da CAS number 96235-19-5 Sequence α subunit + βB subunit (disulfide-linked) Length α: 134 aa + βB: 115 aa (mature forms) Source Endogenous (Sertoli cells, granulosa cells) Half-life 30-60 minutes (circulatory) Targets Activin type II receptors, anterior pituitary gonadotrophs Bioavailability Endogenous hormone Legal status Endogenous hormone / diagnostic reagent Inhibin B is an endogenous glycoprotein hormone of the transforming growth factor-beta (TGF-β) superfamily , composed of an α subunit (18 kDa) disulfide-linked to a βB subunit (14 kDa). ### compound | insulin/overview | What is Insulin (Regular Human)?
kind: overview
title: Insulin (Regular Human)
summary: Recombinant regular human insulin is an established medical therapy for diabetes. This record uses HUMULIN R U-100 as a product anchor, keeps it distinct from insulin analogues, and emphasizes individualized dosing and glucose monitoring.
keyPoint: Recombinant regular human insulin is an established medical therapy for diabetes.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: Insulin (Regular Human)
  connectedTo: Insulin (Regular Human)
section: Why it is researched
  -: Recombinant regular human insulin is an established medical therapy for diabetes.
section: How it works in the research
  -: This record primarily represents recombinant regular human insulin, a 51-amino-acid two-chain hormone that is biochemically identical to endogenous human insulin.
section: Evidence strength
  -: The Peptide Handbook: Randomized or controlled human research; population: Human; Direct controlled human evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Main limitations
  -: Severe hypoglycemia - potentially fatal; risk is highest with dose-food-activity mismatch
  -: Hypoglycemic coma or seizure
  -: Hypokalemia with IV insulin (intracellular K+ shift)

### compound | insulin/evidence | What research is listed for Insulin (Regular Human)?
kind: evidence
title: Insulin (Regular Human): research listed by the sources
summary: strong-human. The DCCT was a landmark randomized study of intensive insulin treatment in type 1 diabetes and supports the clinical importance of glycemic control in that studied population. It is not a HUMULIN R U-100 label and does not support every regular-insulin dose or route claim. Current HUMULIN R U-100 labeling supports product-specific SC and IV use where permitted, individualized dosing, glucose monitoring, and risks including hypoglycemia, hypokalemia, and hypersensitivity. The strong evidence rating is scoped to established medical use of regular human insulin.
keyPoint: strong-human.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: Insulin (Regular Human)
  connectedTo: Insulin (Regular Human)
section: What the research shows
  -: The Peptide Handbook: Recombinant regular human insulin is an established medical therapy for diabetes.
section: Evidence strength
  -: The Peptide Handbook: Randomized or controlled human research; population: Human; Direct controlled human evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Limitations
  -: Severe hypoglycemia - potentially fatal; risk is highest with dose-food-activity mismatch
  -: Hypoglycemic coma or seizure
  -: Hypokalemia with IV insulin (intracellular K+ shift)
  -: Anaphylaxis (rare; historically more common with animal-derived formulations)
  -: Acute mortality risk from off-label athletic misuse due to unpredictable hypoglycemia in non-diabetic individuals
  *: Source rating: 5 out of 5
  *: The Peptide Handbook: strong-human. The DCCT was a landmark randomized study of intensive insulin treatment in type 1 diabetes and supports the clinical importance of glycemic control in that studied population. It is not a HUMULIN R U-100 label and does not support every regular-insulin dose or route claim. Current HUMULIN R U-100 labeling supports product-specific SC and IV use where permitted, individualized dosing, glucose monitoring, and risks including hypoglycemia, hypokalemia, and hypersensitivity. The strong evidence rating is scoped to established medical use of regular human insulin.

### compound | insulinglargine/half-life | What is the half life of Insulin Glargine?
kind: evidence
title: Insulin Glargine: source-listed half-life
summary: Source-listed values, with formulation, route and species context where available.
keyPoint: Source-listed values, with formulation, route and species context where available.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: Insulin Glargine
  connectedTo: Insulin Glargine
  *: Halflife Labs: ~12-19 hours SC. Elimination half-life approximately 12-19 hours SC per Heise T et al. Diabetes Care 2002 (PMID 11815489) and FDA NDA 021081. Peakless (flat) action profile with duration approximately 24 hours, supporting once-daily dosing. Mechanism: formulated at pH 4 (acidic solution); upon SC injection at physiological pH 7.4, glargine microprecipitates at the injection site, forming a depot that slowly dissolves to release insulin monomers over 24 hours. Two additional arginine residues at B30-C-terminus and A21 Asn→Gly substitution shift the isoelectric point to pH 6.7, driving microprecipitation at physiological pH. Not compatible with IV administration.
  followUp: What does the research say about how Insulin Glargine works?

### compound | ipamorelin/overview | What is Ipamorelin?
kind: overview
title: Ipamorelin
summary: A growth hormone secretagogue that stimulates GH release without significant effects on cortisol or prolactin. Developed by Novo Nordisk (Denmark); limited clinical development despite promising early data.
keyPoint: A growth hormone secretagogue that stimulates GH release without significant effects on cortisol or prolactin.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: Ipamorelin
  connectedTo: Ipamorelin
section: Why it is researched
  -: A growth hormone secretagogue that stimulates GH release without significant effects on cortisol or prolactin.
section: How it works in the research
  -: Ipamorelin acts as a selective growth hormone secretagogue through the ghrelin receptor: GHS -R1a Agonism Binds to the ghrelin receptor (GHS-R1a) on pituitary somatotrophs, triggering growth hormone release through Gq/11 protein activation.
section: Evidence strength
  -: PepCodex: Human clinical research; population: Human; Human evidence with design limitations to check. 4 human studies listed by the source
section: Main limitations
  -: The reviewed record does not state a specific limitation. The linked paper still needs to be checked for design, size and bias.

  -: Long-term safety and clinically meaningful outcomes have not been established
  -: The source does not clearly state the study population or design in PEARL's reviewed record.
  -: limited to a handful of trials, and its development program ended before approval.
  -: limited to two PK/PD studies and a discontinued Phase II trial; the majority of evidence derives from rodent models.
  -: not significantly stimulate ACTH, cortisol, or prolactin release at physiological doses (PMID: 9849822).
  -: not a limitation, preserving the physiologic pulsatility of GH secretion.
  -: No accumulation occurs with repeated dosing.
  -: not what it stimulates but what it does not - a selectivity profile that distinguishes it from earlier growth hormone secretagogues.
  -: not elevate plasma cortisol or ACTH at growth hormone-releasing doses.
  -: No significant prolactin elevation occurs, eliminating the gynecomastia concerns associated with GHRP-2 at higher doses.
  -: This is a commercial educational source. Its uncited figures and modelled outputs must remain labelled as source-listed rather than clinical evidence.
  *: Source rating: 3 out of 5
  *: PepCodex: Moderate evidence; 4 human studies listed
  *: The Peptide Handbook: preliminary. Preclinical research characterises ipamorelin as a selective growth-hormone secretagogue with minimal effects on cortisol and prolactin compared with older GHRPs (Raun et al. 1998). One prospective, randomized, controlled Phase II study evaluated ipamorelin for the management of postoperative ileus in bowel resection patients and did not establish significant efficacy versus placebo for that clinical endpoint (Beck et al. 2014). No large randomised outcome trials establish efficacy for age-related, body-composition, sleep, or performance claims. The evidence is limited to preclinical pharmacology and one exploratory clinical trial.
  *: Halflife Labs: Evidence context is stated on the linked compound page.
  *: Peptpedia: Human data comprises pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic study in volunteers and a completed Phase II trial for postoperative ileus (NCT00672074); ipamorelin's development for that indication was subsequently discontinued without approval, and no efficacy trials for growth-hormone deficiency, body composition, or anti-aging have been published. Long-term safety is uncharacterized.
  *: Peptide Hub: Protocol-focused educational summary. Linked papers, site-listed ranges and commercial context are retained with source attribution.
  *: Ipamorelin, the first selective growth hormone secretagogue (European Journal of Endocrinology 1998): Ipamorelin stimulated GH release comparably to GHRP-6 without elevating ACTH, cortisol, or prolactin at doses 200-fold above the ED50 - establishing it as the first GHRP-receptor agonist with true GH selectivity.

### compound | ipatesablend/overview | What is Ipamorelin + Tesamorelin?
kind: overview
title: Ipamorelin + Tesamorelin
summary: The Ipamorelin + Tesamorelin blend is an 18mg co-lyophilized advanced GH axis stimulation and visceral fat reduction stack (12mg Tesamorelin / 6mg Ipamorelin) - a 2:1 Tesamorelin-dominant ratio reflecting Tesamorelin's outsized role as the primary therapeutic driver in this combination. Tesamorelin is a synthetic analog of growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH) consisting of the full 44-amino acid GHRH(1-44) sequence with a trans-3-hexenoic acid modification at the N-terminus that dramatically increases plasma stability versus native GHRH (half-life approximately 30 minutes versus native GHRH's 7 minutes); it acts directly on GHRH receptors (GHRHR) in the anterior pituitary somatotroph cells to stimulate pulsatile growth hormone (GH) secretion and downstream hepatic IGF-1 production.

### compound | ipatesablend/safety | What are the risks of Ipamorelin + Tesamorelin?
kind: safety
title: Ipamorelin + Tesamorelin: source-listed risks
summary: Source-listed risks only. Missing human safety data does not mean a compound is safe.
keyPoint: Source-listed risks only.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: Ipamorelin + Tesamorelin
  connectedTo: Ipamorelin + Tesamorelin
  *: Injection site erythema and irritation - Tesamorelin (as the larger 44-amino acid peptide in this blend) is known to produce injection site redness and subcutaneous nodule formation more frequently than Ipamorelin alone; the FDA label for Egrifta (Tesamorelin) specifically lists injection site reactions as the most. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Joint pain and arthralgia - GH-mediated fluid retention and soft tissue changes produce joint discomfort, particularly in the wrists and ankles; more pronounced at higher doses (Advanced Recomposition protocol at 2.0mg Tesamorelin); typically resolves with dose reduction or cycle cessation. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Water retention and peripheral edema - GH stimulation increases renal sodium retention and antidiuretic hormone sensitivity; manifests as facial puffiness, ankle swelling, and body weight increase without fat gain; common in the first 2-4 weeks; typically attenuates as GH levels equilibrate. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Mild blood sugar fluctuations - GH-induced insulin resistance produces mild fasting glucose elevation; in non-diabetic subjects this typically remains within the normal range but warrants monitoring; more significant at the Advanced Recomposition 3.0mg/day dose. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Carpal tunnel syndrome symptoms - wrist paresthesias, nocturnal hand numbness, and grip weakness secondary to GH-driven soft tissue edema compressing the carpal tunnel; dose-dependent; typically reverses on cycle cessation. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Headache - commonly reported in the first 1-2 weeks; possibly related to GH-mediated intracranial pressure changes or fluid shifts; typically resolves with continued administration as GH levels stabilize. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Mild nausea - occasionally reported particularly with Tesamorelin at initiation; mechanism unclear; typically transient. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Vivid dreams and altered sleep architecture - GH secretion is closely linked to slow-wave sleep; amplifying the nocturnal GH pulse with pre-bed administration frequently produces vivid, highly detailed dreaming; typically reported as neutral to positive but occasionally disruptive in some subjects. [source-listed source severity]

### compound | ipatesablend/evidence | What research is listed for Ipamorelin + Tesamorelin?
kind: evidence
title: Ipamorelin + Tesamorelin: research listed by the sources
summary: Peptide University labels its records as aggregated from empirical research and anecdotal community data. This record is retained as supplied and is not upgraded to clinical evidence.
keyPoint: Peptide University labels its records as aggregated from empirical research and anecdotal community data.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: Ipamorelin + Tesamorelin
  connectedTo: Ipamorelin + Tesamorelin
section: What the research shows
  -: Peptide University Codex: The Ipamorelin + Tesamorelin blend is an 18mg co-lyophilized advanced GH axis stimulation and visceral fat reduction stack (12mg Tesamorelin / 6mg Ipamorelin) - a 2:1 Tesamorelin-dominant ratio reflecting Tesamorelin's outsized role as the primary therapeutic driver in this combination.
section: Evidence strength
  -: Peptide University Codex: Source summary; study design not clearly stated; population: Not clearly stated; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Limitations
  -: Active malignancy - both Tesamorelin (via IGF-1 elevation) and Ipamorelin (via GH stimulation) increase circulating IGF-1, a potent cellular growth factor with established roles in tumor cell proliferation, survival signaling (PI3K/AKT/mTOR), and angiogenesis; IGF-1 receptor (IGF-1R) overexpression or upregulation is
  -: History of rapidly progressive cancer - a history of cancer with documented rapid growth kinetics, IGF-1R expression, or hormonal sensitivity warrants particular caution; the time elapsed since treatment completion and the specific cancer type should be evaluated before initiating any GH axis compound.
  -: Disruption of the hypothalamic-pituitary axis - tumors of the pituitary (pituitary adenoma) or hypothalamus, or prior pituitary surgery or radiation, produce abnormal baseline GH regulation; exogenous GHRH and GHS-R agonism in subjects with hypothalamic-pituitary axis pathology has unpredictable GH secretory effects
  -: Acromegaly or GH excess states - subjects with pathological GH excess have already elevated IGF-1; further GH axis stimulation is absolutely contraindicated.
  -: Active diabetic retinopathy - GH elevation worsens diabetic retinopathy through IGF-1-mediated retinal neovascularization; subjects with pre-proliferative or proliferative diabetic retinopathy must not use GH secretagogues.
  -: Severe insulin resistance or uncontrolled type 2 diabetes - GH axis stimulation produces transient insulin resistance through GH receptor-mediated inhibition of insulin signaling in peripheral tissue; this is manageable in subjects with well-controlled diabetes but can significantly destabilize glycemic control in
  -: Carpal tunnel syndrome - GH elevation causes fluid retention and soft tissue edema that worsens carpal tunnel syndrome; a pre-existing carpal tunnel diagnosis requires dose reduction or avoidance.
  -: Known hypersensitivity to Tesamorelin, Ipamorelin, or formulation excipients.
  *: Source rating: 1 out of 5, very limited evidence
  *: Peptide University Codex: Peptide University labels its records as aggregated from empirical research and anecdotal community data. This record is retained as supplied and is not upgraded to clinical evidence.

### compound | kisspeptin-10/evidence | What research is listed for KissPeptin-10?
kind: evidence

section: What the research shows
  -: PepCodex: An endogenous neuropeptide that serves as the master regulator of reproductive function.
  -: The Peptide Handbook: A naturally occurring hypothalamic peptide that acts as a master upstream regulator of the reproductive hormone axis, triggering GnRH release and initiating the cascade that drives LH, FSH, and sex hormone production.
  -: Peptpedia: Triggers up to 50-fold LH surges and acts as the master switch of human puberty.
  -: PeptideDosage.org: Kisspeptin is a family of RF-amide neuropeptides encoded by the KISS1 gene (the founder peptide kisspeptin-54 and its cleavage products kisspeptin-14, -13, and -10) that act through the G-protein-coupled receptor KISS1R (GPR54) to control the hypothalamic gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) pulse generator [1][2].
  -: PeptideDeck: Recommended
section: Evidence strength
  -: PepCodex: Human clinical research; population: Human; Human evidence with design limitations to check. 18 human studies listed by the source
  -: The Peptide Handbook: Human clinical research; population: Human; Human evidence with design limitations to check. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: Peptpedia: Source summary; study design not clearly stated; population: Animal model; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: PeptideDosage.org: Human clinical research; population: Human; Human evidence with design limitations to check. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: PeptideDeck: Animal research; population: Animal; Preclinical animal evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.

  -: The reviewed record does not state a specific limitation. The linked paper still needs to be checked for design, size and bias.
  -: Endocrine effects vary by route, exposure pattern, sex, and menstrual phase
  -: Hormonal dysregulation
  -: No long-term human safety data for research use
  -: not just hormone secretion control.
  -: limited LH pulse rather than the sustained pharmacological hCG stimulation that causes ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (OHSS).
  -: not medical advice, and the compounds covered are research chemicals not approved for human use unless explicitly stated otherwise.
  -: Kisspeptin is a family of RF-amide neuropeptides encoded by the KISS1 gene (the founder peptide kisspeptin-54 and its cleavage products kisspeptin-14, -13, and -10) that act through the G-protein-coupled receptor KISS1R (GPR54) to control the hypothalamic gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) pulse generator [1][2].
  -: The reviewed record is animal research and cannot establish human effectiveness or safety.
  *: Source rating: 3 out of 5
  *: PepCodex: Moderate evidence; 18 human studies listed
  *: The Peptide Handbook: moderate. Direct KP-10 studies in healthy participants report endocrine responses after IV bolus, SC bolus, and IV infusion exposures. Responses vary by sex, menstrual phase, route, and study context. The direct comparison publication distinguishes KP-10 from KP-54 and GnRH. These physiology findings do not establish infertility-treatment efficacy, a universal pharmacokinetic value, or a standardized regimen; the cited continuous KP-10 study does not support a blanket suppression or tachyphylaxis claim.
  *: PeptideDosage.org: Across published clinical studies in over 1,000 cumulative participants, kisspeptin has been very well tolerated, with no serious adverse events attributable to the peptide and an adverse event profile comparable to placebo.; Injection site reactions including transient erythema, mild discomfort, and pruritus have been described in 5 to 20 percent of subcutaneous administrations, generally resolving within 24 hours.; Transient flushing and mild headache have been reported in approximately 5 to 10 percent of subjects after bolus dosing, consistent with the rapid LH/FSH surge.; In IVF protocols, the risk of ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome with kisspeptin-54 triggers is dramatically lower than with hCG, but mild and moderate cases have still been reported in women with very high follicle counts.; Theoretical concerns about KISS1R desensitization with continuous dosing have been raised; current protocols generally use intermittent bolus or short-duration infusion to preserve responsiveness.; Use in pregnancy has been studied (kisspeptin levels naturally rise dramatically during
  *: PeptideDeck: Stimulates natural LH and FSH release Increases endogenous testosterone production Potential fertility enhancement for both sexes Works through physiological pathways (GnRH system) May support natural hormone optimization Alternative PCT approach to hCG Rapid but transient effects (controllable) Extensively researched in reproductive medicine Kisspeptin research has accelerated rapidly since its discovery, particularly in reproductive medicine. Research published in the Journal of Clinical Endocrinology & Metabolism demonstrated that kisspeptin-10 administration to healthy men produced rapid, dose-dependent LH release, with consequent testosterone elevation. The response confirms kisspeptin's role as a physiological activator of the reproductive axis. Clinical studies have used doses ranging from 1-10mcg/kg for acute stimulation testing, typically IV or subcutaneous.
  *: PeptideDeck: Master regulator of GnRH pulsatile release Triggers LH and FSH secretion for reproductive function Stimulates natural testosterone production in males Promotes ovulation and follicular development in females Potential IVF trigger with reduced OHSS risk May restore hypothalamic function in functional hypothalamic amenorrhea Research applications in puberty and pubertal disorders Possible role in metabolic regulation and energy balance Research on kisspeptin has expanded dramatically since its reproductive role was discovered in 2003. Clinical trials have explored applications from infertility treatment to understanding puberty disorders, with particularly promising results in IVF protocols.
  *: Kisspeptin-10 Stimulates LH and Testosterone in Healthy Men (JCEM 2011): Kisspeptin-10 infusion potently stimulated LH pulsatility and testosterone in healthy men, establishing it as a physiological regulator of the HPG axis.

### compound | kisspeptin-54/overview | What is Kisspeptin-54?
kind: overview
title: Kisspeptin-54
summary: From Wikipep - The Peptide Encyclopedia Kisspeptin-54 Chemical name Metastin, KISS1 peptide Molecular formula C258H401N79O78 Molecular weight 5857.2 g/mol CAS number 338458-53-0 Sequence 54 amino acid peptide derived from KISS1 gene Length 54 amino acids Source Full-length KISS1 gene product Half-life 27-35 minutes Targets GPR54 (KISS1R) receptor Bioavailability Intravenous, subcutaneous injection Legal status Research compound only Kisspeptin-54 (also known as Metastin) is the full-length bioactive peptide derived from the KISS1 gene product, representing the complete 54-amino acid sequence with maximum biological activity for reproductive hormone regulation. Originally discovered as a metastasis suppressor peptide in melanoma cells, kisspeptin-54 has emerged as the master regulator of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal (HPG) axis and is considered the most potent natural stimulator of reproductive hormone release.

### compound | kisspeptin10oxytocinpt141blend/overview | What is EROS?
kind: overview
title: EROS
summary: EROS is a sexual wellness and reproductive-axis blend combining Kisspeptin-10, Oxytocin, and PT-141 into a single coordinated libido, arousal, bonding, and HPG-axis support system. The blend is structured around a 5mg Kisspeptin-10, 2mg Oxytocin, and 5mg PT-141 ratio, creating a 12mg total vial with a 5:2:5 composition. Kisspeptin-10 provides the hormonal infrastructure layer through KISS1R activation upstream of GnRH, LH, and FSH signaling. Oxytocin adds the emotional bonding, attachment, intimacy, and trust-signaling component through OXTR-mediated social and limbic circuitry. PT-141 provides the central arousal and desire layer through melanocortin MC3R/MC4R signaling. From a performance and optimization standpoint, EROS is positioned for low libido, HSDD, menopausal or andropausal libido decline, post-SSRI sexual dysfunction, sexual dysfunction with emotional disconnection, fertility-support contexts, and situational intimacy enhancement.
keyPoint: EROS is a sexual wellness and reproductive-axis blend combining Kisspeptin-10, Oxytocin, and PT-141 into a single coordinated libido, arousal, bonding, and HPG-axis support system.
understood: resolved
method: canonical

  -: Pregnancy or active attempts to conceive unless medically supervised due to the Oxytocin component and reproductive-axis signaling.
  -: Breastfeeding due to insufficient safety data and Oxytocin involvement in lactation physiology.

title: EROS: research listed by the sources
summary: Peptide University labels its records as aggregated from empirical research and anecdotal community data. This record is retained as supplied and is not upgraded to clinical evidence.
keyPoint: Peptide University labels its records as aggregated from empirical research and anecdotal community data.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: EROS
  connectedTo: EROS
section: What the research shows
  -: Peptide University Codex: EROS is a sexual wellness and reproductive-axis blend combining Kisspeptin-10, Oxytocin, and PT-141 into a single coordinated libido, arousal, bonding, and HPG-axis support system.
section: Evidence strength
  -: Peptide University Codex: Source summary; study design not clearly stated; population: Animal; Preclinical animal evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Limitations
  -: Known hypersensitivity to Kisspeptin-10, Oxytocin, PT-141, or formulation excipients.
  -: Pregnancy or active attempts to conceive unless medically supervised due to the Oxytocin component and reproductive-axis signaling.
  -: Breastfeeding due to insufficient safety data and Oxytocin involvement in lactation physiology.
  -: Uncontrolled hypertension or significant cardiovascular disease due to PT-141-associated blood pressure and flushing concerns.
  -: Concurrent use with uterotonic agents or prostaglandins unless medically supervised.
  -: History of hyponatremia, SIADH, or clinically significant water-balance disorders due to Oxytocin-related antidiuretic signaling concerns.
  -: Concurrent use with desmopressin or vasopressin analogs unless medically supervised due to additive water-retention and hyponatremia risk.

TB-500 is the synthetic fragment of thymosin beta-4 comprising amino acids 17-23 (Ac-LKKTETQ), which contains the actin-binding domain responsible for most biological effects. Cleared primarily via proteolytic degradation. No published human PK data as of May 2026.

### compound | kpv/overview | What is KPV?
kind: overview
title: KPV
summary: A naturally occurring tripeptide derived from the C-terminus of alpha-melanocyte-stimulating hormone (alpha-MSH). Preclinical studies demonstrate potent anti-inflammatory effects via NF-kB inhibition, but no human clinical trials have been conducted. Research has focused on inflammatory bowel disease and skin inflammation models.
keyPoint: A naturally occurring tripeptide derived from the C-terminus of alpha-melanocyte-stimulating hormone (alpha-MSH).
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: KPV
  connectedTo: KPV
section: Why it is researched
  -: A naturally occurring tripeptide derived from the C-terminus of alpha-melanocyte-stimulating hormone (alpha-MSH).
section: How it works in the research
  -: KPV acts as an “inflammation brake” that works at the cellular level through several pathways: NF-kB Inhibition Blocks the master inflammation switch by preventing IkBa degradation .
section: Evidence strength
  -: Peptide Authority: Animal research; population: Human; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Main limitations
  -: Whether a UK-purchased KPV product contains the tripeptide at the labelled concentration.
  -: Whether oral administration produces meaningful systemic exposure.
  -: How it interacts with biologics (anti-TNF) or steroids used in IBD.

### compound | kpv/evidence | What research is listed for KPV?
kind: evidence
title: KPV: research listed by the sources
summary: Strong animal data. Limited human trials.
keyPoint: Strong animal data.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: KPV
  connectedTo: KPV
section: What the research shows
  -: PepCodex: A naturally occurring tripeptide derived from the C-terminus of alpha-melanocyte-stimulating hormone (alpha-MSH).
  -: The Peptide Handbook: A short tripeptide derived from alpha-MSH, studied in animal and laboratory research for anti-inflammatory mechanisms - particularly in the gut - including NF-κB pathway-related work.
  -: Halflife Labs: KPV (Lys-Pro-Val), the C-terminal tripeptide fragment of alpha-melanocyte-stimulating hormone (α-MSH), has an estimated plasma half-life of minutes based on peptide class characteristics.
  -: Peptpedia: The anti-inflammatory tail of alpha-MSH - cuts NF-kB activation up to 80% without tanning or appetite effects.
  -: PeptideDosage.org: KPV is the C-terminal tripeptide of alpha-melanocyte-stimulating hormone (Lys-Pro-Val, residues 11-13 of alpha-MSH) that retains the broad anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory activity of the parent hormone while lacking the pigmentary effects mediated through melanocortin-1 receptor activation on melanocytes [1][2].
section: Evidence strength
  -: PepCodex: Source summary; study design not clearly stated; population: Not clearly stated; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: The Peptide Handbook: Laboratory or mechanistic research; population: Laboratory; Early laboratory evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: Halflife Labs: Animal research; population: Animal; Preclinical animal evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: Peptpedia: Source summary; study design not clearly stated; population: Not clearly stated; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: PeptideDosage.org: Animal research; population: Animal; Preclinical animal evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Limitations
  -: The source does not clearly state the study population or design in PEARL's reviewed record.
  -: Current evidence in this record is animal and in-vitro; human safety has not been established.
  -: The reviewed record is animal research and cannot establish human effectiveness or safety.
  -: not blocked by melanocortin receptor antagonists, confirming receptor-independent mechanisms.
  -: not bind melanocortin receptors at physiologically relevant concentrations-its anti-inflammatory mechanism is entirely receptor-independent, involving direct intracellular NF-κB pathway inhibition.
  -: not fully characterized but may relate to its small size (3 amino acids), resistance to standard proteolytic cleavage at its Pro-Val junction, and possible paracellular uptake at inflamed intestinal epithelium.
  -: no Phase 3 clinical trials.
  -: not immunosuppressive-it selectively blunts pro-inflammatory signaling while preserving beneficial immune responses.
  -: No human wound healing clinical trials of KPV exist as of 2026.
  -: limited by the lack of commercial development funding.
  -: not cause darkening of skin or mucous membranes, making it more suitable for chronic use in inflammatory conditions.
  -: KPV is the C-terminal tripeptide of alpha-melanocyte-stimulating hormone (Lys-Pro-Val, residues 11-13 of alpha-MSH) that retains the broad anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory activity of the parent hormone while lacking the pigmentary effects mediated through melanocortin-1 receptor activation on melanocytes
  *: Source rating: 2 out of 5, limited evidence
  *: The Peptide Handbook: preliminary. KPV has preclinical and mechanistic evidence in this record. Murine inflammatory bowel disease work, in-vitro bronchial epithelial research, and intestinal uptake experiments support further investigation of anti-inflammatory mechanisms, but do not establish human therapeutic efficacy, oral clinical bioavailability, or chronic safety.
  *: Halflife Labs: Animal/In-vitro
  *: PeptideDosage.org: KPV has been broadly described as well tolerated in preclinical studies, with no serious adverse events attributable to the peptide in published animal studies and the limited human pilot data.; Injection site reactions including mild erythema and transient discomfort are the most common adverse events with subcutaneous administration; oral dosing has been associated with rare mild gastrointestinal symptoms.; Unlike alpha-MSH, KPV does not cause hyperpigmentation because it does not significantly activate MC1R on melanocytes; this is a key advantage for chronic use.; Theoretical concerns include immunosuppression with prolonged high-dose use; KPV's anti-inflammatory mechanism could theoretically attenuate normal immune surveillance, although this has not been demonstrated in published studies.; Long-term safety data are limited; published human exposure is restricted to short-term courses, and chronic dosing safety has not been characterized.; Use in pregnancy, lactation, and pediatric populations has not been adequately studied and is not recommended.; Drug-drug interactions have
  *: PeptideDeck: Potent anti-inflammatory activity without melanocortin receptor activation Reduction of pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-6, IL-1β) Intestinal epithelial barrier protection and healing NF-κB signaling pathway inhibition Wound healing acceleration in skin models Antimicrobial properties against certain pathogens Colitis symptom reduction in animal models Minimal side effect profile due to targeted mechanism The research literature on KPV spans over two decades, with particular acceleration in IBD-related studies over the past several years. While human clinical trials remain limited, the preclinical evidence provides a consistent picture of KPV's anti-inflammatory capabilities.

  -: Glutathione (γ-L-glutamyl-L-cysteinyl-glycine, GSH) is an endogenous tripeptide and the body's principal intracellular antioxidant.

  *: Source rating: 3 out of 5
  *: PepCodex: Moderate evidence; 20 human studies listed
  *: The Peptide Handbook: preliminary. Glutathione's endogenous redox biology is extremely well established, but therapeutic-administration evidence is indication- and formulation-specific. A small open-label study (n=9) of IV glutathione in early Parkinson's disease reported symptom changes over 30 days without a placebo comparator - suggestive, not definitive. A historical randomized trial found IV/IM glutathione reduced cisplatin-induced neurotoxicity in a specific chemotherapy protocol for advanced gastric cancer - evidence specific to that regimen and population, not general chemoprotection. A subsequent review characterizes the Parkinson's disease evidence base as still limited. No citation supporting NAFLD or male-infertility efficacy claims was identified despite a targeted search, and those claims have been removed rather than carried forward unsupported. Oral bioavailability remains limited by intestinal hydrolysis.
  *: PeptideDosage.org: Intravenous glutathione is generally well tolerated, but rare cases of bronchospasm, particularly in asthmatic patients, have been reported and the infusion should be administered slowly and discontinued at the first sign of respiratory symptoms.; Anaphylactoid reactions, hypotension, flushing, and rash have been documented with IV glutathione; Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis have been reported in unregulated cosmetic skin-lightening protocols using high-dose IV GSH.; Intramuscular administration can produce injection-site pain, induration, and rarely sterile abscess; intranasal use can cause local irritation and rhinorrhea.; Oral GSH is generally well tolerated; mild gastrointestinal upset, flatulence, and a transient sulfur taste or odor (from cysteine release) are the most common complaints.; Sulfite hypersensitivity may be relevant because some IV glutathione formulations contain sulfite preservatives; asthmatic patients should be evaluated for sulfite sensitivity before treatment.; Use during pregnancy and lactation has not been adequately studied; while
  *: PeptideDeck: Neutralizes reactive oxygen species and free radicals Phase II liver detoxification of drugs, pollutants, and heavy metals Regenerates vitamins C and E back to their active forms Supports T-cell proliferation and natural killer cell activity Protects mitochondrial DNA from oxidative damage Reduces melanin synthesis - studied for skin lightening effects Modulates inflammatory cytokine signaling (NF-κB pathway) Maintains cellular redox balance critical for protein folding and DNA repair With over 170,000 published papers, glutathione research spans virtually every field of medicine. The following summarizes key findings across the most active research areas.
  *: PeptideDeck: Published March 15, 2026 Updated September 4, 2026 Quick Brief Glutathione is the body's most powerful intracellular antioxidant. This guide covers every documented benefit, which forms actually absorb, the right doses for each application, and what to watch for. Glutathione Peptide: Benefits, Dosage and Side Effects (2026) Procurement Embody Glutathione Ships from USA Start Glutathione Treatment Your body makes its own antioxidant. Glutathione is a tripeptide produced naturally in every cell, and it's the most abundant intracellular antioxidant in the human body. The problem is levels decline significantly with age, stress, illness, and alcohol use. By middle age, most people are running on roughly half the glutathione they had at 20. Supplementing directly or supporting the body's production is one of the most evidence-backed interventions in the antioxidant space. This guide covers the benefits, the forms that actually work, the right doses, and what to watch for.
  *: Intravenous glutathione prevents renal oxidative stress after coronary angiography more effectively than oral N-acetylcysteine (Heart and Vessels 2011): Prospective controlled clinical study (n=21) demonstrating IV glutathione administered before coronary angiography prevented contrast-induced renal oxidative stress more effectively than oral NAC, providing direct human evidence for IV glutathione's antioxidant protection.

### compound | lactoferricin/overview | What is Lactoferricin?
kind: overview
title: Lactoferricin
summary: An antimicrobial peptide derived from lactoferrin, a protein found in milk and other secretions. Shows broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity in laboratory studies. Research focuses on potential applications in infectious disease, food safety, and cancer. Primarily studied preclinically with very limited human clinical data. Not approved as a therapeutic by any regulatory agency.

  -: PeptideJournal: Review or official medicine information; population: Not clearly stated; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Limitations
  -: Long-term safety data are limited.
  -: No FDA-approved indication.
  -: This is a commercial educational source. Its uncited figures and modelled outputs must remain labelled as source-listed rather than clinical evidence.
  -: The source does not clearly state the study population or design in PEARL's reviewed record.
  -: The Phase 3 Failure The most significant limitation is that larazotide did not demonstrate sufficient efficacy in its Phase 3 trial.
  -: The treatment effect may have been modest enough that it did not reproduce in a larger, more diverse population.
  -: High placebo response rates in celiac symptom trials - a well-known challenge - likely compounded the problem.
  -: Outcome Measure Challenges Celiac disease is difficult to study with patient-reported outcome measures.
  -: Symptoms overlap with irritable bowel syndrome, dietary indiscretions are hard to monitor, and the subjective nature of GI symptoms introduces noise.
  -: The switch from CeD-GSRS (Phase 2b) to CeD PRO abdominal domain (Phase 3) may have contributed to the different results.
  -: The Zonulin Measurement Controversy Studies from 2018 onward revealed that widely used commercial ELISA kits marketed for measuring serum zonulin do not actually detect zonulin (pre-haptoglobin-2).
  -: Instead, they detect unrelated proteins including properdin and complement C3.

### compound | larazotideacetate/overview | What is Larazotide acetate?
kind: overview
title: Larazotide acetate
summary: Larazotide acetate (AT-1001, INN-202) is a synthetic single-chain octapeptide (Gly-Gly-Val-Leu-Val-Gln-Pro-Gly) derived from the zonula occludens toxin of Vibrio cholerae and developed as a first-in-class tight-junction regulator, or zonulin antagonist, for celiac disease. Rather than suppressing the immune system, it acts locally at the apical surface of the small-intestinal epithelium to blunt zonulin-driven opening of the paracellular tight junctions, reducing the leak of gluten peptides across the gut barrier. Because it is minimally absorbed into the bloodstream, it has no meaningful systemic exposure and is taken by mouth as a delayed-release capsule before meals. In the pivotal Phase 2b trial, the most-studied and only statistically effective Larazotide acetate dosage was 0.5 mg three times daily before meals; counter-intuitively, the higher 1 mg and 2 mg arms performed no better than placebo, producing an inverted dose-response curve.

### compound | larazotideacetate/evidence | What research is listed for Larazotide acetate?
kind: evidence
title: Larazotide acetate: research listed by the sources
summary: Larazotide acetate has a notably favorable tolerability profile across more than 15 years of trials; single and multiple oral doses from roughly 0.25 mg up to 36 mg were generally well tolerated with no serious drug-related adverse events reported in early studies [1][4].; Headache was the most commonly reported adverse event in clinical studies, but its frequency did not differ meaningfully between larazotide and placebo groups, making it difficult to attribute directly to the drug [1].; Gastrointestinal symptoms (abdominal pain, bloating, diarrhea, nausea, flatulence) were reported, but in celiac patients these are often indistinguishable from the underlying disease and from gluten exposure rather than the peptide itself [1][2].; No clinically significant hepatic, renal, or bone toxicity was observed in the trial program, consistent with the drug's minimal systemic absorption and gut-restricted action [4].; Because larazotide acts locally and is essentially not absorbed, systemic and off-target effects are expected to be low; however, it is not a substitute for a gluten-free diet

### compound | lcarnitine/overview | What is L-Carnitine?
kind: overview
title: L-Carnitine
summary: L-Carnitine is a quaternary ammonium compound synthesized endogenously from lysine and methionine that serves as an obligate cofactor in long-chain fatty acid transport into mitochondria for β-oxidation. The carnitine palmitoyltransferase (CPT-1 and CPT-2) system shuttles long-chain acyl-CoA across the inner mitochondrial membrane, supplying substrate for cardiac, skeletal muscle, and hepatic ATP production. Primary and secondary carnitine deficiencies cause cardiomyopathy, skeletal myopathy, and hypoketotic hypoglycemia. Oral L-carnitine is FDA-approved for primary and secondary carnitine deficiency (Carnitor) at doses of 1000-3000 mg per day in adults. Off-label clinical uses include diabetes, fatty liver disease, peripheral artery disease, infertility, and fatigue. A meta-analysis of 37 randomized trials found 2000 mg/day maximizes weight-loss effects. Research IM/SC injection of 200-500 mg is used in performance and recovery protocols, although evidence is largely anecdotal.
keyPoint: L-Carnitine is a quaternary ammonium compound synthesized endogenously from lysine and methionine that serves as an obligate cofactor in long-chain fatty acid transport into mitochondria for β-oxidation.

### compound | lcarnitine/safety | What are the risks of L-Carnitine?
kind: safety
title: L-Carnitine: source-listed risks
summary: Source-listed risks only. Missing human safety data does not mean a compound is safe.

understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: L-Carnitine
  connectedTo: L-Carnitine
  *: 10 Potential Benefits & Side Effects Observations from clinical and preclinical literature on L-Carnitine supplementation. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Potential Benefits Enhanced fat metabolism: Facilitates mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation and ATP production from lipid stores [1] . [source-listed source severity]
  *: Weight management: Meta-analysis shows modest weight loss (~1.2 kg average) and reduction in BMI with oral supplementation at ~2 g/day [2] . [source-listed source severity]
  *: Exercise performance: May improve exercise capacity and reduce fatigue, particularly in carnitine-deficient populations [5] . [source-listed source severity]
  *: Avoids TMAO production: Subcutaneous route bypasses gut bacterial conversion to TMAO, potentially reducing cardiovascular risk associated with oral dosing [4] [9] . [source-listed source severity]
  *: Energy support: Clinical studies in dialysis patients show reduced fatigue and improved well-being with parenteral L-Carnitine [5] . [source-listed source severity]
  *: Potential Side Effects Injection-site reactions: Mild redness, swelling, or irritation at injection sites (typically transient). [source-listed source severity]
  *: Gastrointestinal effects (oral): High oral doses (>3 g/day) can cause nausea, diarrhea, and fishy body odor from metabolite accumulation [9] . [source-listed source severity]

### compound | lcarnitine/evidence | What research is listed for L-Carnitine?
kind: evidence
title: L-Carnitine: research listed by the sources
summary: Oral L-carnitine commonly produces mild gastrointestinal effects including nausea, abdominal cramping, diarrhea, and a fishy body odor caused by gut microbial conversion to trimethylamine; the odor effect is dose-dependent and reversible.; Intravenous and intramuscular L-carnitine can cause injection-site pain, transient hypotension, and rarely allergic reactions; sterile preparations and standard injection technique mitigate most local risks.; Carnitine can lower seizure threshold in patients with epilepsy who are not on valproic acid, but conversely is used to mitigate valproate-induced hyperammonemia and hepatotoxicity in seizure populations.; Concerns have been raised about gut microbial conversion of dietary L-carnitine to trimethylamine-N-oxide (TMAO), a metabolite associated with cardiovascular risk in epidemiologic studies, although supplementation trials have not demonstrated adverse cardiac outcomes.; Pharmacological doses can interact with thyroid hormone signaling, potentially reducing thyroid hormone receptor activity; supplementation should be approached cautiously in Peptide University labels its records as aggregated from empirical research and anecdotal community data. This record is retained as supplied and is not upgraded to clinical evidence.

section: Limitations
  -: L-Carnitine is a quaternary ammonium compound synthesized endogenously from lysine and methionine that serves as an obligate cofactor in long-chain fatty acid transport into mitochondria for β-oxidation.
  -: 14 Important Note This content is intended for therapeutic educational purposes only and does not constitute medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment.
  -: L-Carnitine is provided for research purposes only and is not intended for human consumption.
  -: All protocols described are for educational and informational purposes.
  -: Consult qualified professionals before beginning any supplementation or research protocol.
  -: Hypothyroidism (may interfere with thyroid hormone action) - L-Carnitine acts as a functional thyroid hormone antagonist at the receptor level; it inhibits thyroid hormone entry into cell nuclei, reducing gene transactivation by T3 and T4; subjects with hypothyroidism should be aware that L-Carnitine supplementation
  -: Concurrent levothyroxine or thyroid hormone therapy - L-Carnitine's peripheral anti-thyroid action may reduce the effectiveness of thyroid replacement therapy; monitor thyroid function if co-administering.
  -: End-stage renal disease (ESRD) without dialysis - L-Carnitine is renally excreted; accumulation to toxic levels is possible in severe renal failure; patients on hemodialysis may actually require carnitine supplementation due to dialytic losses, but administration should be clinically supervised.
  -: Seizure disorder - rare reports of increased seizure frequency in subjects with pre-existing seizure disorders using L-Carnitine supplementation; mechanism not fully characterized; use with caution.
  -: Known hypersensitivity to L-Carnitine or injectable formulation excipients.
  -: Concurrent anticoagulant therapy (warfarin) - case reports suggest L-Carnitine potentiates the anticoagulant effect of warfarin; INR monitoring is warranted if co-administering.
  -: Trimethylaminuria (fish odor syndrome) - subjects with impaired FMO3 enzyme activity cannot efficiently oxidize TMA to TMAO; even injectable carnitine metabolism may produce systemic TMA accumulation and severe body odor.
  *: Source rating: 1 out of 5, very limited evidence

### compound | lcarnitinelc500/overview | What is L-Carnitine (LC500)?
kind: overview
title: L-Carnitine (LC500)
summary: L-Carnitine (product code LC500) is a single-ingredient injectable delivering a high 500mg dose of L-Carnitine per milliliter. It is an amino acid derivative rather than a peptide, and it works through a well-defined metabolic mechanism rather than a hormone receptor, given as a fixed direct dose with no titration. L-Carnitine is a compound the body uses to transport long-chain fatty acids across the mitochondrial membrane so they can be oxidized for energy. Injectable delivery bypasses the relatively poor and variable absorption of oral carnitine, which allows a much higher effective dose to reach circulation and, in turn, the muscle and other tissues that rely on fatty-acid oxidation. In practice, LC500 is used by people focused on fat metabolism, endurance, and recovery who want a potent, standalone carnitine injection rather than a multi-ingredient blend.
keyPoint: L-Carnitine (product code LC500) is a single-ingredient injectable delivering a high 500mg dose of L-Carnitine per milliliter.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high

### compound | leptin/overview | What is Leptin?
kind: overview
title: Leptin
summary: An endogenous metabolic hormone from adipose tissue that signals energy stores to the brain; metreleptin (MYALEPT) is its recombinant replacement therapy for complications of leptin deficiency in generalized lipodystrophy.
keyPoint: An endogenous metabolic hormone from adipose tissue that signals energy stores to the brain; metreleptin (MYALEPT) is its recombinant replacement therapy for complications of leptin deficiency in generalized lipodystrophy.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: Leptin
  connectedTo: Leptin
section: Why it is researched
  -: An endogenous metabolic hormone from adipose tissue that signals energy stores to the brain; metreleptin (MYALEPT) is its recombinant replacement therapy for complications of leptin deficiency in generalized lipodystrophy.
section: How it works in the research
  -: Leptin is an adipose-derived hormone that helps signal energy stores to the hypothalamus, influencing appetite, energy homeostasis, and neuroendocrine physiology.
section: Evidence strength
  -: Peptide Authority: Animal research; population: Human; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Main limitations
  -: Whether a UK-purchased 'leptin' product contains the protein at the labelled concentration.
  -: Whether you actually have leptin deficiency - almost certainly not (extremely rare condition).
  -: Whether your weight regulation problem is leptin-driven (mostly it isn't; common obesity is leptin-resistant).

### compound | leptin/safety | What are the risks of Leptin?
kind: safety
title: Leptin: source-listed risks
summary: Source-listed risks only. Missing human safety data does not mean a compound is safe.
keyPoint: Source-listed risks only.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: Leptin
  connectedTo: Leptin
  *: Hypoglycemia, particularly when used with insulin or insulin secretagogues. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Injection site reactions (bruising, erythema, hematoma). [source-listed source severity]
  *: Anti-metreleptin antibodies with neutralizing activity may inhibit endogenous leptin action and/or cause loss of MYALEPT efficacy; worsening metabolic control or severe infection has been reported. [source-listed source severity]
  *: T-cell lymphoma has been reported in patients with acquired generalized lipodystrophy both treated and not treated with MYALEPT; a causal relationship has not been established. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Hypoglycemia can occur when MYALEPT is used with insulin or insulin secretagogues; dose adjustment and glucose monitoring may be required. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Progression of autoimmune disorders has been observed with MYALEPT. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Serious hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis, have been reported with MYALEPT. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Moderate Safety profile partly characterised; some signals from observational or preclinical data. [source-listed source severity]

### compound | leptin/evidence | What research is listed for Leptin?
kind: evidence
title: Leptin: research listed by the sources
summary: strong-human. Leptin is an adipose-derived hormone that signals energy stores to the hypothalamus and helps regulate appetite, energy balance, and neuroendocrine physiology. Metreleptin is approved as replacement therapy for complications of leptin deficiency in congenital or acquired generalized lipodystrophy, a rare population distinct from common obesity. Long-term human evidence in generalized lipodystrophy demonstrated sustained improvements in glycemic control, triglycerides, and liver volume. Common obesity generally does not represent simple leptin deficiency; leptin resistance and other biological and environmental factors may contribute, and metreleptin is not an established treatment for common obesity. Moderate human evidence Endogenous satiety hormone. The recombinant analogue metreleptin (Myalept) is licensed in some jurisdictions for rare leptin-deficiency states; common obesity is leptin-resistant, so adding leptin generally does not help. Human evidence grade B, Moderate human evidence. Citation quality grade B, Moderate human evidence.
keyPoint: strong-human.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high

### compound | leuphasyl/overview | What is Leuphasyl?
kind: overview
title: Leuphasyl
summary: Leuphasyl is the trade name for Pentapeptide-18 (INCI: Pentapeptide-18; CAS 64963-01-5), a synthetic cosmetic anti-wrinkle peptide developed by Lipotec (now Lubrizol). Its sequence, Tyr-D-Ala-Gly-Phe-Leu, is an enkephalin mimic modeled on natural leucine-enkephalin (Tyr-Gly-Gly-Phe-Leu); a single D-alanine substitution at position 2 makes it far more resistant to aminopeptidase degradation than the native opioid pentapeptide [1][2]. Like enkephalins, Leuphasyl binds neuronal enkephalin (opioid) receptors and, through G-protein modulation of calcium and potassium channels, reduces acetylcholine release at the neuromuscular junction of facial mimetic muscles, softening dynamic expression lines without paralysis [1][5]. In real-world use it is a topical cosmeceutical, formulated at roughly 2-10% in serums and creams and applied twice daily; it is frequently paired with Argireline (Acetyl Hexapeptide-8) in the Argirelox blend for a synergistic effect [2][6].
keyPoint: Leuphasyl is the trade name for Pentapeptide-18 (INCI: Pentapeptide-18; CAS 64963-01-5), a synthetic cosmetic anti-wrinkle peptide developed by Lipotec (now Lubrizol).

### compound | leuphasyl/evidence | What research is listed for Leuphasyl?
kind: evidence
title: Leuphasyl: research listed by the sources
summary: Used as intended (a topical cosmetic), Leuphasyl is generally very well tolerated; the most common reactions are mild, transient erythema, stinging, or a sensation of tightness at the application site, especially when layered with retinoids or exfoliating acids.; Allergic contact dermatitis to Pentapeptide-18 itself is uncommon, but reactions to other components of the finished formulation (preservatives, fragrance, penetration enhancers) can produce eczematous patches and warrant dermatologic evaluation if persistent.; Because the peptide is used near the eyes and forehead, accidental ocular contact may cause transient conjunctival irritation, watering, or burning; keep the product off the eye margin and rinse promptly with water if it migrates onto the ocular surface.; No systemic neuromuscular adverse events (dysphagia, ptosis, generalized weakness) have been reported, because the peptide is not meaningfully absorbed into the circulation through intact skin and does not produce the chemodenervation associated with botulinum toxin.; Safety data in pregnancy, lactation, and Lipotec Study (In Vivo) : 5% Leuphasyl cream × 15 days → 11.6% reduction in wrinkle depth around eyes (N=20) Synergy Study : Leuphasyl + Argireline combination → 24.6% reduction in wrinkle depth (vs. 11.6% Leuphasyl alone and 16.3% Argireline alone) - demonstrating true synergy In Vitro : Reduced neurotransmitter release in cell culture models at 100ppm concentration 🧪 Vial Dex The World's Most Advanced Peptide Calculator 100% FREE 💧 Reconstitution Vial + BAC water mixing 📉 Dose & Units Syringe units to draw 🔀 Blend Multi-peptide vial ratios 📚 Stack Protocol Multi-vial dose planning 💨 Nasal Spray Spray bottle concentrations 50+ Peptides 7 Calculators 0 Signup Required Peptide: Leuphasyl Open Free Calculator → [ 1 ] [ 2 ] [ 3 ] [ 4 ] ↑ 1.0 1.1 Lipotec Technical Data: Leuphasyl (Pentapeptide-18).   *: PeptideJournal: Every time you smile, frown, or squint, the muscles beneath your skin contract. Repeat this thousands of times over the years, and you get expression lines - the forehead creases, crow's feet, and frown lines that etch themselves into the face. Leuphasyl is a synthetic pentapeptide designed to mimic enkephalin, a naturally occurring neurotransmitter that reduces neuronal excitability and acetylcholine release. By binding to opioid receptors at the neuromuscular junction, Leuphasyl reduces the signal that tells facial muscles to contract. This leads to fewer dynamic wrinkles - particularly in expression-prone areas like the forehead and around the eyes. The peptide has a unique mechanism compared to other anti-wrinkle ingredients. While Argireline blocks vesicle fusion and Syn-Ake blocks acetylcholine receptors on the muscle, Leuphasyl works upstream at the receptor level on the nerve. This makes it a natural candidate for combination formulations, where its effects can be amplified by peptides that target different steps in the contraction pathway.

### compound | leuprolide/evidence | What research is listed for Leuprolide?
kind: evidence
title: Leuprolide: research listed by the sources
summary: strong-human. Current Lupron Depot labeling establishes the represented product's authorized indications and risk information. This record does not make a comparative efficacy claim across all leuprolide products, GnRH agonists, antagonists, or clinical contexts. Vasomotor hot flashes are the most common adverse effect across all indications, reflecting the intended drop in sex steroids; sweating and flushing are frequently reported [1][7].; A testosterone 'flare' occurs in the first 1-2 weeks as LH/FSH transiently surge; in advanced prostate cancer this can briefly worsen bone pain, urinary obstruction, or spinal-cord-compression risk, and is commonly pre-empted with an antiandrogen during initiation [1][6].; Hypogonadal effects predominate with continued use: in men, decreased libido, erectile dysfunction, and testicular atrophy; in women, hypoestrogenic symptoms such as vaginal dryness, irregular bleeding, and mood changes [2][7].; Prolonged therapy reduces bone mineral density and raises fracture risk; gynecologic courses are generally limited (e.g., ~6 months, or up to 12 months with add-back therapy), and bone monitoring or calcium/vitamin D and add-back hormones may be advised [2].; Metabolic and cardiovascular warnings on GnRH agonist labeling include hyperglycemia and new or worsening diabetes, plus an increased risk of myocardial

### compound | libidon/overview | What is Libidon?
kind: overview
title: Libidon
summary: Libidon (Prostate Cytomax A-16) is an oral peptide bioregulator from the Khavinson family of tissue-specific "cytomax" preparations developed at the St. Petersburg Institute of Bioregulation and Gerontology. Each capsule supplies 10 mg of peptide complex A-16, a low-molecular-weight fraction (under ~5,000 Da) of di-, tri- and tetrapeptides isolated from the prostate tissue of young cattle [4][8]. Rather than acting as a hormone or enzyme blocker, these ultrashort peptides are proposed to enter cells, reach the nucleus, and bind specific promoter regions of DNA, modulating tissue-specific gene expression and protein synthesis in prostate and immune cells [1][2]. The most-cited Libidon dosage is 20 mg per day, taken as one 10 mg capsule twice daily with meals across a 30-day course, with a lighter 10 mg/day option and a 10-day maintenance pulse repeated every 3-6 months [4].

### compound | libidon/safety | What are the risks of Libidon?
kind: safety
title: Libidon: source-listed risks
summary: Source-listed risks only. Missing human safety data does not mean a compound is safe.
keyPoint: Source-listed risks only.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: Libidon
  connectedTo: Libidon
  *: Mild transient urinary changes in first cycle days - as prostatic tissue remodeling begins, some subjects note mild transient changes in urinary stream or frequency in the first 3-5 days; typically self-limiting. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Transient mild pelvic pressure - uncommon; as prostatic bioregulator activity initiates, mild pelvic awareness is occasionally reported in the first days; not associated with pain; resolves within the first week. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Mild PSA fluctuation - as prostatic epithelial cell kallikrein production normalizes, PSA levels may undergo minor fluctuations during active cycle days; clinically relevant context for subjects with monitored PSA. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Mild gastrointestinal discomfort from oral capsule - as a with-meals oral cytomedin; occasional mild gastric discomfort in first days. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Mild ejaculatory changes - as prostatic secretory function normalizes, some subjects notice minor changes in ejaculate volume or consistency during active cycle periods; typically normalizes post-cycle. [source-listed source severity]
  *: No serious prostate-related adverse events documented in the Khavinson clinical study or research literature at standard protocol doses - Libidon's safety profile in BPH, prostatitis, and aging male reproductive health populations is clean. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Unknown interaction with 5-alpha reductase inhibitors (finasteride, dutasteride) - androgen-dependent prostatic mechanisms of Libidon may be partially blunted by reduced DHT levels produced by 5-ARI therapy; not documented as an adverse interaction. [source-listed source severity]

### compound | libidon/evidence | What research is listed for Libidon?
kind: evidence
title: Libidon: research listed by the sources
summary: Manufacturer and institute sources report that Libidon was well tolerated with no adverse effects, complications, or dependence over the 30-day course [4]; however, this rests on short-term, institute-internal observation, so an absence of side effects has not been confirmed by independent randomized trials.; Because the product is a bovine tissue extract, there is a theoretical risk of hypersensitivity or allergic reaction; it should be avoided by anyone with known allergy to beef or bovine proteins, and animal-tissue sourcing carries general (if low) prion/contaminant considerations addressed through manufacturing controls.; Libidon is not a substitute for medical evaluation of prostate symptoms: lower urinary tract symptoms, an elevated PSA, urinary retention, or new pelvic pain require physician work-up to exclude prostate cancer and other pathology, and self-treating can delay diagnosis.; Route caveat: actually injecting a bovine tissue extract, as the educational model on this page depicts, is not how the product is used and could cause injection-site reactions, infection, or Peptide University labels its records as aggregated from empirical research and anecdotal community data. This record is retained as supplied and is not upgraded to clinical evidence.

  -: Peptide University Codex: Libidon is a Khavinson cytomedin - peptide complex A-16 - extracted from prostate gland tissue of young animals, developed as the oral prostatic bioregulator of the Khavinson framework and the commercial cytomedin counterpart to Prostamax (the injectable synthetic tetrapeptide Lys-Glu-Asp-Trp).
section: Evidence strength
  -: PeptideDosage.org: Randomized or controlled human research; population: Human; Direct controlled human evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: Peptide University Codex: Source summary; study design not clearly stated; population: Animal; Preclinical animal evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Limitations
  -: Libidon (Prostate Cytomax A-16) is an oral peptide bioregulator from the Khavinson family of tissue-specific "cytomax" preparations developed at the St. Petersburg Institute of Bioregulation and Gerontology.
  -: Known or suspected prostate cancer - prostatic cell gene program normalization in malignant prostate tissue has not been evaluated; absolute contraindication pending oncological evaluation; PSA elevation without biopsy evaluation requires exclusion of malignancy before initiating.
  -: Active bacterial prostatitis in acute phase - bioregulator activity during active bacterial prostate infection should be deferred until antimicrobial treatment is complete.
  -: Active androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) - Libidon's prostatic bioregulator mechanism depends on androgen receptor signaling; in the context of ADT-induced castrate testosterone levels, androgen-dependent prostatic tissue homeostasis pathways are pharmacologically suppressed.
  -: Known hypersensitivity to Libidon (prostate gland tissue cytomedin peptide complex A-16) or formulation excipients including gelatin.
  -: Female subjects - Libidon is a prostate-specific bioregulator with no established tissue target, mechanism, or indication in female biology.
  -: Recent radical prostatectomy - with surgically removed prostate, Libidon has no target organ.
  -: PSA > 10 ng/mL without prior prostate biopsy - unexplained significant PSA elevation requires prostate cancer exclusion before initiating a prostate-targeted bioregulator.
  -: High-grade prostatic intraepithelial neoplasia (HGPIN) - pre-malignant prostatic lesions represent an intermediate-risk category where prostatic cell gene program modulation has not been characterized.

### compound | linaclotide/overview | What is Linaclotide?
kind: overview
title: Linaclotide
summary: An FDA-approved oral peptide drug that acts mainly inside the intestine through GC-C/cGMP signaling to increase fluid secretion and bowel transit. It is used for IBS-C in adults and pediatric patients 7 years of age and older, CIC in adults, and functional constipation in pediatric patients 2 years of age and older.
keyPoint: An FDA-approved oral peptide drug that acts mainly inside the intestine through GC-C/cGMP signaling to increase fluid secretion and bowel transit.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: Linaclotide
  connectedTo: Linaclotide
section: Why it is researched
  -: An FDA-approved oral peptide drug that acts mainly inside the intestine through GC-C/cGMP signaling to increase fluid secretion and bowel transit.
section: How it works in the research
  -: Linaclotide is a 14-amino-acid peptide agonist of guanylate cyclase-C (GC-C), structurally related to human guanylin and uroguanylin.
section: Evidence strength
  -: The Peptide Handbook: Randomized or controlled human research; population: Human; Direct controlled human evidence. 12 human studies listed by the source; 35 animal studies listed by the source
section: Main limitations
  -: Pediatric serious dehydration - LINZESS carries a boxed warning for risk of serious dehydration in pediatric patients less than 2 years of age and is contraindicated in this age group
  -: Severe diarrhea can occur; if it occurs, suspend dosing and rehydrate the patient
  -: Mechanical gastrointestinal obstruction - LINZESS is contraindicated in patients with known or suspected mechanical gastrointestinal obstruction

kind: safety

  connectedTo: Linaclotide
  *: Pediatric serious dehydration - LINZESS carries a boxed warning for risk of serious dehydration in pediatric patients less than 2 years of age and is contraindicated in this age group. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Severe diarrhea can occur; if it occurs, suspend dosing and rehydrate the patient. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Mechanical gastrointestinal obstruction - LINZESS is contraindicated in patients with known or suspected mechanical gastrointestinal obstruction. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Open-label extension studies followed patients for up to 18 months of continuous treatment. Key findings included: Sustained efficacy with no evidence of tolerance developing No new safety signals with prolonged use Consistent improvement in quality of life measures Low discontinuation rates due to lack of efficacy. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Linaclotide has a well-characterized safety profile based on clinical trials involving over 2,800 patients and more than a decade of post-marketing experience. The most significant side effects relate directly to its mechanism of action. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Diarrhea is the most frequent adverse event, occurring in 16-20% of linaclotide-treated patients compared to about 5% on placebo. In the majority of cases, diarrhea is mild to moderate in severity and occurs within the first 2 weeks of treatment. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Common (≥2%): Abdominal pain, flatulence, abdominal distension Less common (1-2%): Headache, viral gastroenteritis, decreased appetite Rare (<1%): Dizziness, fecal incontinence, nausea Severe diarrhea leading to clinically significant dehydration has been reported in post-marketing surveillance. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Long-term studies up to 18 months have not revealed additional safety concerns. Importantly, unlike stimulant laxatives, there is no evidence of: Tolerance development (requiring increasing doses) Rebound constipation upon discontinuation Electrolyte abnormalities with prolonged use Structural damage to the colon. [source-listed source severity]

### compound | linaclotide/evidence | What research is listed for Linaclotide?
kind: evidence
title: Linaclotide: research listed by the sources
summary: strong-human. In the 26-week randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase III IBS-C trial, 804 patients received linaclotide 290 mcg once daily or placebo. The FDA combined responder definition over the first 12 weeks required both at least 30% improvement from baseline in average daily worst abdominal pain and at least 1 additional complete spontaneous bowel movement from baseline in the same week for at least 6 of 12 weeks. Response was 33.7% with linaclotide versus 13.9% with placebo (P < 0.0001). The trial also showed statistically significant improvements in abdominal pain, bloating, and bowel symptoms versus placebo. Current FDA labeling provides the indication and safety context, including pediatric functional constipation in patients 2 years of age and older. FDA-approved treatment for IBS-C and chronic constipation Increases intestinal fluid secretion and accelerates transit Reduces visceral hypersensitivity and abdominal pain Minimal systemic absorption (acts locally in gut) Once-daily oral dosing for patient convenience Clinically proven in large Phase 3 trials Dual mechanism: addresses both constipation and pain Well-characterized safety profile from post-marketing surveillance Active research area with published studies Linaclotide's approval was supported by an extensive clinical trial program involving thousands of patients across multiple Phase 3 studies. The evidence base continues to grow with long-term extension studies and real-world effectiveness data. Two pivotal Phase 3 trials evaluated linaclotide 290 mcg daily in patients with IBS-C according to Rome II criteria. These were randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials lasting 12 and 26 weeks respectively. 26% of linaclotide patients achieved FDA-defined responder status vs.

### compound | lipocb12lc1201/overview | What is Lipo-C with B12 (LC1201)?
kind: overview
title: Lipo-C with B12 (LC1201)
summary: Lipo-C with B12 (product code LC1201) is the enhanced version of the standard Lipo-C lipotropic injection, taking the same fat-metabolism and methylation base and adding methylated vitamin B12 for an energy and recovery boost. It is a vitamin and amino acid compound rather than a peptide, so it acts through nutritional and metabolic pathways rather than a hormone receptor, and it is given as a fixed direct dose with no titration. Each milliliter contains Methionine 15mg, Choline Chloride 50mg, Carnitine 50mg, Dexpanthenol (provitamin B5) 5mg, and B12 as Methylcobalamin 1mg. The methionine, choline, carnitine, and B5 provide the classic lipotropic action of supporting the liver in mobilizing and burning fat, while the added methylcobalamin supports red blood cell formation, nervous system function, and cellular energy production through its role in the methylation and Krebs cycle pathways.
keyPoint: Lipo-C with B12 (product code LC1201) is the enhanced version of the standard Lipo-C lipotropic injection, taking the same fat-metabolism and methylation base and adding methylated vitamin B12 for an energy and recovery boost.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: Lipo-C with B12 (LC1201)
  connectedTo: Lipo-C with B12 (LC1201)
section: Why it is researched
  -: Lipo-C with B12 (product code LC1201) is the enhanced version of the standard Lipo-C lipotropic injection, taking the same fat-metabolism and methylation base and adding methylated vitamin B12 for an energy and recovery boost.
section: How it works in the research
  -: Lipo-C with B12 (product code LC1201) is the enhanced version of the standard Lipo-C lipotropic injection, taking the same fat-metabolism and methylation base and adding methylated vitamin B12 for an energy and recovery boost.
section: Evidence strength
  -: Peptide University Codex: Source summary; study design not clearly stated; population: Animal; Preclinical animal evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Main limitations
  -: Known hypersensitivity to methionine, choline, L-carnitine, dexpanthenol, methylcobalamin, or any formulation excipient.
  -: Pregnancy or breastfeeding unless directed and supervised by a physician.
  -: Active liver or kidney disease unless medically supervised.
  followUp: Show the research evidence for Lipo-C with B12 (LC1201)
