  *: SS-31: Halflife Labs: approximately 2 hours IV in animal studies, with Phase 2 human clinical trial data in heart failure. Plasma half-life approximately 2 hours following IV administration in animal studies (Chatfield et al. 2019, PMID 30898597). Limited human PK data from Phase 2 clinical trials in heart failure. D-amino acid and dimethyltyrosine modifications confer protease resistance relative to L-peptide analogs. Selectively partitions to inner mitochondrial membrane via cardiolipin interaction. Reduces mitochondrial ROS and restores electron transport chain efficiency.

### compound | mk-677/overview | What is MK-677?
kind: overview
title: MK-677
summary: An orally-active, non-peptide growth hormone secretagogue that mimics ghrelin's effects on GHS-R1a. While not technically a peptide, it is frequently researched alongside peptides for its sustained IGF-1 elevation. Completed Phase 2 trials for muscle wasting, sleep, and bone density. Not FDA approved; WADA prohibited.
keyPoint: An orally-active, non-peptide growth hormone secretagogue that mimics ghrelin's effects on GHS-R1a.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: MK-677
  connectedTo: MK-677

  -: MK-677 mimics ghrelin to stimulate growth hormone release through four key pathways: GHS -R1a Activation Binds to ghrelin receptor on pituitary somatotrophs, triggering calcium-mediated GH vesicle release without affecting pulse frequency.

  -: The reviewed record does not state a specific limitation. The linked paper still needs to be checked for design, size and bias.

  *: PeptideDosage.org: Markedly increased appetite is the most consistent effect, driven by ghrelin-receptor activation; this can promote weight gain and complicate fat-loss goals [3].; Fluid and sodium retention can cause transient peripheral edema, joint and muscle aches (arthralgia/myalgia), and a sensation of fullness or puffiness, typically most pronounced in the first weeks of use [2][3].; Reduced insulin sensitivity and rising fasting glucose were observed across trials at 25 mg/day, a clinically important metabolic concern; people with prediabetes, diabetes, or metabolic syndrome are at particular risk [2][3].; Lethargy, daytime drowsiness, headache, and altered sleep can occur, partly reflecting the compound's pronounced effects on slow-wave and REM sleep [6].; Sustained elevation of GH and IGF-1 raises theoretical long-term concerns (e.g., effects on glucose metabolism, soft-tissue growth, and potential tumor promotion); the FDA has also warned of a potential for congestive heart failure in susceptible individuals, with at least one trial program raising cardiac safety questions.; Despite
  *: PeptideDeck: Increases endogenous growth hormone secretion Elevates IGF-1 levels to youthful ranges Oral administration - no injections required Improves sleep quality and REM sleep duration Supports lean muscle mass preservation May improve bone mineral density Once-daily dosing due to 24-hour half-life Does not suppress natural GH production long-term MK-677 has been evaluated in numerous clinical trials, providing a substantial evidence base for its effects on growth hormone, body composition, bone health, and sleep. Here's what the research demonstrates: 40-60% increase in IGF-1 levels documented in multiple clinical trials GH elevation occurs within first week, IGF-1 peaks by week 2-4 Effects sustained over 2+ years of continuous administration Lean mass preservation during caloric restriction Sleep quality improvement, particularly REM sleep The majority of clinical research has used 25mg daily as the standard dose. This dosage consistently produces 40-60% increases in IGF-1 and significant GH elevation.
  *: MK-677 Effects on GH and IGF-1 in Adults (JCEM 1998): 25mg orally for 2 years maintained GH/IGF-1 increases. Increased fat-free mass.

### compound | mk0616/overview | What is MK-0616?
kind: overview
title: MK-0616
summary: An oral macrocyclic peptide PCSK9 inhibitor in Phase 3 development by Merck. Pivotal Phase 3 LDL-C trials are now published, and the CORALreef Outcomes cardiovascular trial (~14,500 participants) is ongoing. Phase 2 data showed greater than 60% LDL-C reduction. Would be the first oral peptide-based PCSK9 drug if approved.
keyPoint: An oral macrocyclic peptide PCSK9 inhibitor in Phase 3 development by Merck.

It is the primary hormonal regulator of the migrating motor complex (MMC) - the cyclical pattern of gastrointestinal motility that sweeps undigested material, bacteria, and cellular debris through the small intestine during fasting periods (the "interdigestive housekeeper"). Motilin was discovered by Brown et al.

title: Motixafortide

It was developed by BioLineRx and received FDA approval in September 2023 for use in combination with filgrastim (G-CSF) for the mobilization of hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) to the peripheral blood for collection and subsequent autologous transplantation in patients with multiple myeloma .

### compound | mots-c/overview | What is MOTS-c?
kind: overview
title: MOTS-c
summary: A 16-amino acid mitochondrial-derived peptide encoded in mtDNA that targets AMPK/mTOR pathways for metabolic regulation. Preclinical studies show exercise mimetic and geroprotective effects. Lower MOTS-c levels found in T2D patients. No clinical trials yet conducted in humans.
keyPoint: A 16-amino acid mitochondrial-derived peptide encoded in mtDNA that targets AMPK/mTOR pathways for metabolic regulation.

### compound | mots-c/evidence | What research is listed for MOTS-c?
kind: evidence
title: MOTS-c: research listed by the sources
summary: No completed human RCTs. Animal data strong. Human pilot studies range 5-10mg 2-3x weekly. Conservative approach recommended given experimental status. NOTE: Dosing protocols vary widely - some sources suggest daily low-dose (1-2mg), others suggest 5mg 2-3x weekly. We default to the more conservative 2-3x weekly protocol.
keyPoint: No completed human RCTs.
understood: resolved
method: alias
confidence: high
matchedText: MOTS C
disclosure: I've interpreted 'MOTS C' as MOTS-c.
  connectedTo: MOTS C
  connectedTo: MOTS-c
section: What the research shows
  -: PepCodex: A 16-amino acid mitochondrial-derived peptide encoded in mtDNA that targets AMPK/mTOR pathways for metabolic regulation.
  -: The Peptide Handbook: A 16-amino-acid peptide encoded within mitochondrial DNA, discovered in 2015.
  -: Halflife Labs: MOTS-C half-life is not established in published human pharmacokinetic studies.
  -: Peptpedia: A mitochondria-encoded peptide that mimics exercise through AMPK activation.
  -: Peptide Hub: MOTS-c (Mitochondrial ORF of the 12S rRNA type-c) is a 16-amino acid peptide uniquely encoded within the mitochondrial genome - one of the few known peptides not originating from nuclear DNA.
section: Evidence strength
  -: PepCodex: Human clinical research; population: Human; Human evidence with design limitations to check. 6 human studies listed by the source
  -: The Peptide Handbook: Animal research; population: Animal; Preclinical animal evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: Halflife Labs: Observational or case-based human research; population: Animal; Limited observational human evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: Peptpedia: Observational or case-based human research; population: Human; Limited observational human evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: Peptide Hub: Source summary; study design not clearly stated; population: Not clearly stated; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Limitations
  -: The reviewed record does not state a specific limitation. The linked paper still needs to be checked for design, size and bias.
  -: Insufficient long-term human safety data; broad AMPK activation has systemic metabolic effects; mechanism not fully characterized in humans
  -: The reviewed record is animal research and cannot establish human effectiveness or safety.
  -: no published formal pharmacokinetic characterization in any species.
  -: No peer-reviewed study reports a plasma half-life, clearance, volume of distribution, or absolute bioavailability for exogenous MOTS-c.
  -: not correlate with fitness measures - the exercise-MOTS-c signal is real but modest and protocol-dependent (PMID 34351816).
  -: not measured in those animals, the exposure multiple over endogenous levels cannot be calculated (PMID 25738459).
  -: No Formal Human PK: No published study measures the half-life, clearance, or bioavailability of exogenous MOTS-c in humans, and no human clinical trial of the peptide has been published; the human data that exist are exercise-physiology and observational measurements of endogenous levels (PMID 33473109).
  -: No Published Analog PK Either: Even for clinical-stage MOTS-c analogs such as CB4211, no PubMed-indexed pharmacokinetic data has appeared - the peptide class's entire clinical exposure record remains unpublished (PMID 34520826).
  -: no pharmacokinetic validation behind them (PMID 25738459).
  -: No human safety or clinical trials of MOTS-c have been conducted; all interventional evidence is from animal studies, and the pharmacokinetics of exogenous MOTS-c (bioavailability, distribution, half-life, metabolism) are incompletely characterized.
  -: This is a commercial educational source. Its uncited figures and modelled outputs must remain labelled as source-listed rather than clinical evidence.
  *: Source rating: 2 out of 5, limited evidence
  *: PepCodex: Low evidence; 6 human studies listed
  *: The Peptide Handbook: preliminary. MOTS-c is a mitochondrial-derived peptide discovered as a metabolic stress signal. The cited work is preclinical and examines metabolic homeostasis, obesity, insulin sensitivity, and related exercise biology in animal models. These findings do not establish human efficacy, a self-administration schedule, or a universal pharmacokinetic profile.
  *: Halflife Labs: Animal Study + early human observational
  *: Peptpedia: MOTS-c was only discovered in 2015. There are no human interventional, safety, or efficacy trials; human evidence is limited to observational and genetic-association studies.
  *: Peptide Hub: Protocol-focused educational summary. Linked papers, site-listed ranges and commercial context are retained with source attribution.
  *: MOTS-c Regulates Metabolic Homeostasis (Cell Metabolism 2015): MOTS-c reduced obesity and improved insulin sensitivity via AMPK activation in mice. Discovery paper establishing mitochondria-encoded peptide concept.

### compound | mots-c-analog/evidence | What research is listed for MOTS-c (Analog)?
kind: evidence
title: MOTS-c (Analog): research listed by the sources
summary: Animal model data strong. Analog formulations emerging 2023-2025.
keyPoint: Animal model data strong.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: MOTS-c (Analog)
  connectedTo: MOTS-c (Analog)
section: What the research shows
  -: PepCodex: A 16-amino acid mitochondrial-derived peptide encoded in mtDNA that targets AMPK/mTOR pathways for metabolic regulation.
  -: The Peptide Handbook: A 16-amino-acid peptide encoded within mitochondrial DNA, discovered in 2015.
  -: Halflife Labs: MOTS-C half-life is not established in published human pharmacokinetic studies.
  -: Peptpedia: A mitochondria-encoded peptide that mimics exercise through AMPK activation.
  -: Peptide Hub: MOTS-c (Mitochondrial ORF of the 12S rRNA type-c) is a 16-amino acid peptide uniquely encoded within the mitochondrial genome - one of the few known peptides not originating from nuclear DNA.
section: Evidence strength
  -: PepCodex: Human clinical research; population: Human; Human evidence with design limitations to check. 6 human studies listed by the source
  -: The Peptide Handbook: Animal research; population: Animal; Preclinical animal evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: Halflife Labs: Observational or case-based human research; population: Animal; Limited observational human evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: Peptpedia: Observational or case-based human research; population: Human; Limited observational human evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: Peptide Hub: Source summary; study design not clearly stated; population: Not clearly stated; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Limitations
  -: The reviewed record does not state a specific limitation. The linked paper still needs to be checked for design, size and bias.
  -: Insufficient long-term human safety data; broad AMPK activation has systemic metabolic effects; mechanism not fully characterized in humans
  -: The reviewed record is animal research and cannot establish human effectiveness or safety.
  -: no published formal pharmacokinetic characterization in any species.
  -: No peer-reviewed study reports a plasma half-life, clearance, volume of distribution, or absolute bioavailability for exogenous MOTS-c.
  -: not correlate with fitness measures - the exercise-MOTS-c signal is real but modest and protocol-dependent (PMID 34351816).
  -: not measured in those animals, the exposure multiple over endogenous levels cannot be calculated (PMID 25738459).
  -: No Formal Human PK: No published study measures the half-life, clearance, or bioavailability of exogenous MOTS-c in humans, and no human clinical trial of the peptide has been published; the human data that exist are exercise-physiology and observational measurements of endogenous levels (PMID 33473109).
  -: No Published Analog PK Either: Even for clinical-stage MOTS-c analogs such as CB4211, no PubMed-indexed pharmacokinetic data has appeared - the peptide class's entire clinical exposure record remains unpublished (PMID 34520826).
  -: no pharmacokinetic validation behind them (PMID 25738459).
  -: No human safety or clinical trials of MOTS-c have been conducted; all interventional evidence is from animal studies, and the pharmacokinetics of exogenous MOTS-c (bioavailability, distribution, half-life, metabolism) are incompletely characterized.
  -: This is a commercial educational source. Its uncited figures and modelled outputs must remain labelled as source-listed rather than clinical evidence.
  *: Source rating: 2 out of 5, limited evidence
  *: PepCodex: Low evidence; 6 human studies listed
  *: The Peptide Handbook: preliminary. MOTS-c is a mitochondrial-derived peptide discovered as a metabolic stress signal. The cited work is preclinical and examines metabolic homeostasis, obesity, insulin sensitivity, and related exercise biology in animal models. These findings do not establish human efficacy, a self-administration schedule, or a universal pharmacokinetic profile.
  *: Halflife Labs: Animal Study + early human observational
  *: Peptpedia: MOTS-c was only discovered in 2015. There are no human interventional, safety, or efficacy trials; human evidence is limited to observational and genetic-association studies.
  *: Peptide Hub: Protocol-focused educational summary. Linked papers, site-listed ranges and commercial context are retained with source attribution.
  *: MOTS-c and Metabolic Regulation (Cell Metabolism 2015): MOTS-c activated AMPK and improved metabolic homeostasis. Foundational paper for the class.

### compound | mrna4157/overview | What is mRNA-4157/V940?
kind: overview
title: mRNA-4157/V940
summary: A personalized mRNA cancer vaccine encoding up to 34 patient-specific neoantigens, developed jointly by Moderna and Merck. Designed for use in combination with pembrolizumab (Keytruda) for adjuvant treatment of resected high-risk melanoma and other solid tumors. Phase 2b KEYNOTE-942 demonstrated 44-50% reduction in recurrence or death. FDA Breakthrough Therapy designation granted. Multiple Phase 3 trials (INTerpath) ongoing.

### compound | nac/overview | What is NAC?
kind: overview
title: NAC
summary: N-Acetyl Cysteine - a well-established acetylated form of the amino acid cysteine, used for over 50 years as a mucolytic and as the definitive treatment for acetaminophen overdose. Extensively studied as a glutathione precursor, antioxidant, and anti-inflammatory agent across a wide range of conditions.
keyPoint: N-Acetyl Cysteine - a well-established acetylated form of the amino acid cysteine, used for over 50 years as a mucolytic and as the definitive treatment for acetaminophen overdose.

  connectedTo: NAC
section: Why it is researched
  -: N-Acetyl Cysteine - a well-established acetylated form of the amino acid cysteine, used for over 50 years as a mucolytic and as the definitive treatment for acetaminophen overdose.
section: How it works in the research
  -: A cysteine prodrug and direct precursor to intracellular glutathione (GSH), the body's primary endogenous antioxidant.
section: Evidence strength
  -: The Peptide Handbook: Randomized or controlled human research; population: Human; Direct controlled human evidence. 80 human studies listed by the source; 45 animal studies listed by the source
section: Main limitations
  -: IV administration: anaphylactoid reactions (rare, ~0.2%); high-dose IV: hypotension; very high oral doses: GI toxicity

### compound | nac/mechanism | How does NAC work?
kind: overview
title: NAC
summary: N-Acetyl Cysteine - a well-established acetylated form of the amino acid cysteine, used for over 50 years as a mucolytic and as the definitive treatment for acetaminophen overdose. Extensively studied as a glutathione precursor, antioxidant, and anti-inflammatory agent across a wide range of conditions.
keyPoint: N-Acetyl Cysteine - a well-established acetylated form of the amino acid cysteine, used for over 50 years as a mucolytic and as the definitive treatment for acetaminophen overdose.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: NAC
  connectedTo: NAC
section: Why it is researched
  -: N-Acetyl Cysteine - a well-established acetylated form of the amino acid cysteine, used for over 50 years as a mucolytic and as the definitive treatment for acetaminophen overdose.
section: How it works in the research
  -: A cysteine prodrug and direct precursor to intracellular glutathione (GSH), the body's primary endogenous antioxidant.
section: Evidence strength
  -: The Peptide Handbook: Randomized or controlled human research; population: Human; Direct controlled human evidence. 80 human studies listed by the source; 45 animal studies listed by the source
section: Main limitations
  -: IV administration: anaphylactoid reactions (rare, ~0.2%); high-dose IV: hypotension; very high oral doses: GI toxicity
  followUp: Show the research evidence for NAC
  followUp: Show the human research studies for NAC

### compound | nac/evidence | What research is listed for NAC?
kind: evidence
title: NAC: research listed by the sources
summary: strong-human. NAC has one of the broadest and deepest human evidence bases in this database. Efficacy for acetaminophen overdose is definitively established - FDA-approved IV formulation (Acetadote, NDA 018829) is the standard of care for acetaminophen toxicity. Mucolytic efficacy for COPD and cystic fibrosis is supported by multiple RCTs and international guidelines. Psychiatric applications including OCD have positive RCT evidence (Afshar et al., 2012, add-on RCT in refractory OCD), though the broader controlled evidence base in psychiatry is mixed and effect sizes are modest; NAC efficacy for OCD should not be characterized as settled. The COVID-19 adjunct role has mixed and uncertain evidence across published trials; the previously cited systematic review PMID (34375847) was confirmed as an entity mismatch and has been removed; no replacement COVID-19 systematic review citation is added to this record per implementation rules.
keyPoint: strong-human.

### compound | nac/conflicts | Why do the sources disagree about NAC?
kind: evidence
title: NAC: source differences
summary: The knowledge base keeps conflicting claims and records why one is preferred or why no single value has been chosen.
keyPoint: The knowledge base keeps conflicting claims and records why one is preferred or why no single value has been chosen.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: NAC
  connectedTo: NAC
  *: Resolved: site-listed dose ranges. Published study protocols with species, route, population, frequency and duration take priority. Uncited commercial ranges remain labelled and secondary. A product or calculator range is not evidence that a dose was studied, effective or safe. Confidence: high.
  *: Resolved: modelled administration routes. Use only the route stated in the original study or official product information. Do not convert an oral, intranasal, intramuscular or investigational product into a generic subcutaneous vial protocol. PeptideDosage.org applies a common reconstitution and syringe format even to products such as Ventfort that it identifies as oral. That format is not evidence that the modelled route was studied or is suitable. Confidence: high.
  *: Resolved: mental-health citation identity. Exclude three unrelated PubMed identifiers copied under Semax, NAC and Selank claims. Keep only links whose NCBI record matches the stated research subject. NCBI identifies PMID 11157505 as a Hodgkin-disease cell-fusion paper, PMID 16640009 as a Freeman-Sheldon syndrome case report, and PMID 18677858 as a neonatal-mortality paper. None supports the peptide claim beside which it appeared. Confidence: high.

### compound | nad/overview | What is NAD+?
kind: overview
title: NAD+
summary: Oxidized NAD+ studied mainly through direct IV disposition and short-term tolerability research. Direct human evidence exists, but therapeutic effectiveness and wellness or longevity benefits remain limited and uncertain.
keyPoint: Oxidized NAD+ studied mainly through direct IV disposition and short-term tolerability research.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: NAD+
  connectedTo: NAD+
section: Why it is researched
  -: Oxidized NAD+ studied mainly through direct IV disposition and short-term tolerability research.
section: How it works in the research
  -: NAD+ is oxidized nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide, a cellular coenzyme involved in redox reactions and metabolism.
section: Evidence strength
  -: Peptide Authority: Animal research; population: Human; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Main limitations
  -: Whether IV NAD+ produces any longevity / wellness benefit beyond the placebo and infusion-experience effect.
  -: Long-term safety of sustained pharmacological NAD+ elevation.
  -: Phase 3 longevity / disease-prevention outcome trials absent.

  *: Source rating: 3 out of 5
  *: The Peptide Handbook: preliminary. Direct human NAD+ administration evidence is limited to early research. A six-hour IV infusion pilot examined changes in the human plasma and urine NAD+ metabolome, supporting disposition and metabolite observations rather than longevity, cognitive, energy, or disease efficacy. A separate retrospective real-world pilot compared IV NAD+ and NR for short-term tolerability; its symptoms and findings are study-specific and are not randomized efficacy evidence. Broad wellness, anti-aging, longevity, and metabolic-optimization claims remain inadequately established.
  *: Peptide Hub: Protocol-focused educational summary. Linked papers, site-listed ranges and commercial context are retained with source attribution.
  *: PeptideDosage.org: Oral NAD+ precursors (NR, NMN) are generally well tolerated at doses up to 1000 mg/day; the most common side effects are mild nausea, flushing, headache, and gastrointestinal upset, typically resolving with dose reduction.; Intravenous NAD+ infusion can produce uncomfortable flushing, chest tightness, dyspnea, and abdominal discomfort during administration if infused too rapidly; slowing the infusion rate substantially mitigates these symptoms.; Subcutaneous and intramuscular NAD+ injections may produce significant injection-site pain and induration, sometimes lasting hours; some users describe these injections as substantially more uncomfortable than typical peptide injections.; Anxiety, restlessness, and palpitations have been reported during high-dose IV NAD+ infusions, possibly reflecting effects on adrenergic tone or rapid intracellular metabolic shifts; these usually resolve on slowing or pausing the infusion.; Theoretical concerns about supraphysiologic NAD+ levels driving cancer growth in occult malignancy have not been borne out in published cohort data, but caution is
  *: PeptideDeck: Essential redox coenzyme in cellular energy metabolism Substrate for sirtuin and PARP research assays Used in aging and mitochondrial biology studies Relevant to NAD+/NADH ratio and metabolic flux research Active research area with published studies Active research area with published studies NAD+ is the subject of extensive research spanning fundamental biochemistry, mitochondrial biology, DNA repair, and the biology of aging. Much of this work examines the consequences of the age-related decline in NAD+ and whether restoring it can support cellular function.

summary: NAD+ injectable plasma half-life is approximately 1-5 minutes IV (rapidly metabolised to NMN/NAM). Cellular NAD+ half-life approximately 1-2 hours. Not FDA approved as a drug. Data quality: Human PK Study (limited). Trammell SA et al. Nat Commun 2016, PMID 27511844.

  -: NAD+ injectable plasma half-life is approximately 1-5 minutes IV (rapidly metabolised to NMN/NAM).
section: How it works in the research
  -: Plasma half-life of exogenous NAD+ is approximately 1-5 minutes following intravenous administration, as it is rapidly cleaved by ectoenzymes (CD38, CD73) to NMN and then NAM (nicotinamide).

  -: Halflife Labs: Source summary; study design not clearly stated; population: Not clearly stated; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.

  -: The source does not clearly state the study population or design in PEARL's reviewed record.

kind: evidence

matchedText: NAD+ Injectable
  connectedTo: NAD+ Injectable
  *: Halflife Labs: approximately 1-5 minutes IV (rapidly metabolised to NMN/NAM). Plasma half-life of exogenous NAD+ is approximately 1-5 minutes following intravenous administration, as it is rapidly cleaved by ectoenzymes (CD38, CD73) to NMN and then NAM (nicotinamide). Intracellular NAD+ turnover half-life is approximately 1-2 hours in most cell types. Not FDA-approved as a drug product; NAD+ is classified as a dietary supplement precursor. Cleared primarily via enzymatic degradation to nicotinamide and subsequent methylation/excretion.

  -: Continuous GnRH-receptor stimulation is followed by pituitary desensitisation and reduced gonadotropin secretion.

### compound | naselankamidate/evidence | What research is listed for N-Acetyl Selank Amidate?
kind: evidence
title: N-Acetyl Selank Amidate: research listed by the sources
summary: Because no human safety studies of N-Acetyl Selank Amidate exist, its risk profile is inferred from the parent Selank, which has a favorable record across two decades of Russian clinical use; the most common parent-compound effect is transient nasal irritation or mild rhinorrhea at the site of intranasal application.; Route-specific note: this educational page models subcutaneous injection, which is not the validated route; injection adds risks not seen with the intranasal product, including injection-site pain, bruising, bleeding, and infection if sterile technique is not followed.; Headache has been reported in a minority of Selank users, usually at higher cumulative daily doses and often linked to dehydration or concurrent stimulant use; it generally resolves with dose reduction and fluids.; Unlike benzodiazepines, Selank does not produce documented sedation, psychomotor slowing, amnesia, tolerance, or withdrawal/rebound anxiety on discontinuation, though this has not been formally confirmed for the amidate analog.; Rare reports describe transient mood blunting or emotional N-Acetyl Selank Amidate is used in research settings to investigate: GABAergic and enkephalinergic mechanisms of anxiolysis Non-benzodiazepine approaches to anxiety treatment Peptide stability optimization through terminal modifications Intranasal delivery of neuropeptides Immune-neuro interactions Zozulya et al. (2008) reported that intranasal Selank (0.15%) significantly reduced anxiety scores (Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale) in patients with generalized anxiety disorder, with efficacy comparable to medazepam (a benzodiazepine) but without sedation or cognitive impairment. Kost et al. (2007) demonstrated that Selank modulates the expression of genes related to the immune response, inflammation, and neurotransmitter metabolism in human blood cells, providing molecular-level evidence for its multi-target mechanism. Research has demonstrated that Selank normalizes dysregulated cytokine profiles in both animal models and human subjects, supporting its dual anxiolytic-immunomodulatory mechanism. [ 1 ] [ 2 ] [ 3 ] [ 4 ] [ 5 ] ↑ 1.0 1.1 Zozulya AA, Kost NV, Sokolov OY, et al. (2008).

### compound | nasemaxamidate/overview | What is N-Acetyl Semax Amidate?
kind: overview
title: N-Acetyl Semax Amidate
summary: A chemically modified version of Semax with N-terminal acetylation and C-terminal amidation designed to enhance peptide stability. While parent Semax is approved in Russia for nootropic and neuroprotective applications, this specific modification has no independent clinical research.
keyPoint: A chemically modified version of Semax with N-terminal acetylation and C-terminal amidation designed to enhance peptide stability.

### compound | nasemaxamidate/evidence | What research is listed for N-Acetyl Semax Amidate?
kind: evidence
title: N-Acetyl Semax Amidate: research listed by the sources
summary: The Semax family is generally well tolerated in published trials; in stroke studies at 12-18 mg/day intranasal, no significant adverse events were reported [3].; Route-specific (intranasal) effects include local nasal irritation, dryness, sneezing, congestion, and an unpleasant taste or sore throat from the metered spray.; Stimulant-like over-activation can occur, including anxiety, irritability, restlessness, or insomnia if dosed late in the day; because NA-Semax Amidate is more potent than native Semax, starting low (around 300 mcg) reduces the chance of overshooting.; Headache and lightheadedness are occasionally reported, usually transient.; Because Semax modulates dopaminergic and serotonergic signaling, theoretical caution applies when combining it with antidepressants, MAO inhibitors, or stimulants; formal interaction data do not exist [5].; Safety has not been established in pregnancy, breastfeeding, or pediatric use in Western practice, and long-term human safety of the modified analog is unknown; it should be avoided in these populations.; The subcutaneous route modeled on Enhanced cognitive function and mental clarity Improved focus and concentration Increased BDNF expression Neuroprotective properties Better stability than standard Semax Potential mood enhancement May support memory formation Improved stress resilience Research on NA-Semax Amidate specifically is limited; most scientific literature examines standard Semax. However, the modifications are well-understood from pharmaceutical chemistry, and Semax research provides the mechanistic foundation. BDNF Effects: Multiple studies have confirmed Semax increases BDNF expression in the brain. Research published in Doklady Biological Sciences showed significant upregulation of BDNF mRNA following Semax administration in animal models. Cognitive Enhancement: Russian clinical studies have examined Semax for cognitive impairment following stroke and in healthy individuals. Results showed improvements in attention, memory, and processing speed. While these studies don't always meet Western clinical trial standards, they provide substantial observational support.

### compound | natriureticpeptides/evidence | What research is listed for Natriuretic Peptides?
kind: evidence
title: Natriuretic Peptides: research listed by the sources
summary: When your heart stretches under pressure, it doesn't just pump harder-it talks back. The language it speaks comes through a family of signaling molecules called natriuretic peptides, hormones that play a central role in regulating blood pressure, fluid balance, and cardiac function. Natriuretic peptides are the heart's endogenous defense against volume overload and cardiovascular stress. ANP and BNP regulate blood pressure, fluid balance, and cardiac remodeling by promoting natriuresis, vasodilation, and neurohumoral antagonism. CNP functions locally to regulate vascular tone, cardiac structure, and skeletal growth. BNP and NT-proBNP have become gold-standard biomarkers for diagnosing heart failure, with sensitivity exceeding 90% and excellent negative predictive value. These tests help clinicians quickly identify or exclude heart failure in patients presenting with dyspnea, guiding treatment decisions and predicting outcomes. Therapeutic applications are reshaping cardiovascular medicine.

  *: Resolved: modelled administration routes. Use only the route stated in the original study or official product information. Do not convert an oral, intranasal, intramuscular or investigational product into a generic subcutaneous vial protocol. That format is not evidence that the modelled route was studied or is suitable. Confidence: high.

### compound | neuropeptides/overview | What is Neuropeptides?
kind: overview
title: Neuropeptides
summary: From Wikipep - The Peptide Encyclopedia Neuropeptides are small protein-like molecules (typically 3-100 amino acids) used by neurons to communicate with each other. Unlike classical neurotransmitters (glutamate, GABA, dopamine), neuropeptides are synthesized in the cell body, packaged into dense-core vesicles, and released at higher stimulation frequencies. They act as neuromodulators - adjusting the sensitivity and responsiveness of neural circuits rather than directly opening ion channels - and play critical roles in pain, appetite, stress, sleep, mood, and cognition. This article serves as a hub linking to all neuropeptide articles on WikiPep.
keyPoint: From Wikipep - The Peptide Encyclopedia Neuropeptides are small protein-like molecules (typically 3-100 amino acids) used by neurons to communicate with each other.

### compound | neurotensin/conflicts | Why do the sources disagree about Neurotensin?
kind: evidence
title: Neurotensin: source differences
summary: The knowledge base keeps conflicting claims and records why one is preferred or why no single value has been chosen.
keyPoint: The knowledge base keeps conflicting claims and records why one is preferred or why no single value has been chosen.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: Neurotensin
  connectedTo: Neurotensin
  *: Resolved: site-listed dose ranges. Published study protocols with species, route, population, frequency and duration take priority. Uncited commercial ranges remain labelled and secondary. A product or calculator range is not evidence that a dose was studied, effective or safe. Confidence: high.
  *: Resolved: modelled administration routes. Use only the route stated in the original study or official product information. Do not convert an oral, intranasal, intramuscular or investigational product into a generic subcutaneous vial protocol. PeptideDosage.org applies a common reconstitution and syringe format even to products such as Ventfort that it identifies as oral. That format is not evidence that the modelled route was studied or is suitable. Confidence: high.
  *: Resolved: mental-health citation identity. Exclude three unrelated PubMed identifiers copied under Semax, NAC and Selank claims. Keep only links whose NCBI record matches the stated research subject. NCBI identifies PMID 11157505 as a Hodgkin-disease cell-fusion paper, PMID 16640009 as a Freeman-Sheldon syndrome case report, and PMID 18677858 as a neonatal-mortality paper. None supports the peptide claim beside which it appeared. Confidence: high.

### compound | neuroxelin/overview | What is Neuroxelin?
kind: overview
title: Neuroxelin
summary: Neuroxelin is a research-only neuropeptide blend formulated in the broader category of compounded neuroprotective peptide preparations used in exploratory cognitive and neurodegenerative research, with no single defined structure, no FDA or EMA approval, and no published randomized controlled trials specific to the branded combination [1][2]. The composition of branded Neuroxelin preparations varies by source and typically includes selank, semax, cerebrolysin-derived fragments, or other neurotrophic peptides aimed at modulating BDNF expression, monoaminergic tone, and neuroinflammatory signaling [3][4]. Research applications draw on the much larger published evidence base for the individual constituent peptides (selank for anxiolysis, semax for attention and stroke recovery, cerebrolysin for vascular dementia and ischemic stroke), without specific data on the blend itself [5][6].

### compound | neuroxelin/evidence | What research is listed for Neuroxelin?
kind: evidence
title: Neuroxelin: research listed by the sources
summary: Because the composition of Neuroxelin preparations varies by manufacturer, side effect profiles cannot be characterized with precision; the safety profile depends on the specific peptides present and their concentrations.; Constituent peptides such as selank and semax have been described as well tolerated in the published literature, with mild adverse events including transient nasal irritation, mild headache, and occasional sleep disturbance with evening dosing.; Cerebrolysin and other brain-derived hydrolysate components can produce hypersensitivity reactions in subjects with allergy to porcine proteins; rare cases of anaphylaxis have been reported with intravenous cerebrolysin.; Theoretical concerns include modulation of monoaminergic neurotransmission that could interact with antidepressants, anxiolytics, and stimulants; concurrent use with psychotropic medications has not been systematically studied.; Long-term safety data are essentially absent for the blend; constituent peptide literature is limited to short-term courses of weeks to a few months.; Use in pregnancy, lactation,

### compound | ngf/conflicts | Why do the sources disagree about NGF?

title: NGF: source differences
summary: The knowledge base keeps conflicting claims and records why one is preferred or why no single value has been chosen.

understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: NGF
  connectedTo: NGF
  *: Resolved: site-listed dose ranges. Published study protocols with species, route, population, frequency and duration take priority. Uncited commercial ranges remain labelled and secondary. A product or calculator range is not evidence that a dose was studied, effective or safe. Confidence: high.
  *: Resolved: modelled administration routes. Use only the route stated in the original study or official product information. Do not convert an oral, intranasal, intramuscular or investigational product into a generic subcutaneous vial protocol. PeptideDosage.org applies a common reconstitution and syringe format even to products such as Ventfort that it identifies as oral. That format is not evidence that the modelled route was studied or is suitable. Confidence: high.
  *: Resolved: mental-health citation identity. Exclude three unrelated PubMed identifiers copied under Semax, NAC and Selank claims. Keep only links whose NCBI record matches the stated research subject. NCBI identifies PMID 11157505 as a Hodgkin-disease cell-fusion paper, PMID 16640009 as a Freeman-Sheldon syndrome case report, and PMID 18677858 as a neonatal-mortality paper. None supports the peptide claim beside which it appeared. Confidence: high.

The study does not establish broad metabolic, cardiovascular, cognitive, safety, or longevity benefit. NCT03151239 is a registry record rather than standalone efficacy evidence.
  *: NMN Supplementation in Older Women with Prediabetes (Science 2021): NMN supplementation elevated blood NAD+ levels and improved muscle insulin sensitivity in postmenopausal women with prediabetes. Subjects were not healthy - all had prediabetes and impaired muscle function.

  *: Source rating: 3 out of 5
  *: The Peptide Handbook: preliminary. The record is limited to its small-molecule identity and does not retain general dosing, route, half-life, product-form, or unsupported safety claims.
  *: Peptide Hub: Protocol-focused educational summary. Linked papers, site-listed ranges and commercial context are retained with source attribution.
  *: PeptideDosage.org: In the controlled human trial of Noopept 20 mg/day, the most frequently reported adverse effects were increased blood pressure (about 7 of 31 patients), sleep disturbance or insomnia (about 5 of 31), and irritability or emotional lability (about 3 of 31); for this reason later-evening doses are usually avoided [5].; Headache is a commonly reported Noopept side effect in anecdotal and clinical use, sometimes paradoxical given its use for cognitive complaints; staying hydrated and lowering the dose are the usual mitigations.; Overstimulation, restlessness, anxiety or a 'wired' feeling can occur, particularly at the upper 30 mg/day end of the range or when combined with caffeine or other stimulants.; Allergic and hypersensitivity reactions have been reported in product labeling for the Russian medicine; the drug is contraindicated in known hypersensitivity and in pregnancy, lactation, and (per its license) children, where it has not been adequately studied.; Sublingual administration, popular in the nootropic community, can cause transient oral or mucosal irritation; the oral tablet is
  *: The original novel nootropic and neuroprotective agent noopept (Eksperimental'naia i Klinicheskaia Farmakologiia 2002): Ostrovskaya et al. introduced noopept (GVS-111) as a novel dipeptide nootropic, characterizing its pharmacological profile including memory enhancement, neuroprotection, and NGF/BDNF-related mechanisms - the foundational paper establishing noopept as a distinct compound.
  *: Neuroprotective properties of nootropic dipeptide GVS-111 in in vitro oxygen-glucose deprivation, glutamate toxicity and oxidative stress (Bulletin of Experimental Biology and Medicine 2000): Andreeva et al. demonstrated noopept's neuroprotective effects against multiple insults including oxygen-glucose deprivation, glutamate excitotoxicity, and oxidative stress, establishing the mechanistic basis for its neuroprotective clinical use.

title: Neuropeptide Y: source-listed risks
summary: Source-listed risks only. Missing human safety data does not mean a compound is safe.
keyPoint: Source-listed risks only.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: Neuropeptide Y
  connectedTo: Neuropeptide Y
  *: Appetite stimulation (orexigenic effect - may be undesirable outside controlled research contexts). [source-listed source severity]
  *: Transient vasodilation or vasoconstriction depending on route and dose. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Blood pressure changes (sympathomimetic at peripheral Y1 receptors). [source-listed source severity]
  *: Sedation at higher doses (research context). [source-listed source severity]
  *: No established human safety profile for exogenous NPY administration; all available human pharmacology data comes from small controlled research studies. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Cardiovascular effects - peripheral NPY acts as a vasoconstrictor at Y1 receptors and co-transmitter with norepinephrine; potential hemodynamic effects require careful monitoring. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Metabolic effects - potent orexigenic signalling from hypothalamic NPY neurons; prolonged receptor activation could affect food intake regulation. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Lack of receptor subtype selectivity with exogenous full-length NPY complicates safety prediction across CNS and peripheral compartments. [source-listed source severity]

### compound | npy/evidence | What research is listed for Neuropeptide Y?
kind: evidence
title: Neuropeptide Y: research listed by the sources
summary: preliminary. NPY has one of the largest preclinical evidence bases of any neuropeptide, with published animal studies spanning appetite, anxiety, stress, sleep, and neuroprotection, though human translational research remains limited. The most clinically developed research area is stress resilience and PTSD: human studies have found lower cerebrospinal fluid NPY levels in individuals with PTSD compared to trauma-exposed controls, and in special operations forces, higher NPY response to training stress correlated with better psychological performance under simulated captivity. Intranasal NPY administration studies in humans have explored acute anxiolytic effects, though sample sizes are small and dose optimization is ongoing. Potent orexigenic (appetite-stimulating) effects through hypothalamic signaling Anxiolytic properties-reduces anxiety and fear responses in animal models Stress resilience enhancement in research settings Cardiovascular regulation including vasoconstriction and cardiac function Bone formation stimulation through Y1 receptor activation Circadian rhythm modulation and sleep-wake cycle regulation Neuroprotective effects in ischemia and seizure models Wound healing promotion through angiogenic activity NPY research spans multiple disciplines and therapeutic areas, supported by thousands of published studies. The peptide's involvement in fundamental physiological processes has generated substantial clinical and translational interest. NPY's role as the most potent known appetite stimulant has driven extensive obesity research. Studies consistently show elevated hypothalamic NPY in obese animals and humans, particularly in diet-induced and genetic obesity models. This elevation appears to be both cause and consequence-NPY promotes weight gain, and obesity itself alters NPY regulation.
keyPoint: preliminary.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: Neuropeptide Y
  connectedTo: Neuropeptide Y
section: What the research shows
  -: The Peptide Handbook: One of the most abundant neuropeptides in the brain, regulating appetite, stress resilience, anxiety, sleep, and cardiovascular tone.
  -: PeptideDeck: Recommended
  -: WikiPep: From Wikipep - The Peptide Encyclopedia Neuropeptide Y Chemical name NPY Molecular formula C190H287N55O57 Molecular weight 4254.8 g/mol CAS number 83652-28-2 Sequence Tyr-Pro-Ser-Lys-Pro-Asp-Asn-Pro-Gly-Glu-Asp-Ala-Pro-Ala-Glu-Asp-Met-Ala-Arg-Tyr-Tyr-Ser-Ala-Leu-Arg-His-Tyr-Ile-Asn-Leu-Ile-Thr-Arg-Gln-Arg-Tyr-NH₂...
section: Evidence strength
  -: The Peptide Handbook: Animal research; population: Animal; Preclinical animal evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: PeptideDeck: Animal research; population: Animal; Preclinical animal evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: WikiPep: Source summary; study design not clearly stated; population: Not clearly stated; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Limitations
  -: No established human safety profile for exogenous NPY administration; all available human pharmacology data comes from small controlled research studies
  -: Cardiovascular effects - peripheral NPY acts as a vasoconstrictor at Y1 receptors and co-transmitter with norepinephrine; potential hemodynamic effects require careful monitoring
  -: Metabolic effects - potent orexigenic signalling from hypothalamic NPY neurons; prolonged receptor activation could affect food intake regulation
  -: Lack of receptor subtype selectivity with exogenous full-length NPY complicates safety prediction across CNS and peripheral compartments
  -: ⚠️ Important: Most NPY safety data comes from single-dose or short-term studies. Long-term safety with repeated administration is unknown. As an investigational compound, NPY should only be used in controlled research settings under appropriate supervision.
  -: Human Translation : Limited translation from animal to human studies Long-term Effects : Unknown consequences of chronic NPY modulation Individual Variation : High variability in response between individuals Complex Interactions : Multiple physiological systems affected simultaneously
  *: Source rating: 2 out of 5, limited evidence

  *: Resolved: site-listed dose ranges. Published study protocols with species, route, population, frequency and duration take priority. Uncited commercial ranges remain labelled and secondary. A product or calculator range is not evidence that a dose was studied, effective or safe. Confidence: high.
  *: Resolved: modelled administration routes. Use only the route stated in the original study or official product information. Do not convert an oral, intranasal, intramuscular or investigational product into a generic subcutaneous vial protocol. PeptideDosage.org applies a common reconstitution and syringe format even to products such as Ventfort that it identifies as oral. That format is not evidence that the modelled route was studied or is suitable. Confidence: high.
  *: Resolved: mental-health citation identity. Exclude three unrelated PubMed identifiers copied under Semax, NAC and Selank claims. Keep only links whose NCBI record matches the stated research subject. NCBI identifies PMID 11157505 as a Hodgkin-disease cell-fusion paper, PMID 16640009 as a Freeman-Sheldon syndrome case report, and PMID 18677858 as a neonatal-mortality paper. None supports the peptide claim beside which it appeared. Confidence: high.

### compound | nr-nicotinamide-riboside/evidence | What research is listed for NR (Nicotinamide Riboside)?
kind: evidence
title: NR (Nicotinamide Riboside): research listed by the sources
summary: Multiple human RCTs. ChromaDex ELYSIUM studies. Strong NAD+ elevation data.
keyPoint: Multiple human RCTs.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: NR (Nicotinamide Riboside)
  connectedTo: NR (Nicotinamide Riboside)
section: What the research shows
  -: The Peptide Handbook: An NAD+ precursor with human biomarker and tolerability research; clinical benefits for aging or disease are unestablished.
section: Evidence strength
  -: The Peptide Handbook: Source summary; study design not clearly stated; population: Human; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Limitations
  -: Long-term clinical safety and disease-outcome benefit remain unestablished.
  -: NAD-related biomarker changes do not by themselves demonstrate a health or longevity benefit.
  *: Source rating: 3 out of 5
  *: The Peptide Handbook: preliminary. Trammell et al. reported oral NR bioavailability in a human study, and Conze et al. reported tolerability and NAD-related biomarker findings in healthy middle-aged and older adults. Those findings do not prove prevention or treatment of disease, cognitive benefit, or longevity benefit. NCT02950441 has no posted results and is not used as standalone efficacy evidence.
  *: Nicotinamide Riboside Increases NAD+ in Humans (Nature Communications 2016): First human trial showing NR safely elevated blood NAD+ levels in a dose-dependent manner. Established NR as effective oral NAD+ precursor.

kind: overview

summary: A long-acting synthetic somatostatin analogue used in FDA-approved treatment of acromegaly and symptomatic hormone excess from carcinoid tumors and VIPomas. It also has extensive research and off-label use across neuroendocrine and gastrointestinal medicine.

### compound | octreotide/safety | What are the risks of Octreotide?

matchedText: Octreotide
  connectedTo: Octreotide
  *: Abdominal pain or cramping. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Gallbladder sludge or gallstones. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Hyperglycemia or hypoglycemia. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Octreotide can reduce gallbladder contractility and bile secretion, leading to gallstones or biliary sludge; complications such as cholecystitis, cholangitis, and pancreatitis have been reported. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Octreotide can alter insulin, glucagon, and growth-hormone regulation and may cause either hyperglycemia or hypoglycemia. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Bradycardia, conduction abnormalities, and other ECG changes have been reported; patients with relevant cardiac disease or interacting medications may require monitoring. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Octreotide can suppress thyroid-stimulating hormone and may lead to hypothyroidism during prolonged therapy. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Reduced pancreatic enzyme and bile secretion can contribute to fat malabsorption and nutritional deficiencies during long-term treatment. [source-listed source severity]

### compound | octreotide/evidence | What research is listed for Octreotide?
kind: evidence
title: Octreotide: research listed by the sources
summary: strong-human. Octreotide has established product-specific uses in the Sandostatin Injection and Sandostatin LAR Depot labels. The PROMID randomized trial and NCT00171873 apply specifically to octreotide LAR in metastatic well-differentiated midgut neuroendocrine tumors; they do not establish effects for immediate-release octreotide, other formulations, or all indications. Immediate-release and LAR claims, including dosing and administration, remain formulation-specific. Suppresses growth hormone secretion in acromegaly Controls symptoms of neuroendocrine tumors Reduces diarrhea and flushing in carcinoid syndrome Decreases tumor hormone production Slows progression of some neuroendocrine tumors Reduces variceal bleeding risk in cirrhosis Long-acting monthly depot formulations available Well-established 35+ year safety profile Octreotide's therapeutic benefits are supported by decades of clinical research, including landmark randomized controlled trials that established standard of care in multiple conditions.

  *: The Peptide Handbook: strong-human. Octreotide has established product-specific uses in the Sandostatin Injection and Sandostatin LAR Depot labels. The PROMID randomized trial and NCT00171873 apply specifically to octreotide LAR in metastatic well-differentiated midgut neuroendocrine tumors; they do not establish effects for immediate-release octreotide, other formulations, or all indications.   *: PeptideDeck: Suppresses growth hormone secretion in acromegaly Controls symptoms of neuroendocrine tumors Reduces diarrhea and flushing in carcinoid syndrome Decreases tumor hormone production Slows progression of some neuroendocrine tumors Reduces variceal bleeding risk in cirrhosis Long-acting monthly depot formulations available Well-established 35+ year safety profile Octreotide's therapeutic benefits are supported by decades of clinical research, including landmark randomized controlled trials that established standard of care in multiple conditions.
  *: WikiPep: PROMID trial: Demonstrated that octreotide LAR 30 mg significantly prolonged time to tumor progression vs. placebo in metastatic midgut neuroendocrine tumors (median 14.3 months vs. 6 months; HR 0.34). Acromegaly studies: Multiple trials demonstrating GH/IGF-1 normalization in 50-65% of patients and tumor shrinkage in a subset. CLARINET analogy: While this trial specifically studied lanreotide, it confirmed the class effect of somatostatin analogs in antiproliferative efficacy for GEP-NETs. Somatostatin receptor imaging: Radiolabeled octreotide (OctreoScan / In-111 pentetreotide) was historically a key diagnostic tool for localizing somatostatin receptor-positive tumors. Now largely supplanted by Ga-68 DOTATATE PET/CT. PRRT carrier: Octreotide derivatives (DOTATOC, DOTATATE) serve as targeting vectors for peptide receptor radionuclide therapy (PRRT) with Lu-177 or Y-90 in neuroendocrine tumors. ### compound | ogp/overview | What is OGP?
kind: overview
title: OGP
summary: From Wikipep - The Peptide Encyclopedia OGP Chemical name Osteogenic Growth Peptide Molecular formula C₇₅H₁₁₆N₂₂O₂₁ Molecular weight 1701.9 Da CAS number 137562-74-4 Sequence ALKRQGRTLYGFGG Length 14 amino acids Source Synthetic (also endogenous, derived from histone H4) Half-life ~20-30 minutes Targets Osteoblast GPR signaling; MAPK pathway activation Bioavailability Subcutaneous/systemic injection Legal status Research compound (not approved) OGP ( Osteogenic Growth Peptide ) is an endogenous 14-amino acid peptide (sequence: ALKRQGRTLYGFGG ) derived from the C-terminal region of histone H4 that naturally circulates in human serum at concentrations of 10⁻¹²-10⁻¹⁰ M. Discovered by Itai Bab and colleagues at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem in 1992, OGP is released from bone matrix during remodeling and acts as a systemic regulator of bone formation and hematopoietic activity.

### compound | orexina/overview | What is Orexin-A?
kind: overview
title: Orexin-A
summary: An endogenous hypothalamic neuropeptide that is the brain's principal wakefulness-promoting signal. The selective destruction of orexin-producing neurons is the direct biological cause of narcolepsy type 1, making it central to sleep medicine and circadian research.
keyPoint: An endogenous hypothalamic neuropeptide that is the brain's principal wakefulness-promoting signal.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high

section: How it works in the research
  -: Orexin-A (Hypocretin-1) is a 33-amino-acid hypothalamic neuropeptide and one of two orexin peptides, the other being Orexin-B.
section: Evidence strength
  -: The Peptide Handbook: Source summary; study design not clearly stated; population: Human; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Main limitations
  -: Unknown in humans; theoretical cardiovascular stimulation; addiction/reward pathway activation (orexin system regulates reward); off-label self-administration not advisable

### compound | orexina/evidence | What research is listed for Orexin-A?
kind: evidence
title: Orexin-A: research listed by the sources
summary: preliminary. Orexin-A is a wakefulness-promoting hypothalamic neuropeptide with extensive pathway and preclinical research. Direct human evidence for exogenous Orexin-A consists of small experimental intranasal studies in narcolepsy and a study of autonomic/vascular effects. These studies do not establish Orexin-A as a routine treatment, and any administered amount is study-specific exposure. Approved orexin receptor antagonists act differently and provide pathway context only; they are not evidence for exogenous Orexin-A efficacy or safety. Promotes wakefulness and alertness Regulates appetite and feeding behavior Supports energy homeostasis and metabolism Modulates reward and motivation pathways Influences stress response regulation Coordinates autonomic nervous system function Impacts cognitive function and memory consolidation Plays role in emotional processing The three decades since orexin's discovery have produced an extensive body of research illuminating this peptide's roles in health and disease. From the definitive link to narcolepsy to emerging implications in addiction and neurodegeneration, orexin-A continues to reveal new dimensions of physiological significance. Narcolepsy type 1 is caused by loss of orexin-producing neurons CSF orexin-A levels below 110 pg/mL are diagnostic for narcolepsy type 1 The destruction appears to be autoimmune, often triggered by infections HLA-DQB1*06:02 genotype is present in 98% of narcolepsy type 1 cases Given the challenges of orexin-A crossing the blood-brain barrier, researchers have explored intranasal delivery as a route to achieve therapeutic brain concentrations.
keyPoint: preliminary.

### compound | orforglipron/evidence | What research is listed for Orforglipron?
kind: evidence
title: Orforglipron: research listed by the sources
summary: High evidence; 18 human studies listed Gastrointestinal effects are the most common and are dose-related: nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and constipation, generally mild-to-moderate and concentrated during the titration period [4][5].; In Phase 3 ATTAIN-1, dose-by-dose rates were nausea 28.9-35.9%, constipation 21.7-29.8%, diarrhea 21.0-23.1%, and vomiting 13.0-24.0%, all substantially higher than placebo [5][7].; Treatment discontinuation due to adverse events rose with dose - about 5.3% at 6 mg, 7.9% at 12 mg, and 10.3% at 36 mg versus 2.7% with placebo - underscoring the trade-off between higher doses and tolerability [5][7].; Slow titration (starting at 1 mg and stepping up roughly every four weeks) is the principal strategy to limit gastrointestinal effects; skipping steps or escalating too quickly markedly increases nausea and vomiting [3][4].; As a class, GLP-1 receptor agonists carry risks of dehydration from vomiting or diarrhea, gallbladder events (cholelithiasis), and pancreatitis; hypoglycemia risk increases when combined with insulin or sulfonylureas, which may require dose reductions of those agents.; Class

### compound | ovagen/evidence | What research is listed for Ovagen?
kind: evidence
title: Ovagen: research listed by the sources
summary: Across the published Khavinson literature spanning decades of clinical use in Russia, Ovagen and other short-peptide bioregulators are described as having no serious adverse events, no allergic reactions of significance, and no observed toxicity at multiples of the clinical dose.; However, no FDA-grade toxicology dossier, no good-laboratory-practice safety pharmacology, and no controlled drug-interaction studies have been published, so the safety claim relies on observational data of variable quality.; Theoretical concerns include altered gene expression in non-target tissues if peptide binding is not as specific as proposed, particularly in patients with active hepatic malignancy where pro-proliferative signaling could be undesirable.; Because Ovagen is sometimes formulated with carrier proteins or animal-derived excipients, individuals with bovine protein allergy should review the specific product composition; pure synthetic EDL would not pose this risk.; Mild gastrointestinal symptoms such as transient nausea or bloating have been described anecdotally with high-dose oral courses Peptide University labels its records as aggregated from empirical research and anecdotal community data. This record is retained as supplied and is not upgraded to clinical evidence.

section: Limitations
  -: The source does not clearly state the study population or design in PEARL's reviewed record.
  -: Ovagen is a synthetic short-chain peptide bioregulator (Glu-Asp-Leu, EDL tripeptide) developed at the St. Petersburg Institute of Bioregulation and Gerontology by Vladimir Khavinson as the active fragment isolated from bovine liver tissue extracts [1][2].
  -: 14 Important Note This content is intended for therapeutic educational purposes only and does not constitute medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment.
  -: Active hepatitis (viral hepatitis A, B, or C in active replication) - hepatocyte bioregulator activity during active viral hepatic inflammation and injury has not been characterized; antiviral therapy is the priority in active viral hepatitis.
  -: Decompensated cirrhosis (Child-Pugh B or C) - in end-stage hepatic fibrosis where functional hepatocyte mass is severely reduced, the bioregulator target cell population is insufficient for meaningful response and the complex coagulopathy/portal hypertension of decompensated cirrhosis creates an unpredictable context.
  -: Active drug-induced liver injury (DILI) - concurrent hepatocyte bioregulator activity during active toxic hepatocyte injury from drugs has not been evaluated; the causative drug should be discontinued first.
  -: Hepatocellular carcinoma or active hepatic malignancy - Ovagen's hepatocyte survival, regenerative proliferation, and gene program normalization activity has not been evaluated in malignant hepatocytes; hepatic oncology evaluation required.
  -: Known hypersensitivity to Ovagen (Ile-Glu-Pro tripeptide) or formulation excipients.
  -: Pregnancy - hepatic metabolic reprogramming during pregnancy involves substantial changes to lipid metabolism, bile acid metabolism, and hepatic blood flow; exogenous hepatic bioregulator activity during these pregnancy-specific hepatic adaptations has not been evaluated.
  -: Active alcohol use disorder with ongoing consumption - the ongoing hepatocyte injury from active alcohol consumption creates a futile cycle with hepatocyte bioregulator activity; sobriety is a prerequisite.
  -: Recent liver transplantation on immunosuppression - hepatocyte bioregulator activity in immunosuppressed recipients with donor hepatocytes requires hepatology supervision.
  *: Source rating: 1 out of 5, very limited evidence

### compound | oveporexton/overview | What is Oveporexton?
kind: overview
title: Oveporexton
summary: A first-in-class oral orexin receptor 2 (OX2R) selective agonist developed by Takeda for narcolepsy type 1. Though not a peptide itself, oveporexton restores orexin peptide signaling lost due to autoimmune destruction of orexin-producing neurons. A Phase 2 trial (NEJM 2025) demonstrated significant reductions in excessive daytime sleepiness and cataplexy; Phase 3 trials are ongoing. Granted FDA Breakthrough Therapy designation.

### compound | oxyntomodulin/overview | What is Oxyntomodulin?
kind: overview
title: Oxyntomodulin
summary: Oxyntomodulin (OXM) is a native 37-amino-acid gut hormone and GLP-1/glucagon dual agonist cleaved from proglucagon by prohormone convertase 1/3 in intestinal L-cells. Structurally it is the full glucagon sequence extended by a C-terminal octapeptide, which lets one molecule activate both the GLP-1 receptor (appetite suppression, delayed gastric emptying, glucose-dependent insulin release) and the glucagon receptor (increased energy expenditure and hepatic fat oxidation). The most-studied Oxyntomodulin dosage in humans is 400 nmol, roughly 1.77 mg, injected subcutaneously three times a day, 30 minutes before each main meal, the regimen used in the four-week randomized controlled weight-loss trial by Wynne and colleagues, which produced about 2.3 kg of weight loss versus 0.5 kg on placebo.
keyPoint: Oxyntomodulin (OXM) is a native 37-amino-acid gut hormone and GLP-1/glucagon dual agonist cleaved from proglucagon by prohormone convertase 1/3 in intestinal L-cells.

### compound | oxyntomodulin/evidence | What research is listed for Oxyntomodulin?

title: Oxyntomodulin: research listed by the sources
summary: Mild, transient nausea is the most common effect (reported in roughly 3% of injections in the four-week trial); higher or more rapidly escalated doses can provoke more nausea and occasional vomiting, consistent with the GLP-1 receptor arm of its activity [1][4].; Subcutaneous administration can cause local injection-site reactions such as redness, itching, or transient soreness; rotating sites between the abdomen and thigh reduces irritation.; Delayed gastric emptying can produce early satiety, fullness, bloating, or reduced appetite, which is part of the intended effect but may be uncomfortable.; Through glucagon-receptor activation, OXM-class agents can transiently raise heart rate and, in some individuals, blunt the glucose-lowering effect; native oxyntomodulin did not cause clinically significant hyperglycemia in trials, but glucose effects warrant caution.; Hypoglycemia risk is low with the peptide alone because its insulinotropic action is glucose-dependent, but the risk rises if combined with insulin or sulfonylureas.; As a GLP-1-receptor agonist, the broader drug class Continuous IV infusion (3.1 pmol/kg/min × 4 days): −0.5 kg weight loss SC injection (400 nmol TID × 4 weeks): −2.3 kg weight loss + 9.4% increase in energy expenditure 26% reduction in ad libitum food intake (acute infusion) No compensatory decrease in activity (unlike caloric restriction) [ 1 ] [ 2 ] [ 3 ] ↑ 1.0 1.1 Wynne K, et al.   *: Source rating: 4 out of 5
  *: The Peptide Handbook: preliminary. Kosfeld et al. reported an intranasal oxytocin effect on trust-game behavior in a controlled experimental setting. That result is not evidence for a general increase in trust or for treatment of autism, PTSD, anxiety, or other conditions. The NCT05672667 registry record identifies a specific pharmacokinetic study and does not itself report therapeutic efficacy.
  *: Halflife Labs: Evidence context is stated on the linked compound page.
  *: PeptideDosage.org: Intravenous oxytocin used for labor induction can cause uterine tachysystole, fetal heart rate abnormalities, and uterine rupture if doses or rates are excessive; ACOG guidelines emphasize fetal monitoring and titration safety [3].; Water intoxication and hyponatremia can occur with prolonged high-dose intravenous oxytocin because the peptide has structural similarity to vasopressin and modest antidiuretic activity; this risk increases with hypotonic IV fluid use.; Hypotension and reflex tachycardia can occur with rapid intravenous bolus dosing; current obstetric practice avoids bolus administration in favor of slow infusion.; Intranasal oxytocin in research doses (24 to 40 IU) has been very well tolerated, with adverse event rates similar to placebo in randomized trials; mild nasal irritation, headache, and transient sedation have been reported at low frequency.; Theoretical concerns about psychiatric effects (anxiety, paranoia in subjects with insecure attachment styles) have been raised based on findings that oxytocin amplifies salience of social signals rather than uniformly
  *: PeptideDeck: Promotes social bonding and attachment Reduces social anxiety and stress responses Enhances trust and empathy in social interactions Supports maternal bonding and lactation May improve social cognition in autism spectrum research Potential wound healing acceleration Modulates pain perception Supports cardiovascular function and blood pressure regulation Oxytocin research has exploded over the past two decades, generating thousands of studies across behavioral science, psychiatry, and medicine. Here we summarize key findings across major research domains.
  *: WikiPep: Autism Spectrum Disorders : Investigation for social communication difficulties Social Anxiety Disorder : Research on social interaction improvements Relationship Therapy : Potential enhancement of couples therapy outcomes PTSD Treatment : Investigation for trauma-related social difficulties Depression Research : Studies on mood and social connection improvements Intranasal Dosing : 12-48 IU typically used in research studies Intravenous Administration : Medical settings for obstetric applications Timing Considerations : Effects typically last 30-60 minutes Single vs.

Nonapeptide hormone cleaved by oxytocinase (cystyl aminopeptidase) and other plasma proteases. Cleared primarily by renal excretion and hepatic metabolism. CNS oxytocin pools are partially separate from peripheral plasma - intranasal delivery achieves CNS penetration via olfactory and trigeminal nerve pathways.

### compound | p021/overview | What is P021?
kind: overview
title: P021
summary: P021 (also known as P21) is a synthetic tetrapeptide derived from the CNTF (Ciliary Neurotrophic Factor) binding domain - specifically designed to act as a small, BBB-permeable peptide mimetic of CNTF that activates downstream neurotrophic signaling without engaging the JAK/STAT3 pathway that mediates CNTF's adverse inflammatory side effects. CNTF is a potent neurotrophic factor for motor neurons, hippocampal neurons, and retinal ganglion cells, but as a large protein it cannot cross the blood-brain barrier and its systemic administration produces dose-limiting inflammatory side effects. P021 was engineered at the Buck Institute for Research on Aging by researchers including Bhanu Bhanu and colleagues to capture CNTF's neurotrophic benefits in a small, BBB-permeable peptide form.
keyPoint: P021 (also known as P21) is a synthetic tetrapeptide derived from the CNTF (Ciliary Neurotrophic Factor) binding domain - specifically designed to act as a small, BBB-permeable peptide mimetic of CNTF that activates downstream neurotrophic...

method: canonical

  connectedTo: P021

  -: P021 (also known as P21) is a synthetic tetrapeptide derived from the CNTF (Ciliary Neurotrophic Factor) binding domain - specifically designed to act as a small, BBB-permeable peptide mimetic of CNTF that activates downstream neurotrophic...
section: Evidence strength
  -: Peptide University Codex: Source summary; study design not clearly stated; population: Animal; Preclinical animal evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Main limitations
  -: Active brain malignancies or aggressive metastatic cancers involving CNS tissue due to theoretical neurotrophic signaling concerns.
  -: Concurrent use during active chemotherapy or cranial radiation unless medically supervised.
  -: History of severe bipolar disorder, mania, or psychotic-spectrum illness due to potential neurochemical destabilization.

### compound | p21/overview | What is P21?
kind: overview
title: P21
summary: A hexapeptide (Ac-DGGLAG-NH2) derived from ciliary neurotrophic factor (CNTF) that is claimed to mimic BDNF effects and promote neurogenesis. Developed primarily at the New York State Institute for Basic Research. Limited to preclinical rodent studies with no human clinical trials. Sold as a research chemical with unknown safety profile.
keyPoint: A hexapeptide (Ac-DGGLAG-NH2) derived from ciliary neurotrophic factor (CNTF) that is claimed to mimic BDNF effects and promote neurogenesis.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: P21
  connectedTo: P21
section: Why it is researched
  -: A hexapeptide (Ac-DGGLAG-NH2) derived from ciliary neurotrophic factor (CNTF) that is claimed to mimic BDNF effects and promote neurogenesis.
section: How it works in the research
  -: P21 is designed to bypass the blood-brain barrier and activate neurotrophic signaling: BDNF Enhancement Increases brain-derived neurotrophic factor expression by inhibiting leukemia inhibitory factor (LIF) signaling pathway.
section: Evidence strength
  -: PeptideDeck: Animal research; population: Animal; Preclinical animal evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Main limitations
  -: Important caveats apply to interpreting P21 research. Published studies come from a limited number of research groups, reducing independent replication. The translation from rodent maze performance to human cognitive enhancement involves substantial uncertainty.

### compound | p21/mechanism | How does P21 work?
kind: overview
title: P21
summary: A hexapeptide (Ac-DGGLAG-NH2) derived from ciliary neurotrophic factor (CNTF) that is claimed to mimic BDNF effects and promote neurogenesis. Developed primarily at the New York State Institute for Basic Research. Limited to preclinical rodent studies with no human clinical trials. Sold as a research chemical with unknown safety profile.
keyPoint: A hexapeptide (Ac-DGGLAG-NH2) derived from ciliary neurotrophic factor (CNTF) that is claimed to mimic BDNF effects and promote neurogenesis.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: P21
  connectedTo: P21
section: Why it is researched
  -: A hexapeptide (Ac-DGGLAG-NH2) derived from ciliary neurotrophic factor (CNTF) that is claimed to mimic BDNF effects and promote neurogenesis.
section: How it works in the research
  -: P21 is designed to bypass the blood-brain barrier and activate neurotrophic signaling: BDNF Enhancement Increases brain-derived neurotrophic factor expression by inhibiting leukemia inhibitory factor (LIF) signaling pathway.
section: Evidence strength
  -: PeptideDeck: Animal research; population: Animal; Preclinical animal evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Main limitations
  -: Important caveats apply to interpreting P21 research. Published studies come from a limited number of research groups, reducing independent replication. The translation from rodent maze performance to human cognitive enhancement involves substantial uncertainty.
