### compound | pt-141/overview | What is PT-141?
kind: overview
title: PT-141
summary: An FDA-approved melanocortin receptor agonist for hypoactive sexual desire disorder (HSDD) in premenopausal women. Acts centrally rather than on vascular mechanisms. Phase 3 RECONNECT trials demonstrated efficacy.
keyPoint: An FDA-approved melanocortin receptor agonist for hypoactive sexual desire disorder (HSDD) in premenopausal women.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: PT-141
  connectedTo: PT-141
section: Why it is researched
  -: An FDA-approved melanocortin receptor agonist for hypoactive sexual desire disorder (HSDD) in premenopausal women.
section: How it works in the research
  -: PT-141 acts through central nervous system pathways to enhance sexual desire: MC4R Activation Crosses the blood-brain barrier and binds MC4R in the hypothalamus, triggering dopamine release in sexual motivation circuits.
section: Evidence strength
  -: PepCodex: Human clinical research; population: Human; Human evidence with design limitations to check. 18 human studies listed by the source

  -: The reviewed record does not state a specific limitation. The linked paper still needs to be checked for design, size and bias.

### compound | pt141melanotanii/overview | What is PT-141 + Melanotan II?
kind: overview
title: PT-141 + Melanotan II
summary: PT-141 (bremelanotide) and Melanotan II are structurally related melanocortin receptor agonists derived from the same University of Arizona research program. Melanotan II is a non-selective MC1R/MC3R/MC4R/MC5R agonist used in research for tanning and sexual function. PT-141 is a metabolite of Melanotan II with greater selectivity for MC3R and MC4R and minimal MC1R-driven pigmentation; the FDA approved it in 2019 as Vyleesi for hypoactive sexual desire disorder in premenopausal women. Some users combine the two peptides to achieve cosmetic tanning (MT-II) plus enhanced sexual response (PT-141). Combined dosing has not been formally studied. Research subcutaneous protocols typically use 0.25-1 mg MT-II during a loading phase plus 0.5-1.75 mg PT-141 as needed before sexual activity. The stack amplifies common melanocortin side effects (nausea, flushing, blood pressure changes) and adds the long-term dermatologic and oncologic risks associated with MT-II, including new and darkening nevi.
keyPoint: PT-141 (bremelanotide) and Melanotan II are structurally related melanocortin receptor agonists derived from the same University of Arizona research program.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: PT-141 + Melanotan II
  connectedTo: PT-141 + Melanotan II
section: Why it is researched
  -: PT-141 (bremelanotide) and Melanotan II are structurally related melanocortin receptor agonists derived from the same University of Arizona research program.
section: How it works in the research

### compound | pt141melanotanii/mechanism | How does PT-141 + Melanotan II work?
kind: overview
title: PT-141 + Melanotan II
summary: PT-141 (bremelanotide) and Melanotan II are structurally related melanocortin receptor agonists derived from the same University of Arizona research program. Melanotan II is a non-selective MC1R/MC3R/MC4R/MC5R agonist used in research for tanning and sexual function. PT-141 is a metabolite of Melanotan II with greater selectivity for MC3R and MC4R and minimal MC1R-driven pigmentation; the FDA approved it in 2019 as Vyleesi for hypoactive sexual desire disorder in premenopausal women. Some users combine the two peptides to achieve cosmetic tanning (MT-II) plus enhanced sexual response (PT-141). Combined dosing has not been formally studied. Research subcutaneous protocols typically use 0.25-1 mg MT-II during a loading phase plus 0.5-1.75 mg PT-141 as needed before sexual activity. The stack amplifies common melanocortin side effects (nausea, flushing, blood pressure changes) and adds the long-term dermatologic and oncologic risks associated with MT-II, including new and darkening nevi.
keyPoint: PT-141 (bremelanotide) and Melanotan II are structurally related melanocortin receptor agonists derived from the same University of Arizona research program.

### compound | pt141melanotanii/evidence | What research is listed for PT-141 + Melanotan II?
kind: evidence
title: PT-141 + Melanotan II: research listed by the sources
summary: Nausea is the most common adverse effect of both peptides and is amplified when they are combined, particularly with the first one or two doses; it typically peaks thirty to ninety minutes after injection and improves with gradual titration and concurrent food intake.; Facial flushing, yawning, fatigue, headache, and transient elevation of blood pressure and heart rate are reported with both peptides individually and may be additive when combined, especially with higher PT-141 doses.; Spontaneous penile erection in men and increased genital arousal in both sexes can be useful in the sexual-medicine context but may be inconvenient, embarrassing, or in rare cases prolonged; priapism has been reported with melanocortin agonists.; Skin hyperpigmentation including darkening of moles, freckles, lips, areolae, and palmar creases is driven primarily by the MT-II component; the addition of PT-141 does not substantially alter pigmentation but may slightly prolong overall melanocortin exposure.; Case reports describe new pigmented nevi, dysplastic nevi, and rare melanomas in Melanotan II

### compound | ptddbm/overview | What is PTD-DBM?
kind: overview
title: PTD-DBM
summary: PTD-DBM (Protein Transduction Domain-Dishevelled Binding Motif) is a synthetic cell-penetrating peptide developed by the Kang-Yell Choi laboratory at Yonsei University as a cosmetic and research hair-growth agent. It fuses an octa-arginine protein transduction domain to a short Dishevelled-binding motif copied from CXXC5, a negative-feedback brake on Wnt/beta-catenin signaling. By competitively occupying the Dishevelled binding pocket that CXXC5 normally uses, PTD-DBM releases that brake and reactivates Wnt/beta-catenin signaling in hair-follicle stem cells, promoting hair regrowth and wound-induced hair neogenesis in mouse models [1][2]. The commonly cited PTD-DBM dosage is a topical 0.5-1 mg/mL aqueous solution applied once daily to the scalp, frequently combined with valproic acid and microneedling; the per-injection microgram figures on this page are an educational subcutaneous reconstitution reference, because the real-world route is topical rather than injected.
keyPoint: PTD-DBM (Protein Transduction Domain-Dishevelled Binding Motif) is a synthetic cell-penetrating peptide developed by the Kang-Yell Choi laboratory at Yonsei University as a cosmetic and research hair-growth agent.

### compound | ptddbm/mechanism | How does PTD-DBM work?
kind: overview
title: PTD-DBM
summary: PTD-DBM (Protein Transduction Domain-Dishevelled Binding Motif) is a synthetic cell-penetrating peptide developed by the Kang-Yell Choi laboratory at Yonsei University as a cosmetic and research hair-growth agent. It fuses an octa-arginine protein transduction domain to a short Dishevelled-binding motif copied from CXXC5, a negative-feedback brake on Wnt/beta-catenin signaling. By competitively occupying the Dishevelled binding pocket that CXXC5 normally uses, PTD-DBM releases that brake and reactivates Wnt/beta-catenin signaling in hair-follicle stem cells, promoting hair regrowth and wound-induced hair neogenesis in mouse models [1][2]. The commonly cited PTD-DBM dosage is a topical 0.5-1 mg/mL aqueous solution applied once daily to the scalp, frequently combined with valproic acid and microneedling; the per-injection microgram figures on this page are an educational subcutaneous reconstitution reference, because the real-world route is topical rather than injected.
keyPoint: PTD-DBM (Protein Transduction Domain-Dishevelled Binding Motif) is a synthetic cell-penetrating peptide developed by the Kang-Yell Choi laboratory at Yonsei University as a cosmetic and research hair-growth agent.

### compound | ptddbm/evidence | What research is listed for PTD-DBM?
kind: evidence
title: PTD-DBM: research listed by the sources
summary: Local application-site effects are the most likely issues with the topical route: scalp redness, itching, dryness, stinging, or contact dermatitis, particularly when the solution is applied to broken or microneedled skin.; When combined with microneedling/dermarolling (a common protocol), expect pinpoint bleeding, transient inflammation, and a real risk of infection if devices, hands, or the peptide solution are not kept sterile.; Valproic acid, the agent most often stacked with PTD-DBM, is a known hepatotoxin and a potent human teratogen; even topical or off-label use is unstudied for safety and should be avoided in pregnancy and in anyone of child-bearing potential without medical supervision.; Mechanistically, PTD-DBM amplifies Wnt/beta-catenin signaling, a proliferative pathway implicated in several cancers; sustained or broad pathway activation carries a theoretical neoplasia/abnormal-growth concern, and no long-term human safety data exist to address it.; Systemic absorption, distribution, and pharmacokinetics in humans are uncharacterized, so there is no established safety The preferred numerical record is a topical mouse experiment from a full primary paper. PeptideDeck's generic concentration and cycle suggestions were not imported.

### compound | pyy336/overview | What is PYY 3-36?
kind: overview
title: PYY 3-36
summary: A gut-derived peptide hormone released after meals that suppresses appetite by acting on Y2 receptors in the hypothalamus and gut. Studied as one of the body's natural satiety signals and of research interest in obesity and appetite neuroscience.
keyPoint: A gut-derived peptide hormone released after meals that suppresses appetite by acting on Y2 receptors in the hypothalamus and gut.
understood: resolved

section: How it works in the research
  -: Peptide YY 3-36 (PYY 3-36) is a gut hormone fragment released postprandially by L-cells of the ileum, colon, and rectum.

  -: The Peptide Handbook: Animal research; population: Human; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.

### compound | pyy336/evidence | What research is listed for PYY 3-36?
kind: evidence
title: PYY 3-36: research listed by the sources
summary: moderate. PYY 3-36 has direct human research involving appetite and food intake, including intravenous administration in obese subjects, an intranasal clinical study that did not establish an effective approved obesity treatment, and supraphysiologic intravenous exposure associated with nausea without additional food-intake reduction. These are study-specific findings, not a routine treatment protocol. AM833, cagrilintide, and other analog or combination programs are separate evidence and must not be attributed to native PYY 3-36. Batterham et al. (2002) : PYY(3-36) IV infusion reduced caloric intake by 33% in lean subjects over 24 hours - landmark Nature paper establishing PYY as satiety hormone Batterham et al. (2003) : Obese subjects retained sensitivity to exogenous PYY(3-36) - appetite was reduced by 30%, and obese individuals had lower endogenous PYY levels Bariatric Surgery : Post-RYGB PYY levels increase 5-10x; this exaggerated PYY response is considered a major mechanism for sustained weight loss after surgery Combination Therapy : PYY(3-36) + GLP-1 co-administration produces additive appetite suppression (>50% reduction in food intake in some studies) Intranasal Delivery : Achieves sufficient CNS exposure for appetite effects without IV infusion; Novo Nordisk advanced intranasal PYY to Phase II [ 1 ] [ 2 ] [ 3 ] [ 4 ] ↑ 1.0 1.1 Batterham RL, et al. N Engl J Med . 2003;349:941-948. ↑ 3.0 3.1 le Roux CW, et al.

### compound | quercetin/evidence | What research is listed for Quercetin?
kind: evidence
title: Quercetin: research listed by the sources
summary: Mayo Clinic QD senolytic protocol. Anti-inflammatory data extensive.
keyPoint: Mayo Clinic QD senolytic protocol.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: Quercetin
  connectedTo: Quercetin
section: What the research shows
  -: The Peptide Handbook: Parent flavonol with preliminary longevity evidence.
section: Evidence strength
  -: The Peptide Handbook: Systematic review or meta-analysis; population: Human; Higher-level human evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Limitations
  -: The dasatinib-quercetin senolytic combination is a supervised research protocol - dasatinib is an FDA-approved prescription chemotherapy drug with significant toxicity and should never be self-administered
  -: Adequate long-term safety data for high supplemental doses are limited
  -: Potential drug-interaction concerns exist; the evidence represented here does not establish universal safety or formulation equivalence
  -: Commercial products may not contain the labeled amount or the specific quercetin form studied in research
  *: Source rating: 3 out of 5
  *: The Peptide Handbook: preliminary. Longevity and senolytic claims remain preliminary. The cited human pilot evaluated D+Q, not quercetin alone, in nine people with diabetic kidney disease and reported biomarker and senescent-cell findings after the combination. That selected, early-phase study does not demonstrate healthy-adult longevity benefit or a quercetin-alone effect. For standalone quercetin, a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized supplementation trials assessed blood pressure; any reported effect was modest and its clinical importance remains uncertain. A safety review found adverse effects were rarely reported in published human intervention studies and generally mild, while noting limited adequate long-term safety data for high supplemental doses and drug-interaction concerns. Oral quercetin undergoes extensive metabolism, and pharmacokinetics can vary by formulation and analyte.
  *: The Achilles Heel of Senescent Cells: From Transcriptome to Senolytic Drugs (Aging Cell 2015): Identified the first senolytic drugs by analyzing the pro-survival transcriptome of senescent cells. A single dose of dasatinib + quercetin in old mice improved cardiac function within 5 days - establishing the D+Q protocol.
  *: Senolytics in Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis: Results from a First-in-Human, Open-Label, Pilot Study (EBioMedicine 2019): Three intermittent cycles of dasatinib + quercetin in 14 IPF patients significantly reduced circulating senescent cell burden and improved physical function - first human evidence that senolytic clearance has measurable clinical benefit.

  -: Sirolimus (rapamycin) is an established prescription medicine with product-specific transplant and rare-disease uses.
section: How it works in the research
  -: Rapamycin is the common name for sirolimus, an established prescription drug distinct from everolimus, temsirolimus, and other rapalogs.
section: Evidence strength
  -: The Peptide Handbook: Animal research; population: Animal; Preclinical animal evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Main limitations
  -: Serious and opportunistic infections: including Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (PCP), cytomegalovirus (CMV), and invasive fungal infections - prophylaxis required in transplant settings per FDA labeling
  -: Increased risk of lymphoma and non-melanoma skin cancers with prolonged immunosuppression
  -: Hepatic artery thrombosis: reported in liver transplant recipients; use in this population is not recommended per FDA labeling

### compound | rapamycin/evidence | What research is listed for Rapamycin?
kind: evidence
title: Rapamycin: research listed by the sources
summary: Extends lifespan in every model organism tested. PEARL trial published April 2025: 5-10mg weekly safe in healthy aging adults over 48 weeks. Significant lean tissue improvement in women at 10mg. Long-term longevity benefits still under study.
keyPoint: Extends lifespan in every model organism tested.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: Rapamycin
  connectedTo: Rapamycin
section: What the research shows
  -: The Peptide Handbook: Sirolimus (rapamycin) is an established prescription medicine with product-specific transplant and rare-disease uses.
section: Evidence strength
  -: The Peptide Handbook: Animal research; population: Animal; Preclinical animal evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Limitations
  -: Serious and opportunistic infections: including Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (PCP), cytomegalovirus (CMV), and invasive fungal infections - prophylaxis required in transplant settings per FDA labeling
  -: Increased risk of lymphoma and non-melanoma skin cancers with prolonged immunosuppression
  -: Hepatic artery thrombosis: reported in liver transplant recipients; use in this population is not recommended per FDA labeling
  -: Interstitial lung disease and non-infectious pneumonitis: reported with use; may require dose reduction or discontinuation
  -: Angioedema: risk is increased when used with ACE inhibitors or angiotensin receptor blockers
  -: Impaired male fertility: reduced testosterone, altered spermatogenesis, and azoospermia reported in clinical settings
  -: Prescription-only immunosuppressant: should never be used without physician supervision, therapeutic drug monitoring, and appropriate infection prophylaxis
  *: Source rating: 4 out of 5
  *: The Peptide Handbook: strong-human. Sirolimus has established human medical use in approved product- and indication-specific contexts, including renal-transplant rejection prophylaxis and applicable rare-disease labeling. In genetically heterogeneous mice, rapamycin fed late in life extended lifespan; that is animal preclinical evidence and does not establish human longevity efficacy. Human sirolimus safety and therapeutic monitoring must remain label-specific. The strong exact-drug rating reflects established approved medicine, while longevity evidence remains preliminary and investigational.
  *: Rapamycin Fed Late in Life Extends Lifespan in Mice (Nature 2009): Rapamycin extended median lifespan by 14% in female and 9% in male mice even when started at 20 months of age. Landmark longevity study.
  *: PEARL Trial: Low-Dose Rapamycin in Healthy Aging Adults (Aging (Aging-US) · April 2025): 48-week RCT. 5mg and 10mg weekly rapamycin safe and well-tolerated in healthy aging adults. Significant lean tissue mass improvement in women at 10mg. Modest biomarker changes. First major human longevity RCT for rapamycin.

### compound | rapamycin-low-dose/evidence | What research is listed for Rapamycin (Low Dose)?
kind: evidence
title: Rapamycin (Low Dose): research listed by the sources
summary: Most replicated longevity compound in science. PEARL trial published April 2025: 5-10mg weekly safe in healthy adults over 48 weeks with lean tissue benefits in women. Long-term clinical longevity benefits still to be established.
keyPoint: Most replicated longevity compound in science.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: Rapamycin (Low Dose)
  connectedTo: Rapamycin (Low Dose)
section: What the research shows
  -: The Peptide Handbook: Sirolimus (rapamycin) is an established prescription medicine with product-specific transplant and rare-disease uses.
section: Evidence strength
  -: The Peptide Handbook: Animal research; population: Animal; Preclinical animal evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Limitations
  -: Serious and opportunistic infections: including Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (PCP), cytomegalovirus (CMV), and invasive fungal infections - prophylaxis required in transplant settings per FDA labeling
  -: Increased risk of lymphoma and non-melanoma skin cancers with prolonged immunosuppression
  -: Hepatic artery thrombosis: reported in liver transplant recipients; use in this population is not recommended per FDA labeling
  -: Interstitial lung disease and non-infectious pneumonitis: reported with use; may require dose reduction or discontinuation
  -: Angioedema: risk is increased when used with ACE inhibitors or angiotensin receptor blockers
  -: Impaired male fertility: reduced testosterone, altered spermatogenesis, and azoospermia reported in clinical settings
  -: Prescription-only immunosuppressant: should never be used without physician supervision, therapeutic drug monitoring, and appropriate infection prophylaxis
  *: Source rating: 4 out of 5
  *: The Peptide Handbook: strong-human. Sirolimus has established human medical use in approved product- and indication-specific contexts, including renal-transplant rejection prophylaxis and applicable rare-disease labeling. In genetically heterogeneous mice, rapamycin fed late in life extended lifespan; that is animal preclinical evidence and does not establish human longevity efficacy. Human sirolimus safety and therapeutic monitoring must remain label-specific. The strong exact-drug rating reflects established approved medicine, while longevity evidence remains preliminary and investigational.
  *: Targeting the Biology of Aging with mTOR Inhibitors (Nature Aging 2023): Low-dose intermittent rapamycin extends lifespan in every model organism tested and shows promise for human longevity without immunosuppression.

### compound | relamorelin/overview | What is Relamorelin?
kind: overview
title: Relamorelin
summary: Relamorelin (RM-131, formerly BIM-28131; CAS 661472-41-9) is a synthetic pentapeptide ghrelin/growth hormone secretagogue receptor (GHSR-1a) agonist developed as a gastrointestinal prokinetic. It is a stabilized analog of native ghrelin with non-natural amino acid substitutions that resist enzymatic degradation, giving it roughly six-fold greater receptor potency and a much longer plasma half-life than the parent hormone [1]. By activating GHSR-1a on vagal afferents and enteric neurons, relamorelin accelerates gastric emptying and stimulates antral and colonic motility, which is why it was investigated for diabetic gastroparesis and chronic constipation [1][4][5]. Unlike many compounds on this site, relamorelin's real-world route genuinely IS subcutaneous injection, so the reconstitution figures below mirror how it was actually given in trials.
keyPoint: Relamorelin (RM-131, formerly BIM-28131; CAS 661472-41-9) is a synthetic pentapeptide ghrelin/growth hormone secretagogue receptor (GHSR-1a) agonist developed as a gastrointestinal prokinetic.

### compound | relamorelin/evidence | What research is listed for Relamorelin?
kind: evidence
title: Relamorelin: research listed by the sources
summary: Dose-dependent worsening of glycemic control is the most important effect: higher relamorelin doses raised fasting blood glucose and HbA1c in diabetic patients, with about 14.5% showing hyperglycemia on drug and some needing diabetes-medication adjustment; close glucose monitoring is essential and the 100 mcg twice-daily dose was the worst offender [4][6].; Hyperhidrosis (excessive sweating) is a characteristic on-target adverse effect of ghrelin-receptor activation reported in relamorelin trials [6].; Gastrointestinal effects such as diarrhea and abdominal cramping occurred dose-dependently, consistent with the drug's pro-motility action on the stomach and colon [4][6].; Appetite stimulation and weight gain can occur because GHSR-1a is the central hunger receptor; transient rises in growth hormone, prolactin, and cortisol are expected on-target endocrine effects [1].; Dizziness, fatigue, and headache were reported, generally mild and more common at higher doses [6].; Across the pooled phase 2 program no consistent drug-related serious cardiovascular signal emerged, but isolated

### compound | relaxationpmrp226/overview | What is Relaxation PM (RP226)?
kind: overview
title: Relaxation PM (RP226)
summary: Relaxation PM (product code RP226) is an evening recovery and sleep-support injection built from calming amino acids and melatonin. It is a vitamin and amino blend rather than a peptide, working through neurotransmitter support and circadian signaling, and given as a fixed direct dose with no titration. Each milliliter contains GABA 100mg, Melatonin 1mg, Arginine 100mg, and Glutamine 25mg. GABA is the primary inhibitory neurotransmitter and supports a calm, relaxed state, melatonin is the hormone that signals the onset of sleep and helps regulate the circadian rhythm, arginine supports growth hormone release during sleep and improves blood flow, and glutamine supports recovery, immune function, and gut health. In practice, Relaxation PM is used by people who want support for sleep quality, evening relaxation, and overnight recovery, making it the counterpart to the energizing daytime blends in this category.
keyPoint: Relaxation PM (product code RP226) is an evening recovery and sleep-support injection built from calming amino acids and melatonin.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high

### compound | relaxin/overview | What is Relaxin?
kind: overview
title: Relaxin
summary: A two-chain insulin-superfamily peptide hormone that remodels connective tissue, reduces fibrosis, and dilates blood vessels. Studied in acute heart failure (Phase III trial failed primary endpoint), renal protection, and anti-fibrotic applications. Produced naturally in pregnancy.
keyPoint: A two-chain insulin-superfamily peptide hormone that remodels connective tissue, reduces fibrosis, and dilates blood vessels.

  -: A peptide hormone of the insulin/relaxin superfamily encoded by the RLN2 gene.

  -: The Peptide Handbook: Animal research; population: Human; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.

  -: Clinically significant hypotension - particularly relevant with IV administration; blood pressure monitoring required in clinical settings

### compound | relaxin/evidence | What research is listed for Relaxin?
kind: evidence
title: Relaxin: research listed by the sources
summary: moderate. Relaxin-2 has a moderate human evidence base, primarily from the serelaxin heart failure clinical program. The Phase II RELAX-AHF trial (n=1,161) demonstrated improvements in dyspnoea relief and a striking 37% reduction in 180-day cardiovascular mortality (exploratory endpoint), generating significant interest in relaxin as a cardioprotective and vasodilatory agent. However, the confirmatory Phase III RELAX-AHF-2 trial did not meet its primary endpoint of 180-day cardiovascular mortality, and clinical development for acute heart failure was discontinued. The anti-fibrotic evidence base is largely preclinical - animal models of renal, hepatic, pulmonary, and cardiac fibrosis show consistent reversal with relaxin, mediated through MMP induction and inhibition of TGF-β profibrotic signalling. Connective tissue and reproductive biology research provides strong mechanistic context. The gap between compelling preclinical anti-fibrotic data and clinical trial outcomes reflects a recurring challenge in translational peptide research.
keyPoint: moderate.

### compound | renisamin/overview | What is Renisamin?
kind: overview
title: Renisamin
summary: Renisamin is a Khavinson cytomedin - a natural low-molecular-weight polypeptide complex extracted from the kidney tissue of young animals - developed at the St. Petersburg Institute of Bioregulation and Gerontology as the kidney-specific bioregulator in the Khavinson framework. It works by entering renal tubular epithelial cells and glomerular cells, binding to nuclear DNA at organ-specific gene promoter regions, and normalizing the gene expression programs that govern how those cells function, survive, and regenerate. In plain terms: the kidneys lose functional units (nephrons) with age and stress, and Renisamin signals the surviving nephron cells to behave more like young, healthy kidney cells - improving their filtration efficiency, reducing fibrotic scarring, and supporting cellular survival under metabolic stress.
keyPoint: Renisamin is a Khavinson cytomedin - a natural low-molecular-weight polypeptide complex extracted from the kidney tissue of young animals - developed at the St.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: Renisamin
  connectedTo: Renisamin
section: Why it is researched
  -: Renisamin is a Khavinson cytomedin - a natural low-molecular-weight polypeptide complex extracted from the kidney tissue of young animals - developed at the St.
section: How it works in the research
  -: Renisamin is a Khavinson cytomedin - a natural low-molecular-weight polypeptide complex extracted from the kidney tissue of young animals - developed at the St.
section: Evidence strength
  -: Peptide University Codex: Source summary; study design not clearly stated; population: Animal; Preclinical animal evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Main limitations
  -: eGFR < 30 (CKD Stage 4-5) without nephrologist supervision - severely reduced functional nephron mass limits bioregulator target cell availability; the altered pharmacokinetics of oral peptide absorption and renal clearance in advanced CKD require specialist oversight for dose adjustment.
  -: Active acute kidney injury (AKI) in the anuric or oliguric phase - Renisamin is a tissue regenerative bioregulator, not an acute intervention for AKI management; initiation during active oliguric AKI has not been evaluated and could interact with the acute injury-repair process.
  -: Renal cell carcinoma or urothelial malignancy - renal tubular cell gene program normalization activity has not been evaluated in the context of malignant renal cells; nephron bioregulator activity in malignant tissue requires oncological evaluation.

section: What the research shows
  -: Peptide University Codex: Renisamin is a Khavinson cytomedin - a natural low-molecular-weight polypeptide complex extracted from the kidney tissue of young animals - developed at the St.
section: Evidence strength
  -: Peptide University Codex: Source summary; study design not clearly stated; population: Animal; Preclinical animal evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Limitations
  -: eGFR < 30 (CKD Stage 4-5) without nephrologist supervision - severely reduced functional nephron mass limits bioregulator target cell availability; the altered pharmacokinetics of oral peptide absorption and renal clearance in advanced CKD require specialist oversight for dose adjustment.
  -: Active acute kidney injury (AKI) in the anuric or oliguric phase - Renisamin is a tissue regenerative bioregulator, not an acute intervention for AKI management; initiation during active oliguric AKI has not been evaluated and could interact with the acute injury-repair process.
  -: Renal cell carcinoma or urothelial malignancy - renal tubular cell gene program normalization activity has not been evaluated in the context of malignant renal cells; nephron bioregulator activity in malignant tissue requires oncological evaluation.
  -: Active nephrotic syndrome with severe hypoalbuminemia (albumin < 2.0 g/dL) - the profound protein losses of active nephrotic syndrome create an unpredictable pharmacokinetic context for oral peptide absorption.
  -: Known hypersensitivity to Renisamin (renal tissue cytomedin polypeptide complex) or formulation excipients.
  -: Pregnancy - renal hemodynamic changes during pregnancy (50% increase in GFR, renal enlargement, altered tubular function) create an unevaluated context for exogenous renal bioregulator activity.
  -: Renal transplantation on immunosuppression - renal tubular cell bioregulator activity in immunosuppressed recipients with donor nephron tissue requires transplant nephrology supervision; interactions with calcineurin inhibitor-induced nephrotoxicity and the immunosuppression-modified renal transcriptome are not
  -: Active pyelonephritis or renal abscess - acute bacterial renal parenchymal infection requires antimicrobial management; bioregulator activity during active renal infection has not been characterized.
  *: Source rating: 1 out of 5, very limited evidence
  *: Peptide University Codex: Peptide University labels its records as aggregated from empirical research and anecdotal community data. This record is retained as supplied and is not upgraded to clinical evidence.

  *: Source rating: 3 out of 5
  *: The Peptide Handbook: preliminary. The cited human intervention was a randomized double-blind crossover study in 11 obese men using 150 mg/day for 30 days. It provides short-term metabolic and mitochondrial context only; it does not show disease prevention, calorie-restriction equivalence, or human longevity benefit. A separate human pharmacokinetic study found high absorption but very low oral bioavailability of unchanged resveratrol due to extensive metabolism. Resveratrol has been linked to SIRT1-related signaling, but direct activation claims were challenged with native substrates and remain substrate- and assay-dependent. Animal and pathway findings do not establish human lifespan extension.
  *: Resveratrol and Metabolic Health in Obese Men (Cell Metabolism 2011): Resveratrol improved metabolic markers, mitochondrial function, and activated SIRT1 in obese men. Subjects were clinically obese - results may not generalize to healthy-weight individuals.

  *: The Peptide Handbook: strong-human. Retatrutide has published controlled Phase II evidence and sponsor-reported Phase 3 topline results while it remains investigational. In TRIUMPH-2 (NCT05929079), 1,152 adults with type 2 diabetes and obesity or overweight were randomized; Lilly reported average body-weight changes at 80 weeks of -12.7% with 4 mg, -19.1% with 9 mg, and -20.8% with 12 mg, compared with -4.0% with placebo. In TRIUMPH-3 (NCT05882045), 1,949 adults with severe obesity and established cardiovascular disease, with or without type 2 diabetes, were randomized; Lilly reported average body-weight changes at 80 weeks of -21.6% with 9 mg and -22.6% with 12 mg, compared with -3.2% with placebo. These are company-reported topline results and have not yet been published as complete peer-reviewed trial reports; the registry records confirm trial identity and design but do not currently provide posted results. TRIUMPH-3 included exploratory/event analyses of major cardiovascular events, but the reported estimates were imprecise and do not establish cardiovascular-event reduction.
  *: Halflife Labs: Evidence context is stated on the linked compound page.
  *: Peptpedia: Human evidence is comparatively extensive for an investigational peptide: completed first-in-human Phase 1b and Phase 2 trials in type 2 diabetes, obesity, and MASLD, with a Phase 3 program (TRIUMPH) ongoing. Long-term safety and cardiovascular outcomes are not yet established - no completed cardiovascular outcomes trial exists as of 2026 - and dose-dependent increases in heart rate were observed in Phase 2, a class effect under continued study.
  *: Peptide Hub: Protocol-focused educational summary. Linked papers, site-listed ranges and commercial context are retained with source attribution.
  *: Retatrutide for Obesity: Phase 2 Trial (NEJM 2023): 338 obese adults. 24.2% weight loss at 48 weeks. 100% on 8-12mg achieved ≥5% loss. Historic Phase 2 data.
  *: TRIUMPH-4: Retatrutide Phase 3 - 28.7% Weight Loss (Eli Lilly Press Release / Phase 3 2025): 445 adults with obesity and knee osteoarthritis. Retatrutide 12mg: 28.7% average weight loss at 68 weeks - highest ever Phase 3 result. Also reduced WOMAC pain by 75.8%. New dysesthesia signal at 20.9%.

### compound | secretin/overview | What is Secretin?
kind: overview
title: Secretin
summary: A 27-amino-acid intestinal hormone used clinically as synthetic human secretin (ChiRhoStim) for diagnostic procedures involving pancreatic secretion, gastrin secretion, and ERCP. Controlled clinical trials did not demonstrate efficacy for autism.
keyPoint: A 27-amino-acid intestinal hormone used clinically as synthetic human secretin (ChiRhoStim) for diagnostic procedures involving pancreatic secretion, gastrin secretion, and ERCP.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: Secretin
  connectedTo: Secretin
section: Why it is researched
  -: A 27-amino-acid intestinal hormone used clinically as synthetic human secretin (ChiRhoStim) for diagnostic procedures involving pancreatic secretion, gastrin secretion, and ERCP.
section: How it works in the research
  -: Secretin is a 27-amino-acid peptide hormone produced by the duodenum in response to nutrients and gastric acid.
section: Evidence strength
  -: The Peptide Handbook: Randomized or controlled human research; population: Human; Direct controlled human evidence. 85 human studies listed by the source; 110 animal studies listed by the source
section: Main limitations
  -: Diagnostic testing limitation: anticholinergic drugs may cause a hyporesponse to ChiRhoStim stimulation testing; discontinue anticholinergic drugs at least five half-lives before testing.
  -: Test interpretation precaution: H2-receptor antagonists or proton-pump inhibitors may cause increased gastrin secretion and falsely suggest gastrinoma; discontinue H2-receptor antagonists at least two days before testing and follow the individual PPI prescribing information.
  -: Diagnostic testing limitation: alcoholic or other liver disease may cause a hyperresponse to ChiRhoStim and mask coexisting pancreatic disease; consider additional testing and clinical assessment.
  followUp: Show the research evidence for Secretin
  followUp: Show the human research studies for Secretin
  compound: Secretin

  source: WikiPep <https://wikipep.org/wiki/Secretin>

### compound | secretin/evidence | What research is listed for Secretin?
kind: evidence
title: Secretin: research listed by the sources
summary: strong-human. Secretin has established human clinical use as a diagnostic agent. Current ChiRhoStim labeling supports stimulation of pancreatic secretions, including bicarbonate, to aid diagnosis of exocrine pancreas dysfunction; stimulation of gastrin secretion to aid diagnosis of gastrinoma; and stimulation of pancreatic secretions to facilitate ERCP. Its established use is diagnostic rather than chronic therapeutic. Historical interest in autism was not supported by controlled evidence: a double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of synthetic human secretin did not demonstrate improvement versus placebo, and a Cochrane systematic review concluded that randomized controlled trials did not show improvement in core autism-spectrum-disorder features. Multiple randomized controlled trials and systematic reviews failed to demonstrate clinical benefit for autism. Diagnostic Utility (Pancreatic Function) : Gold standard stimulant for pancreatic function testing; quantifies exocrine reserve Gastrinoma Diagnosis : Secretin stimulation test has >90% sensitivity for Zollinger-Ellison syndrome MRCP Enhancement : Secretin-enhanced magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography (S-MRCP) improves visualization of pancreatic duct anatomy ERCP Facilitation : Aids duodenal relaxation and papilla identification during endoscopic procedures Historical Significance : First hormone ever discovered; foundational to modern endocrinology Safety : Excellent safety profile at diagnostic doses; serious adverse events extremely rare [ 1 ] [ 2 ] [ 3 ] [ 4 ] [ 5 ] [ 6 ] ↑ 1.0 1.1 Bayliss WM, Starling EH. "The Mechanism of Pancreatic Secretion." J Physiol . 1902;28(5):325-353. [Historical landmark - first use of the word "hormone"] ↑ 2.0 2.1 Chey WY, Chang TM. "Secretin: Historical Perspective and Current Status." Pancreas . 2014;43(2):162-182. ↑ 3.0 3.1 Dreiling DA, Janowitz HD. "The Measurement of Pancreatic Secretory Function."

### compound | selank/overview | What is Selank?
kind: overview
title: Selank
summary: A synthetic heptapeptide derived from the immunomodulatory peptide tuftsin, developed by Russian researchers and approved in Russia since 2009 for anxiety and neurasthenia. Demonstrates anxiolytic effects comparable to benzodiazepines without sedation, cognitive impairment, or dependence liability. Extensive Russian clinical research supports efficacy, though Western independent replication remains limited.
keyPoint: A synthetic heptapeptide derived from the immunomodulatory peptide tuftsin, developed by Russian researchers and approved in Russia since 2009 for anxiety and neurasthenia.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: Selank
  connectedTo: Selank
section: Why it is researched
  -: A synthetic heptapeptide derived from the immunomodulatory peptide tuftsin, developed by Russian researchers and approved in Russia since 2009 for anxiety and neurasthenia.
section: How it works in the research
  -: GABA Enhancement Modulates gene expression of GABA-A receptor subunits, enhancing inhibitory neurotransmission for calming effects without the sedation or dependence of benzodiazepines.
section: Evidence strength
  -: The Peptide Handbook: Human clinical research; population: Human; Human evidence with design limitations to check. 6 human studies listed by the source; 20 animal studies listed by the source
section: Main limitations
  -: No well-defined serious adverse-event profile has been established in controlled human trials. FDA has identified potential immunogenicity concerns for compounded Selank acetate related to aggregation and peptide impurities and notes that important human safety information is lacking.

### compound | selank/mechanism | How does Selank work?
kind: overview
title: Selank
summary: A synthetic heptapeptide derived from the immunomodulatory peptide tuftsin, developed by Russian researchers and approved in Russia since 2009 for anxiety and neurasthenia. Demonstrates anxiolytic effects comparable to benzodiazepines without sedation, cognitive impairment, or dependence liability. Extensive Russian clinical research supports efficacy, though Western independent replication remains limited.

### compound | selank/evidence | What research is listed for Selank?

summary: Approved in Russia. Limited English-language RCT data.

understood: resolved

matchedText: Selank
  connectedTo: Selank
section: What the research shows
  -: PepCodex: A synthetic heptapeptide derived from the immunomodulatory peptide tuftsin, developed by Russian researchers and approved in Russia since 2009 for anxiety and neurasthenia.
  -: The Peptide Handbook: A synthetic tuftsin-derived peptide studied primarily for anxiety, stress, and cognitive-related effects.
  -: Halflife Labs: Selank (synthetic tuftsin analogue heptapeptide Thr-Lys-Pro-Arg-Gly-Pro-Pro) has a plasma half-life of minutes after intranasal administration due to rapid proteolytic cleavage.
  -: Peptpedia: Russia's approved anxiolytic peptide: GABA modulation without sedation or dependence.
  -: PeptideDosage.org: Selank (Thr-Lys-Pro-Arg-Pro-Gly-Pro) is a synthetic heptapeptide anxiolytic derived from the endogenous immunomodulator tuftsin, developed at the Russian Academy of Sciences' Institute of Molecular Genetics.
section: Evidence strength
  -: PepCodex: Human clinical research; population: Human; Human evidence with design limitations to check. 5 human studies listed by the source
  -: The Peptide Handbook: Human clinical research; population: Human; Human evidence with design limitations to check. 6 human studies listed by the source; 20 animal studies listed by the source
  -: Halflife Labs: Human clinical research; population: Human; Human evidence with design limitations to check. The source does not give a reliable study count.

  -: PeptideDosage.org: Animal research; population: Animal; Preclinical animal evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Limitations
  -: The reviewed record does not state a specific limitation. The linked paper still needs to be checked for design, size and bias.
  -: No well-defined serious adverse-event profile has been established in controlled human trials. FDA has identified potential immunogenicity concerns for compounded Selank acetate related to aggregation and peptide impurities and notes that important human safety information is lacking.
  -: not merely a stability enhancer - it contributes its own pharmacological activity and alters tissue distribution patterns.
  -: not produce tolerance, dependence, or withdrawal symptoms even after prolonged administration in research settings, making it valuable for chronic anxiety treatment studies.
  -: not approved for any clinical use.
  -: not reviewed it.
  -: not available for most research peptides.
  -: no published head-to-head trials compare the two directly.
  -: No standardized Western clinical protocols exist as Selank has not completed FDA or EMA review.
  -: No controlled combination trials have been published in international peer-reviewed literature.
  -: Selank (Thr-Lys-Pro-Arg-Pro-Gly-Pro) is a synthetic heptapeptide anxiolytic derived from the endogenous immunomodulator tuftsin, developed at the Russian Academy of Sciences' Institute of Molecular Genetics.
  *: Source rating: 2 out of 5, limited evidence
  *: PepCodex: Moderate evidence; 5 human studies listed
  *: The Peptide Handbook: moderate. Selank has been evaluated in several small human studies, including research in generalized anxiety disorder, neurasthenia, phobic-anxiety and somatoform disorders. These studies reported anxiolytic effects and some cognitive-related findings. Human research has also examined immune signaling and brain functional connectivity. Mechanistic studies suggest effects involving GABAergic signaling, neurotransmission-related gene expression, and BDNF-related pathways, although much of this mechanistic work is preclinical. The main limitation is the relatively small and geographically concentrated human evidence base, with limited large-scale independent replication.
  *: Halflife Labs: animal study plus limited Russian clinical trials
  *: PeptideDosage.org: Selank's safety profile in Russian clinical use over 20+ years is favorable; the most common adverse event is transient nasal irritation or mild rhinorrhea at the site of intranasal application, typically resolving without intervention within minutes.; Headache has been reported in a minority of users, usually at higher cumulative daily doses (above 1500 mcg) and often associated with dehydration or concurrent stimulant use; it generally resolves on dose reduction.; Unlike benzodiazepines, Selank does not produce sedation, psychomotor slowing, or amnesia on standard psychomotor batteries, and driving impairment has not been demonstrated in controlled studies.; Selank has no documented abuse liability, no tolerance development over 30-day courses, and no withdrawal or rebound anxiety on abrupt discontinuation, distinguishing it sharply from GABA-A orthosteric agonists.; Rare reports describe transient mood blunting or emotional flatness at supraphysiologic doses; this is reversible on cessation and may relate to over-modulation of serotonergic turnover.; Drug interaction data are
  *: PeptideDeck: A PubMed-indexed Russian randomized comparison enrolled 62 people with generalized anxiety disorder or neurasthenia: 30 received Selank and 32 received medazepam. The abstract reports similar anxiolytic effects, with additional antiasthenic and psychostimulant effects for Selank. The study is small, Russian-language and not independently replicated in a large modern trial.
  *: Efficacy and possible mechanisms of action of a new peptide anxiolytic selank in the therapy of generalized anxiety disorders and neurasthenia (Zhurnal Nevrologii i Psikhiatrii 2008): Randomized clinical trial in 62 patients comparing Selank to medazepam (benzodiazepine). Selank demonstrated equivalent anxiolytic efficacy on Hamilton/Zung/CGI scales without sedation or dependence - the foundational human RCT establishing Selank's clinical profile.
  *: The inhibitory effect of Selank on enkephalin-degrading enzymes as a possible mechanism of its anxiolytic activity (Bulletin of Experimental Biology and Medicine 2001): Kozlovskaya et al. demonstrated Selank's dose-dependent inhibition of enkephalinase (IC50 ~15 µM), establishing enkephalin system modulation as the primary mechanism of its anxiolytic effects.

Plasma half-life estimated at minutes after intranasal administration, based on proteolytic cleavage data from animal studies. No English-language formal human pharmacokinetic study published. Heptapeptide synthetic analogue of the immunomodulatory tetrapeptide tuftsin (Thr-Lys-Pro-Arg), extended with a Gly-Pro-Pro tripeptide to enhance metabolic stability. Primary mechanisms include GABAergic potentiation, serotonergic modulation, and enkephalin-degrading enzyme inhibition. Anxiolytic and nootropic effects documented in animal models and limited Russian clinical literature.

### compound | selanksemakoxytocinblend/overview | What is NeuroSync?
kind: overview
title: NeuroSync
summary: NeuroSync is a neuroregulatory peptide blend combining Semax, Selank, and Oxytocin into a single coordinated cognitive, emotional, and social-performance support system. The blend is structured around a 10mg Semax, 10mg Selank, and 1mg Oxytocin ratio, allowing each 2.1mg of total blend to yield approximately 1mg Semax, 1mg Selank, and 100mcg Oxytocin. Semax provides the cognitive and neurotrophic backbone of the formulation through support of BDNF-related signaling, dopaminergic tone, executive function, alertness, and mental endurance. Selank adds the anxiolytic and mood-regulatory layer through GABAergic, serotonergic, and stress-buffering pathways, helping reduce excessive mental noise without creating the heavy sedation associated with stronger calming agents. Oxytocin provides the social and emotional modulation component, supporting emotional openness, trust signaling, interpersonal ease, and parasympathetic tone.
keyPoint: NeuroSync is a neuroregulatory peptide blend combining Semax, Selank, and Oxytocin into a single coordinated cognitive, emotional, and social-performance support system.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: NeuroSync
  connectedTo: NeuroSync

  -: NeuroSync is a neuroregulatory peptide blend combining Semax, Selank, and Oxytocin into a single coordinated cognitive, emotional, and social-performance support system.

section: Main limitations
  -: Pregnancy or active attempts to conceive due to the oxytocin component and potential uterotonic signaling concerns.
  -: Breastfeeding due to insufficient safety data and the oxytocin component’s role in lactation physiology.
  -: Concurrent use with uterotonic agents or prostaglandins unless medically supervised.

section: Limitations
  -: Pregnancy or active attempts to conceive due to the oxytocin component and potential uterotonic signaling concerns.
  -: Breastfeeding due to insufficient safety data and the oxytocin component’s role in lactation physiology.

  -: Concurrent use with desmopressin or vasopressin analogs unless medically supervised due to additive water-retention and hyponatremia risk.

  -: Known hypersensitivity to Semax, Selank, Oxytocin, or formulation excipients.
  -: Seizure disorder or unstable neurologic disease unless medically supervised.

matchedText: Semaglutide
  connectedTo: Semaglutide
section: What the research shows
  -: PepCodex: A GLP-1 receptor agonist FDA-approved for type 2 diabetes, obesity, cardiovascular risk reduction, and MASH.
  -: The Peptide Handbook: An FDA-approved GLP-1 receptor agonist used in the treatment of type 2 diabetes and chronic weight management.
  -: Halflife Labs: Detailed pharmacokinetic reference for semaglutide covering SC and oral half-lives, bioavailability, clearance timeline, and dosing intervals based on FDA-approved labeling.
  -: Peptpedia: Averages ~15% weight loss and cut cardiac events 20% in SELECT.
  -: PeptideDosage.org: Semaglutide is a once-weekly GLP-1 receptor agonist developed by Novo Nordisk and marketed as Ozempic (type 2 diabetes), Wegovy (chronic weight management) and Rybelsus (oral T2D).
section: Evidence strength
  -: PepCodex: Human clinical research; population: Human; Human evidence with design limitations to check. 78 human studies listed by the source
  -: The Peptide Handbook: Randomized or controlled human research; population: Human; Direct controlled human evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: Halflife Labs: Source summary; study design not clearly stated; population: Not clearly stated; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: Peptpedia: Source summary; study design not clearly stated; population: Not clearly stated; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: PeptideDosage.org: Human clinical research; population: Human; Human evidence with design limitations to check. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Limitations
  -: The reviewed record does not state a specific limitation. The linked paper still needs to be checked for design, size and bias.
  -: Pancreatitis (rare)
  -: Gallbladder disease
  -: Medullary thyroid carcinoma risk (boxed warning; contraindicated with MEN2/MTC history)
  -: Hypoglycemia (when combined with insulin/sulfonylureas)
  -: Gastroparesis
  -: The source does not clearly state the study population or design in PEARL's reviewed record.
  -: No dose adjustment is required for mild-to-moderate renal impairment.
  -: not statistically significant.
  -: not-diabetic group to show benefit from a GLP-1 agonist; (3) it expanded the approved indication for Wegovy to include CV risk reduction in the US.
  -: unknown but it is contraindicated in personal/family history of MTC or MEN2; (2) Pancreatitis: rare but potential risk; discontinue if suspected; (3) Gallbladder disease: rapid weight loss with semaglutide increases cholelithiasis risk; (4) Hypoglycemia: rare with semaglutide alone but significant risk when combined
  -: not permanently reset the body's adiposity 'set point'-once the appetite suppression is removed, hunger returns to pre-treatment intensity.

  *: Source rating: 5 out of 5
  *: PepCodex: High evidence; 78 human studies listed
  *: The Peptide Handbook: strong-human. Large randomized trials support semaglutide for labeled metabolic indications. SUSTAIN-6 demonstrated fewer major adverse cardiovascular events with semaglutide versus placebo in adults with type 2 diabetes at elevated cardiovascular risk (Marso et al. 2016). STEP 1 found substantial mean weight loss with semaglutide 2.4 mg in adults with overweight or obesity, and SELECT demonstrated cardiovascular-event reduction in adults with established cardiovascular disease and overweight or obesity without diabetes. The FLOW trial (completed January 2024) found that semaglutide reduced the composite risk of kidney failure and major kidney-disease events in adults with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease. The EVOKE Phase III trial (primary endpoint completed September 2025) found that semaglutide did not slow clinical progression in early Alzheimer's disease; this completed negative result should not be characterized as an unanswered or ongoing program.
  *: Halflife Labs: Evidence context is stated on the linked compound page.
  *: PeptideDosage.org: Gastrointestinal events are the dominant side effect: nausea 44% (vs 16% placebo), diarrhea 32%, vomiting 24% and constipation 24% in STEP-1. Most events were mild-to-moderate, concentrated during titration and resolved within 1-2 weeks of dose stabilization; 4.5% discontinued for GI reasons [1].; Cholelithiasis and acute cholecystitis occurred in 2.6% on semaglutide vs 1.2% on placebo in pooled STEP data - a recognized class effect of rapid weight loss and altered bile-flow dynamics. Patients should be counseled on right-upper-quadrant pain warning signs [1].; Acute pancreatitis remains a label concern, with an absolute event rate <0.4% in STEP trials, broadly consistent with background population rates. The FDA label advises discontinuation if pancreatitis is suspected and avoidance in patients with a history of pancreatitis.; Heart-rate elevation of 2-4 beats per minute on average was observed in STEP-1; clinical significance appears minimal but pre-existing tachyarrhythmia warrants caution.
  *: PeptideDeck: Supports significant reduction in body weight through appetite suppression and reduced caloric intake Helps regulate blood glucose levels by enhancing insulin secretion when blood sugar rises May reduce cardiovascular risk factors including blood pressure and inflammatory markers Promotes feelings of fullness and satiety that persist between meals Supports metabolic health improvements including reduced visceral fat accumulation The clinical evidence supporting semaglutide spans dozens of large, well-designed trials. The STEP (Semaglutide Treatment Effect in People with Obesity) program alone enrolled thousands of participants across multiple studies. Results consistently show substantial, sustained weight loss with acceptable safety profiles. The SELECT trial represented a landmark moment for obesity treatment. This massive study enrolled over 17,000 people with established cardiovascular disease and overweight or obesity but without diabetes. After following participants for over four years, semaglutide reduced major adverse cardiovascular events by 20% compared to placebo.
  *: STEP-1: Semaglutide 2.4mg for Weight Management (NEJM 2021): 14.9% weight loss vs 2.4% placebo over 68 weeks. Established 2.4mg as standard obesity dose.
  *: STEP UP: Semaglutide 7.2mg (Wegovy HD) (Lancet Diabetes & Endocrinology 2025): 20.7% average weight loss at 72 weeks. ~1 in 3 patients achieved ≥25% loss. Dysesthesia signal at 22.9%. FDA approved March 2026.

### compound | semax/overview | What is Semax?
kind: overview
title: Semax
summary: A synthetic heptapeptide analogue of ACTH(4-7) with a C-terminal Pro-Gly-Pro extension, developed by Russian researchers and approved in Russia since ~1997 for stroke, cognitive impairment, and optic nerve disorders. Demonstrates nootropic and neuroprotective effects through BDNF/NGF upregulation, dopaminergic and serotonergic modulation, and anti-inflammatory mechanisms. Extensive Russian clinical research supports efficacy, particularly in stroke rehabilitation, though Western independent replication remains limited.
keyPoint: A synthetic heptapeptide analogue of ACTH(4-7) with a C-terminal Pro-Gly-Pro extension, developed by Russian researchers and approved in Russia since ~1997 for stroke, cognitive impairment, and optic nerve disorders.

### compound | semax/evidence | What research is listed for Semax?
kind: evidence
title: Semax: research listed by the sources
summary: Approved in Russia for stroke, nootropic use.
keyPoint: Approved in Russia for stroke, nootropic use.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: Semax
  connectedTo: Semax
section: What the research shows
  -: PepCodex: A synthetic heptapeptide analogue of ACTH(4-7) with a C-terminal Pro-Gly-Pro extension, developed by Russian researchers and approved in Russia since ~1997 for stroke, cognitive impairment, and optic nerve disorders.
  -: The Peptide Handbook: A synthetic heptapeptide derived from a fragment of ACTH, used in clinical practice in Russia for neuroprotection and cognitive support following stroke and brain injury.
  -: Halflife Labs: Semax (ACTH 4-10 analogue heptapeptide Met-Glu-His-Phe-Pro-Gly-Pro) has a plasma half-life of minutes after intranasal administration due to rapid proteolytic cleavage.
  -: Peptpedia: Approved in Russia since the 1990s, Semax raises BDNF and NGF without stimulant action.
  -: PeptideDosage.org: Semax (Met-Glu-His-Phe-Pro-Gly-Pro, MEHFPGP) is a synthetic heptapeptide analogue of adrenocorticotropic hormone fragment ACTH(4-10), with a stabilizing Pro-Gly-Pro tail added to confer resistance to proteolysis.
section: Evidence strength
  -: PepCodex: Human clinical research; population: Human; Human evidence with design limitations to check. 8 human studies listed by the source
  -: The Peptide Handbook: Animal research; population: Animal; Preclinical animal evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: Halflife Labs: Human clinical research; population: Human; Human evidence with design limitations to check. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: Peptpedia: Source summary; study design not clearly stated; population: Not clearly stated; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: PeptideDosage.org: Animal research; population: Animal; Preclinical animal evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Limitations
  -: The reviewed record does not state a specific limitation. The linked paper still needs to be checked for design, size and bias.
  -: Human safety and seizure risk are not sufficiently characterized for a universal contraindication or dosing rule
  -: not approved it.
  -: not stimulate adrenal steroidogenesis.
  -: not prevent systemic clearance.
  -: not alter dopamine or its metabolites, but when given before D-amphetamine it dramatically enhanced the amphetamine-induced rise in extracellular striatal dopamine and locomotor activity.
  -: not approved for any clinical use and remains a research compound.
  -: not reviewed or approved Semax.
  -: not replicated in large Western RCTs, however, and the quality of Russian clinical trial reporting varies.
  -: not function like classical stimulants (which work by elevating catecholamines acutely).
  -: Semax (Met-Glu-His-Phe-Pro-Gly-Pro, MEHFPGP) is a synthetic heptapeptide analogue of adrenocorticotropic hormone fragment ACTH(4-10), with a stabilizing Pro-Gly-Pro tail added to confer resistance to proteolysis. Developed at the M. M. Shemyakin and Yu. A.
  *: Source rating: 3 out of 5
  *: PepCodex: Moderate evidence; 8 human studies listed
  *: The Peptide Handbook: preliminary. Preliminary human studies have examined Semax in acute ischemic stroke and post-ischemic rehabilitation, including clinical, electrophysiologic, functional, and biomarker outcomes. The cited 2018 study reported plasma BDNF findings; it does not establish CSF BDNF or human NGF elevation. Most of the human literature comes from Eastern European clinical settings, and independent replication remains limited. Semax is also discussed and used in some peptide/nootropic communities for focus, attention, and cognitive performance. These uses are based largely on real-world experience and anecdotal reports and should not be interpreted as established treatment for ADHD or cognitive disorders.
  *: Halflife Labs: animal study plus limited Russian clinical trials
  *: PeptideDosage.org: Semax is well tolerated at clinical and research doses; the most frequent adverse effect is transient nasal irritation, sneezing, or rhinorrhea at the site of intranasal application, typically resolving within minutes.; Mild headache may occur, particularly at higher cumulative daily doses (above 1500 mcg) or with concurrent stimulant use; it usually responds to dose reduction or adequate hydration.; Increased alertness can produce difficulty initiating sleep if Semax is administered late in the day; dosing earlier in the morning and at midday is the conservative practice in research protocols.; Unlike classical psychostimulants, Semax has not been associated with abuse liability, tolerance, dependence, or withdrawal in animal models or in Russian clinical experience spanning 30 years.; Rare reports describe transient blood pressure elevations at supraphysiologic doses; cardiovascular monitoring is reasonable in patients with uncontrolled hypertension, particularly when high stroke-protocol doses are used.; Semax does not stimulate cortisol release despite its derivation from
  *: PeptideDeck: The PubMed paper most often cited for Semax and ADHD is a 2007 Medical Hypotheses article, not an efficacy trial. A Russian review describes a small open-label group of 20 children receiving Semax within a wider non-randomized comparison and reports improvement in 50%, but it lacks a blinded placebo-controlled design.
  *: Semax and BDNF in Neurological Disorders (Doklady Biochemistry 2001): Significantly increased BDNF expression and demonstrated neuroprotection.

  *: Halflife Labs: minutes after intranasal administration due to rapid proteolytic cleavage. Plasma half-life estimated at minutes after intranasal administration, based on proteolytic cleavage data from animal studies. No English-language formal human pharmacokinetic study published. Heptapeptide ACTH(4-10) analogue (Met-Glu-His-Phe-Pro-Gly-Pro) with nootropic and neuroprotective effects. Proposed mechanisms include BDNF upregulation, enkephalin degradation inhibition, and serotonin/dopamine modulation. CNS penetration documented via intranasal route.
  *: Peptpedia: Several minutes in serum; CNS effects may persist longer. Species and route are retained when stated in the profile's molecular field or research table.
  *: PeptideDeck: No preferred human half-life from this editorial source. PeptideDeck is retained as a topic-discovery page. Pharmacokinetic figures remain source-specific elsewhere in PEARL.
  *: Peptide Authority: Short plasma half-life; CNS effects persist longer. Peptide Authority profile summary. Species and route must be checked in the cited pharmacokinetic paper.
  *: Licensed reference library: Unknown (minutes). Short plasma half-life; intranasal administration is common to improve CNS delivery. Precise human values not well standardized.

  connectedTo: Semax
  *: Resolved: site-listed dose ranges. Published study protocols with species, route, population, frequency and duration take priority. Uncited commercial ranges remain labelled and secondary. A product or calculator range is not evidence that a dose was studied, effective or safe. Confidence: high.
  *: Resolved: ADHD evidence level. Describe Semax as ADHD-related research with limited, hypothesis-generating evidence, not as an established ADHD treatment. Peptpedia highlights ADHD relevance, while PeptideDeck says Semax has not been robustly studied specifically for ADHD. The often-cited PMID 16996699 is a Medical Hypotheses article rather than a clinical efficacy trial. A small Russian open-label pediatric report exists, but it was not a modern blinded randomized placebo-controlled study. Confidence: high for the evidence limitation.
  *: Resolved: modelled administration routes. Use only the route stated in the original study or official product information. Do not convert an oral, intranasal, intramuscular or investigational product into a generic subcutaneous vial protocol. PeptideDosage.org applies a common reconstitution and syringe format even to products such as Ventfort that it identifies as oral. That format is not evidence that the modelled route was studied or is suitable. Confidence: high.
  *: Resolved: mental-health citation identity. Exclude three unrelated PubMed identifiers copied under Semax, NAC and Selank claims. Keep only links whose NCBI record matches the stated research subject. NCBI identifies PMID 11157505 as a Hodgkin-disease cell-fusion paper, PMID 16640009 as a Freeman-Sheldon syndrome case report, and PMID 18677858 as a neonatal-mortality paper. None supports the peptide claim beside which it appeared. Confidence: high.

### compound | sermorelin/evidence | What research is listed for Sermorelin?
kind: evidence
title: Sermorelin: research listed by the sources
summary: FDA approved for pediatric GH deficiency.
keyPoint: FDA approved for pediatric GH deficiency.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: Sermorelin
  connectedTo: Sermorelin
section: What the research shows
  -: PepCodex: A GHRH analog that was FDA-approved for pediatric GH deficiency.
  -: The Peptide Handbook: A synthetic version of the first 29 amino acids of growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH), the natural signal the hypothalamus uses to prompt pituitary growth hormone production.
  -: Halflife Labs: Sermorelin half-life is approximately 10-20 minutes per human pharmacokinetic data (Prakash & Goa, BioDrugs 1999).
  -: Peptpedia: Sermorelin (Geref) won FDA approval for pediatric GH deficiency before its discontinuation (not safety-related).
  -: Peptide Hub: STIMULATES THE RELEASE OF ENDOGENOUS GROWTH HORMONE - IMPROVED MUSCLE STRENGTH, GROWTH AND REPAIR - ANTI AGING - IMPROVED BONE DENSITY
section: Evidence strength
  -: PepCodex: Human clinical research; population: Human; Human evidence with design limitations to check. 32 human studies listed by the source
  -: The Peptide Handbook: Animal research; population: Animal; Preclinical animal evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: Halflife Labs: Source summary; study design not clearly stated; population: Not clearly stated; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: Peptpedia: Source summary; study design not clearly stated; population: Not clearly stated; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: Peptide Hub: Review or official medicine information; population: Not clearly stated; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Limitations
  -: The reviewed record does not state a specific limitation. The linked paper still needs to be checked for design, size and bias.
  -: Long-term safety and outcome data for contemporary compounded use have not been established
  -: The source does not clearly state the study population or design in PEARL's reviewed record.
  -: not safety-related).
  -: not for safety reasons - and is now available mainly as a compounded drug.
  -: not withdrawn for safety or effectiveness reasons.
  -: no abstract) argues for sermorelin-an analog of growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH 1-29)-as an approach to adult-onset growth hormone insufficiency.
  -: not present original clinical trial data on efficacy or safety outcomes.
  -: not change serum IGF-1, IGFBP-3, or GH binding protein, and produced no change in body weight, BMI, or DEXA measures of muscle and fat.
  -: no adverse effects on glucose, insulin, or lipids.
  -: not pituitary failure, is a primary driver of age-related GH decline.
  -: This is a commercial educational source. Its uncited figures and modelled outputs must remain labelled as source-listed rather than clinical evidence.
  *: Source rating: 3 out of 5
  *: PepCodex: Moderate evidence; 32 human studies listed
  *: The Peptide Handbook: moderate. Sermorelin (GHRH(1-29)-NH₂) has documented human pharmacodynamic activity: intravenous administration produces dose-dependent growth-hormone release in normal men, with a reported IV disappearance half-time of approximately 4.3 minutes (Barron et al. 1985; Soule et al. 1994). Prolonged subcutaneous infusion promoted growth in children with partial GH insufficiency over one year (Brain et al. 1990). As Geref, sermorelin was historically FDA-approved; the marketed product was voluntarily withdrawn, and FDA determined the withdrawal was not for reasons of safety or effectiveness. This historical regulatory status and documented human pharmacodynamic data do not establish clinical benefit for adult anti-aging, longevity, sleep, or body-composition claims in contemporary compounded formulations.
  *: Halflife Labs: Evidence context is stated on the linked compound page.
  *: Peptide Hub: Protocol-focused educational summary. Linked papers, site-listed ranges and commercial context are retained with source attribution.
  *: PeptideDosage.org: Localised injection-site reactions (small wheal, transient erythema, mild pruritus) are the most common adverse effect, occurring in roughly 16% of subjects in the Geref paediatric trial and typically resolving within hours.; Mild flushing and warm facial sensation within 5-15 minutes of injection occur in approximately 20% of users, reflecting vasodilation from GHRH-R expression on vascular endothelium; tolerance develops within 1-2 weeks.; Headache and lightheadedness in the first sessions affect 5-10% of users and reflect blood-pressure changes from acute GH release.; Mild peripheral oedema and hand stiffness during the first 2-3 weeks of therapy reflect IGF-1-driven extracellular fluid expansion; typically self-resolves with continued dosing.; Drowsiness within 30-60 minutes of evening dosing is common and mirrors the natural sleep-promoting GH-pulse effect; most subjects schedule the injection pre-bed.; Mild glucose intolerance with HbA1c rise of 0.1-0.2% can develop with chronic dosing through GH-mediated reduction in peripheral insulin sensitivity; quarterly glucose
  *: Once daily subcutaneous growth hormone-releasing hormone therapy accelerates growth in growth hormone-deficient children during the first year of therapy (Journal of Clinical Endocrinology & Metabolism 1996): Multicenter trial (n=110 GH-deficient children) showing sermorelin 30 mcg/kg/day SubQ at bedtime increased mean height velocity from 4.1 cm/yr at baseline to 8.0 cm/yr at 6 months - the pivotal pediatric efficacy trial supporting FDA approval.

Synthetic GHRH(1-29) analog; cleared by serum peptidases. Stimulates pituitary GH release via GHRHR. Once-nightly dosing times GH pulse with natural nocturnal GH secretion. Cleared primarily via proteolytic degradation and renal filtration.

  *: Spontaneous penile erection. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Depression and suicidal ideation have occurred; monitor for new or worsening depression, suicidal thoughts, or suicidal behavior. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Serious hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis, have been reported; prior serious hypersensitivity to setmelanotide or IMCIVREE excipients is a formal contraindication. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Generalized skin hyperpigmentation, darkening of existing nevi, and development of new melanocytic nevi can occur; full-body skin examination is recommended before treatment and periodically during treatment. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Spontaneous penile erections and other sexual adverse effects can occur; erections lasting longer than 4 hours require urgent medical attention. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Patients with acquired hypothalamic obesity require monitoring for acute adrenal insufficiency. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Extension studies have followed patients for up to 3 years, demonstrating: Sustained weight loss maintenance with continued treatment Consistent safety profile without new signals emerging Skin hyperpigmentation stabilizes and partially reverses after discontinuation No evidence of tachyphylaxis (loss of effect over. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Setmelanotide's side effect profile reflects its mechanism as a melanocortin receptor agonist with predominant MC4R activity but some residual effects at other receptor subtypes. [source-listed source severity]

### compound | setmelanotide/evidence | What research is listed for Setmelanotide?
kind: evidence
title: Setmelanotide: research listed by the sources
summary: strong-human. Direct Phase 3 human evidence includes POMC/PCSK1/LEPR-deficiency obesity and Bardet-Biedl syndrome populations. Administration, pharmacokinetics, and safety remain product- and label-specific. Skin hyperpigmentation and darkening of pre-existing moles are very common (up to about 67% in the BBS trial) because MC4R agonism spills over onto melanocortin-1 receptors, increasing melanin; baseline and periodic full-body skin examinations are advised [2][4].; Injection-site reactions are very common (erythema, pruritus, induration, bruising), reflecting the daily subcutaneous route [4].; Gastrointestinal effects - nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and abdominal pain - occur frequently, are usually dose-related, and tend to appear early in treatment [1][4].; Disturbances in sexual arousal can occur, including spontaneous penile erections in males and genital effects in females; a male erection lasting longer than 4 hours warrants emergency care [4].; Depression and suicidal ideation have been reported; clinicians should monitor for new or worsening mood symptoms and consider discontinuation if they emerge [4].; Serious hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis, have occurred within minutes to hours of dosing and require immediate treatment and discontinuation [4].;
keyPoint: strong-human.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
