  *: PeptideDosage.org: Skin hyperpigmentation and darkening of pre-existing moles are very common (up to about 67% in the BBS trial) because MC4R agonism spills over onto melanocortin-1 receptors, increasing melanin; baseline and periodic full-body skin examinations are advised [2][4].; Injection-site reactions are very common (erythema, pruritus, induration, bruising), reflecting the daily subcutaneous route [4].; Gastrointestinal effects - nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and abdominal pain - occur frequently, are usually dose-related, and tend to appear early in treatment [1][4].; Disturbances in sexual arousal can occur, including spontaneous penile erections in males and genital effects in females; a male erection lasting longer than 4 hours warrants emergency care [4].; Depression and suicidal ideation have been reported; clinicians should monitor for new or worsening mood symptoms and consider discontinuation if they emerge [4].; Serious hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis, have occurred within minutes to hours of dosing and require immediate treatment and discontinuation [4].;
  *: PeptideDeck: Significant weight loss in patients with qualifying genetic mutations Reduction in hunger and food-seeking behavior Improved metabolic parameters including glucose and lipid profiles First targeted therapy addressing root cause of genetic obesity Once-daily subcutaneous administration Demonstrated efficacy in both pediatric and adult patients Restoration of functional melanocortin signaling Sustained weight management with continued treatment Setmelanotide's approval was based on two pivotal clinical trials demonstrating substantial efficacy in genetically-confirmed patients-remarkable results that reflect the power of precision medicine in the right patient population. The first pivotal trial enrolled 10 patients with POMC deficiency and 1 patient with PCSK1 deficiency. After approximately one year of treatment: 80% Achieved ≥10% Weight Loss ~25% Mean Weight Loss in Responders Significant Hunger Score Reduction The hunger reduction was particularly striking.
  *: WikiPep: Phase III pivotal trials: Demonstrated significant weight loss and hunger reduction in POMC, PCSK1, and LEPR deficiency patients. Due to the extreme rarity of these conditions, trials used open-label designs with withdrawal periods to confirm treatment effects. BBS pivotal trial: Phase III trial in 44 patients with BBS demonstrated clinically meaningful weight loss compared to placebo. Long-term extension studies: Weight loss maintained over 3+ years of continued treatment with sustained hunger reduction. Expanded genetic obesity indications: Investigating efficacy in other rare genetic causes of obesity, including SH2B1 deficiency and MC4R heterozygous deficiency. Hypothalamic obesity: Studied for obesity following hypothalamic injury (e.g., craniopharyngioma surgery). Smith-Magenis syndrome: Under investigation for obesity management in this genetic condition. [ 1 ] [ 2 ] [ 3 ] [ 4 ] [ 5 ] ↑ 1.0 1.1 Clément K, van den Akker E, Argente J, et al.

### compound | shlp2/overview | What is SHLP-2?
kind: overview
title: SHLP-2
summary: A 26-amino acid mitochondria-derived peptide (MDP) discovered in 2016 from the same mitochondrial DNA region as humanin. Shows cytoprotective, metabolic, and potential longevity effects in preclinical studies. Part of an emerging class of mitochondrial signaling molecules, but human therapeutic data is lacking.

### compound | shredshr/overview | What is Shred (SHR)?
kind: overview
title: Shred (SHR)
summary: Shred (product code SHR) is a straightforward fat-metabolism and energy injection that combines carnitine, a MIC methylation base, and B-vitamins in a balanced, non-stimulant formula. It is a vitamin and amino blend rather than a peptide, working through nutritional and metabolic pathways, and given as a fixed direct dose with no titration. Each milliliter contains L-Carnitine 200mg, B12 250mcg, B6 (Pyridoxine) 25mg, Inositol 50mg, Methionine 25mg, and Choline 50mg. The carnitine supports mitochondrial fatty-acid transport, the methionine, inositol, and choline provide the lipotropic fat-mobilization base, and the B6 and B12 support amino acid metabolism, energy production, and red blood cell formation. In practice, Shred is used by people who want a clean, reliable lipotropic fat-loss injection without stimulants or beta-agonists, positioning it as a solid everyday cutting-support option.
keyPoint: Shred (product code SHR) is a straightforward fat-metabolism and energy injection that combines carnitine, a MIC methylation base, and B-vitamins in a balanced, non-stimulant formula.

method: canonical

### compound | sia31c18/overview | What is Single Regulator (SIA-31-C18)?
kind: overview
title: Single Regulator (SIA-31-C18)
summary: SIA-31-C18 (Single Regulator) is a 31-amino acid GLP-1 receptor agonist belonging to the Peptide Receptor Modulator Research Series. It is a semaglutide-class single incretin agonist featuring a C18 fatty diacid (octadecanedioyl) side chain attached via a γ-Glu-2x AEEA linker at Lys20, enabling albumin binding and extended half-life comparable to once-weekly dosing formats. The backbone closely mirrors the GLP-1 incretin sequence with Aib (alpha-aminoisobutyric acid) substitutions at key positions for DPP-4 resistance and enhanced receptor affinity. CAS: 910463-68-2. Structurally analogous in class to semaglutide. Once-weekly subcutaneous injection. Key reference literature: Wilding et al. (NEJM 2021) - once-weekly semaglutide in adults with overweight or obesity, 15% mean weight loss at 68 weeks; Lincoff et al. (NEJM 2023) - semaglutide and cardiovascular outcomes in obesity without diabetes; Perkovic et al. (NEJM 2024) - semaglutide effects on chronic kidney disease.
keyPoint: SIA-31-C18 (Single Regulator) is a 31-amino acid GLP-1 receptor agonist belonging to the Peptide Receptor Modulator Research Series.

### compound | sia31c18/mechanism | How does Single Regulator (SIA-31-C18) work?
kind: overview
title: Single Regulator (SIA-31-C18)
summary: SIA-31-C18 (Single Regulator) is a 31-amino acid GLP-1 receptor agonist belonging to the Peptide Receptor Modulator Research Series. It is a semaglutide-class single incretin agonist featuring a C18 fatty diacid (octadecanedioyl) side chain attached via a γ-Glu-2x AEEA linker at Lys20, enabling albumin binding and extended half-life comparable to once-weekly dosing formats. The backbone closely mirrors the GLP-1 incretin sequence with Aib (alpha-aminoisobutyric acid) substitutions at key positions for DPP-4 resistance and enhanced receptor affinity. CAS: 910463-68-2. Structurally analogous in class to semaglutide. Once-weekly subcutaneous injection. Key reference literature: Wilding et al. (NEJM 2021) - once-weekly semaglutide in adults with overweight or obesity, 15% mean weight loss at 68 weeks; Lincoff et al. (NEJM 2023) - semaglutide and cardiovascular outcomes in obesity without diabetes; Perkovic et al. (NEJM 2024) - semaglutide effects on chronic kidney disease.

### compound | sigumir/evidence | What research is listed for Sigumir?
kind: evidence
title: Sigumir: research listed by the sources
summary: Human safety data specific to Sigumir are limited; it has not undergone the controlled toxicology and adverse-event reporting required of an approved drug, so its side-effect profile is not well characterised [1].; Because the peptides are extracted from animal (bovine) cartilage and bone, people with allergies to animal proteins may react; hypersensitivity and the theoretical risks of animal-tissue sourcing (for example prion/BSE concerns and batch-to-batch quality variation) cannot be fully excluded.; Mild gastrointestinal complaints (nausea, stomach discomfort) are the most plausible effects from the oral capsules and are usually managed by taking them with food.; Manufacturer labelling lists pregnancy, breastfeeding and childhood as contraindications, advises use only from age 14 onward, and recommends that repeat or chronic-condition courses be taken under physician supervision.; The subcutaneous route modelled on this page is not validated: injecting a capsule-grade, animal-tissue-derived peptide complex risks injection-site reactions, sterile abscess, infection and immune Peptide University labels its records as aggregated from empirical research and anecdotal community data. This record is retained as supplied and is not upgraded to clinical evidence.

  -: PepCodex: Source summary; study design not clearly stated; population: Not clearly stated; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.

section: Limitations
  -: The source does not clearly state the study population or design in PEARL's reviewed record.
  -: Sigumir is a cartilage-and-bone peptide bioregulator (a "Cytomax") from the Khavinson family of short-peptide preparations, manufactured by the St. Petersburg Institute of Bioregulation and Gerontology from peptide fractions of young-animal cartilage and bone tissue.
  -: Bone malignancy (primary or metastatic) - osteoblast gene program normalization and bone matrix synthesis stimulation in the context of malignant bone involvement has not been characterized; bone metastases from prostate, breast, or other primary tumors require oncological evaluation before any bone bioregulator use.
  -: Osteosarcoma or chondrosarcoma - direct contraindication; malignant bone and cartilage cell gene program normalization activity is not established.
  -: Active bone infection (osteomyelitis) - bioregulator activity at the bone tissue level during active bacterial bone infection has not been characterized; antimicrobial management takes priority.
  -: Paget's disease of bone with active high bone turnover phase - the dysregulated coupled bone remodeling of Paget's disease creates an unpredictable context for osteoblast bioregulator normalization; requires specialist evaluation.
  -: Known hypersensitivity to Sigumir (bone and cartilage tissue cytomedin peptide complex) or formulation excipients (including gelatin capsule).
  -: Pregnancy - bone and cartilage remodeling during pregnancy involves significant hormonal regulation (relaxin, estrogen, PTH-rP); exogenous skeletal bioregulator activity has not been evaluated in this context.
  -: Concurrent teriparatide therapy without specialist supervision - teriparatide's direct PTH receptor-mediated osteoblast stimulation combined with Sigumir's osteoblast gene program normalization creates an additive pro-anabolic skeletal effect; beneficial but should be initiated under specialist oversight in subjects
  -: Hypercalcemia of any cause - bone formation stimulation in the context of elevated baseline calcium may worsen hypercalcemia; calcium levels should be normalized before initiating Sigumir.

### compound | slu-pp-332/overview | What is SLU-PP-332?
kind: overview
title: SLU-PP-332
summary: A small molecule ERR (Estrogen-Related Receptor) agonist developed at Saint Louis University. Preclinical studies suggest exercise-mimetic properties, but no human data exists. Represents early-stage research into pharmacologically activating exercise pathways.
keyPoint: A small molecule ERR (Estrogen-Related Receptor) agonist developed at Saint Louis University.
understood: resolved
method: alias
confidence: high
matchedText: SLUPP332

  connectedTo: SLUPP332
  connectedTo: SLU-PP-332
section: Why it is researched
  -: A small molecule ERR (Estrogen-Related Receptor) agonist developed at Saint Louis University.
section: How it works in the research
  -: SLU-PP-332 aims to activate “exercise pathways” pharmacologically by targeting ERR receptors: ERR Activation Binds to ERRalpha and ERRgamma receptors, triggering transcription of metabolic genes normally activated by exercise.
section: Evidence strength
  -: PeptideDosage.org: Animal research; population: Human; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Main limitations
  -: SLU-PP-332 is a synthetic small-molecule pan-agonist of the estrogen-related receptors ERRα, ERRβ, and ERRγ developed at Saint Louis University by Burris, Billon, Kahn, and colleagues.

### compound | snap-8/overview | What is Snap-8?
kind: overview
title: Snap-8
summary: Reduced expression-wrinkle depth up to 63% in 28 days in clinical testing - a topical SNARE-complex blocker. Mechanism, formulation data & limitations.
keyPoint: Reduced expression-wrinkle depth up to 63% in 28 days in clinical testing - a topical SNARE-complex blocker.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: Snap-8
  connectedTo: Snap-8
section: Why it is researched
  -: Reduced expression-wrinkle depth up to 63% in 28 days in clinical testing - a topical SNARE-complex blocker.
section: How it works in the research
  -: SNAP-8 is believed to work by inhibiting the SNARE complex formation, which is required for neurotransmitter release at neuromuscular junctions.
section: Evidence strength
  -: PeptideDosage.org: Randomized or controlled human research; population: Human; Direct controlled human evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Main limitations
  -: SNAP-8 (Acetyl Octapeptide-3) is a synthetic octapeptide derivative of Argireline developed as a topical cosmetic ingredient for reducing the appearance of expression lines and dynamic wrinkles.

  *: Source rating: 2 out of 5, limited evidence
  *: PeptideDosage.org: Topical SNAP-8 is generally very well tolerated, with the most commonly reported adverse effects limited to mild, transient erythema, stinging, or a sensation of tightness at the site of application, particularly when used with other actives such as retinoids or alpha-hydroxy acids.; Allergic contact dermatitis to SNAP-8 itself is rare, but reactions to other components of the finished cosmetic formulation, including preservatives, fragrances, or penetration enhancers, can produce eczematous patches and should be evaluated by a dermatologist if persistent.; Because SNAP-8 is intended for topical periocular and forehead use, accidental ocular contact may cause transient conjunctival irritation, watering, and burning; the product should be kept away from the eye margin and rinsed promptly with water if it migrates onto the ocular surface.; There is no published evidence that SNAP-8 produces systemic muscle weakness, dysphagia, ptosis, or other neuromuscular adverse events characteristic of botulinum toxin, since the peptide is too large and polar to be absorbed into systemic
  *: PeptideDeck: Reduces appearance of expression lines and wrinkles Non-invasive topical application Modulates rather than paralyzes muscle activity Well-tolerated with minimal side effects Can be combined with other anti-aging peptides Progressive improvement with consistent use May enhance results of professional treatments Suitable for preventive anti-aging care SNAP-8 has been studied in the context of cosmetic peptide science, where research examines its interaction with the neurotransmitter-release machinery and its effect on the appearance of expression lines. SNAP-8 research centers on its ability to interfere with SNARE complex formation by mimicking a portion of SNAP-25. Laboratory investigation of this class of peptides has explored how effectively they compete with the native protein and how that competition translates into reduced neurotransmitter release. This mechanistic work provides the rationale for using SNAP-8 to soften dynamic wrinkles topically.

  *: PeptideDeck: This is where the comparison gets interesting, because the evidence gap between these two peptides is larger than most skincare articles admit. Argireline has the most published clinical data of any cosmeceutical SNARE-targeting peptide. Key findings: Periorbital trial: ~30% reduction in wrinkle depth after 30 days of twice-daily application at 10% solution concentration. Controlled against vehicle. Published by Blanes-Mira et al. Dose-response data: 5% concentration showed measurable but lower efficacy than 10%. Going above 10% didn't produce proportional gains. Independent confirmatory studies: Multiple labs have reproduced the basic finding, not just the manufacturer. This is unusual for cosmeceutical peptides. Mechanism validation: In vitro SNARE competition assays confirm the proposed pathway, with catecholamine release inhibition demonstrated in chromaffin cell models Long-term use: Widespread commercial use since 2002 without significant safety signals SNAP-8 has a thinner evidence base.
  *: PeptideDeck: Honest assessment time. For researchers working with peptides directly (not commercial serums), quality matters enormously. Requirements: HPLC purity ≥98% with batch-specific COA Mass spectrometry verification of molecular identity Proper lyophilization and cold-chain shipping Transparent third-party testing documentation third-party seller carries GHK-Cu and other research peptides with transparent COA documentation. Establishes quantitative analytical basis for SNAP-8 cosmetic formulations.

### compound | somatostatin/overview | What is Somatostatin-14?
kind: overview
title: Somatostatin-14
summary: The endogenous hypothalamic hormone that broadly suppresses growth hormone, TSH, insulin, glucagon, and multiple gastrointestinal hormones. Breaks down within minutes in the body, limiting direct therapeutic use, but its long-acting analogs Octreotide and Lanreotide are FDA-approved and widely used.
keyPoint: The endogenous hypothalamic hormone that broadly suppresses growth hormone, TSH, insulin, glucagon, and multiple gastrointestinal hormones.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: Somatostatin-14
  connectedTo: Somatostatin-14
section: Why it is researched
  -: The endogenous hypothalamic hormone that broadly suppresses growth hormone, TSH, insulin, glucagon, and multiple gastrointestinal hormones.
section: How it works in the research
  -: Somatostatin-14 is an endogenous cyclic tetradecapeptide produced in the hypothalamus, pancreatic delta cells, and gastrointestinal tract.
section: Evidence strength
  -: The Peptide Handbook: Animal research; population: Animal; Preclinical animal evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Main limitations
  -: Significant hormonal suppression across multiple axes
  -: Glucose dysregulation requiring monitoring
  -: Not suitable for unsupervised use due to pleiotropic suppressive effects

### compound | somatostatin/evidence | What research is listed for Somatostatin-14?
kind: evidence
title: Somatostatin-14: research listed by the sources
summary: strong-human. Somatostatin-14 is a native endocrine and gastrointestinal inhibitory peptide. Human physiology studies describe hormonal and gastric-secretory responses to the native peptide. Its short duration prompted development of longer-acting analogues, but analogue approvals, efficacy, dosing, pharmacokinetics, and safety do not transfer to native somatostatin-14. ### compound | somatropin/overview | What is Somatropin (HGH)?
kind: overview
title: Somatropin (HGH)
summary: Recombinant human growth hormone used in multiple FDA-approved products for growth hormone deficiency and other product-specific indications. It is one of the best-established therapeutic proteins in the growth hormone/IGF-1 field.
keyPoint: Recombinant human growth hormone used in multiple FDA-approved products for growth hormone deficiency and other product-specific indications.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: Somatropin (HGH)
  connectedTo: Somatropin (HGH)
section: Why it is researched
  -: Recombinant human growth hormone used in multiple FDA-approved products for growth hormone deficiency and other product-specific indications.
section: How it works in the research
  -: Somatropin is recombinant human growth hormone, a 191-amino-acid protein corresponding to human growth hormone.
section: Evidence strength
  -: The Peptide Handbook: Randomized or controlled human research; population: Human; Direct controlled human evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Main limitations
  -: Somatropin is contraindicated in active malignancy; patients with prior malignancy require appropriate monitoring for recurrence or progression
  -: Acute critical illness after major surgery, trauma, or acute respiratory failure is a labeled contraindication for pharmacologic somatropin doses because increased mortality was observed in trials
  -: Somatropin can reduce insulin sensitivity and may unmask or worsen glucose intolerance or diabetes
  followUp: Show the research evidence for Somatropin (HGH)

### compound | somatropin/evidence | What research is listed for Somatropin (HGH)?
kind: evidence
title: Somatropin (HGH): research listed by the sources
summary: strong-human. Somatropin has direct human evidence in adults with confirmed growth hormone deficiency, including a double-blind randomized placebo-controlled trial of growth hormone replacement and body-composition outcomes. NORDITROPIN provides the product-specific U.S. regulatory anchor; other somatropin products may have different indications, devices, strengths, storage, or dosing instructions. Somatropin is not an approved anti-aging treatment, and anti-aging, bodybuilding, or performance promotion are not established indications.

Developed by Stealth BioTherapeutics for mitochondrial diseases, heart failure, and age-related macular degeneration. summary: Clinical trials used 4mg and 40mg daily SubQ - but these were in SICK patients (heart failure, Barth syndrome). Healthy biohacker doses are far lower: 1-10 mg/day is the typical range. The 40mg TAZPOWER dose was for a rare genetic mitochondrial disease; it is not a biohacker target. Safety is well-established up to 40mg/day from trial data, but therapeutic need does not apply to healthy users. Doses shown above reflect biohacker practice, not clinical trial protocols.

  -: Peptide Hub: SS-31 (also known as elamipretide, Bendavia, and Forzinity) is a synthetic aromatic-cationic tetrapeptide engineered to concentrate at the inner mitochondrial membrane at levels approximately 1,000-5,000 times higher than surrounding cellular tissue.

  *: Source rating: 3 out of 5
  *: PepCodex: High evidence; 12 human studies listed
  *: The Peptide Handbook: strong-human. SS-31 (Elamipretide) has strong mechanistic preclinical evidence for mitochondrial cardiolipin stabilization and ATP restoration across cardiac, renal, and neurological animal models. Phase 2/3 randomized clinical trials in Barth syndrome established safety and early efficacy signals; the TAZPOWER trial (NCT03098797, completed October 2021) did not meet its primary endpoint (6-minute walk test) but demonstrated significant improvements in secondary functional and quality-of-life outcomes. FDA granted accelerated approval in September 2025 for FORZINITY (elamipretide) for improving muscle strength in adult and pediatric patients (≥30 kg) with Barth syndrome - the first FDA-approved treatment for this condition (NDA 215244). Additional Phase III trials include NCT05162768 (completed December 2024) and NCT06373731 (active not recruiting as of August 2026, estimated completion September 2027). The previously stored PubMed identifiers (PMID 29668615 and PMID 31154001) were confirmed as entity mismatches and have been removed.
  *: Halflife Labs: Animal Study + early human trials
  *: Peptpedia: Extensive human exposure exists across completed randomized placebo-controlled trials in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, primary mitochondrial myopathy, Barth syndrome, and dry age-related macular degeneration, plus a single-dose pharmacokinetic study in older adults. Despite this, the efficacy record is largely negative outside Barth syndrome: PROGRESS-HF, MMPOWER-3, the randomized crossover phase of TAZPOWER, and ReCLAIM-2 all failed their primary endpoints. The FDA-approved Barth syndrome use was granted under accelerated approval based on an intermediate endpoint, with continued approval contingent on verification of clinical benefit in a confirmatory trial. Safety statements about specific adverse-event rates below come from the FDA prescribing information (Forzinity, DailyMed), which is a regulatory label rather than a PubMed-indexed paper, so those points carry no PMID.
  *: Peptide Hub: Protocol-focused educational summary. Linked papers, site-listed ranges and commercial context are retained with source attribution.
  *: First-in-class cardiolipin-protective compound as a therapeutic agent to restore mitochondrial bioenergetics (British Journal of Pharmacology 2014): Szeto HH reviewed the mechanism of SS-31 (Elamipretide/MTP-131) as a cardiolipin-protective compound that selectively concentrates in the inner mitochondrial membrane, restoring cristae structure and mitochondrial bioenergetics. Established the foundational pharmacology for this class.
  *: Novel Mitochondria-Targeting Peptide in Heart Failure Treatment: A Randomized, Placebo-Controlled Trial of Elamipretide (HERA Trial) (Circulation: Heart Failure 2017): Phase 2 ascending-dose HERA trial. Elamipretide was well tolerated across all doses and showed improvements in left ventricular end-systolic volume in heart failure patients with reduced ejection fraction.

Plasma half-life approximately 2 hours following IV administration in animal studies (Chatfield et al. 2019, PMID 30898597). Limited human PK data from Phase 2 clinical trials in heart failure. ### compound | ss31motschumaninblend/overview | What is MITO-3?
kind: overview
title: MITO-3
summary: MITO-3 is a mitochondrial restoration blend combining SS-31, MOTS-c, and Humanin in a 1:1:1 ratio, with each 15mg vial containing 5mg SS-31, 5mg MOTS-c, and 5mg Humanin. SS-31 targets the inner mitochondrial membrane through cardiolipin interaction, supporting electron transport chain structure, membrane potential, and ATP production. MOTS-c functions as a mitochondrial-derived metabolic signal that activates AMPK, supports mitochondrial biogenesis, improves glucose handling, and promotes fatty acid oxidation. Humanin provides the cellular survival layer by opposing BAX-mediated apoptotic signaling and supporting cytoprotection during mitochondrial stress. Together, the blend targets mitochondrial dysfunction from three separate angles: repair of existing mitochondria, construction of new mitochondrial capacity, and protection of stressed cells during the repair process.
keyPoint: MITO-3 is a mitochondrial restoration blend combining SS-31, MOTS-c, and Humanin in a 1:1:1 ratio, with each 15mg vial containing 5mg SS-31, 5mg MOTS-c, and 5mg Humanin.

### compound | stamakort/evidence | What research is listed for Stamakort?
kind: evidence
title: Stamakort: research listed by the sources
summary: Stamakort is reported by manufacturers to be very well tolerated, with claims of 'no side effects, complications, or drug dependence'; however, independent safety data from controlled trials are essentially absent, so this favorable profile is not externally verified [8].; Because it is taken orally, mild gastrointestinal effects such as nausea, abdominal discomfort, belching, or altered bowel habits are plausible and consistent with the route, even if rarely formally documented.; Hypersensitivity or allergic reactions are possible given the bovine (calf gastric mucosa) origin of the peptide complex; people with known animal-protein allergies should be cautious.; The proposed broad modulation of gene expression raises a theoretical, uncharacterized risk of off-target effects in tissues other than the stomach; this concern is unquantified because human safety studies are lacking.; Use during pregnancy, breastfeeding, and in children has not been studied and is generally advised against by manufacturers and distributors.; Caution is warranted in people with active or treated

### compound | substancep/overview | What is Substance P?
kind: overview
title: Substance P
summary: An 11-amino-acid, C-terminally amidated neuropeptide central to pain-signaling research. Direct human studies show it can induce headache/vascular effects and skin inflammation when administered; NK1 receptor antagonists that block its signaling are FDA-approved for chemotherapy-induced nausea, though not for pain.

### compound | substancep/mechanism | How does Substance P work?
kind: overview
title: Substance P
summary: An 11-amino-acid, C-terminally amidated neuropeptide central to pain-signaling research. Direct human studies show it can induce headache/vascular effects and skin inflammation when administered; NK1 receptor antagonists that block its signaling are FDA-approved for chemotherapy-induced nausea, though not for pain.

### compound | substancep/evidence | What research is listed for Substance P?
kind: evidence
title: Substance P: research listed by the sources
summary: moderate. Substance P has an extensive mechanistic literature and a well-validated NK1 receptor pathway. Direct human evidence is more limited than the mechanistic literature might suggest: a small (n=6) intradermal-challenge study demonstrated neurogenic skin inflammation, and a 2025 randomized, placebo-controlled crossover trial found that IV Substance P reliably induced headache and vascular dilation in healthy volunteers - useful for headache-pathophysiology research but not evidence of therapeutic or migraine-treatment efficacy. A CSF biomarker study in PTSD found Substance P levels similar between patients and controls, correcting an earlier claim of elevated or severity-correlated levels. The clearest human translational success is indirect: NK1 receptor antagonists (aprepitant, netupitant) are FDA-approved for chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting, demonstrating that the SP-NK1R axis is druggable - but this is evidence about NK1 antagonism, not about administering Substance P itself, and the antagonist's dosing does not apply to Substance P. Despite strong preclinical rationale, NK1 receptor antagonists have generally failed to demonstrate analgesic efficacy in clinical trials of various pain conditions. This paradoxical failure has been attributed to species differences in NK1R pharmacology between rodents and humans, redundancy in pain transmission pathways, and the finding that conventional NK1R antagonists may not adequately block endosomal NK1R signaling, which sustains pain. Novel endosome-targeted NK1R antagonists represent a promising new approach to overcoming this limitation. === Psychiatric and Neurological Research === [ 1 ] [ 2 ] [ 3 ] [ 4 ] NK1R antagonists have shown antidepressant and anxiolytic effects in preclinical models, and early clinical trials of the NK1R antagonist MK-869 showed promising antidepressant efficacy. However, subsequent larger trials failed to confirm these findings. Research continues into the role of substance P in PTSD, anxiety disorders, and substance abuse.
keyPoint: moderate.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high

Citation quality grade A, Strong human evidence.
  *: PeptideJournal: In 1931, two scientists in a London laboratory discovered a mysterious powder that caused intestinal tissue to contract. They called it "substance P"-the "P" standing for the powdered preparation they'd isolated. Substance P represents one of the most extensively studied neuropeptides in biomedical research. Discovered in 1931 and structurally characterized in 1971, this 11-amino-acid peptide has proven to be a versatile signaling molecule with roles spanning pain transmission, inflammation, emesis, mood regulation, and even cancer biology. The clinical success of NK1 receptor antagonists as antiemetics demonstrates that blocking substance P can provide meaningful therapeutic benefit. Aprepitant and related drugs have improved quality of life for millions of chemotherapy patients by preventing nausea and vomiting-one of the most dreaded side effects of cancer treatment. However, substance P research also illustrates how biological complexity can confound efforts to translate mechanism into therapy.

### compound | sulanemadlin/overview | What is Sulanemadlin?
kind: overview
title: Sulanemadlin
summary: First-in-class stapled alpha-helical peptide and dual MDM2/MDMX inhibitor that reactivates wild-type p53 tumor suppressor function. Phase 1/2 trials demonstrated 59% disease control rate with notably low hematologic toxicity compared to MDM2-only inhibitors. Novel chemoprotection application being developed for retinoblastoma with Advancium Biosciences partnership.
keyPoint: First-in-class stapled alpha-helical peptide and dual MDM2/MDMX inhibitor that reactivates wild-type p53 tumor suppressor function.

kind: overview
title: Super Human Blend (SHB)
summary: The Super Human Blend (product code SHB) is a comprehensive amino acid injection built for performance, recovery, and circulation, combining nine amino acids into a single administration. It is an amino acid blend rather than a peptide, working through nutritional and metabolic support, and given as a fixed direct dose with no titration. Each milliliter contains L-Arginine 110mg, L-Ornithine 110mg, L-Citrulline 120mg, L-Lysine 70mg, L-Glutamine 40mg, L-Proline 60mg, L-Taurine 60mg, L-Carnitine 220mg, and NAC 75mg. Arginine, ornithine, and citrulline form a nitric oxide and growth hormone support axis that improves blood flow and recovery, lysine and proline support collagen and connective tissue, glutamine supports recovery and gut health, taurine supports cellular hydration and cardiovascular function, carnitine supports fat metabolism and energy, and NAC provides antioxidant and glutathione precursor support.

### compound | supershredlc553/mechanism | How does Super Shred (LC553) work?
kind: overview
title: Super Shred (LC553)
summary: Super Shred (product code LC553) is an advanced thermogenic fat-loss injection that pairs a strong lipotropic and cellular-energy base with albuterol, a beta-agonist bronchodilator used off-label for its fat-mobilizing and metabolic-rate effects. It is a vitamin, amino, and pharmaceutical blend rather than a peptide, delivered as a fixed direct dose with no titration. Each milliliter contains L-Carnitine 400mg, a MIC blend at 100mg, ATP 50mg, Albuterol 2mg, and B12 (Methylcobalamin) 1mg. The very high carnitine dose plus MIC base provides potent lipotropic fat transport, ATP supplies cellular energy substrate, B12 supports energy metabolism, and the albuterol adds a thermogenic, metabolism-raising component that distinguishes this as one of the more aggressive blends in the category.

### compound | suprefort/evidence | What research is listed for Suprefort?
kind: evidence
title: Suprefort: research listed by the sources
summary: Suprefort is generally described as well tolerated in manufacturer and Russian-practice reports, but this reflects the absence of rigorous controlled safety data rather than proof of safety; the side-effect profile in humans is not well characterized [8].; Hypersensitivity/allergy is the most plausible adverse effect: the product is derived from animal (bovine) pancreatic tissue and capsules contain excipients such as lactose, gelatin, beetroot sugar, starch and Tween-80, any of which can trigger allergic or intolerance reactions.; It contains lactose, so people with lactose intolerance may experience digestive upset (bloating, cramping, diarrhea).; As an animal-tissue-derived product, it carries the general theoretical concerns of bovine-origin material; manufacturers state the source tissue is screened young livestock, but independent verification of sourcing and purity is limited.; It is NOT a substitute for prescribed therapy: people with diabetes, chronic pancreatitis, or pancreatic enzyme insufficiency should not replace insulin, antidiabetic drugs, or pancreatic enzyme Peptide University labels its records as aggregated from empirical research and anecdotal community data. This record is retained as supplied and is not upgraded to clinical evidence.

section: Limitations
  -: The source does not clearly state the study population or design in PEARL's reviewed record.
  -: Suprefort (Pancreas Cytomax A-1) is a natural peptide bioregulator from Professor Vladimir Khavinson's St. Petersburg school of "cytomax" preparations: a low-molecular-weight peptide complex (standardized as "peptide complex A-1") extracted from the pancreas of young animals and marketed as a pancreas-supporting
  -: Insulin-dependent Type 1 diabetes mellitus without medical supervision - pancreatic bioregulator activity in the context of autoimmune beta cell destruction and exogenous insulin therapy requires physician oversight for the same reasons as Pancragen.
  -: Concurrent insulin therapy - Suprefort's beta cell normalizing effects combined with exogenous insulin creates additive hypoglycemia risk; blood glucose monitoring and potential insulin dose adjustment required.
  -: Concurrent sulfonylurea therapy - additive insulin secretagogue effect increases hypoglycemia risk; blood glucose monitoring required.
  -: Acute pancreatitis or active chronic pancreatitis flare - bioregulator activity during acute inflammatory pancreatic injury has not been characterized; acute management takes priority.
  -: Pancreatic malignancy - pancreatic cell gene program normalization in the context of pancreatic cancer has not been evaluated.
  -: Known hypersensitivity to Suprefort (pancreatic tissue cytomedin peptide complex A-1) or formulation excipients including gelatin.
  -: Pregnancy - pancreatic insulin regulation changes substantially during pregnancy; exogenous pancreatic bioregulator activity has not been evaluated in this context.
  -: Post-total pancreatectomy - with surgically absent pancreatic tissue, Suprefort has no viable target cells and no mechanism of action.
  *: Source rating: 1 out of 5, very limited evidence

### compound | survodutide/evidence | What research is listed for Survodutide?
kind: evidence
title: Survodutide: research listed by the sources
summary: High evidence; 16 human studies listed Gastrointestinal events were the most common adverse events in the Phase 2 obesity trial, with nausea reported in 47-57% of active-arm participants, vomiting in 21-30% and diarrhea in 22-27%. Most events were mild-to-moderate; discontinuation for GI adverse events occurred in approximately 18% on 4.8 mg, higher than seen with pure GLP-1 agonists [1].; Heart-rate elevation of 4-10 beats per minute on average was observed, somewhat higher than seen with semaglutide but consistent with the glucagon-receptor component. No clinically meaningful arrhythmia signals were identified.; Fasting plasma glucose increased transiently by 5-10 mg/dL in non-diabetic participants during early titration before reverting toward baseline - a recognized class effect of glucagon-receptor agonism that resolves with continued dosing.; Injection-site reactions (mild erythema, induration) occurred in approximately 7-10% of participants.

  *: PeptideDeck: Significant body weight loss (up to 18.7% in Phase 2 trials) Dramatic reduction in liver fat content in MASH patients Enhanced energy expenditure through glucagon receptor activation Improved glycemic control and insulin sensitivity Histological improvement and MASH resolution in clinical studies Reduction in liver fibrosis markers Favorable lipid profile improvements Once-weekly subcutaneous administration Survodutide has progressed through a robust clinical development program, with particularly impressive results in two pivotal areas: obesity and MASH. The data from Phase 2 trials provided the foundation for the ongoing Phase 3 SYNCHRONIZE program. The Phase 2 dose-ranging trial enrolled adults with obesity (BMI ≥30) or overweight (BMI ≥27 with comorbidities) without diabetes. Participants were randomized to survodutide at escalating doses (0.6 mg, 2.4 mg, 3.6 mg, or 4.8 mg) or placebo for 46 weeks.
  *: PeptideDeck: The clinical trial data reveals significant differences in weight loss efficacy between these two investigational drugs. View All sexual health comparisons

### compound | svetinorm/overview | What is Svetinorm?
kind: overview
title: Svetinorm
summary: A cytamin-class peptide supplement derived from liver tissue, part of the Russian bioregulator framework. Marketed as an oral supplement for liver health support. Contains peptide complexes rather than defined sequences. No Western clinical validation.
keyPoint: A cytamin-class peptide supplement derived from liver tissue, part of the Russian bioregulator framework.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: Svetinorm
  connectedTo: Svetinorm
section: Why it is researched
  -: A cytamin-class peptide supplement derived from liver tissue, part of the Russian bioregulator framework.
section: How it works in the research
  -: Svetinorm is a cytamin: a natural peptide bioregulator obtained by patented extraction of short polypeptide fractions from the livers of young calves and pigs, then purified and formulated as enteric capsules.
section: Evidence strength
  -: PeptideDosage.org: Systematic review or meta-analysis; population: Animal; Preclinical animal evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Main limitations
  -: Svetinorm (also sold as Liver Cytomax A-7) is a natural liver peptide bioregulator from the Khavinson cytamin family: a tissue-specific complex of short peptides and free amino acids extracted from the livers of young calves and pigs at the St. Petersburg Institute of Bioregulation and Gerontology [1][2].

### compound | svetinorm/evidence | What research is listed for Svetinorm?
kind: evidence
title: Svetinorm: research listed by the sources
summary: Across decades of use in Russia, Khavinson cytamins including liver preparations are described as well tolerated with no serious adverse events reported, but there is no FDA-grade toxicology dossier, GLP safety pharmacology, or controlled drug-interaction data to back that claim [4][5].; Svetinorm is an animal-tissue product (peptides extracted from calf and pig liver); people with bovine or porcine protein allergy should avoid it, and anyone uneasy about animal-sourced tissue extracts should note this origin [8].; Mild, transient gastrointestinal symptoms such as nausea or bloating can occur with oral peptide-complex capsules and are the most commonly mentioned tolerability issue.; Because the proposed mechanism is pro-proliferative gene modulation, use is theoretically inadvisable in active hepatic malignancy or other proliferative liver disease without specialist oversight.; The product has not been studied in pregnancy, lactation, or pediatric populations, and standard bioregulator guidance excludes these groups.; The subcutaneous route shown here is illustrative only; Svetinorm Peptide University labels its records as aggregated from empirical research and anecdotal community data. This record is retained as supplied and is not upgraded to clinical evidence.

section: Limitations
  -: The source does not clearly state the study population or design in PEARL's reviewed record.
  -: Svetinorm (also sold as Liver Cytomax A-7) is a natural liver peptide bioregulator from the Khavinson cytamin family: a tissue-specific complex of short peptides and free amino acids extracted from the livers of young calves and pigs at the St. Petersburg Institute of Bioregulation and Gerontology [1][2].
  -: Active viral hepatitis with significant liver fibrosis (Metavir F3-F4) - hepatocyte bioregulator activity during active viral hepatic inflammation and injury in the context of severe fibrosis has not been characterized.
  -: Decompensated cirrhosis (Child-Pugh B or C) - insufficient viable hepatocyte mass for meaningful bioregulator response; the coagulopathy and portal hypertension of decompensated cirrhosis create an unfavorable context.
  -: Hepatocellular carcinoma or active hepatic malignancy - hepatocyte survival and gene program normalization in malignant hepatocytes has not been evaluated.
  -: Active drug-induced liver injury (DILI) - concurrent bioregulator activity during active toxic hepatocyte injury has not been evaluated; the causative drug should be discontinued first.
  -: Known hypersensitivity to Svetinorm (liver tissue cytomedin peptide complex A-7) or formulation excipients including gelatin.
  -: Pregnancy - hepatic metabolic reprogramming during pregnancy involves substantial changes to lipid metabolism, bile acid metabolism, and hepatic blood flow; exogenous hepatic bioregulator activity has not been evaluated in this context.
  -: Active alcohol use disorder with ongoing consumption - ongoing hepatocyte injury from active alcohol consumption creates a futile cycle; sobriety is a prerequisite.
  -: Recent liver transplantation on immunosuppression - hepatocyte bioregulator activity in immunosuppressed recipients with donor hepatocytes requires hepatology supervision.
  *: Source rating: 1 out of 5, very limited evidence
  *: PeptideDosage.org: Across decades of use in Russia, Khavinson cytamins including liver preparations are described as well tolerated with no serious adverse events reported, but there is no FDA-grade toxicology dossier, GLP safety pharmacology, or controlled drug-interaction data to back that claim [4][5].; Svetinorm is an animal-tissue product (peptides extracted from calf and pig liver); people with bovine or porcine protein allergy should avoid it, and anyone uneasy about animal-sourced tissue extracts should note this origin [8].; Mild, transient gastrointestinal symptoms such as nausea or bloating can occur with oral peptide-complex capsules and are the most commonly mentioned tolerability issue.; Because the proposed mechanism is pro-proliferative gene modulation, use is theoretically inadvisable in active hepatic malignancy or other proliferative liver disease without specialist oversight.; The product has not been studied in pregnancy, lactation, or pediatric populations, and standard bioregulator guidance excludes these groups.; The subcutaneous route shown here is illustrative only; Svetinorm

### compound | synake/overview | What is Syn-Ake?
kind: overview
title: Syn-Ake
summary: Syn-Ake (INCI: Dipeptide Diaminobutyroyl Benzylamide Diacetate; CAS 823202-99-9) is a synthetic cosmetic anti-wrinkle peptide, a small beta-Ala-Pro-Dab-benzylamide molecule engineered by Pentapharm (now DSM-firmenich) to mimic Waglerin-1, a 22-amino-acid neurotoxin from the venom of the temple viper (Tropidolaemus wagleri) [2][3]. Like its venom template, it behaves as a reversible competitive antagonist at the muscle-type nicotinic acetylcholine receptor (mnAChR), dampening acetylcholine-driven contraction of the facial mimic muscles so expression lines such as crow's feet and forehead and glabellar creases appear softened, a topical "Botox-like" effect [1][4]. The real-world Syn-Ake dosage is a topical concentration rather than an injected amount: roughly 1-4% of the trade solution in a serum or cream applied once or twice daily, with manufacturer trials using 4% twice daily for four weeks [7].

### compound | synake/evidence | What research is listed for Syn-Ake?
kind: evidence
title: Syn-Ake: research listed by the sources
summary: Applied topically at cosmetic concentrations, Syn-Ake is generally well tolerated; the most common issues are mild, transient local reactions at the application site - redness, stinging, tingling, itching, or dryness - which are often driven by the overall formulation rather than the peptide alone.; Irritant or allergic contact dermatitis is possible to the peptide or to co-formulated ingredients (preservatives, fragrance, solvents); a patch test on the inner forearm before facial use is advisable, especially for sensitive or reactive skin.; Avoid contact with the eyes, mucous membranes, and broken or inflamed skin; because crow's-feet application is near the eye, keep product off the lash line and rinse if accidental eye contact occurs.; At cosmetic topical concentrations no meaningful systemic absorption or systemic neuromuscular effect is expected; however, the parent venom peptide (Waglerin-1) is systemically lethal, so the educational subcutaneous reconstitution model on this page must NOT be taken literally - Syn-Ake is not a validated injectable and should not be injected.; Pentapharm's original research demonstrated that SYN-AKE reduces the frequency of contraction in cultured human muscle cells by up to 82% at 4% concentration. The peptide showed selectivity for the muscular nicotinic acetylcholine receptor subtype, consistent with the known pharmacology of its parent toxin Waglerin-1. A manufacturer-sponsored clinical study involving 45 female volunteers aged 40-65 showed: 52% reduction in forehead wrinkle depth after 28 days of twice-daily application Statistically significant improvements in skin roughness parameters High subject satisfaction scores for wrinkle reduction and skin smoothness In vitro comparisons with other muscle-relaxing peptides have positioned SYN-AKE as one of the most potent topical neuromuscular-acting cosmetic ingredients, with muscle relaxation effects exceeding those of Argireline and Leuphasyl at equivalent concentrations.   *: WikiPep: Pentapharm's original research demonstrated that SYN-AKE reduces the frequency of contraction in cultured human muscle cells by up to 82% at 4% concentration. The peptide showed selectivity for the muscular nicotinic acetylcholine receptor subtype, consistent with the known pharmacology of its parent toxin Waglerin-1. A manufacturer-sponsored clinical study involving 45 female volunteers aged 40-65 showed: 52% reduction in forehead wrinkle depth after 28 days of twice-daily application Statistically significant improvements in skin roughness parameters High subject satisfaction scores for wrinkle reduction and skin smoothness In vitro comparisons with other muscle-relaxing peptides have positioned SYN-AKE as one of the most potent topical neuromuscular-acting cosmetic ingredients, with muscle relaxation effects exceeding those of Argireline and Leuphasyl at equivalent concentrations. Marketing leans on the venom-mimetic story; effect size is modest. Human evidence grade D, Animal/cell evidence only. Citation quality grade D, Animal/cell evidence only.
  *: PeptideJournal: The idea of applying snake venom to your face sounds like something from a dubious beauty hack list. But here's what's actually happening: Syn-Ake is a synthetic tripeptide that mimics a specific component of Temple Viper venom-one that temporarily blocks nerve signals to facial muscles. Syn-Ake is a synthetic peptide that mimics the neuromuscular blocking action of waglerin-1, a component of Temple Viper venom. It works by antagonizing nicotinic acetylcholine receptors on facial muscles, temporarily reducing muscle contraction and smoothing expression lines. Clinical studies show that 4% Syn-Ake applied twice daily can reduce wrinkle depth by 10-52% over four weeks, with results varying by individual. The peptide is safe at cosmetic concentrations, with minimal risk of irritation and no documented systemic toxicity. It's a viable option for people seeking a non-invasive alternative to Botox, though it's slower and less dramatic. Best results come from consistent, long-term use on moderate expression lines.

### compound | ta1ll37thymulinblend/overview | What is Deep Immune?
kind: overview
title: Deep Immune
summary: Deep Immune is a systemic immune restoration blend combining Thymosin Alpha-1, LL-37, and Thymulin into a single coordinated immune-support platform. The blend is structured around a 6mg Thymosin Alpha-1, 3mg LL-37, and 2mg Thymulin ratio, creating an 11mg total vial with a 3:1.5:1 composition. Thymosin Alpha-1 provides the adaptive immune orchestration layer through dendritic cell maturation, MHC class I upregulation, NK cell cytotoxicity support, CD4:CD8 ratio normalization, and Th1 balance restoration. LL-37 adds innate antimicrobial defense through broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity, biofilm disruption, and neutrophil and monocyte recruitment. Thymulin provides the thymic restoration layer by supporting final T-lymphocyte precursor differentiation into competent immunocompetent T-cells.
keyPoint: Deep Immune is a systemic immune restoration blend combining Thymosin Alpha-1, LL-37, and Thymulin into a single coordinated immune-support platform.

### compound | tabimorelin/overview | What is Tabimorelin?
kind: overview
title: Tabimorelin
summary: Tabimorelin (NN703) is an orally active, ipamorelin-derived ghrelin / growth hormone secretagogue receptor (GHS-R1a) agonist developed by Novo Nordisk in the late 1990s and early 2000s [5][7]. As a small peptidomimetic engineered to survive the gut, it mimics endogenous ghrelin to drive pulsatile growth hormone (GH) release, with downstream rises in IGF-1 and IGFBP-3 [1][2]. The studied Tabimorelin dosage came entirely from clinical trials: single oral doses of 0.05-12 mg/kg and once-daily 7-day courses of about 1.5-6.86 mg/kg/day, which for a typical adult is roughly 100-840 mg per day [1][2][3]. GH and IGF-1 rose dose-dependently in healthy volunteers, but the compound disappointed in its target population: only about 11% of growth-hormone-deficient adults reached a clinically meaningful peak GH response, GH output fell from day 1 to day 7 (tachyphylaxis), and tabimorelin proved to be a mechanism-based CYP3A4 inhibitor that increased midazolam exposure by up to 93% [2][3][4].
keyPoint: Tabimorelin (NN703) is an orally active, ipamorelin-derived ghrelin / growth hormone secretagogue receptor (GHS-R1a) agonist developed by Novo Nordisk in the late 1990s and early 2000s [5][7].

### compound | tabimorelin/evidence | What research is listed for Tabimorelin?
kind: evidence
title: Tabimorelin: research listed by the sources
summary: GHS-R1a activation is not fully GH-specific: at doses above ~3 mg/kg, single-dose studies recorded transient individual increases in ACTH, cortisol, and prolactin, reflecting off-target pituitary stimulation [1].; Tabimorelin is a mechanism-based CYP3A4 inhibitor and raised exposure to the test substrate midazolam by up to 93%; in practice this means a high potential for serious interactions with the many drugs metabolized by CYP3A4 (statins, benzodiazepines, certain immunosuppressants, some antiarrhythmics, and others) [4].; Because it inhibits its own metabolism, repeated daily dosing can lead to drug accumulation and a progressively longer effective half-life, complicating dose titration [1][4].; GH responsiveness diminished over a week of dosing (tachyphylaxis), so sustained efficacy was not maintained [2].; As a ghrelin-receptor agonist it would be expected to stimulate appetite and may cause gastrointestinal symptoms; sustained GH/IGF-1 elevation from GH secretagogues as a class is associated with fluid retention, peripheral edema, arthralgia, and reduced insulin sensitivity /

### compound | taxorest/overview | What is Taxorest?
kind: overview
title: Taxorest
summary: Taxorest (bronchial Cytomax A-19) is a natural peptide bioregulator in Vladimir Khavinson's Cytomax line, a concentrated complex of low-molecular-weight peptides extracted from the bronchial mucosa of young animals and sold in 10 mg capsules for the bronchopulmonary system. Like the rest of the Khavinson tissue-specific peptide program, it is hypothesized to act as an epigenetic regulator that restores gene expression and protein synthesis in bronchial epithelial cells, normalizing ciliated-cell architecture, secretory IgA, and the pro-inflammatory cytokine balance [1][2]. Its synthetic tetrapeptide counterpart, Bronchogen (Ala-Glu-Asp-Leu), is the form used in most peer-reviewed laboratory work on chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and bronchial remodeling [1][3]. The headline Taxorest dosage is 20 mg per day (two capsules) taken before meals for a 10- to 30-day course and repeated every 3-6 months, with a practical range of 10-40 mg/day.

### compound | taxorest/mechanism | How does Taxorest work?
kind: overview
title: Taxorest
summary: Taxorest (bronchial Cytomax A-19) is a natural peptide bioregulator in Vladimir Khavinson's Cytomax line, a concentrated complex of low-molecular-weight peptides extracted from the bronchial mucosa of young animals and sold in 10 mg capsules for the bronchopulmonary system. Like the rest of the Khavinson tissue-specific peptide program, it is hypothesized to act as an epigenetic regulator that restores gene expression and protein synthesis in bronchial epithelial cells, normalizing ciliated-cell architecture, secretory IgA, and the pro-inflammatory cytokine balance [1][2]. Its synthetic tetrapeptide counterpart, Bronchogen (Ala-Glu-Asp-Leu), is the form used in most peer-reviewed laboratory work on chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and bronchial remodeling [1][3]. The headline Taxorest dosage is 20 mg per day (two capsules) taken before meals for a 10- to 30-day course and repeated every 3-6 months, with a practical range of 10-40 mg/day.

### compound | taxorest/safety | What are the risks of Taxorest?
kind: safety
title: Taxorest: source-listed risks
summary: Source-listed risks only. Missing human safety data does not mean a compound is safe.
keyPoint: Source-listed risks only.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: Taxorest
  connectedTo: Taxorest
  *: Mild increased mucus production in first cycle days - as mucociliary clearance normalizes and bronchial secretory activity is restored, some subjects note mildly increased mucus production or productive cough in the first 3-7 days; reflects restoration of normal airway clearance; typically resolves as normalization. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Mild throat clearing or cough on initiation - related to the increased mucociliary activity described above; not pathological. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Mild fatigue on initial days - uncommon; related to bronchial tissue repair gene program activation; typically resolves within 3-5 days. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Mild gastrointestinal discomfort from oral capsule - as a before-meals oral cytomedin; occasional mild gastric discomfort in first days. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Allergic reactions to gelatin or lactose - subjects with known gelatin or lactose sensitivity should note these as potential capsule excipient reactions. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Potential mild bronchospasm (rare) - a small minority of subjects with pre-existing bronchial hyperreactivity may experience mild transient bronchospasm as bronchial epithelial activity changes in the first days; typically resolves; subjects with asthma should initiate at lower dose and monitor closely. [source-listed source severity]
  *: No serious pulmonary adverse events documented in the Khavinson research literature - Taxorest's safety profile in COPD, chronic bronchitis, and aging respiratory decline populations is clean. [source-listed source severity]

### compound | taxorest/evidence | What research is listed for Taxorest?
kind: evidence
title: Taxorest: research listed by the sources
summary: Manufacturer and Russian-language sources describe Taxorest as well tolerated, with the principal documented contraindications being individual hypersensitivity to the peptide complex, pregnancy, and breastfeeding.; As an oral capsule, the most plausible adverse effects are mild gastrointestinal upset (nausea, fullness) and, rarely, allergic or hypersensitivity reactions to the peptide fractions or capsule excipients.; Because the peptides are extracted from animal (bovine) bronchial tissue, there is a theoretical, unquantified concern about animal-sourced biologic material; product quality and purity vary by supplier and are not subject to pharmaceutical-grade regulatory oversight.; Independent human safety, toxicology, and long-term data are essentially absent, and the proposed broad gene-expression modulation has not been characterized for off-target effects on tissues other than the bronchopulmonary system.; Use in pregnancy, lactation, children, and in patients with active or treated malignancy has not been studied and is generally discouraged.; Drug-interaction data are Peptide University labels its records as aggregated from empirical research and anecdotal community data. This record is retained as supplied and is not upgraded to clinical evidence.

section: What the research shows
  -: PeptideDosage.org: Taxorest (bronchial Cytomax A-19) is a natural peptide bioregulator in Vladimir Khavinson's Cytomax line, a concentrated complex of low-molecular-weight peptides extracted from the bronchial mucosa of young animals and sold in 10 mg capsules for the bronchopulmonary system.
  -: Peptide University Codex: Taxorest is a Khavinson cytomedin - peptide complex A-19 - extracted from the bronchial mucosal tissue of young animals, developed as the oral bronchopulmonary bioregulator of the Khavinson framework and the commercial cytomedin counterpart to Bronchogen (the injectable synthetic tetrapeptide Ala-Glu-Asp-Leu).
section: Evidence strength
  -: PeptideDosage.org: Systematic review or meta-analysis; population: Animal; Preclinical animal evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: Peptide University Codex: Source summary; study design not clearly stated; population: Animal; Preclinical animal evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Limitations
  -: Taxorest (bronchial Cytomax A-19) is a natural peptide bioregulator in Vladimir Khavinson's Cytomax line, a concentrated complex of low-molecular-weight peptides extracted from the bronchial mucosa of young animals and sold in 10 mg capsules for the bronchopulmonary system.
  -: Active pulmonary malignancy - bronchial epithelial cell gene program normalization in the context of malignant bronchial or alveolar cells has not been characterized; oncological evaluation required.
  -: Active pulmonary tuberculosis - bronchial bioregulator activity during active mycobacterial infection has not been characterized; antitubercular therapy takes priority.
  -: Severe active asthma exacerbation - Taxorest is a chronic regenerative bioregulator, not an acute bronchodilator; acute asthmatic bronchoconstriction requires emergency bronchodilator management.
  -: Known hypersensitivity to Taxorest (bronchial mucosal tissue cytomedin peptide complex A-19) or formulation excipients including gelatin or lactose.
  -: Pregnancy - respiratory epithelial bioregulator activity during pregnancy has not been characterized.
  -: Recent lung transplantation - bronchial epithelial bioregulator activity in immunosuppressed transplant recipients with donor airway epithelium requires transplant pulmonology supervision.
  -: Acute respiratory failure requiring ventilatory support - Taxorest is not an acute intervention for active respiratory decompensation.
  *: Source rating: 1 out of 5, very limited evidence

### compound | tb500bpc157/overview | What is TB-500 + BPC-157?
kind: overview
title: TB-500 + BPC-157
summary: The TB-500 and BPC-157 stack is the most widely studied combination protocol in unregulated peptide research, pairing two regenerative peptides with distinct loading and maintenance dosing schedules designed to match the very different pharmacokinetic profiles of the two molecules and the different tissue compartments their mechanisms address [1][2][3]. TB-500 (the active fragment of thymosin beta-4) has a plasma half-life of approximately 2 hours but durable tissue incorporation that supports twice-weekly dosing during loading and once-weekly maintenance [4][5]. BPC-157 (the gastric pentadecapeptide originally isolated by Sikiric and colleagues) is unusually stable in serum and gastric juice and is typically given as small daily injections to maintain steady angiogenic and growth factor signaling at the site of injury throughout the cycle [6][7]. Goldstein, Crockford, Sikiric, Chang, and colleagues provide the preclinical evidence base for each component [4][5][6][8].

### compound | tb500bpc157/evidence | What research is listed for TB-500 + BPC-157?
kind: evidence
title: TB-500 + BPC-157: research listed by the sources
summary: Loading-phase tolerability is typically the most challenging period; injection site reactions are most common during the first 1 to 2 weeks while injection technique is being refined, and rotating injection sites between abdomen, thigh, and gluteal regions helps minimize local discomfort.; Transient fatigue, mild lethargy, and flu-like symptoms have been described anecdotally during the first 3 to 7 days of loading, possibly reflecting initial immune modulation; most users find these resolve spontaneously without dose adjustment.; Maintenance-phase tolerability is usually excellent because weekly TB-500 spacing eliminates the cumulative injection burden of loading; BPC-157 daily dosing remains the principal source of injection site reactions during maintenance.; Theoretical concerns about angiogenesis-related effects on occult malignancy apply throughout the protocol; both peptides drive vascular and progenitor-cell activity that could theoretically support tumor growth, although no direct clinical evidence has been demonstrated.; WADA prohibition under category S2 applies to both

### compound | teduglutide/overview | What is Teduglutide?
kind: overview
title: Teduglutide
summary: An FDA-approved GLP-2 analog for adults and pediatric patients 1 year of age and older with short bowel syndrome who are dependent on parenteral support. It promotes intestinal adaptation and absorption and can reduce parenteral-support requirements.
keyPoint: An FDA-approved GLP-2 analog for adults and pediatric patients 1 year of age and older with short bowel syndrome who are dependent on parenteral support.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: Teduglutide
  connectedTo: Teduglutide
section: Why it is researched
  -: An FDA-approved GLP-2 analog for adults and pediatric patients 1 year of age and older with short bowel syndrome who are dependent on parenteral support.
section: How it works in the research
  -: Teduglutide is a DPP-4-resistant analog of native GLP-2 (glucagon-like peptide-2), differing from the endogenous 33-amino-acid peptide by a glycine substitution at position 2.
section: Evidence strength
  -: The Peptide Handbook: Randomized or controlled human research; population: Human; Direct controlled human evidence. 18 human studies listed by the source; 45 animal studies listed by the source
section: Main limitations
  -: Acceleration of neoplastic growth and gastrointestinal polyps - GATTEX has the potential to cause hyperplastic changes including neoplasia.
  -: Intestinal or stomal obstruction has been reported; temporarily discontinue GATTEX while obstruction is clinically managed.
  -: Biliary and pancreatic disease - cholecystitis, cholangitis, cholelithiasis, and pancreatitis have been reported; bilirubin, alkaline phosphatase, lipase, and amylase monitoring is recommended before treatment and at least every 6 months during treatment.
  followUp: Show the research evidence for Teduglutide
  followUp: Show the human research studies for Teduglutide

### compound | teduglutide/mechanism | How does Teduglutide work?
kind: overview
title: Teduglutide
summary: An FDA-approved GLP-2 analog for adults and pediatric patients 1 year of age and older with short bowel syndrome who are dependent on parenteral support. It promotes intestinal adaptation and absorption and can reduce parenteral-support requirements.
keyPoint: An FDA-approved GLP-2 analog for adults and pediatric patients 1 year of age and older with short bowel syndrome who are dependent on parenteral support.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: Teduglutide
  connectedTo: Teduglutide
section: Why it is researched
  -: An FDA-approved GLP-2 analog for adults and pediatric patients 1 year of age and older with short bowel syndrome who are dependent on parenteral support.
section: How it works in the research
  -: Teduglutide is a DPP-4-resistant analog of native GLP-2 (glucagon-like peptide-2), differing from the endogenous 33-amino-acid peptide by a glycine substitution at position 2.
section: Evidence strength
  -: The Peptide Handbook: Randomized or controlled human research; population: Human; Direct controlled human evidence. 18 human studies listed by the source; 45 animal studies listed by the source
section: Main limitations
  -: Acceleration of neoplastic growth and gastrointestinal polyps - GATTEX has the potential to cause hyperplastic changes including neoplasia.
  -: Intestinal or stomal obstruction has been reported; temporarily discontinue GATTEX while obstruction is clinically managed.
  -: Biliary and pancreatic disease - cholecystitis, cholangitis, cholelithiasis, and pancreatitis have been reported; bilirubin, alkaline phosphatase, lipase, and amylase monitoring is recommended before treatment and at least every 6 months during treatment.

### compound | teduglutide/evidence | What research is listed for Teduglutide?
kind: evidence
title: Teduglutide: research listed by the sources
summary: strong-human. In the pivotal 24-week randomized study in patients with short bowel syndrome and intestinal failure, 43 patients received teduglutide 0.05 mg/kg/day and 43 received placebo. The primary responder definition was a reduction of at least 20% in weekly parenteral-support volume from baseline at weeks 20 and 24. Responders included 27 of 43 patients (63%) receiving teduglutide and 13 of 43 patients (30%) receiving placebo (P = .002). At week 24, mean reduction in parenteral-support volume was 4.4 ± 3.8 L/week with teduglutide and 2.3 ± 2.7 L/week with placebo. Teduglutide is an established treatment for reducing parenteral-support requirements in SBS patients who are dependent on parenteral support. The most common adverse reactions (incidence 10% or higher) in controlled trials were abdominal pain (~30%), nausea (~23%), upper respiratory tract infection (~21%), abdominal distension (~20%), and injection-site reactions such as pain, swelling, or rash (~13%); vomiting and peripheral edema are also frequent [1].; Acceleration of neoplastic growth is the principal warning: because teduglutide is trophic to the bowel, it may promote growth of existing malignancy.
keyPoint: strong-human.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: Teduglutide
  connectedTo: Teduglutide
section: What the research shows
  -: The Peptide Handbook: An FDA-approved GLP-2 analog for adults and pediatric patients 1 year of age and older with short bowel syndrome who are dependent on parenteral support.
  -: Peptpedia: The only FDA-approved GLP-2 agonist (Gattex), reducing parenteral nutrition needs 20%+ in short bowel syndrome.
  -: PeptideDosage.org: Teduglutide (brand names Gattex in the US and Revestive in the EU) is a recombinant 33-amino-acid analog of human glucagon-like peptide-2 (GLP-2) and a selective GLP-2 receptor agonist developed to treat short bowel syndrome (SBS) in patients who depend on parenteral nutrition or intravenous support.
  -: WikiPep: From Wikipep - The Peptide Encyclopedia Teduglutide Chemical name [Gly²]-GLP-2(1-33) Molecular formula C₁₆₄H₂₅₂N₄₄O₅₅S Molecular weight 3752 g/mol CAS number 197922-42-2 Sequence HGDGSFSDEMNTILDNLAARDFINWLIQTKITD Length 33 amino acids Source Recombinant (E.
section: Evidence strength
  -: The Peptide Handbook: Randomized or controlled human research; population: Human; Direct controlled human evidence. 18 human studies listed by the source; 45 animal studies listed by the source
  -: Peptpedia: Source summary; study design not clearly stated; population: Not clearly stated; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: PeptideDosage.org: Randomized or controlled human research; population: Human; Direct controlled human evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: WikiPep: Human clinical research; population: Human; Human evidence with design limitations to check. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Limitations
  -: Acceleration of neoplastic growth and gastrointestinal polyps - GATTEX has the potential to cause hyperplastic changes including neoplasia.
  -: Intestinal or stomal obstruction has been reported; temporarily discontinue GATTEX while obstruction is clinically managed.
  -: Biliary and pancreatic disease - cholecystitis, cholangitis, cholelithiasis, and pancreatitis have been reported; bilirubin, alkaline phosphatase, lipase, and amylase monitoring is recommended before treatment and at least every 6 months during treatment.
  -: Fluid overload and congestive heart failure can occur due to enhanced fluid absorption; adjust parenteral support and reassess treatment, especially in patients with underlying cardiovascular disease.
  -: Increased absorption of concomitant oral medications can increase exposure; monitor drugs requiring titration or with a narrow therapeutic index for adverse reactions, and a dose reduction may be required.
  -: not demonstrated a definitive increased cancer signal in SBS patients, but the patient population (older, multiple comorbidities) and limited long-term data make definitive conclusions difficult.
  -: not medical advice, and the compounds covered are research chemicals not approved for human use unless explicitly stated otherwise.
  -: The reviewed record does not state a specific limitation. The linked paper still needs to be checked for design, size and bias.
