### compound | urocortini/overview | What is Urocortin I?
kind: overview
title: Urocortin I
summary: From Wikipep - The Peptide Encyclopedia Urocortin I Chemical name Urocortin 1 (Ucn1) Molecular formula C₁₉₈H₃₁₂N₅₈O₅₈S₂ Molecular weight ~4,696 Da CAS number 178636-07-0 Sequence 40 amino acids (human) Length 40 amino acids Source Endogenous (brain, heart, GI tract) Half-life ~10 minutes (estimated, IV) Targets CRF-R1 and CRF-R2 (non-selective CRF agonist) Bioavailability Parenteral administration Legal status Research compound (unscheduled) Urocortin I ( Ucn1 , also Urocortin ) is an endogenous 40-amino acid neuropeptide belonging to the corticotropin-releasing factor (CRF) family , which includes CRF (CRH), urocortin I, Urocortin II (Ucn2), and urocortin III (Ucn3). Discovered in 1995 by Vaughan and colleagues at the Salk Institute, urocortin I was isolated from the rat midbrain Edinger-Westphal nucleus and represents the first CRF-related peptide identified outside the classic hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis.

A randomized trial in middle-aged adults reported selected muscle strength, exercise-performance, and mitochondrial-biomarker outcomes. These findings do not establish disease prevention, general clinical treatment efficacy, or longer human lifespan.

  -: The Peptide Handbook: Native arginine vasopressin with VASOSTRICT label-scoped U.S.
  -: Peptide Hub: Vasopressin (also called arginine vasopressin, AVP, or antidiuretic hormone, ADH) is a 9-amino acid neuropeptide produced in the supraoptic and paraventricular nuclei of the hypothalamus and secreted by the posterior pituitary gland.
  -: WikiPep: From Wikipep - The Peptide Encyclopedia Vasopressin Chemical name Arginine vasopressin (AVP); Argipressin; Antidiuretic hormone (ADH) Molecular formula C₄₆H₆₅N₁₅O₁₂S₂ Molecular weight 1084.2 g/mol CAS number 11000-17-2 Sequence Cys-Tyr-Phe-Gln-Asn-Cys-Pro-Arg-Gly-NH₂ (disulfide bridge: Cys¹-Cys⁶) Length 9 amino acids...
  -: Peptide Authority: A hormone essential for water balance and blood pressure regulation, also involved in social behavior and stress responses.

  -: Peptide Hub: Source summary; study design not clearly stated; population: Not clearly stated; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: WikiPep: Randomized or controlled human research; population: Human; Direct controlled human evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.

section: Limitations
  -: The reviewed record is animal research and cannot establish human effectiveness or safety.
  -: This is a commercial educational source. Its uncited figures and modelled outputs must remain labelled as source-listed rather than clinical evidence.
  -: The reviewed record does not state a specific limitation. The linked paper still needs to be checked for design, size and bias.
  -: Whether a grey-market nasal-vasopressin product contains the labelled compound at the labelled concentration.
  -: Whether off-label cognitive-enhancement use is safe long-term.
  -: Cognitive-enhancement RCTs in healthy adults are limited; replication poor.
  *: Source rating: 5 out of 5
  *: The Peptide Handbook: strong-human. Route, preparation, dosing, warnings, safety, and storage are label-specific. This record does not include generic diabetes-insipidus approval, intranasal, cognitive, desmopressin, WADA, or universal half-life claims.
  *: Peptide Hub: Protocol-focused educational summary. Linked papers, site-listed ranges and commercial context are retained with source attribution.
  *: WikiPep: The landmark Vasopressin and Septic Shock Trial (VASST) randomized 778 patients with septic shock to receive low-dose vasopressin (0.01-0.03 units/min) versus norepinephrine in addition to open-label vasopressors. While there was no significant difference in 28-day mortality overall (35.4% vs 39.3%, p=0.26), a pre-specified subgroup analysis showed that vasopressin reduced mortality in patients with less severe septic shock (norepinephrine dose 5-14 mcg/min at randomization): 26.5% vs 35.7% (p=0.05). The VANISH trial compared early vasopressin with norepinephrine as the first-line vasopressor in septic shock. Vasopressin did not improve kidney failure-free days (the primary endpoint) but was associated with a reduced need for renal replacement therapy, suggesting a potential renal-protective effect mediated through V1a-mediated efferent arteriolar constriction improving glomerular filtration.
  *: Peptide Authority: Strong human evidence Endogenous hormone. Synthetic analogues (vasopressin itself for vasopressor / GI bleeding use; desmopressin for diabetes insipidus and nocturnal enuresis) are UK prescription-only medicines. Prohibited under WADA S5 (diuretics / masking agents). Human evidence grade A, Strong human evidence. Citation quality grade A, Strong human evidence.

### compound | vasostatin/overview | What is Vasostatin?
kind: overview
title: Vasostatin
summary: From Wikipep - The Peptide Encyclopedia Vasostatin Chemical name Chromogranin A (1-76) Fragment Molecular formula Large polypeptide Molecular weight ~8,600 Da CAS number N/A (endogenous fragment) Sequence N-terminal 76 amino acids of CgA Length 76 amino acids Source Endogenous (chromogranin A cleavage) Half-life 15-30 minutes (estimated) Targets Endothelial cells, cardiomyocytes, smooth muscle Bioavailability Requires parenteral administration Legal status Research compound (unscheduled) Vasostatin (also designated vasostatin-1 or CgA₁₋₇₆ ) is a 76-amino acid bioactive peptide derived from the N-terminal region of Chromogranin A (CgA), a 439-amino acid acidic glycoprotein stored in secretory granules of neuroendocrine, endocrine, and neuronal cells. Vasostatin is generated through proteolytic processing of CgA by prohormone convertases and other endopeptidases within the regulated secretory pathway.

### compound | ventfort/evidence | What research is listed for Ventfort?
kind: evidence
title: Ventfort: research listed by the sources
summary: Manufacturer and reseller materials report Ventfort to be well tolerated with no characteristic toxic or allergic effects in their own data; however, this safety claim comes from the producer rather than from independent pharmacovigilance, so the real adverse-effect profile is poorly defined [3].; Because it is an animal-tissue extract (calf vascular tissue), allergic or hypersensitivity reactions are possible, particularly in people with known sensitivity to bovine proteins.; The capsule excipients (lactose, beet sugar/sucrose, starch, microcrystalline cellulose) are relevant to people with lactose intolerance or those managing carbohydrate and sugar intake.; Human pharmacokinetics, long-term safety, drug interactions, and carcinogenicity have not been formally studied; theoretical concerns about stimulating cell proliferation (for example endothelial Ki-67/MKI67) in people with active cancer or proliferative vascular disease cannot be excluded.; There are no established safety data in pregnancy, breastfeeding, or in children, and these groups should avoid it.; The subcutaneous Peptide University labels its records as aggregated from empirical research and anecdotal community data. This record is retained as supplied and is not upgraded to clinical evidence.

section: Evidence strength
  -: PepCodex: Source summary; study design not clearly stated; population: Not clearly stated; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.

section: Limitations
  -: The source does not clearly state the study population or design in PEARL's reviewed record.
  -: Ventfort is an oral Khavinson vascular peptide bioregulator, a "Cytomax" tissue complex (peptide complex A-3) extracted from the blood-vessel tissue of young calves at the St. Petersburg Institute of Bioregulation and Gerontology.
  -: Active vasculitis requiring immunosuppressive management - endothelial gene program normalization during active inflammatory vascular injury has not been characterized.
  -: Recent vascular surgery or endovascular intervention within 4 weeks - the acute endothelial healing phase post-intervention involves specific pro-healing programs; exogenous bioregulator activity during this window has not been evaluated.
  -: Known hypersensitivity to Ventfort (vascular tissue cytomedin peptide complex A-3) or formulation excipients including gelatin.
  -: Pregnancy - vascular remodeling during pregnancy (placental angiogenesis, uterine artery remodeling, 50% increase in blood volume) is tightly regulated; exogenous vascular endothelial bioregulator activity has not been evaluated in this context.
  -: Active anticoagulation with narrow therapeutic window (warfarin) - Ventfort's normalization of endothelial coagulation regulation (thrombomodulin, tPA, vWF) could produce modest coagulation parameter changes; INR monitoring is prudent during the first Ventfort course in anticoagulated subjects.
  -: Severe active infection with vascular involvement - septic emboli, endovascular infection; endothelial immune modulation during active vascular infection has not been characterized.
  -: Severe decompensated heart failure - in the context of severely reduced cardiac output and systemic congestion, vascular endothelial remodeling has not been evaluated; stabilization before initiating Ventfort is appropriate.

### compound | vesugen/overview | What is Vesugen?
kind: overview
title: Vesugen
summary: A synthetic tripeptide (Lys-Glu-Asp) developed by Russian scientist Vladimir Khavinson, claimed to support vascular health by modulating endothelial gene expression. The only published primary research is Russian in-vitro work on cultured endothelium. No animal vascular studies, no human clinical validation, and no regulatory approval anywhere.

### compound | vesugen/evidence | What research is listed for Vesugen?
kind: evidence
title: Vesugen: research listed by the sources
summary: Vesugen is generally well tolerated in Russian observational use; reported adverse effects are infrequent and mild.; The most common reported effect is transient injection-site discomfort with subcutaneous administration.; Occasional mild gastrointestinal upset (nausea, loose stools) has been reported with oral capsule formulations.; Theoretical hypotensive effects on initial dosing have been reported anecdotally in users with pre-existing low blood pressure, possibly reflecting reduced endothelin-1 tone; this is generally transient.; No tolerance, dependence, or withdrawal phenomena have been reported, consistent with epigenetic rather than receptor-occupancy mechanism.; Hypersensitivity reactions are rare; allergic skin responses should prompt discontinuation.; No HPA axis activation, hormonal disturbance, or significant metabolic effects documented at research-typical doses.; Reproductive, pregnancy, and lactation safety data are absent; use during these periods is not recommended.   -: Vesugen is a synthetic tripeptide (Lys-Glu-Asp, KED) developed by Vladimir Khavinson and colleagues as a tissue-specific bioregulator targeting the vascular endothelium and broader cardiovascular system [1][2].
  -: The reviewed record does not state a specific limitation. The linked paper still needs to be checked for design, size and bias.
  -: 14 Important Note This content is for educational purposes only and is not medical advice.
  -: Active vascular inflammatory conditions requiring immunosuppressive management (vasculitis, Behçet's disease, polyarteritis nodosa) - Vesugen's endothelial normalization activity during active vasculitic injury has not been characterized; the interaction between bioregulator endothelial remodeling and the inflammatory
  -: Recent vascular surgery or endovascular intervention (within 4 weeks) - the acute remodeling phase immediately following vascular repair involves specific pro-healing endothelial programs; superimposing exogenous bioregulator activity during this window has not been evaluated.
  -: Known hypersensitivity to Vesugen (Lys-Glu-Asp tripeptide) or formulation excipients.
  -: Pregnancy - vascular remodeling is a highly active and tightly regulated process during pregnancy (placental angiogenesis, uterine artery remodeling); exogenous endothelial bioregulator activity has not been evaluated in this context.
  -: Active anticoagulation therapy requiring stable INR (warfarin) - theoretical interaction with endothelial coagulation regulation normalization; coagulation monitoring is prudent.
  -: Severe active infection with vascular involvement (septic emboli, endovascular infection) - the endothelial immune function modulation from Vesugen during active vascular infection has not been characterized.
  *: Source rating: 4 out of 5
  *: PeptideDosage.org: Vesugen is generally well tolerated in Russian observational use; reported adverse effects are infrequent and mild.; The most common reported effect is transient injection-site discomfort with subcutaneous administration.; Occasional mild gastrointestinal upset (nausea, loose stools) has been reported with oral capsule formulations.; Theoretical hypotensive effects on initial dosing have been reported anecdotally in users with pre-existing low blood pressure, possibly reflecting reduced endothelin-1 tone; this is generally transient.; No tolerance, dependence, or withdrawal phenomena have been reported, consistent with epigenetic rather than receptor-occupancy mechanism.; Hypersensitivity reactions are rare; allergic skin responses should prompt discontinuation.; No HPA axis activation, hormonal disturbance, or significant metabolic effects documented at research-typical doses.; Reproductive, pregnancy, and lactation safety data are absent; use during these periods is not recommended.

### compound | vialox/overview | What is Vialox?
kind: overview
title: Vialox
summary: Vialox (INCI Pentapeptide-3; also sold as Pentapeptide-3V) is a synthetic cosmetic anti-wrinkle peptide with the sequence Gly-Pro-Arg-Pro-Ala-NH2 (CAS 135679-88-8, molecular weight ~495.6 Da), developed by the Swiss firm Pentapharm as a topical, needle-free alternative to botulinum toxin. It is a short synthetic fragment inspired by waglerin-1, a competitive nicotinic acetylcholine receptor antagonist from the venom of Wagler's pit viper (Tropidolaemus wagleri) [1][4]. By acting as a curare-like antagonist at the postsynaptic nicotinic acetylcholine receptor of the neuromuscular junction, Vialox is proposed to keep sodium channels closed, blunting depolarization and the contraction of the facial mimetic muscles that drive expression lines [2][3].

summary: Topical Vialox is generally well tolerated; the most common effects are mild, transient local reactions such as redness, stinging, tightness, or dryness at the application site, especially when layered with retinoids, acids, or other active ingredients.; Allergic or irritant contact dermatitis is possible, more often from other formulation components (preservatives, fragrance, penetration enhancers) than from the peptide itself; a persistent rash warrants dermatologic review and patch testing.; Because Vialox is applied near the eyes and forehead, accidental ocular contact can cause transient stinging, watering, and conjunctival irritation; keep product off the lash line and rinse with water if it migrates into the eye.; Vialox is a curare-like nicotinic receptor antagonist by design; while topical systemic absorption is negligible, this mechanism is the basis for caution against any non-cosmetic, injected, or off-label systemic use, which has no safety data and could in principle affect neuromuscular function.; Research-grade Vialox/Pentapeptide-3V sold as lyophilized powder is DSM Study (In Vivo) : Pentapeptide-3 cream × 28 days → 49% reduction in wrinkle depth in forehead/periorbital area (N=15) In Vitro : Reduced muscle cell contraction amplitude by 71% in neuromuscular junction cell model 🧪 Vial Dex The World's Most Advanced Peptide Calculator 100% FREE 💧 Reconstitution Vial + BAC water mixing 📉 Dose & Units Syringe units to draw 🔀 Blend Multi-peptide vial ratios 📚 Stack Protocol Multi-vial dose planning 💨 Nasal Spray Spray bottle concentrations 50+ Peptides 7 Calculators 0 Signup Required Peptide: Vialox Open Free Calculator → [ 1 ] [ 2 ] [ 3 ] ↑ 1.0 1.1 DSM Technical Data Sheet: Vialox (Pentapeptide-3). matchedText: Vilon
  connectedTo: Vilon
  *: 10 Potential Benefits & Side Effects Observations from preclinical literature. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Supports immune cell marker expression (CD5+ lymphocytes) and IL‑2 gene activity in cell culture models [1] [2] . [source-listed source severity]
  *: May modulate inflammatory cytokines such as TGF‑β1 under experimental renal stress conditions [3] . [source-listed source severity]
  *: Early mouse studies suggest potential effects on tumor growth inhibition and lifespan extension, though human data remain limited [6] . [source-listed source severity]
  *: Generally well tolerated in preclinical settings; occasional mild injection‑site reactions (redness/itch) may occur with subcutaneous administration. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Excellent Safety : No adverse effects reported in any published preclinical or clinical study Minimal Immunogenicity : Dipeptides are far too small for MHC presentation or antibody recognition Compatible With All Medications : No drug interactions documented; common amino acid components Long-Term Safety : Used in. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Transient immune activation symptoms - as T-cell output normalizes and immune competence is restored, some subjects experience mild flu-like symptoms (low-grade fatigue, mild myalgia) in the first days of a new cycle; reflects immune system reactivation rather than infection or adverse response. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Mild injection site reaction - standard subcutaneous dipeptide injection response; minimal due to the small molecular size of Vilon. [source-listed source severity]

  -: Peptide University Codex: Vilon is a synthetic dipeptide (Lys-Glu) developed by Vladimir Khavinson as the minimized bioactive core of thymus gland polypeptide extracts - the result of systematic fractionation work that identified the smallest peptide sequence retaining the full immunoregulatory bioregulator activity of the thymic extract...

section: Limitations
  -: The source does not clearly state the study population or design in PEARL's reviewed record.
  -: Vilon is a synthetic dipeptide (Lys-Glu, KE) developed by Khavinson and colleagues as one of the shortest active peptide bioregulators, derived by directed synthesis from the amino acid composition of Thymalin, a bovine thymic extract used in Russian clinical immunology since the 1970s [1][2].
  -: The reviewed record is animal research and cannot establish human effectiveness or safety.
  -: 14 Important Note This content is intended for therapeutic educational purposes only and does not constitute medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment.
  -: Organ transplant recipients on immunosuppressive therapy - Vilon's T-cell restoration and thymopoietic stimulation directly counteracts the immunosuppressive regimens (calcineurin inhibitors, mTOR inhibitors, corticosteroids) required to prevent allograft rejection; restored T-cell activity increases the risk of acute
  -: Active autoimmune disease in acute flare - the immune normalization activity of Vilon, while not non-specific immunostimulation, could exacerbate the T-cell-mediated pathology driving active autoimmune flares in conditions such as rheumatoid arthritis, lupus, multiple sclerosis, or inflammatory bowel disease; use
  -: Concurrent immunosuppressive therapy for non-transplant indications (high-dose corticosteroids, methotrexate, azathioprine, biologic immunosuppressants) - Vilon's immunoregulatory activity works against the therapeutic intent of these medications.
  -: Known hypersensitivity to Vilon (Lys-Glu dipeptide) or formulation excipients.
  -: Active hematological malignancies involving T-cell lineages (T-cell lymphoma, T-cell leukemia) - Vilon's thymopoietic stimulation in the context of malignant T-cell clonal expansion could theoretically support tumor cell proliferation.
  -: Pregnancy - immune regulation changes substantially during pregnancy; exogenous thymic bioregulator activity during gestation is not characterized.
  -: Pediatric use in subjects with intact thymic function - the thymus is highly active in children and young adults; Vilon's therapeutic target (the involuted aging thymus) does not exist in young subjects and the effects of superimposed thymic bioregulator stimulation on normally functioning thymopoiesis are not
  *: Source rating: 1 out of 5, very limited evidence

  -: Peptide Authority: Animal research; population: Human; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.

  -: Whether grey-market VIP products contain the labelled compound.

section: What the research shows
  -: The Peptide Handbook: A naturally occurring 28-amino-acid neuropeptide.
  -: Peptide Hub: VIP (Vasoactive Intestinal Peptide) is a 28-amino acid neuropeptide and potent endogenous immune modulator found in the brain, gut, and throughout the nervous system.
  -: PeptideDosage.org: VIP (vasoactive intestinal peptide; the synthetic form is marketed as aviptadil, RLF-100/ZYESAMI) is a 28-amino-acid neuropeptide of the secretin/glucagon superfamily encoded by the VIP gene.
  -: PeptideDeck: Recommended
  -: WikiPep: From Wikipep - The Peptide Encyclopedia VIP (Vasoactive Intestinal Peptide) Chemical name Vasoactive Intestinal Polypeptide Molecular formula C₁₄₇H₂₃₈N₄₄O₄₂S Molecular weight 3326.82 g/mol CAS number 37221-79-7 Sequence...
section: Evidence strength
  -: The Peptide Handbook: Source summary; study design not clearly stated; population: Human; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: Peptide Hub: Source summary; study design not clearly stated; population: Not clearly stated; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: PeptideDosage.org: Randomized or controlled human research; population: Human; Direct controlled human evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: PeptideDeck: Animal research; population: Animal; Preclinical animal evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: WikiPep: Source summary; study design not clearly stated; population: Not clearly stated; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Limitations
  -: Route-specific cardiovascular and hemodynamic risks require direct formulation-specific evaluation; long-term human safety and broad clinical efficacy are not established
  -: This is a commercial educational source. Its uncited figures and modelled outputs must remain labelled as source-listed rather than clinical evidence.
  -: VIP (vasoactive intestinal peptide; the synthetic form is marketed as aviptadil, RLF-100/ZYESAMI) is a 28-amino-acid neuropeptide of the secretin/glucagon superfamily encoded by the VIP gene.
  -: The reviewed record is animal research and cannot establish human effectiveness or safety.
  -: The source does not clearly state the study population or design in PEARL's reviewed record.
  *: Source rating: 3 out of 5
  *: The Peptide Handbook: preliminary. VIP/aviptadil remains preliminary. Human evidence is limited and route-specific: IV VIP pharmacology and inhaled pulmonary-hypertension research. Aviptadil COVID-19 registry records establish study status only, not efficacy. No FDA-approved indication or general therapeutic dosing exists.
  *: Peptide Hub: Protocol-focused educational summary. Linked papers, site-listed ranges and commercial context are retained with source attribution.
  *: PeptideDosage.org: Systemic vasodilation can cause hypotension, facial flushing, warmth, headache, and reflex tachycardia or palpitations; these are most relevant with intravenous aviptadil and were among the known effects managed in the TESICO trial [6].; Diarrhea is a recognized dose-limiting effect of VIP, consistent with its role in stimulating intestinal water and electrolyte secretion (the peptide was originally isolated from gut and is the mediator in VIPoma-associated watery diarrhea) [6].; Intranasal VIP can cause local nasal irritation, rhinorrhea, stinging, or transient lightheadedness shortly after spraying; the CIRS literature also describes early symptom flares when VIP is started before other steps are completed [8].; In the Shoemaker protocol, VIP is intended as a final step after MARCoNS nasal colonization is cleared and visual contrast sensitivity is normalized; using it too early is reported to worsen symptoms, underscoring that it is not a stand-alone therapy [8][9].; Caution or avoidance is advised in people with low blood pressure, recent cardiac events, significant arrhythmia,
  *: PeptideDeck: Potent anti-inflammatory effects in multiple tissue types Immunomodulatory activity promoting immune tolerance Neuroprotection against oxidative stress and inflammation Gut barrier function support and mucosal healing Circadian rhythm regulation through the suprachiasmatic nucleus Vasodilation and blood flow improvement Bronchodilation in respiratory conditions Cardioprotective effects in ischemia models VIP has been extensively studied in preclinical models for over four decades, with research demonstrating therapeutic potential across a remarkable range of conditions. More recently, clinical trials have begun evaluating VIP and its analogs in human patients. Clinical trials with VIP and its analogs have reported a favorable safety profile. In COVID-19 respiratory trials, inhaled VIP (Aviptadil) was generally well-tolerated. Adverse events were mostly mild and related to vasodilation. However, the total human exposure remains limited compared to approved therapeutics, and long-term safety data are not available.

### compound | visoluten/overview | What is Visoluten?
kind: overview
title: Visoluten
summary: A cytamin-class peptide supplement derived from ocular (eye) tissue, part of the Khavinson bioregulator framework. Marketed as an oral supplement for vision and eye health support. Contains peptide complexes rather than defined sequences. Some Russian clinical data exists, primarily alongside retinalamin studies.

### compound | visoluten/evidence | What research is listed for Visoluten?
kind: evidence
title: Visoluten: research listed by the sources
summary: No controlled human safety data exist for the Visoluten capsule; its adverse-effect profile is essentially unknown, and the points below are extrapolated from the injectable retina peptide and the Khavinson bioregulator class generally.; Taken orally as labeled, the most plausible effects are mild and gastrointestinal (nausea, fullness, or loose stools); the marketed product reports few complaints, but no rigorous tolerability study has been published.; For the educational subcutaneous reference, injection can cause local reactions including redness, itching, swelling, bruising, or transient pain at the injection site.; Any injected peptide complex carries a theoretical risk of immune or hypersensitivity reactions; stop use and seek care for rash, hives, facial or throat swelling, or difficulty breathing.

### compound | vitaminb12b1201/overview | What is Vitamin B12 (B1201)?
kind: overview
title: Vitamin B12 (B1201)
summary: Vitamin B12 (product code B1201) is a single-ingredient injectable delivering vitamin B12, typically as methylcobalamin, the active and readily usable form. It is a vitamin rather than a peptide, working as an essential cofactor in energy metabolism, nervous system function, and blood cell production, and it is given as a fixed direct dose with no titration. B12 is required for red blood cell formation, DNA synthesis, and the health of the myelin sheath that protects nerves, and it plays a central role in the methylation cycle that governs energy production and homocysteine clearance. Injectable delivery is valued because it bypasses the digestive absorption steps that many people, particularly older adults, vegetarians, and those with gut issues, struggle with. In practice, B1201 is used by people who want an energy, mood, and cognitive lift, or who need to correct a B12 deficiency that oral supplements are not adequately resolving.
keyPoint: Vitamin B12 (product code B1201) is a single-ingredient injectable delivering vitamin B12, typically as methylcobalamin, the active and readily usable form.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: Vitamin B12 (B1201)
  connectedTo: Vitamin B12 (B1201)
section: Why it is researched
  -: Vitamin B12 (product code B1201) is a single-ingredient injectable delivering vitamin B12, typically as methylcobalamin, the active and readily usable form.
section: How it works in the research
  -: Vitamin B12 (product code B1201) is a single-ingredient injectable delivering vitamin B12, typically as methylcobalamin, the active and readily usable form.
section: Evidence strength
  -: Peptide University Codex: Source summary; study design not clearly stated; population: Animal; Preclinical animal evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Main limitations
  -: Known hypersensitivity to cobalamin, cobalt, or any formulation excipient.
  -: Leber hereditary optic neuropathy, in which high-dose B12 is contraindicated.
  -: Pregnancy or breastfeeding unless directed and supervised by a physician, though B12 is generally considered safe.

### compound | vitamind3d320/overview | What is Vitamin D3 (D320)?
kind: overview
title: Vitamin D3 (D320)
summary: Vitamin D3 (product code D320) is a single-ingredient injectable delivering cholecalciferol, the form of vitamin D the body produces in response to sunlight. It is a vitamin rather than a peptide, working as a hormone-like nutrient that regulates gene expression across many tissues, and it is given as a fixed direct dose with no titration. Vitamin D3 is essential for calcium absorption and bone health, immune function, muscle strength, mood regulation, and healthy testosterone and hormone production. Injectable delivery is valued because it provides a reliable, high dose that bypasses the variability of oral absorption and is especially useful for people with low vitamin D status or absorption issues. In practice, D320 is used by people who want to correct or maintain healthy vitamin D levels, which is one of the most common nutrient insufficiencies, particularly in those with limited sun exposure, darker skin, or higher body fat that sequesters vitamin D.
keyPoint: Vitamin D3 (product code D320) is a single-ingredient injectable delivering cholecalciferol, the form of vitamin D the body produces in response to sunlight.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: Vitamin D3 (D320)
  connectedTo: Vitamin D3 (D320)
section: Why it is researched
  -: Vitamin D3 (product code D320) is a single-ingredient injectable delivering cholecalciferol, the form of vitamin D the body produces in response to sunlight.
section: How it works in the research
  -: Vitamin D3 (product code D320) is a single-ingredient injectable delivering cholecalciferol, the form of vitamin D the body produces in response to sunlight.
section: Evidence strength
  -: Peptide University Codex: Source summary; study design not clearly stated; population: Animal; Preclinical animal evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Main limitations
  -: Known hypersensitivity to cholecalciferol or any formulation excipient.
  -: Hypercalcemia or elevated blood calcium.
  -: Sarcoidosis or other granulomatous diseases, which increase vitamin D sensitivity.

### compound | vk2735/evidence | What research is listed for VK2735?

title: VK2735: research listed by the sources
summary: Moderate evidence; 11 human studies listed Gastrointestinal effects are the most common and dose-related; in the Phase 2 VENTURE subcutaneous trial, nausea occurred in 36.6% (64/175), constipation in 21.1% (37/175), and vomiting in 12.6% (22/175) of participants [1].; Most adverse events were mild (Grade 1, ~40.6%) or moderate (Grade 2, ~23.4%), with severe (Grade 3) events in ~4.6%; GI effects appeared early, subsided over time, and showed no dose-dependent increase after the initial dosing period [1].; The oral tablet formulation produced higher GI rates (nausea ~58%, vomiting ~26%), with the large majority characterized as mild or moderate and most events concentrated early in treatment [4].; Stepwise dose escalation (for example 2.5 → 5 → 10 → 15 mg weekly) is used specifically to mitigate nausea and vomiting; escalating too quickly increases GI intolerance and risk of dehydration.; As an incretin-class agent, VK2735 carries theoretical class risks seen with GLP-1/GIP drugs - including gallbladder events, pancreatitis, dehydration and acute kidney injury from severe vomiting, and hypoglycemia if combined with insulin or

### compound | vladonix/evidence | What research is listed for Vladonix?
kind: evidence
title: Vladonix: research listed by the sources
summary: The manufacturer's clinical report documented no side effects, complications, contraindications, or drug dependence at the doses studied, and oral thymic-peptide bioregulators are generally described as well tolerated [1] - but this reflects small, unblinded studies, not large controlled safety trials.; Listed contraindications are pregnancy, breastfeeding, age under 14, and individual intolerance to any component; these groups should not use the product.; Because the peptides are extracted from bovine (calf) thymus tissue, there is a theoretical risk of allergic or immunogenic reaction and the general (very low but non-zero) concern attached to any animal-tissue-derived product; sourcing and quality control vary by vendor.; As an immunomodulator it should be used cautiously, and only with medical guidance, by people with autoimmune disease, lymphoproliferative disorders, or organ transplants, where shifting T-cell balance could be undesirable.; It is not a substitute for vaccination, antibiotics, antivirals, or oncologic therapy; using it in place of evidence-based treatment for a Peptide University labels its records as aggregated from empirical research and anecdotal community data. This record is retained as supplied and is not upgraded to clinical evidence.

  -: PeptideDosage.org: Vladonix is a Khavinson thymus peptide bioregulator - the oral A-6 "Cytomax" - a complex of low-molecular-weight peptides (under roughly 10,000 Da) isolated from the thymus of calves under 12 months of age and developed by Professor Vladimir Khavinson at the St.
  -: Peptide University Codex: Vladonix is a Khavinson cytomedin - peptide complex A-6 - extracted from the thymus gland tissue of young animals, developed as the oral thymic bioregulator of the Khavinson framework.
section: Evidence strength
  -: PepCodex: Source summary; study design not clearly stated; population: Not clearly stated; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: PeptideDosage.org: Human clinical research; population: Human; Human evidence with design limitations to check. The source does not give a reliable study count.
  -: Peptide University Codex: Source summary; study design not clearly stated; population: Not clearly stated; Evidence level is not fully described by the source. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Limitations
  -: The source does not clearly state the study population or design in PEARL's reviewed record.
  -: Vladonix is a Khavinson thymus peptide bioregulator - the oral A-6 "Cytomax" - a complex of low-molecular-weight peptides (under roughly 10,000 Da) isolated from the thymus of calves under 12 months of age and developed by Professor Vladimir Khavinson at the St. Petersburg Institute of Bioregulation and Gerontology.
  -: Organ transplant recipients on immunosuppressive therapy - thymopoietic restoration and T-cell output increase directly counteracts the immunosuppressive regimen required to prevent allograft rejection; absolute contraindication shared with Vilon.
  -: Active autoimmune disease in acute flare - the immune normalization activity of Vladonix, while not non-specific immunostimulation, could exacerbate T-cell-mediated autoimmune pathology during active flares of rheumatoid arthritis, lupus, multiple sclerosis, or inflammatory bowel disease; use during active flare
  -: Concurrent high-dose immunosuppressive therapy for non-transplant indications - high-dose corticosteroids, methotrexate, azathioprine, biologic immunosuppressants; thymic bioregulator activity works against the therapeutic intent of these medications.
  -: Known hypersensitivity to Vladonix (thymus tissue cytomedin peptide complex A-6) or formulation excipients including gelatin.
  -: Active hematological malignancies involving T-cell lineages - T-cell lymphoma, T-cell leukemia; thymopoietic stimulation in the context of malignant T-cell clonal expansion could theoretically support tumor cell proliferation.
  -: Pregnancy - thymic immune regulation during pregnancy is tightly modified to permit maternal tolerance of the fetal allograft; exogenous thymic bioregulator activity during gestation has not been evaluated.
  -: Pediatric use in subjects with intact thymic function - the thymus is maximally active in children and young adults; the therapeutic target (the involuted aging thymus) does not exist in young subjects and effects of superimposed bioregulator stimulation on normal thymopoiesis are not characterized.
  *: Source rating: 1 out of 5, very limited evidence

  *: The official label warns about low blood pressure and requires attention to hydration and food intake around dosing. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Injection site reactions: Erythema, swelling, pain, and urticaria at the injection site (35-75%). Vomiting: 27% incidence; can be reduced by timing injection at least 30 minutes after food intake. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Hypotension: Blood pressure should be monitored, particularly at treatment initiation. Severe hypotension is rare but has been reported. Serious injection site reactions: Rare cases of severe local reactions. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Known hypersensitivity to vosoritide or any excipient Closed epiphyses (growth plates) Not for use in adults. [source-listed source severity]

### compound | vosoritide/evidence | What research is listed for Vosoritide?
kind: evidence
title: Vosoritide: research listed by the sources
summary: A phase 3 randomized trial enrolled 121 children aged 5 to under 18 years and compared vosoritide 15 mcg/kg daily with placebo for 52 weeks. Phase III pivotal trial (111-301): Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in 121 children aged 5-18 years with achondroplasia. Demonstrated statistically significant improvement in annualized growth velocity (+1.57 cm/year over placebo) at 52 weeks. Phase II dose-finding study (111-202): Established the 15 mcg/kg/day dose as optimal for efficacy and tolerability. Long-term extension (111-205): Ongoing 5+ year extension study demonstrating sustained growth velocity improvement and cumulative height gains. Phase II in younger children (111-206): Evaluating safety and efficacy in children aged 0-<5 years (ongoing). [ 1 ] [ 2 ] [ 3 ] [ 4 ] [ 5 ] [ 6 ] ↑ 1.0 1.1 Savarirayan R, Tofts L, Irving M, et al. ### compound | zelenectidepevedotin/overview | What is Zelenectide Pevedotin?
kind: overview
title: Zelenectide Pevedotin
summary: A first-in-class Bicycle Drug Conjugate (BDC) targeting Nectin-4 for solid tumors, developed by Bicycle Therapeutics. In the Duravelo-1 Phase 1/2 dose-escalation study it produced a 38% objective response rate (8/21) in urothelial carcinoma using a novel bicyclic peptide platform much smaller than traditional antibody-drug conjugates. Phase 2/3 Duravelo-2 registrational trial ongoing.
keyPoint: A first-in-class Bicycle Drug Conjugate (BDC) targeting Nectin-4 for solid tumors, developed by Bicycle Therapeutics.

### compound | zhenoluten/overview | What is Zhenoluten?
kind: overview
title: Zhenoluten
summary: Zhenoluten (Ovary Cytomax A-15) is a Khavinson ovary peptide bioregulator: a natural complex of low-molecular-weight peptides (up to roughly 5000 Da) isolated from the ovarian tissue of young animals and developed at the St. Petersburg Institute of Bioregulation and Gerontology under Professor Vladimir Khavinson [1][3]. As a member of the "Cytomax" family it is not a single defined molecule but a tissue-specific peptide extract, proposed to enter ovarian cells and modulate transcription of genes that govern follicular and reproductive-cell maintenance rather than to bind a surface receptor [2][4]. A manufacturer clinical study report describes improvements in climacteric (menopausal) symptoms and partial restoration of menstrual function in women with exhausted ovary syndrome, alongside reductions in FSH and LH and a rise in estradiol after a 30-day course [1].

### compound | ziconotide/overview | What is Ziconotide?
kind: overview
title: Ziconotide
summary: An FDA-approved intrathecal-only ziconotide product for severe chronic pain when other treatment is inadequate or not tolerated. Current PRIALT dosing starts at no more than 2.4 mcg/day and has a recommended maximum of 19.2 mcg/day.
keyPoint: An FDA-approved intrathecal-only ziconotide product for severe chronic pain when other treatment is inadequate or not tolerated.
understood: resolved
method: canonical
confidence: high
matchedText: Ziconotide
  connectedTo: Ziconotide
section: Why it is researched
  -: An FDA-approved intrathecal-only ziconotide product for severe chronic pain when other treatment is inadequate or not tolerated.
section: How it works in the research
  -: Ziconotide is a synthetic 25-amino-acid equivalent of omega-conotoxin MVIIA.
section: Evidence strength
  -: The Peptide Handbook: Randomized or controlled human research; population: Human; Direct controlled human evidence. The source does not give a reliable study count.
section: Main limitations
  -: PRIALT carries an FDA boxed warning for severe neuropsychiatric adverse reactions; severe psychiatric symptoms and neurological impairment can occur
  -: PRIALT is contraindicated in patients with a pre-existing history of psychosis
  -: Cognitive impairment, hallucinations, mood changes, reduced alertness, unresponsiveness, and suicidal ideation or behavior have been reported

  *: PRIALT carries an FDA boxed warning for severe neuropsychiatric adverse reactions; severe psychiatric symptoms and neurological impairment can occur. [source-listed source severity]
  *: PRIALT is contraindicated in patients with a pre-existing history of psychosis. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Cognitive impairment, hallucinations, mood changes, reduced alertness, unresponsiveness, and suicidal ideation or behavior have been reported. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Meningitis and other serious infections can occur in association with intrathecal microinfusion systems, particularly when sterility is compromised. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Elevations in serum creatine kinase can occur; symptomatic myopathy and rare rhabdomyolysis-associated acute renal failure have been reported. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Neuropsychiatric: Dizziness (47%), confusion (33%), memory impairment (22%), somnolence (17%), ataxia (14%), speech disorder (14%), nausea (22%), headache (13%), nystagmus (8%), hallucinations (12%). Cognitive impairment: Word-finding difficulty, disorientation, and abnormal thinking are common and dose-related. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Severe psychiatric symptoms: Psychosis, hallucinations, paranoia, hostility, delirium, and suicidal ideation have been reported. Patients with pre-existing psychiatric disorders are at higher risk. Cognitive impairment: Significant cognitive impairment can occur, potentially interfering with daily activities. [source-listed source severity]
  *: Known hypersensitivity to ziconotide or any excipient Pre-existing history of psychosis Infection at the microinfusion injection site Uncontrolled bleeding diathesis Spinal canal obstruction that would impair CSF circulation Concomitant intrathecal chemotherapy. [source-listed source severity]

### compound | ziconotide/evidence | What research is listed for Ziconotide?
kind: evidence
title: Ziconotide: research listed by the sources
summary: strong-human. A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled human study supports slow-titration intrathecal ziconotide in adults with severe chronic pain. Current PRIALT labeling requires initiation at no more than 2.4 mcg/day, titration no more frequently than 2-3 times per week, and a recommended maximum of 19.2 mcg/day. Severe neuropsychiatric reactions, psychosis contraindication, cognitive and consciousness changes, infection/meningitis, and creatine-kinase monitoring remain label-specific safety boundaries. Phase III pivotal trials (301, 302, 303): Three randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials demonstrated significant pain reduction. Trial 301 (cancer pain, n=111) showed mean 53% improvement vs. 18% for placebo. Trials 302/303 (cancer and non-cancer pain) confirmed efficacy with slower titration. Long-term open-label extension studies: Demonstrated maintained analgesic efficacy over 12+ months without tolerance development. Conotoxin analogs: Research into synthetic conotoxin derivatives with improved therapeutic windows and alternative delivery routes. Combination intrathecal therapy: Investigated in combination with intrathecal opioids and local anesthetics for synergistic pain relief. Neuroprotection: N-type calcium channel blockade investigated for potential neuroprotective applications in ischemia and traumatic injury. [ 1 ] [ 2 ] [ 3 ] [ 4 ] [ 5 ] [ 6 ] ↑ 1.0 1.1 Staats PS, Yearwood T, Charapata SG, et al. Intrathecal ziconotide in the treatment of refractory pain in patients with cancer or AIDS: a randomized controlled trial. JAMA. 2004;291(1):63-70.

title: Source entries related to ADHD-related research

They are grouped by connection strength and then ordered by text relevance and evidence strength, not which compound is best or suitable for a person. Each entry shows its source-listed numbers; select any named compound for its full route, population, duration, evidence and limitations. Important evidence note: No peptide is an approved or established ADHD treatment, and none of these entries has randomised controlled trial evidence in an ADHD population. Semax is listed first because the reviewed sources connect it with attention research most directly, but its main PubMed ADHD citation is a hypothesis paper and the small Russian paediatric report was open-label rather than a modern blinded placebo-controlled trial. Everything below it is a weaker or more indirect connection, labelled as such.

section: Limitations
  -: Cerebrolysin: The source does not clearly state the study population or design in PEARL's reviewed record.
  -: Semax: The 2007 ADHD paper proposes a hypothesis and reports no Semax ADHD trial.
  -: Semax: The small Russian pediatric report was open-label and did not provide modern randomized placebo-controlled evidence.
  -: Semax: No FDA or EMA approval for ADHD or another mental-health indication.
  -: P21: Important caveats apply to interpreting P21 research. Published studies come from a limited number of research groups, reducing independent replication. The translation from rodent maze performance to human cognitive enhancement involves substantial uncertainty.
  -: Dihexa: Whether a UK-purchased product contains Dihexa at the labelled concentration.

  -: Dihexa: Long-term oncologic surveillance does not exist.
  -: Dihexa: Cognitive outcome data in humans is absent.
  -: Dihexa: Pharmacokinetic data in humans is absent.
  -: Noopept: Noopept (development code GVS-111; international nonproprietary name Omberacetam) is a synthetic proline-containing dipeptide nootropic, chemically N-phenylacetyl-L-prolylglycine ethyl ester, designed at Russia's Zakusov Institute of Pharmacology to reproduce the activity of the pyrrolidone nootropic piracetam in a
  -: Selank: Whether a UK-purchased nasal spray contains the labelled peptide at the labelled concentration.
  -: Selank: How it interacts with prescribed SSRIs or benzodiazepines a UK patient is already taking.
  -: Selank: Whether tolerance develops with chronic use.
  -: Selank: What the WADA in-competition status is for athletes.

  -: Selank: No registered Western Phase 3 trials.

  -: Calcitonin: this is an indirect connection and does not establish treatment effectiveness.
  -: Calcitonin: Whether off-label long-term use carries the same cancer signal as restricted indication.

  -: PTH 1-34: this is an indirect connection and does not establish treatment effectiveness.

Each entry shows its source-listed numbers; select any named compound for its full route, population, duration, evidence and limitations. section: Limitations
  -: β-Endorphin: What 'endorphin supplements' actually contain.
  -: β-Endorphin: Whether they produce any measurable effect on endogenous endorphin tone.
  -: β-Endorphin: Exogenous endorphin pharmacology is not a viable therapeutic route due to BBB and half-life issues.
  -: PT-141: 16 Important Note This content is for educational purposes only and is not medical advice.
  -: N-Acetyl Semax Amidate: N-Acetyl Semax Amidate (NA-Semax, Semax amidate) is a doubly modified analog of the Russian nootropic neuropeptide Semax, which is itself derived from the adrenocorticotropic hormone fragment ACTH(4-10) fused to the C-terminal tripeptide Pro-Gly-Pro.
  -: Orexin-A: Unknown in humans; theoretical cardiovascular stimulation; addiction/reward pathway activation (orexin system regulates reward); off-label self-administration not advisable
  -: Semax: The 2007 ADHD paper proposes a hypothesis and reports no Semax ADHD trial.
  -: Semax: The small Russian pediatric report was open-label and did not provide modern randomized placebo-controlled evidence.
  -: Semax: No FDA or EMA approval for ADHD or another mental-health indication.
  -: Melanotan II: Melanotan II is a synthetic cyclic heptapeptide analog of alpha-melanocyte-stimulating hormone (α-MSH) developed at the University of Arizona by Hadley, Hruby, Dorr and colleagues in the 1980s as a stable, broadly active melanocortin receptor agonist.
  -: Selank: Small and geographically concentrated human evidence base.
  -: Selank: No FDA or EMA approval for anxiety or another mental-health indication.
  -: Selank: Panic, social-anxiety and stress-resilience wording on tertiary sites extends beyond the directly tested generalized-anxiety population.
  -: GDNF: this is an indirect connection and does not establish treatment effectiveness.
  -: GDNF: The reviewed record does not state a specific limitation. The linked paper still needs to be checked for design, size and bias.
  -: Tesofensine: this is an indirect connection and does not establish treatment effectiveness.
  -: Tesofensine: Whether a UK-purchased product contains tesofensine at the labelled dose.
  -: Tesofensine: How it interacts with SSRIs, beta-blockers, or other cardiovascular medications.
  -: Tesofensine: What the long-term cardiovascular risk profile is.
  -: Tesofensine: Whether discontinuation causes rebound appetite or mood symptoms.
  -: Tesofensine: Phase 3 weight-loss outcome trial not completed.
  -: Tesofensine: Cardiovascular outcome trial not completed.
  -: Tesofensine: Long-term safety beyond ~24 weeks unstudied.
  -: Tesofensine: Interaction profile with other psychoactive and cardiovascular drugs uncharacterised.

section: Limitations
  -: TB4-FRAG: no approved use.
  -: TB4-FRAG: not shared by its parent molecule.
  -: TB4-FRAG: not appear to depend on ACE inhibition by Ac-SDKP, since the peptide did not alter blood pressure responses to exogenous angiotensin I or bradykinin.
  -: TB4-FRAG: not share receptors, mechanisms, or pharmacological properties despite the naming similarity.
  -: TB4-FRAG: not synthesizing DNA, making them resistant to S-phase-active chemotherapy agents (alkylating agents, antimetabolites).
  -: TB4-FRAG: not exist as of 2026.
  -: TB4-FRAG: no standardized human administration protocol exists given the lack of clinical trials.
  -: TB4-FRAG: not been studied in any human neurological context.
  -: Relaxin: Clinically significant hypotension - particularly relevant with IV administration; blood pressure monitoring required in clinical settings
  -: Relaxin: No FDA-approved indication; use outside clinical trial context is without established safety profile
  -: Relaxin: Long-term connective tissue effects of repeated exogenous relaxin administration are not characterized
  -: Relaxin: Phase III trial failure for acute heart failure primary endpoint; clinical development discontinued by Novartis for this indication

section: Limitations
  -: Chonluten: this is an indirect connection and does not establish treatment effectiveness.
  -: Chonluten: The source does not clearly state the study population or design in PEARL's reviewed record.
  -: PYY 3-36: this is an indirect connection and does not establish treatment effectiveness.
  -: PYY 3-36: Cardiovascular effects at supraphysiologic doses require monitoring; nausea at clinical doses can be dose-limiting
  -: Urolithin A: this is an indirect connection and does not establish treatment effectiveness.
  -: Urolithin A: Long-term safety data is limited to the duration of published trials (up to approximately four months in the longest studies available)
  -: Urolithin A: Individual Urolithin A production from dietary ellagitannins varies substantially by gut microbiome composition - dietary intake of precursor foods does not reliably produce equivalent supplemental exposure
  -: Gut Healing Stack: BPC-157 Oral (10mg) / KPV (10mg) / Larazotide (10mg) Research Profile: this is an indirect connection and does not establish treatment effectiveness.
  -: Gut Healing Stack: BPC-157 Oral (10mg) / KPV (10mg) / Larazotide (10mg) Research Profile: This is a commercial educational source. Its uncited figures and modelled outputs must remain labelled as source-listed rather than clinical evidence.
  -: BPC-157: this is an indirect connection and does not establish treatment effectiveness.
  -: BPC-157: An honest accounting of the gaps in the evidence for BPC-157.
  -: BPC-157: The literature clusters around a single research group. The large majority of BPC-157 publications originate from one laboratory (Sikirić and collaborators), and independent replication remains limited.
  -: BPC-157: No specific receptor has been identified. Despite many proposed pathways (VEGFR2, nitric oxide, growth-factor cross-talk), no defined molecular target for BPC-157 has been established.
  -: BPC-157: The PL-14736 Phase 2 trial was halted before completion, and no pivotal human efficacy trial has since been completed and published.
  -: BPC-157: Effect sizes in some rodent papers strain biological plausibility, with near-universal benefit across unrelated injury models.
  -: BPC-157: Long-term safety is genuinely unstudied in humans. There are no controlled data on chronic administration, drug interactions, or oncological risk. ❧ VI
  -: Larazotide: this is an indirect connection and does not establish treatment effectiveness.
  -: Larazotide: The Phase 3 Failure The most significant limitation is that larazotide did not demonstrate sufficient efficacy in its Phase 3 trial.
  -: Larazotide: The treatment effect may have been modest enough that it did not reproduce in a larger, more diverse population.
  -: Larazotide: High placebo response rates in celiac symptom trials - a well-known challenge - likely compounded the problem.
  -: Larazotide: Outcome Measure Challenges Celiac disease is difficult to study with patient-reported outcome measures.
  -: Larazotide: Symptoms overlap with irritable bowel syndrome, dietary indiscretions are hard to monitor, and the subjective nature of GI symptoms introduces noise.
  -: Larazotide: The switch from CeD-GSRS (Phase 2b) to CeD PRO abdominal domain (Phase 3) may have contributed to the different results.
  -: Larazotide: The Zonulin Measurement Controversy Studies from 2018 onward revealed that widely used commercial ELISA kits marketed for measuring serum zonulin do not actually detect zonulin (pre-haptoglobin-2).

section: Limitations
  -: Renisamin: this is an indirect connection and does not establish treatment effectiveness.
  -: Renisamin: eGFR < 30 (CKD Stage 4-5) without nephrologist supervision - severely reduced functional nephron mass limits bioregulator target cell availability; the altered pharmacokinetics of oral peptide absorption and renal clearance in advanced CKD require specialist oversight for dose adjustment.
  -: Renisamin: Active acute kidney injury (AKI) in the anuric or oliguric phase - Renisamin is a tissue regenerative bioregulator, not an acute intervention for AKI management; initiation during active oliguric AKI has not been evaluated and could interact with the acute injury-repair process.
  -: Renisamin: Renal cell carcinoma or urothelial malignancy - renal tubular cell gene program normalization activity has not been evaluated in the context of malignant renal cells; nephron bioregulator activity in malignant tissue requires oncological evaluation.
  -: Renisamin: Active nephrotic syndrome with severe hypoalbuminemia (albumin < 2.0 g/dL) - the profound protein losses of active nephrotic syndrome create an unpredictable pharmacokinetic context for oral peptide absorption.
  -: Renisamin: Known hypersensitivity to Renisamin (renal tissue cytomedin polypeptide complex) or formulation excipients.
  -: Renisamin: Pregnancy - renal hemodynamic changes during pregnancy (50% increase in GFR, renal enlargement, altered tubular function) create an unevaluated context for exogenous renal bioregulator activity.
  -: Renisamin: Renal transplantation on immunosuppression - renal tubular cell bioregulator activity in immunosuppressed recipients with donor nephron tissue requires transplant nephrology supervision; interactions with calcineurin inhibitor-induced nephrotoxicity and the immunosuppression-modified renal transcriptome are not
  -: Renisamin: Active pyelonephritis or renal abscess - acute bacterial renal parenchymal infection requires antimicrobial management; bioregulator activity during active renal infection has not been characterized.
  -: Soluble Klotho: The reviewed record is animal research and cannot establish human effectiveness or safety.
  -: Etelcalcetide: This schedule applies only to adults receiving haemodialysis.
  -: Etelcalcetide: Calcium and parathyroid hormone results determine specialist adjustment.
  -: SS-31: Whether a UK-purchased vial contains elamipretide at the labelled concentration.
  -: SS-31: Whether the trial benefit in specific mitochondrial diseases applies to healthy adults or to long COVID.
  -: SS-31: Long-term safety beyond trial endpoints.
  -: SS-31: Whether commercial 'research peptide' SS-31 is the same compound as the clinical-trial elamipretide.
  -: SS-31: Healthy-adult outcome data absent.
  -: SS-31: Long-COVID and chronic-fatigue RCT evidence absent despite heavy marketing.
  -: SS-31: Long-term safety in non-trial populations unstudied.
  -: EPO: Increased mortality, cardiovascular events, and tumor progression when targeting hemoglobin >11 g/dL Thromboembolic events : Stroke, MI, DVT, PE - risk increases with higher hemoglobin targets Tumor progression : Shortened overall survival in cancer patients in multiple trials (BEST, ENHANCE, DAHANCA-10) PRCA : Rare
  -: Dulaglutide: Official schedules require clinical prescribing and monitoring.
  -: Dulaglutide: A labelled medicine is not a general research-use recommendation.
  -: Erythropoietin: Whether a grey-market EPO product contains the labelled compound or has been adulterated.
  -: Erythropoietin: Whether 'microdose' protocols are truly undetectable (assume not - Athlete Biological Passport tracks erythropoietic markers).

section: Limitations
  -: NAD+: The reviewed record is animal research and cannot establish human effectiveness or safety.
  -: FOXO4-DRI: The reviewed record is animal research and cannot establish human effectiveness or safety.
  -: Epithalon: This is a commercial educational source. Its uncited figures and modelled outputs must remain labelled as source-listed rather than clinical evidence.
  -: SS-31: The reviewed record does not state a specific limitation. The linked paper still needs to be checked for design, size and bias.
  -: Quercetin: The dasatinib-quercetin senolytic combination is a supervised research protocol - dasatinib is an FDA-approved prescription chemotherapy drug with significant toxicity and should never be self-administered
  -: Quercetin: Adequate long-term safety data for high supplemental doses are limited
  -: Quercetin: Potential drug-interaction concerns exist; the evidence represented here does not establish universal safety or formulation equivalence
  -: Quercetin: Commercial products may not contain the labeled amount or the specific quercetin form studied in research
  -: Fisetin: Long-term human safety data is absent - the doses used in some research studies substantially exceed what would be obtained from dietary sources
  -: Fisetin: Potential drug interactions have not been systematically studied in humans
  -: Fisetin: Not recommended during pregnancy or breastfeeding due to insufficient safety data
  -: Fisetin: Bioavailability is a significant limitation: poor absorption may mean tissue concentrations after supplementation are substantially lower than doses shown to be active in preclinical studies
  -: Fisetin: Supplement quality and purity vary considerably across commercial products
  -: Progeline: this is an indirect connection and does not establish treatment effectiveness.
  -: Progeline: The reviewed record is laboratory research and cannot establish effects in people.
  -: GDF-11: No established human safety or pharmacokinetic profile.
  -: GDF-11: Animal concerns should not be generalized beyond the studied model and dose.
  -: Epitalon: this is an indirect connection and does not establish treatment effectiveness.
  -: Epitalon: Whether a UK-purchased vial actually contains Epitalon at the labelled concentration.
  -: Epitalon: Whether telomere lengthening in a Petri dish translates to longevity in humans.
  -: Epitalon: What the cancer risk profile is over decades of intermittent use.
  -: Epitalon: How it interacts with statins, metformin, or other longevity stack drugs.
  -: Epitalon: Most positive human data comes from a single Russian research group.
  -: Epitalon: No independent Western replication of lifespan or telomere findings.

section: Limitations
  -: Selank: The reviewed record does not state a specific limitation. The linked paper still needs to be checked for design, size and bias.
  -: Semax: The reviewed record does not state a specific limitation. The linked paper still needs to be checked for design, size and bias.
  -: DSIP: The reviewed record is animal research and cannot establish human effectiveness or safety.
  -: PE-22-28: PE-22-28 is a 7-amino-acid synthetic peptide derived as a truncated analogue of spadin, the 17-residue sortilin-derived peptide first described by Mazella and colleagues in PLoS Biology 2010 as a selective TREK-1 potassium channel blocker with antidepressant-like activity [1].
  -: Oxytocin: Whether intranasal oxytocin reaches the brain in clinically meaningful amounts.
  -: Oxytocin: Whether off-label psychiatric / relationship benefits exist beyond expectancy effects.
  -: Oxytocin: Whether a grey-market intranasal product contains oxytocin at the labelled dose.
  -: Oxytocin: Long-term safety of repeated intranasal use.
  -: Oxytocin: Intranasal oxytocin RCTs for autism, social anxiety, PTSD are mixed and many have failed replication.
  -: Oxytocin: Pharmacokinetics of intranasal delivery to CNS poorly characterised.
  -: Oxytocin: Long-term off-label use unstudied.
  -: Neuropeptide Y: Human Translation : Limited translation from animal to human studies Long-term Effects : Unknown consequences of chronic NPY modulation Individual Variation : High variability in response between individuals Complex Interactions : Multiple physiological systems affected simultaneously

  -: Insulin (Regular Human): Severe hypoglycemia - potentially fatal; risk is highest with dose-food-activity mismatch

section: Limitations
  -: PACAP-38: Provocation experiment, not treatment evidence.
  -: PACAP-38: Small, female-only completed sample.
  -: PACAP-38: No validated therapeutic dose.
  -: CGRP: The reviewed record does not state a specific limitation. The linked paper still needs to be checked for design, size and bias.
  -: PACAP (Pituitary Adenylate Cyclase-Activating Peptide): Whether grey-market 'PACAP' contains the labelled compound.
  -: PACAP (Pituitary Adenylate Cyclase-Activating Peptide): Long-term safety of exogenous PACAP signalling in healthy adults.
  -: PACAP (Pituitary Adenylate Cyclase-Activating Peptide): Anti-PACAP antibody Phase 3 trials in migraine are the productive direction; native-PACAP therapeutic use is essentially non-viable.
  -: Substance P: Not directly applicable as a therapeutic agent; see NK1 antagonist entries for therapeutic risk profiles
  -: VIP: VIP (vasoactive intestinal peptide; the synthetic form is marketed as aviptadil, RLF-100/ZYESAMI) is a 28-amino-acid neuropeptide of the secretin/glucagon superfamily encoded by the VIP gene.
  -: Ipamorelin: Ipamorelin (Aib-His-D-2-Nal-D-Phe-Lys-NH2) is a synthetic pentapeptide growth hormone secretagogue and a highly selective full agonist at the growth hormone secretagogue receptor type 1a (GHSR1a). Developed by Novo Nordisk in the late 1990s and described in the landmark Raun et al.
  -: Semax: Semax (Met-Glu-His-Phe-Pro-Gly-Pro, MEHFPGP) is a synthetic heptapeptide analogue of adrenocorticotropic hormone fragment ACTH(4-10), with a stabilizing Pro-Gly-Pro tail added to confer resistance to proteolysis. Developed at the M. M. Shemyakin and Yu. A.
  -: Sermorelin: Sermorelin (formerly Geref) is a synthetic 29-amino-acid peptide consisting of the first 29 amino acids of human growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH) and was the first commercially marketed GHRH analogue.
  -: Aviptadil: this is an indirect connection and does not establish treatment effectiveness.
  -: Aviptadil: The reviewed record does not state a specific limitation. The linked paper still needs to be checked for design, size and bias.
  -: BPC-157: The source does not clearly state the study population or design in PEARL's reviewed record.
  -: Selank: Selank (Thr-Lys-Pro-Arg-Pro-Gly-Pro) is a synthetic heptapeptide anxiolytic derived from the endogenous immunomodulator tuftsin, developed at the Russian Academy of Sciences' Institute of Molecular Genetics.
  -: Palmitoyl Tripeptide-8: this is an indirect connection and does not establish treatment effectiveness.
  -: Palmitoyl Tripeptide-8: The reviewed record is animal research and cannot establish human effectiveness or safety.
  -: CJC-1295 NO DAC + Ipamorelin: The CJC-1295 no DAC + ipamorelin stack is the most widely used growth hormone secretagogue combination in research peptide protocols.
  -: HCG: Human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) is a glycoprotein hormone composed of an alpha subunit shared with LH, FSH, and TSH and a unique beta subunit.

  -: PE-22-28: PE-22-28 is a 7-amino-acid synthetic peptide derived as a truncated analogue of spadin, the 17-residue sortilin-derived peptide first described by Mazella and colleagues in PLoS Biology 2010 as a selective TREK-1 potassium channel blocker with antidepressant-like activity [1].

section: Limitations
  -: Ziconotide: PRIALT carries an FDA boxed warning for severe neuropsychiatric adverse reactions; severe psychiatric symptoms and neurological impairment can occur
  -: Ziconotide: PRIALT is contraindicated in patients with a pre-existing history of psychosis
  -: Ziconotide: Cognitive impairment, hallucinations, mood changes, reduced alertness, unresponsiveness, and suicidal ideation or behavior have been reported
  -: Ziconotide: Meningitis and other serious infections can occur in association with intrathecal microinfusion systems, particularly when sterility is compromised
  -: Ziconotide: Elevations in serum creatine kinase can occur; symptomatic myopathy and rare rhabdomyolysis-associated acute renal failure have been reported
  -: Ziconotide: Combination of PRIALT with intrathecal opioids is not recommended
  -: ARA-290: Whether grey-market 'ARA-290' contains the labelled compound.
  -: ARA-290: Whether Phase 3 will confirm Phase 2 neuropathy signal.

  -: PT-141: VYLEESI is contraindicated in patients with uncontrolled hypertension or known cardiovascular disease
  -: PT-141: VYLEESI is not recommended for patients at high risk for cardiovascular disease
  -: PT-141: Focal hyperpigmentation involving areas such as the face, gingiva, or breasts can occur and may not completely resolve after discontinuation
  -: PT-141: Nausea is common and can be severe enough to require anti-emetic treatment or discontinuation
  -: Amino Lipotropic Complex (LC216): this is an indirect connection and does not establish treatment effectiveness.

  -: Amino Lipotropic Complex (LC216): Pregnancy or breastfeeding unless directed and supervised by a physician.
  -: Amino Lipotropic Complex (LC216): Active liver or kidney disease unless medically supervised.
  -: Amino Lipotropic Complex (LC216): History of seizures, as carnitine may lower the seizure threshold in susceptible individuals.
  -: Amino Lipotropic Complex (LC216): Uncontrolled low blood pressure or concurrent high-dose antihypertensive therapy, due to the arginine content.
  -: NeuroSync: this is an indirect connection and does not establish treatment effectiveness.
  -: NeuroSync: Pregnancy or active attempts to conceive due to the oxytocin component and potential uterotonic signaling concerns.
  -: NeuroSync: Breastfeeding due to insufficient safety data and the oxytocin component’s role in lactation physiology.
  -: NeuroSync: Concurrent use with uterotonic agents or prostaglandins unless medically supervised.
  -: NeuroSync: History of hyponatremia, SIADH, or clinically significant water-balance disorders due to oxytocin-related antidiuretic signaling concerns.
  -: NeuroSync: Concurrent use with desmopressin or vasopressin analogs unless medically supervised due to additive water-retention and hyponatremia risk.
  -: NeuroSync: Active mania, hypomania, psychosis, or severe uncontrolled psychiatric instability due to possible dopaminergic, serotonergic, and social-salience modulation.
  -: NeuroSync: Known hypersensitivity to Semax, Selank, Oxytocin, or formulation excipients.

section: Limitations
  -: Melanotan II: The reviewed record is animal research and cannot establish human effectiveness or safety.
  -: Melanotan I: The reviewed record does not state a specific limitation. The linked paper still needs to be checked for design, size and bias.
  -: Afamelanotide: Serious hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis, have been reported with SCENESSE
  -: Afamelanotide: SCENESSE is contraindicated in patients with a history of severe hypersensitivity to afamelanotide or its excipients
  -: Afamelanotide: Darkening of existing nevi and ephelides can occur; twice-yearly full-body skin examinations are recommended to monitor existing and new pigmented lesions

  -: PE-22-28: PE-22-28 is a 7-amino-acid synthetic peptide derived as a truncated analogue of spadin, the 17-residue sortilin-derived peptide first described by Mazella and colleagues in PLoS Biology 2010 as a selective TREK-1 potassium channel blocker with antidepressant-like activity [1].
  -: Semax: The 2007 ADHD paper proposes a hypothesis and reports no Semax ADHD trial.
  -: Semax: The small Russian pediatric report was open-label and did not provide modern randomized placebo-controlled evidence.
  -: Semax: No FDA or EMA approval for ADHD or another mental-health indication.
  -: N-Acetyl Semax Amidate: N-Acetyl Semax Amidate (NA-Semax, Semax amidate) is a doubly modified analog of the Russian nootropic neuropeptide Semax, which is itself derived from the adrenocorticotropic hormone fragment ACTH(4-10) fused to the C-terminal tripeptide Pro-Gly-Pro.
  -: Vasopressin: Whether a grey-market nasal-vasopressin product contains the labelled compound at the labelled concentration.
  -: Vasopressin: Whether off-label cognitive-enhancement use is safe long-term.
  -: Vasopressin: Cognitive-enhancement RCTs in healthy adults are limited; replication poor.
  -: N-Acetyl Selank: The reviewed record is animal research and cannot establish human effectiveness or safety.
  -: DSIP: The reviewed record is animal research and cannot establish human effectiveness or safety.
  -: Neuropeptide Y: Human Translation : Limited translation from animal to human studies Long-term Effects : Unknown consequences of chronic NPY modulation Individual Variation : High variability in response between individuals Complex Interactions : Multiple physiological systems affected simultaneously
  -: β-Endorphin: What 'endorphin supplements' actually contain.
  -: β-Endorphin: Whether they produce any measurable effect on endogenous endorphin tone.
  -: β-Endorphin: Exogenous endorphin pharmacology is not a viable therapeutic route due to BBB and half-life issues.

  -: Tesofensine: Tesofensine (NS2330) is an orally active, small-molecule triple monoamine reuptake inhibitor, a phenyltropane derivative originally developed by the Danish company NeuroSearch and later licensed to Saniona.

SUSTAIN-6 demonstrated fewer major adverse cardiovascular events with semaglutide versus placebo in adults with type 2 diabetes at elevated cardiovascular risk (Marso et al. 2016). STEP 1 found substantial mean weight loss with semaglutide 2.4 mg in adults with overweight or obesity, and SELECT demonstrated cardiovascular-event reduction in adults with established cardiovascular disease and overweight or obesity without diabetes. The FLOW trial (completed January 2024) found that semaglutide reduced the composite risk of kidney failure and major kidney-disease events in adults with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease. The EVOKE Phase III trial (primary endpoint completed September 2025) found that semaglutide did not slow clinical progression in early Alzheimer's disease; this completed negative result should not be characterized as an unanswered or ongoing program.
  *: Halflife Labs: Evidence context is stated on the linked compound page.
  *: PeptideDosage.org: Gastrointestinal events are the dominant side effect: nausea 44% (vs 16% placebo), diarrhea 32%, vomiting 24% and constipation 24% in STEP-1. Most events were mild-to-moderate, concentrated during titration and resolved within 1-2 weeks of dose stabilization; 4.5% discontinued for GI reasons [1].; Cholelithiasis and acute cholecystitis occurred in 2.6% on semaglutide vs 1.2% on placebo in pooled STEP data - a recognized class effect of rapid weight loss and altered bile-flow dynamics. Patients should be counseled on right-upper-quadrant pain warning signs [1].; Acute pancreatitis remains a label concern, with an absolute event rate <0.4% in STEP trials, broadly consistent with background population rates. The FDA label advises discontinuation if pancreatitis is suspected and avoidance in patients with a history of pancreatitis.; Heart-rate elevation of 2-4 beats per minute on average was observed in STEP-1; clinical significance appears minimal but pre-existing tachyarrhythmia warrants caution.
  *: PeptideDeck: Supports significant reduction in body weight through appetite suppression and reduced caloric intake Helps regulate blood glucose levels by enhancing insulin secretion when blood sugar rises May reduce cardiovascular risk factors including blood pressure and inflammatory markers Promotes feelings of fullness and satiety that persist between meals Supports metabolic health improvements including reduced visceral fat accumulation The clinical evidence supporting semaglutide spans dozens of large, well-designed trials. The STEP (Semaglutide Treatment Effect in People with Obesity) program alone enrolled thousands of participants across multiple studies. Results consistently show substantial, sustained weight loss with acceptable safety profiles. The SELECT trial represented a landmark moment for obesity treatment. This massive study enrolled over 17,000 people with established cardiovascular disease and overweight or obesity but without diabetes. After following participants for over four years, semaglutide reduced major adverse cardiovascular events by 20% compared to placebo.
  *: STEP-1: Semaglutide 2.4mg for Weight Management (NEJM 2021): 14.9% weight loss vs 2.4% placebo over 68 weeks. Established 2.4mg as standard obesity dose.
  *: STEP UP: Semaglutide 7.2mg (Wegovy HD) (Lancet Diabetes & Endocrinology 2025): 20.7% average weight loss at 72 weeks. ~1 in 3 patients achieved ≥25% loss. Dysesthesia signal at 22.9%. FDA approved March 2026.

section: Limitations
  -: IGF-1 LR3: The reviewed record does not state a specific limitation. The linked paper still needs to be checked for design, size and bias.
  -: Muscle Architect: this is an indirect connection and does not establish treatment effectiveness.
  -: Muscle Architect: Active malignancy or history of aggressive cancer unless medically supervised due to IGF-1 pathway growth-signaling concerns.
  -: Muscle Architect: Known hypersensitivity to PEG-MGF, IGF-1 LR3, or formulation excipients.
  -: Muscle Architect: Pregnancy or breastfeeding due to insufficient safety data.
  -: Muscle Architect: Uncontrolled diabetes or unstable glucose regulation.
  -: Muscle Architect: History of severe hypoglycemia or inability to recognize hypoglycemia symptoms.
  -: Muscle Architect: Active proliferative diabetic retinopathy unless medically supervised.
  -: Muscle Architect: Children, adolescents, or individuals with open growth plates.
  -: Muscle Architect: Use while fasted.
  -: IGF-1 (Mecasermin): The reviewed record is animal research and cannot establish human effectiveness or safety.
  -: Follistatin 344: Whether a UK-purchased 'follistatin' product contains the protein or is something else entirely.
  -: Follistatin 344: Long-term consequences of myostatin pathway suppression in humans.
  -: Follistatin 344: Whether tendons and connective tissue can match the rate of muscle growth produced.
  -: Follistatin 344: WADA detection windows - assume detection, strict-liability applies.
  -: Follistatin 344: Phase 2 / 3 trials in muscular dystrophy underway but no licensed product.
  -: Follistatin 344: Healthy-adult muscle-building outcome data absent.
  -: Follistatin 344: Long-term safety entirely unstudied.
  -: Follistatin 344: Gene-therapy follistatin trials are early-stage with significant safety questions.
  -: PEG-MGF: The reviewed record is animal research and cannot establish human effectiveness or safety.
  -: TB-500: The reviewed record does not state a specific limitation. The linked paper still needs to be checked for design, size and bias.
  -: BPC-157: Whether BPC-157 is safe or appropriate for you as an individual.
  -: BPC-157: What dose, frequency, or duration is right for any human condition.
  -: BPC-157: Whether the product you might encounter is what its label claims.
